title: Ravens Week 7 Rookie Report: Vega Ioane Left Early With Injury
full_text:
Several members of the Baltimore Ravens' 2026 rookie class saw extended action in Sunday's 35-13 home loss to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 7. They are in an AFC North division in which every team's record is above .500, and after falling to 4-3, they now deservedly sit at the bottom of the standings heading into next week.
Drafted and undrafted first-year players saw extensive playing time in all three phases. The only rookies who were healthy scratches were fourth-round wide receiver Elijah Sarratt and undrafted quarterback Joe Fagnano, who still suited up as an emergency No. 3 option. Fifth-round running back Adam Randall wasn't activated from short-term injured reserve in his third week of eligibility and seventh-round defensive tackle Rayshaun Benny is on the practice squad and has yet to be elevated.
Here’s an overview of how these rookies performed in their late taste of NFL regular-season action.
The first-round interior offensive lineman's return to his natural position at right guard after playing the last three games at center was short-lived and cut short due to injury. After taking a knee to his right knee while making a block downfield, he left the game following that drive and did not return. It marked the first time all season that he missed a single snap on offense, as he only played 16 of the Ravens' 67 total snaps on that side of the ball. According to a report from NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Ioane suffered a sprained MCL, and while it's not a long-term injury, he is expected to miss time. Head coach Jesse Minter alluded to the fact that he'll likely miss this week's massive matchup against the Buffalo Bills following Wednesday's practice.
"We'll see where it's at with (Vega)," Minter said. "If there's anybody that can do something crazy and overcome things, he's got the right mentality. We'll see how that goes, and we'll put the best guy out there that gives us the best opportunity for this particular game."
Despite the Ravens losing sack leader and stout run-defending fourth-year pro Tavius Robinson to a season-ending pectoral injury, the second-rounder didn't see a sharp or even slight uptick in playing time on defense, as many expected . His 21 snaps on that side of the ball were his second-lowest of the season and fewest since he played just a dozen in Week 1. He still helped the Ravens bottle up the Bengals' rushing attack to just 73 yards on the ground with an average of just 3.7 yards per carry. Young recorded his seventh solo tackle of the season on a solo takedown of running back Chase Brown after a four-yard gain to prevent him from moving the chains on a penalty-shortened first down.
The third-rounder picked up where he left off in his return from injury last week by picking up key first-down conversions on the first two of the three receptions that he made on five targets for 25 receiving yards. All three came on third down, with the first being a juggling snag he gained control of before backpedaling out of bounds for a gain of 10 yards on the Ravens' second scoring drive. Two plays later, he came up clutch again with a nine-yard snag on third-and-medium that he had to go low to pluck before it could hit the ground. His third catch came on the final play of the third quarter with the Ravens deep in Bengals territory, and had he not had to work back to the quarterback after getting sufficient depth at the top of his route, Lane likely would've been 3-for-3 on third-down conversions as he dragged down two yards shy of the line to gain.
Since his return from the wrist injury that delayed his impact as a rookie, Ja’Kobi Lane has looked impressive, becoming a popular third-down target. The Ravens struck gold in selecting him in the third round. Any questions over drafting him too early have all but disappeared! pic.twitter.com/BykC9TTRAy
Lane nearly had a mulligan on recording his first career touchdown catch on the Ravens' last possession of the first half on a third-and-short in the low red zone. Unfortunately, backup quarterback Tyler Huntley's pass was just out of reach of the long-limbed wideout, who got nice separation from the corner guarding him on the play.
The fourth-rounder played fewer than 30 offensive snaps for the first time in his last four appearances, but it was also his first game back after missing last week with an injury. Hibner wasn't targeted as a pass catcher and was one of multiple players at the position who struggled as blockers in run blocking, either whiffing or straight-up losing block attempts. With veteran Mark Andrews struggling the Ravens need to get the young tight ends more involved.
The fifth-rounder didn't see any playing time on defense for the second straight game, as the Ravens decided to deploy second-year pro Keyon Martin at the nickel spot over him again. Rivers' 13 snaps on special teams were the second-most among rookies and 52% of the team's total.
The fifth-rounder played his fewest offensive snaps since Week 2 with 15, yet that didn't stop him from having his second-most productive outing in that phase of the game with two catches on three targets for 35 receiving yards. He picked up 16 yards on the first play from the scrimmage of the game off a play-action pass from Huntley that he caught short and rumbled for the rest. His other 19 yards came on a tight end screen that moved the offense past midfield and into Cincinnati territory late in the third quarter.
First drive, double motion with Cuevas, then a chip and release to get him wide open while the defense is busy elsewhere. Good layup for Huntley that became absent one the game script became more established. pic.twitter.com/kLqZsJ4OTn
Cuevas was Huntley's intended target on the final play of that same drive, but he collided with a Bengals defender and was knocked off course just enough for the pass to fall incomplete on a fourth-down gamble by Minter, who bypassed another short field goal that would've given the Ravens the lead back.
The #Ravens failed 4th and 1. #RavensFlock pic.twitter.com/QHHOsYILtp
The sixth-round specialist had a solid yet non-spectacular day at the office with three punts for 145 yards, including an average of 48.3 yards per punt and a long of 57, his third-longest of the season. While Eckley didn't have any touchbacks, he didn't manage to pin the Bengals back inside their own 20-yard line once either.
The undrafted free agent helped fill the void created by Robinson's season-ending injury and did a great job in the effort. Burke tied his career highs with 17 defensive snaps and 22 on special teams, first among rookies and tied for the most on the team overall. He was impressive as an edge-setter against the run with how he stacked and effortlessly shed would-be blockers, and nearly notched his second career sack on Joe Burrow, who somehow managed to throw an incomplete pass before the Maryland native could bring him all the way down with possession. Burke's Pro Football Focus grade of 78.5 was the highest among all defenders on the team and second overall to only two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers, who had another monster game and earned a 90.7.
Ravens UDFA Ethan Burke Welcome back Brent urban pic.twitter.com/Xzmc5DMEZ8
Josh is a writer for Baltimore Ravens On SI focusing primarily on original content and reporting. He provides analysis, breakdowns, profiles, and reports on important news and transactions from and about the Ravens. His professional resume as a sports reporter includes covering local events, teams, and athletes in his hometown of Anchorage, Alaska for Anchorage Daily News. His coverage on the Ravens and other NFL teams has been featured on Heavy.com/sports, Maryland Sports Blog and most recently Baltimore Beatdown from 2021 until 2025.

title: 3 Winners and 8 Losers From Ravens' Deflating Loss To Bengals
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens lost back-to-back games for the first time this season in Week 7 on Sunday by allowing a second straight divisional rival to come from behind as the Cincinnati Bengals beat them 35-13 at home .
With franchise quarterback Lamar Jackson out with an ankle injury for the third week in a row, they came into this game as slight underdogs to come out on top but looked like they were well on their way to defying the odds and pulling off the upset after dominating the first half.
Unfortunately,  they went from pitching a shutout to getting shut out in the second half and blowing another double-digit lead for the second week in a row in even more epic fashion. With the loss, they fell to 4-3 and are bottom of the division, where they rightfully belong given how they've played the past two weeks.
Here are several Ravens players and coaches who stepped up and showed out, and others who made some costly mistakes from coaching and execution standpoints.
The two-time Pro Bowler was the only player who balled out in this game and couldn't be stopped no matter what the opposition did to try to slow him down. Flowers eclipsed 100 receiving yards in the first half of a game for the third time this season and for the first time without Jackson playing either half. He finished with a team-leading eight catches on 11 targets for 137 receiving yards and his third touchdown of the season.
ZAY FLOWERS TOUCHDOWN!!!!! 48-YARD TOUCHDOWN TO @ZayFlowers !!! Tune in on CBS! pic.twitter.com/RDspeiOR3T
In a game where Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow was nearly sacked what felt like a half dozen times, the second-year pro was the only defender who managed to actually get him on the ground. Green's third sack of the season and the Ravens' lone sack of the game came at the perfect time, as it secured their first-half shutout since it came in the final 31 seconds and kept the clock running with Cincinnati out of timeouts.
No one picks up Mike Green up the middle leading to a Ravens sack and a 13-0 halftime lead. pic.twitter.com/u3qtCq5E0k
The second-year pro didn't have to attempt a field goal over 40 yards, but the fact that he made all three of his kicks, which included an extra point, bodes well for him after a costly miss inside 50 yards last week. It remains to be seen if Loop has truly gotten past his second-half kicking issue, as the Ravens bypassed their only field goal opportunity in the second half to try to capitalize in the red zone on fourth and short.
There were so many culprits from this unit who were culpable for the Ravens' downfall in this game that they deserved to be lumped together. After only allowing Burrow to complete half of his dozen passing attempts in the first half for a measly 43 passing yards and no touchdowns, they got carved up and torched for 249 and four touchdowns in the second.  Burrow went 16-of-18 over the final two quarters because the Ravens' defensive backs were being taken advantage of and making mistakes every which way.
They failed to plaster in coverage on extended plays, did not properly pass off routes in zone and just straight lost and were outmatched in one-on-one situations at the intermediate level and deep down the field. Tee Higgins went off for 148 receiving yards on six catches, while Ja'Marr Chase made several impressive key grabs, and both scored touchdowns.
The Ravens were able to build their double-digit lead by predominantly having backup quarterback Tyler Huntley throw the ball all over the yard, in large part because their running game couldn't get going, and that didn't get any better after halftime. They weren't able to get any traction on the ground and were especially poor when it came to short-yardage situations, even before stud first-round rookie left with a knee injury. Their inability to win at the point of attack in the trenches has been the main reason the offense as a whole has struggled in Jackson's absence and why they've gotten held to under 100 yards rushing as a team in back-to-back games for the first time since Weeks 2 and 3 of last season.
In his first game against his former team, the four-time Pro  Bowler went from breathing down Burrow's neck for most of the first half despite facing constant double teams to not being much of a factor in the second, along with the rest of the Ravens' pass rush. He finished with a team-leading two quarterback hits, one of which was nearly a sack, but his revenge game was ultimately spoiled by an epic second-half collapse from the unit as a whole.
After a torrid start to the season, the future first-ballot Hall of Famer has been held to fewer than 100 rushing yards and out of the end zone in back-to-back games for the first time since Weeks 13 and 15 of the 2024 season. While he claimed that he had a "terrible" individual performance, that was simply him falling on the sword for his blocking, or rather lack thereof, since he was contacted in the backfield far too often for negative plays and runs that barely got back to or past the line of scrimmage.
For the second week in a row, the first-year play-caller went from looking like the next coming of Sean McVay in the first half to having no answers or adjustments in the second. With his young tight ends struggling to make and sustain blocks out of condensed formations, he didn't run the ball enough out of spread formations, and his biggest mistake was not using his mobile backup quarterback's legs enough.
Huntley isn't Lamar Jackson in terms of his ability to cut and move laterally; nobody is, but he is a strong North-South runner. Doyle didn't dial up a single quarterback power or draw for him and waited until it was too little, too late to call his first and only quarterback sneak, which didn't come until the fourth quarter when the Bengals were up by 22 points and had all the momentum, and it failed miserably.
As has been the case in all three of their losses and even in some of their wins, the Ravens struggled to bring ball carriers and pass catchers down in open space and short of the line to gain, and especially in high-leverage moments after halftime. They went from flying around and playing fast and physical downhill with great results in the first two quarters to missing multiple opportunities to make key stops and force negative plays for sacks and tackles for loss.
According to PFF, the Ravens missed 11 tackles (7 on pass plays). Here's 4 from the 4th quarter. pic.twitter.com/fkc5MK6DUA
Chances of winning division
While the Ravens still possess a winning record heading into next week's massive road conference matchup with the Buffalo Bills, they're now the only team in the AFC North without a win against a divisional opponent. If the rest of their rivals keep stacking wins, they won't be able to make up any ground until December, since they close out the regular season with four straight division games, concluding with a road primetime game against the Bengals on New Year's Eve and a home finale against the Pittsburgh Steelers 10 days later
Having Huntley under center in this game instead of Jackson nerfed any chance the Ravens had of winning a shootout with Burrow and the Bengals, but it didn't come to that until after halftime. However, as bad as being without a two-time league MVP is, that should have no bearing on how woefully poor the defense played for the final two quarters.
A collection of star-studded talent that was being hailed as a potential top-10, if not top-five, unit got absolutely dog-walked up and down the field on their way to making history in the worst way by becoming the first team in the franchise's 31-year history to get outscored by 35 or more points in a half. The fact that they haven't scored a single second-half point in six of the eight quarters they've played without Jackson is an embarrassing travesty that falls on the shoulders of the players and coaches collectively.
Josh is a writer for Baltimore Ravens On SI focusing primarily on original content and…

title: Everything Ravens Coach Jesse Minter Said About Lamar Jackson And What It Means for Sunday
full_text:
Ravens rookie head coach Jesse Minter, now going on a week into quarterback Lamar Jackson’s absence from an ankle injury, was more guarded than ever speaking about the lingering isse after Wednesday’s practice.
Minter spent three weeks calling it a “day-to-day” situation with Jackson even though the two-time MVP said last week it was a high-ankle sprain that was “very, very painful.” Minter would not even specify whether Jackson did any more or less work than he was able to do last week and he repeatedly referred the injury report.
When the injury report was released, Jackson was listed as a full participant. He suffered the injury at the end of the first half in Week 4 against the Titans, he did not return to practice until last week in a limited capacity, and Baltimore has continued to blow double-digit leads at an astounding rate without him, now 4-3 heading into a crucial game at Buffalo they are frankly unlikely to win without Jackson.
“He was able to get some work in, but I think that will come out about 4 (pm), I believe,” Minter said about his injured QB. When pressed on the matter about the extent of Jackson’s work Wednesday, he said: “Um, yeah, I think the more you are able to do, and respond from and feel from raises your optimism but, again, we’ll kind of see how it goes through the week.”
When Jackson was brought again, Minter offered: “I think the injury report will kind of say how the practice went.”
Minter is wise to take a more cryptic route given how things transpired last Friday when Jackson spoke to the media for the first time since suffering the injury and spoke to a timeline quite different to what the front office was giving Minter as his public marching orders on the situation (just another ugly public embarrasment for the Ravens ignominious PR chief). The CBS broadcast added to what could only be rightfully perceived as a disconnect from how the team was couching the injury, and how the player himself was speaking about it.
Our instincts and reporting have been far better than the media at large since the moment Jackson suffered the injury, and at this point, a short turnaround against Jacksonville at home in prime time, we’d be surprised if Jackson played Sunday unless he practices fully all week.
Kyle Hamilton (knee), by far the best performer on a struggling defense so far, was among those who did not practice Wednesday (rookie guard Vega Ioane did not either and is expected to miss time with a knee injury). Minter said he “felt pretty good” that some of the players who were unable to work on the field Wednesday could still be back for Week 8. Middle linebacker Roquan Smith (knee) also missed practice.
The Ravens have lost 17 times since 2019 when leading by 10-or-more points and have done it twice in a row against AFC teams and three times this season. General manager Eric DeCosta, who loves to gush about his relationship with Jackson but can’t ever get his contract extension like a competent GM, got to handpick Minter and his novice staff, should have been fired when Harbaugh was, and his job security is a major subplot to the upcoming trade deadline for his latest middling roster.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: What Ravens Week 7 Debacle Changed About Their NFL Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
The Ravens’ long-suspect defense was getting exposed by bad NFL quarterbacks in the second half of games all season so the fact they got shredded by Joe Burrow Sunday wasn’t much of a surprise. However, the blasé response from a roster loaded with defenders in the top 10 in compensation at their position was alarming.
Longtime NFL coach Marvin Lewis explained to us the poor coverage technique and communication breakdowns that have crippled this Ravens secondary as it has most of them since 2019. Overwhelmed rookie head coach Jesse Minter was asked about the effort of his defense after yielding 35 unanswered points in the second half to the Bengals and remarked about their tackling issues. He’s openly pondering who, among his highly-compensated defensive roster and a secondary almost entire filled with first-round picks, will emerge as a real leader - 'Who's the guy that's going to grab everybody together, get them together on the sideline?’ he opined at his Monday press conference.
Yeah, this is critical mass, already, nearing the midpoint of the first season without a proven head coach in Baltimore for a loooong time.
The only person in power in Owings Mills who is being more runover and exposed than Minter is the perpetual underachiever who hired him – general manager Eric DeCosta. The guy who amassed even more money and power when longtime head coach John Harbaugh and his experienced staff were fired in January, despite needing to be fired at the same time.
The guy who likes to strut the sidelines like a coach with his sunglasses on at night looking for the cameras during prime time games – oh, he’s sweating now with his head in his hands in the locker room after games. The guy who always blames coaches for his roster failures is alone on the hotseat now; DeCosta knows his defensive backs are a joke and now he needs to do something about it. Already $370M committed in payroll, and with injured MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson able to dictate any more he wants with any team he prefers this offseason , DeCosta must try to salvage his defense, and Sunday brought it all to a head.
Believe it or not, DeCosta needs a defensive back, desperately (preferably a slot corner), and he needs to ship one out.
It’s not just about on-field direction, it’s about sending a message now going on seven years of getting DeCosta-ed game after game: three losses with a double-digit lead in the second half this season – two in a row! - and 17 since 2019, when DeCosta took over for legend Ozzie Newsome (and like every other Newsome protegee, we see just how little of Newsome’s unique genius transfers to others).  Sure, it would be great if DeCosta backed up his silly narrative about wanting both Maxx Crosby and "closer" Trey Hendrickson back in March with a trade to the Raiders without backing out and exposing himself this time. But that was just a grift to try to sell tickets .
Despite years of shunning most every other personnel group on his roster to stock up on DBs, they have a crisis there. The Ravens are getting killed in the slot, their corners and safeties have poor ball skills and never impact the football. And more than anything else, they better change their choking culture with over-entitled and underachieving players on bloated contracts – ever-rewarded for being one of DeCosta’s favorites – and shake up the dynamics of a failing locker room.
They won’t get anything for Humphrey with that $15M salary ($19.3M in total take-home pay this season) at the deadline and it doesn’t matter. He’s worn people out on multiple coaching staffs and in that locker room for years, he’s had one truly good and healthy season in the past four, and if they haven’t moved him to the slot yet, maybe that’s telling us all something. Because the slot coverage has been as bad as any in the NFL.
TJ Tampa could get a run on the outside with Nate Wiggins (you better get a real GM in here before DeCosta does another asinine contract with one of his over-drafted first round picks who lacks anything close to a playmaking gene). Maybe that helps.
But if you keep sending the message to this overhyped and over-coddled secondary (man do DeCosta and complete baseball failure Mike Elias have a lot in common) that everyone keeps their job no matter what, and the performance on the field and in the locker room and on the sidelines doesn’t matter, then keep your mouth shut and eat it when you keep getting DeCosta-ed every week.
Because that’s what’s going to keep happening.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Ravens GM Claimed He Wanted Crosby And Hendrickson In March. He Should Prove it Now
full_text:
Believe it or not, Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta has built another failure defense.
Of course, it happens every year – outside of one time with Mike Macdonald in charge – with a feeble roster devoid of playmakers on that side of the ball but filled with bloated contracts he loves to dole out to his favorites . Turns out even genius rookie head coach Jesse Minter – looking overrun and clueless in the second half of games with the most novice staff in the NFL (like DeCosta wanted) – can’t keep this team from constantly blowing double-digit, second-half leads and losing.
Now they’ve DeCosta-ed two weeks in a row to division foes, and three times already this season and they’ve DeCosta-ed a record 17 times since 2019. Baltimore has allowed more points than any NFL team in the second half (114) with an unfathomable -70 scoring differential. And, as always, DeCosta’s handpicked players offer zero pass rush when it really counts - $30M alleged "closer" Trey Hendrickson has four pressures, a 10% pressure rate and no sacks in the fourth quarter – and the team does not have a second-half interception despite being thrown on constantly.
DeCosta, every bit as smug and condescending and egomaniacal as Orioles baseball failure Mike Elias, thinks he’s a rare roster builder. But his first-round pick corners and safeties (Kyle Hamilton is a linebacker) and top-10 paid corners have combined for as many picks this season as my dog Meatball. Minter, lauded as a defensive scheme savant, is getting undressed every week – usually by bad quarterbacks – in his zone looks in dime coverage; he’s scared to blitz and he can’t muster pass rush late in games bringing just four.
The Ravens are 20th in opposing passer rating; 27th in opposer passer rating targeting the slot. They-re getting destroyed by anything close to a No. 1 receiver and Minter is already opining about aimless locker room leadership. Man, we are only seven games in with DeCosta’s handpicked coach and fraud alerts are going off all over Owings Mills. Did I mention the top two coaches the Ravens fired, to keep DeCosta in charge, John Harbaugh and Todd Monken, are top NFL Coach of the Year candidates?
So, um, what’s this overhyped GM going to do about it? The one who, if the billionaire he works for wasn’t checked out and half-asleep, would have been fired when he fired Harbaugh in January? Maybe DeCosta should just do what he was running his mouth about in March. Seems logical enough. Being a man of his word and all, and such a hotshot dealmaker.
Hey Eric, just go back to that big plan you had this winter. The one you couldn’t shut up about when you bailed out of the Maxx Crosby trade. Surely that wasn’t just a grift to help your boss sell tickets was it? That wouldn’t be you.
You don’t want to be the King Of No Rings forever, do you? Man up, champ.
In case you missed it – this is what was being peddled over at Baltimoreravens.com on March 11 with the breathless headline: Ravens Wanted To Get Crosby And Hendrickson:
“General Manager Eric DeCosta confirmed reports Wednesday that Baltimore actively worked on deals with Crosby and Hendrickson at the same time. “That was definitely a possibility for us. Not to say that it would've happened, but definitely something that we had contemplated and discussed with Trey."
So since then, DeCosta failed to get Lamar Jackson signed – again, as usual – and he could be in his final year here if that’s what the two-time MVP decides he wants . DeCosta built maybe his worst offensive line yet – that truly saying something by his lowly standards – and he’s helped cultivate another controversy about Jackson’s health by having his puppet coach call a high-ankle sprain that’s cost Jackson three games a “day-to-day” situation going on a month.
Boy, this perpetually-underachieving exec, who built a career and reputation off of Ozzie Newsome’s work (DeCosta is the epitome of Newsome’s fruitless scouting family tree ), really has dug himself a big hole this time. But good thing he already told his fanbase what to expect back in March, with that master plan for two dominant edge defenders (well, Hendrickson doesn’t defend much of anything in the run game, but you get the idea).
Because nobody needs Crosby more than this huckster right now. And nobody flapped his jaws about him more in the offseason.
There isn’t a more desperate and panicked exec than DeCosta anywhere in the NFL right now.
The Seahawks (with the kind of elite GM) DeCosta pretends to be) landing All Pro guard Quenton Nelson for far less than DeCosta just gave up for concussed lineman Cam Jurgens, a delusional bounty for a struggling lineman is a bad look (Ravens had their worst run blocking of the season in Jurgens's first game with them, bummer). And multiple GMs I’ve touched base with believe the Raiders would still deal Crosby for two ones. So there’s hope!
Now, the problem is, the league knows DeCosta’s word doesn’t mean much, and they know he played the medical card as an excuse to pull out of the Crosby trade because the entire industry believed he had overpaid (just like he ended up doing for Jurgens, funny how that works). And because Hendrickson had a soft market (since he’s older and become injury prone and is a liability on early downs).
But Eric, your prayers have been answered! Crosby returned for Week 1, miraculously, and guess what? He’s still kicking ass.
Get this, he’s playing like 95% of the reps for the Raiders and can still dominate games. And we all know he’s a significantly better football player than Hendrickson, I mean that’s why you went after him before Hendrickson and then (oh man this is rich) concurrently. And Hendrickson turns out to be the guy who can’t finish a game or stay off the injury report. Yeah, who could have seen that coming.
And worst of all, the guy actually leading your pathetic roster in sacks – Tavius Robinson – is out for year. You already started mortgaging the 2028 draft for Jurgens, Jackson has you by the throat in that negotiation, and with a record $370M payroll, what’s another $15M for Crosby? You think Jurgens was worth $17M? Crosby at $29M next year is a steal.
It's only money, and Steve has plenty; but your word is worth everything, isn't it?
Salary cap issues? Take that base salary down to vet minimum, give Crosby the money up front, maybe tack on money on the back end to get him to come back here. Least you could do for the odious way you handled him in March. Who cares about draft picks now when you’re wasting what could be Lamar’s last year in Baltimore. And let’s be real, most of yours don’t really pan out, anyway.
You weren’t taking your fans for fools back in March, were you? You wouldn’t have your vast in-house media laundering false promises and BS, would you? No way. Not you. So go execute that big plan you and Bisciotti were hatching six months ago.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Three Players the Ravens Need To Move On From Before the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens have reached a crossroads way before the mid-season point, losing two straight in truly ridiculous fashion -- shutting out their opponents in the first half and then getting shutout and overtaken in the second.
Thus, the Ravens currently sit with a 4-3 record in last place in the AFC North -- a division they were heavy favorites to win -- and with a road game in Buffalo on the horizon, things could start to unravel quickly for Baltimore.
With the NFL trade deadline less than two weeks away, the Ravens must consider unloading a few players in order to either acquire some immediate help in return, or start loading up on draft capital for next year. Either way, several names on Baltimore’s roster just don’t make any sense for the team anymore, regardless of what eventually becomes of the 2026 campaign.
Here are three players that the Ravens should consider trading away before the deadline:
As hard as it is to say goodbye to the top pass-catcher in franchise history, it’s time.
Andrews hasn't just become a non-factor in the Ravens’ offense , but also a liability with dropped passes. Sure, there is no clear successor at the tight end position, and Baltimore wasted a huge opportunity by letting Isaiah Likely walk in free agency, but Andrews is just not cutting it anymore (averaging $13M/season makes it tough).
Rookie Matthrew Hibner was, at one point, playing on more than half of the Ravens snaps, and fellow-rookie Josh Cuevas has seen his usage go up steadily as the season has progressed. Veteran Nick Vannett took some snaps away from Hibner once he was promoted from the practice squad in early October, but that was expected. Blocking specialist Durham Smythe, on the other hand, will miss the rest of the season due to an Achilles’ injury.
The depth chart might not be in a great place, but Andrews is not making very much of a difference anyway. He hasn’t reached 50 receiving yards in any game (he's done it once since the start of last season), and has a single receiving touchdown for the season. He’s also recording personal lows of 7.8 yards per catch and 5.5 yards per route run.
Baltimore really needs to spread out Andrews’ targets among the remaining three tight ends and rookie wideout Ja’Kobi Lane, and see who will step up as the passing game’s safety net of the future.
At an average of just 20 rushing yards per game and 12 receiving yards per game -- as a pass-catching alternative to Derrick Henry in the backfield -- Hill is just not working out. At his current pace, he would finish the season with under 350 rushing yards and just over 200 receiving yards, and he hasn’t scored once either way. He hasn’t logged a broken tackle for the year, either.
The Ravens haven’t been great at maximizing Hill, either. He’s averaging 3.0 yards before contact per rush -- compared to Henry’s 1.9 -- and 6.7 yards per rushing attempt, but Baltimore isn’t giving him enough carries to make a difference or at least find a rhythm.
The market for soon-to-be 29-year-old running backs with limited production and no previous experience as the top guy will be miniscule, but Hill does contribute on special teams and is considered a reliable blocker. It’s just that he’s not taking enough of the load off Henry’s shoulders .
Adam Randall is still on IR with no word on when he might be coming back, and the Ravens have Jonathan Ward on the practice squad, so looking for a street agent option could work. The pool of available guys with experience as primary runners is attractive for a team looking at a one-year rental, including Raheem Moster, Alexander Mattison, Kareem Hunt, Antonio Gibson, Miles Sanders and Joe Mixon, and each one of them should have an accessible price tag.
Walker’s case is truly strange. A 25-year-old fourth rounder from 2024 who has the same number of touchdown catches than starts in his pro career (five), but just 11 receptions over 20 games played.
His 0.75 yards per route run this year seem almost impossible to believe, yet here we are.
It seems Baltimore’s passers just don’t trust Walker, because his usage on the field isn’t dramatically low. He’s played in almost 40 percent of the Ravens’ offensive snaps this year, yet has managed just nine targets and four catches. All this despite top wideout Zay Flowers missing one game and top rookie Ja’Kobi Lane missing four this year , so there have been some chances.
If the Ravens aren’t going to try and develop Walker, they should trade him to a team that will. Rookie fourth-rounder Elijah Sarratt has played in just one game and sorely needs some of the reps that Walker has been handed with no returns. The compensation for Walker will be very low, but his production after two and a half years has been even lower.
Rafael brings over two decades of experience writing about all things football.

title: Ranking Buffalo Bills' Biggest NFL Trade Deadline Needs Under Two Weeks Left
full_text:
We are roughly two weeks from the 2026 NFL trade deadline and while the Buffalo Bills aren't seen as an overly aggressive team when it comes to the deadline, general manager Brandon Beane should be willing to make some moves.
Buffalo is considered one of the elite contenders this season, but other teams in line for a title run aren't sitting idly by. The Seattle Seahawks added Quenton Nelson to shore up their defensive line, the Chicago Bears went for a home run with defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons , and even the San Francisco 49ers improved by bringing back DeForest Buckner.
The Bills still have the talent to contend, but they need to take a page from these other teams and address some of their biggest concerns. That said, here's a look at the top four most pressing needs that Beane should be actively looking to fill.
Greg Rousseau was off to a hot start, with six sacks in the first three games of the season. Unfortunately, he's been silenced over the past three games and has been held without a sack. In fact, the pass rush as a whole has been quiet since Rousseau's explosiveness went away.
Buffalo enters Week 8 with 11 total sacks and other than Rousseau, no player has more than Bradley Chubb's 1.5. The Bills did use their first pick in the 2026 NFL draft (which was in Round 2) on T.J. Parker, but he hasn't provided a major spark. He still has plenty of upside, but they need someone who can give them a lift now, which makes outside linebacker a priority.
More concerning that outside linebacker, however, is the inside linebacker position in Buffalo. Dorian Williams is their highest-rated inside linebacker, according to PFF , earning a 64.6 through the first six games of the season. Terrel Bernard, on the other hand, is sitting at a 53.9. That's far better than rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr, who has a 40.8 currently.
The concern is whether or not the Bills will admit this is a problem. They signed Shaq Thompson to the practice squad, but have yet to activate him for a regular season game . They seem committed to Williams and Bernard, and given Bernard's salary, they might not be willing to admit there's an issue.
That doesn't mean they shouldn't add some help, because this remains one of the more problematic positions on their entire defense.
The recent signing of Tre'Davious White gives the Bills some insurance at cornerback, but that doesn't solve all their isses. While White played well for them in 2025, he was returning to a defensive scheme he knew well under Sean McDermott. Now, he joins a defense led by Jim Leonhard and as we saw when he played for the Los Angeles Rams and Baltimore Ravens in 2024, White wasn't the same without McDermott.
That doesn't mean he can't find success under Leonhard, but the Bills can't count on him to be the one to save this underperforming group. Instead, they should be actively looking for someone who can not only help now, but perhaps allow them to move on completely from Maxwell Hairston, who has gone completely into Leonhard's doghouse .
Even before C.J. Gardner-Johnson's recent suspension for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers, there were already reasons to be concerned with him. Gardner-Johnson can come up with some big plays, like when he had the interception against the Los Angeles Chargers, but he also has some big whiffs, including his two missed tackles against the Raiders before losing his cool.
What's worse is his attitude. Not only did he spit at a player, but he refused to admit he did and gave one of the worst excuses afterward , saying it was all about being competitive.
Outside of Gardner-Johnson, Buffalo is leaning heavily on Cole Bishop and Damar Hamlin, and neither are playing particularly well this season. Hamlin has the highest PFF grade of 59.1, while Bishop is struggling with a 51.3. Gardner-Johnson is in the middle, with a 55.2. Simply put, none have been living up to expectations, especially in coverage. That's a huge reason why Buffalo is currently 31st in the league in pass defense.
There are players available, with Amani Hooker of the Tennessee Titans standing out as the best option in coverage, but Beane has to be willing to pull the trigger. If he does nothing else at this deadline, adding someone who can play deep coverage would be a massive win for the Buffalo defense.

title: Bills Trade Rumor From NFL Insider Leaves Open Possibility of Multiple Deals
full_text:
We know the Buffalo Bills need help on the defensive side of the ball, but they also have needs at more than one position, so one trade might not be enough to solve their woes.
The Bills are sporting one of the worst defenses in the NFL , with the unit giving up the third-most points and second-most pass yards per contest.
Expecting a team to make multiple trades before the deadline is usually expecting too much, but for the Bills, it appears to be a possibility.
According to Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer , the Bills might be in the market for more than one player on defense. He didn't say at what positions, but the simple fact that Breer indicates the Bills could make multiple moves is eye-opening and promising for Buffalo.
"The Bills are looking for another piece or two on defense," Breer wrote.
On defense, the interior of the defensive line and edge rusher are the most secure spots, although it wouldn't be totally shocking to see the Bills to add to either one.
The three big needs for Buffalo come at cornerback, safety and inside linebacker, all of which have concerns.
At safety, the unpredictable nature of C.J. Gardner-Johnson, whose play has been a disappointment, also, is a huge worry.
Gardner-Johnson has been known to melt down and get himself cut from teams, and we saw that first hand when he committed a cuttable offense by spitting on a Las Vegas Raiders player and getting himself ejected and then suspended for one game, a suspension he will serve in Week 8.
But Gardner-Johnson isn't the only problem at safety. Cole Bishop has been decent but not great, and the Bills lack reliable depth in Damar Hamlin and Jalon Kilgore that leaves the team one injury away from being in a disastrous situation.
At cornerback, the Bills aren't at the point that they can rely on anyone not named Christian Benford. Maxwell Hairston hasn't taken the step forward the Bills need and Davison Igbinosun remains a wild card.
Dee Alford hasn't been great, either, and he's banged up again this week and is in serious doubt to play after going from limited on Wednesday to a non-participant on Thursday .
At linebacker, the Bills need a starting-caliber player next to Terrel Bernard. Dorian Williams just isn't that guy and rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr needs more time to develop.
General manager Brandon Beane has some work to do before Nov. 10, but the good news is, based on the rumor from Breer, it looks like he might be willing to do what's necessary to get the job done.

title: Bills' Updated Week 8 Injury Report: Optimism for DJ Moore, Ed Oliver vs. Ravens
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills practiced without three key pieces on Thursday in Week 8.
As the Bills prepare for a 1 p.m. ET home kickoff against the Baltimore Ravens on November 1, starting right tackle Spencer Brown missed practice for the second day in a row.
Primary slot cornerback Dee Alford was downgraded from limited on Wednesday to a non-participant on Thursday , suggesting he could have tweaked his ankle during practice.
Additionally, backup running back, and primary kick returner, Ray Davis was absent due to illness.
Davis was one of two names added to Thursday's injury report. After practicing in full without a designation on Wednesday, special teams ace Joe Andreessen popped up as a limited participant one day later.
Andreessen, who has played 77 percent of special teams snaps, was last on the injury report in Week 5 due to a nagging knee issue. It's unknown if he reaggravated the knee at practice on Thursday, but it seems more likely the limited participation is part of a maintenance plan for the linebacker.
Brown left the Week 5 win against the Rams after only 16 snaps due to a back flare-up. The starting bookend, who has a history of back issues, attributed the problem to a muscular "freak out."
After taking 100 percent of the reps on the Week 6 victory over the Raiders, Brown's back apparently responded poorly over the bye week.
"Just lingering stuff from what's happened to me last couple weeks. What happened in that LA game, just kind of got nicked up. Took enough drugs to sedate a small elephant when I was in LA," said Brown on Wednesday . "Just took care of the body the best way I knew how and got through the Vegas game and played pretty well. Got on the bye week, kind of bit me in the butt a little bit."
The experienced Brown doesn't necessarily need to practice during the week to be play come Sunday, but his absences certainly cast some doubt on his potential availability.
"Had a good meeting with [Joe] Brady yesterday, and he has a lot of trust in me and respect for what I've done so far here for the first six years I've been here. He knows I can be ready whenever," said Brown.
As for Alford, his participation downgrade comes as somewhat of a surprise, considering he played a full game against the Raiders last time out. It's possible he reaggravated his ankle injury during Wednesday's practice.
Alford initially injured his ankle during the Week 4 loss to the New England Patriots. He was inactive for the ensuing game against the Rams, but he returned to play 43 snaps against the Raiders.
The Bills don't have much depth behind Alford as backup nickel cornerback Jordan Hancock remains on Injured Reserve.
Moore practice in a limited capacity for the second day in a row. Wearing a red non-contact jersey likely for precautionary reasons, the Bills' top wide receiver was seen reaching over his head to make catches in an encouraging sign for the health of his AC joint.
Initially injuring his shoulder in Week 2 , Moore reaggravated the injury in Week 4. In a rare occurrence, he missed back-to-back games in Weeks 5 and 6. After seeing his consecutive appearance streak end at 91 regular season games, Moore appears itching to return .
"The two weeks [out], it was pretty sad. I was mad at myself," said Moore on Wednesday. "Somebody put out a post on X where I was standing there watching the guys practice, that was the hardest thing about the two weeks."
Meanwhile, in a highly encouraging sign for his Week 8 availability, defensive tackle Ed Oliver increased his participation to full on Thursday.
Like Moore, Oliver missed back-to-back games heading into the bye week. He was forced out during the October 4 game against the Patriots when former Bills' fullback Reggie Gilliam hit the lineman on the left leg in the knee area.
Oliver missed five consecutive practices before finally returning in a limited capacity on October 16.
Defensive lineman TJ Sanders also improved from limited to full on Thursday.

title: Bills' Three Keys to Victory vs. Ravens in Week 8
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills suffered their first loss of the season at home in Week 4 against the New England Patriots. They then went on the road for back-to-back games on the West Coast and regained plenty of confidence.
Buffalo defeated the Los Angeles Rams and Las Vegas Raiders, sending them into their Week 7 bye with a 5-1 record. They also had an extra week to prepare for a talented Baltimore Ravens team who enters the game 4-3.
These two teams last met in Week 1 of the 2025 season, and it was one for the ages. Buffalo won in comeback fashion, with Matt Prater hitting a field goal to give them a 41-40 victory. There should be fireworks once again in this one with these two offenses, but the Bills can win if they focus on these keys to victory.
Buffalo has the No. 1 offense in the NFL, entering Week 8 with 197 points scored in six games. The only thing that has slowed them down is turnovers, with Josh Allen and James Cook both having their issues holding onto the ball at different times.
When facing a team as dangerous as the Ravens, this can't happen. Allen needs to be careful with his throws and Cook has to keep both hands on the football. They can't play scared, but they also have to stay focused and avoid shooting themselves in the foot.
Lamar Jackson missed three games with a high ankle sprain, but there's a chance that he can be back on the field this week. While he's coming off an injury, Buffalo can't anticipate Jackson being limited in any way.
The Bills haven' faced many "running" quarterbacks this year, although they did allow Drake Maye to rush for 54 yards which was critical to the Patriots' success. While Jackson is capable of beating teams with his arm, he's at his most dangerous when he starts running, which is why the Bills have to stay disciplined on defense and keep him in the pocket.
Even if Jackson doesn't play, the focus needs to be the same. Tyler Huntley isn't as dangerous as Jackson, but he's a mobile quarterback who can extend plays. Regardless of who is playing, the Bills need to keep them contained and force them to throw. Of course, they will need the secondary to defend, but the first step is taking the threat of the quarterback run out of the equation.
One thing that could help Buffalo keep Jackson (or Huntley) under control, and perhaps Derrick Henry as well, is the struggles Baltimore has had on the offensive line. They recently traded for Cam Jurgens to try and shore things up, but that's just another shuffle they've had to make due to injuries.
The Bills will have an advantage here because of that, especially in the interior. That's where someone such as Deone Walker could take advantage and collapse the pocket. Of course, it would help to see Greg Rousseau return to the form he showed early in the season and make some plays off the edge as well. Either way, the Bills have an advantage here and must capitalize.

title: Bills' Starters Spencer Brown, Dee Alford Sidelined With Week 8 Availability TBD
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills ' offense was missing its starting right tackle and the defense was without its primary slot cornerback on Thursday in Orchard Park.
As the Bills prepare to host the Baltimore Ravens for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on November 1, bookend Spencer Brown and defensive back Dee Alford were non-participants at practice due to injuries.
It was the second consecutive missed practice for Brown, who is dealing with back issues. Meanwhile, after participating in a limited capacity on Wednesday, Alford was downgraded on Thursday.
Additionally, running back Ray Davis was absent due to illness.
A back flare-up sent Brown to the locker room after 16 snaps against the Los Angeles Rams on October 12.
"Just lingering stuff from what's happened to me last couple weeks. What happened in that LA game, just kind of got nicked up. Took enough drugs to sedate a small elephant when I was in LA," said Brown addressing reporters on Wednesday.
Brown returned to the starting lineup six days later against the Las Vegas Raiders, and he didn't miss a snap . Apparently, his back did not respond well heading into the bye week.
"Just taking it easy and smart. Had a good meeting with [Joe] Brady yesterday, and he has a lot of trust in me and respect for what I've done so far here for the first six years I've been here. He knows I can be ready whenever," said Brown.
Despite a history of back problems, Brown has been readily available in recent seasons for the most part. He's averaging 15 starts per season over the past three years.
"I do pride myself on being ready every single day. I got to roll out of bed and play on Sunday morning and have no problems," said Brown.
Should Brown need the week off, backup Tylan Grable is likely to start in his place.
Alford's regression is somewhat of a surprise, considering he made it through the Week 6 road win over the Raiders. The slot cornerback was on the field for 43 of 66 defensive snaps.
The ankle issue, however, isn't new. Suffering the injury on October 4 against the Patriots, Alford was unavailable in Week 5 against the Rams.
Alford practiced on a limited basis throughout the week leading up to the Raiders game. He was officially questionable to play before soldiering through the 33-30 victory.
It's possible that Alford reaggravated the injury during Wednesday's practice, being that he was listed as a limited participant before sitting out the following day.
While backup nickel cornerback Jordan Hancock remains on Injured Reserve, it's unknown who the Bills would deploy if the event that Alford must sit again. Anthony Kendall, who played emergency snaps against the Rams, was released from the practice squad earlier this week.

title: Titans Give Bills Green Light For Much-Needed Safety Trade After Jeffery Simmons Deal
full_text:
As massive trades continue to go down with just under two weeks left before the Nov. 10 trade deadline hits, the Buffalo Bills have remained quiet.
On Monday, we saw the San Francisco 49ers acquire DeForest Buckner from the Indianapolis Colts. Then, the next day, Indy unloaded Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks .
Last but not least in the flurry of recent trades, the Tennessee Titans sent Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears in a blockbuster trade that included two first-round picks.
The Simmons trade should be of particular interest to the Bills, but not because of Simmons himself.
Now that the Titans have unloaded Simmons, it's a clear sign that Tennessee is open to trading anyone. After all, Simmons was the team's best player and general manager Mike Borgonzi had no interest in dealing him before the Bears made a sick offer.
So, who should the Bills be eyeing in Nashville?
That would be safety Amani Hooker , who won't be anywhere near as expensive as Simmons, of course.
The Bills' situation at safety is shaky.
Cole Bishop has only been OK this season and C.J. Gardner-Johnson has not been good enough. Adding to that, Gardner-Johnson is very unpredictable and his ability to self-destruct means tomorrow is never promised today with him, as we witnessed when he got suspended for spitting recently .
If Gardner-Johnson was to get himself cut, as we've seen happen to him during his career, or if one of Bishop or Gardner-Johnson suffer an injury, the Bills will be in a precarious spot.
The depth options include Damar Hamlin, who we know is not a starting-caliber player, and rookie Jalon Kilgore, who is unproven.
At the very least, the Bills could use more depth, but what they really need is a starter, which Hooker is.
Hooker offers a versatile safety option with his experience playing both free and strong safety, and in the slot.
When he plays near the line of scrimmage, Hooker is an excellent run defender, with his 84.6 run defense grade ranking 10th at his position in 2026, according to Pro Football Focus .
But Hooker is no slouch in coverage, either. His 67 coverage grade ranks 23rd among safeties and he has permitted an impressive passer rating of 70.1 when targeted.
Creating turnovers is something Hooker does well, also. He has 14 career picks, including two this season, five forced fumbles and two fumbles recoveries over his eight seasons in the league.
Another attractive thing about Hooker is he's under contract through 2028, so he won't just be a short-term rental. In the same breath, there are outs in his contract over the next two years, so if this experiment fails, the Bills can easily cut him.
It's hard to say what the price would be for Hooker because we do not know if the Titans want to hold on to him as much as they did Simmons, which would mean it'll take a Godfather-style offer to get him. If that's the case, the Bills should pass.
But if this isn't that kind of situation, we suspect the Bills might be able to get him for a fourth-round pick, in which case it's a no-brainer for Buffalo.

title: Thurman Thomas Says Josh Allen Barely Makes Bills' Mount Rushmore
full_text:
Josh Allen is already known as one of the best players in Buffalo Bills history .
He's second in franchise history in both passing yardage (31,606) and passing touchdowns (229), behind only Jim Kelly. He's also one of the most impressive runners in franchise history, currently sitting at fourth in yardage (4,961), but is first in rushing touchdowns with 87.
Most fans would say he's done enough to be one of the four greatest players in team history, but Bills legend Thurman Thomas isn't sure he's there just yet. While speaking with Julian Edelman, Thomas named three players who would be his top selection for his Bills Mount Rushmore: Jim Kelly, Bruce Smith, and O.J. Simpson.
As for the final spot, Thomas said he would put "Half of Josh Allen up there," although he did express confidence that Allen's on the right path to completely claim that spot.
"I mean, Jim Kelly, Bruce Smith. I would say OJ would be there. And I can say right now, probably you can put half of Josh Allen up there right now," Thomas said.
"If he continues on this run of whatever, and I wish and I hope and pray that we do get a Super Bowl. I hope he does bring a Super Bowl here to Buffalo. But I think the things that this guy has done. When you talk about Josh, there's always, oh, this is the first guy in history to do this. This is the first guy in history to do that. It's always a first. And so, yeah, I'm like, you know what? I'm halfway there of building and Josh being that fourth guy of Mount Rushmore."
Edelman then asked Thomas if the city could survive the party that would follow a Buffalo championshop this season.
"I don't think the city will survive. There's something going around over and under of how many people will die from drinking," Thomas said. "Seriously. Seriously. There would not be a party like the Buffalo Bills with Bills Mafia when we win a Super Bowl. Because I think Josh will get it done."
Thomas has faith that Allen will be the quarterback to finally bring a title to Western New York. The real question is whether general manager Brandon Beane can do enough to build a winner around Allen.
With the 2026 NFL trade deadline approaching , teams such as the Chicago Bears and Seattle Seahawks have been actively addressing their needs , whereas the Bills continue to lean on Allen to make up for their shortcomings.
Perhpaps he can out on the Superman cape and make it happen, but it would be nice to see the organization be more proactive around him.

title: Bills' Most Disappointing Player Thus Far for NFL's Top Scoring Offense
full_text:
It hasn't officially reached sophomore slump territory, but there has undeniably been a noticeable decrease in production.
For a late fifth-round draft pick , his rookie season was so good, it was always going to be difficult for Buffalo Bills ' tight end Jackson Hawes to avoid a step back in Year 2.
Unfortunately, Hawes has seemingly suffered a regression to the mean over his first six games.
Not missing a game as the Bills' third tight end during the 2025 campaign, Hawes quickly established himself as a fierce, effective blocker routinely displacing opposing bodies in the trenches.
Despite continuing to see a significant snap share for the NFL's highest scoring offense (32.8), Hawes hasn't been heard from much this year, except when his number is being called for a penalty.
"I know the questions get brought up on the defense, but offense hasn't played well enough," said head coach Joe Brady this week as the Bills prepare for a November 1 home game against the Baltimore Ravens
Although Brady didn't name names, Hawes has seemingly failed to meet expectations thus far.
After being tabbed a "secret superstar" by Pro Football Focus after his rookie season, Hawes has seen his PFF grade drop by more than half this fall. He sports a 41.4 overall grade this year after an 83.2 mark in 2025.
Bills On SI tabbed Hawes as one of four players with the most to prove following the bye week.
Touted as an incredibly polished blocker , Hawes averaged one reception per game as a rookie.
With the tight end mostly deployed in run formations, an ability to keep the defense honest by effectively running routes adds another element to Buffalo's high-powered offense, which ranks first overall in yards per pass attempt (8.38).
"I think everybody thinks of Jackson as the blocking guy, the blocking tight end. He's got some real nuance to his receiving game. I think his hands are better than people give him credit for," said quarterback Josh Allen this past summer .
Surprisingly, Hawes has no receptions through 154 snaps as a sophomore. His lone target was 36 yards downfield against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 3.
While the Bills continue to use three tight ends as often as any other team in the NFL, Hawes has seen a marginal dip from 43 to 40 percent of offensive snaps this season.
The fundamentally-sound Hawes was flagged for only three penalties during the 2025 regular season. This year, he already has been charged with four fouls through six games.
Hawes committed all four penalties over the past two outings with three infractions coming during the October 12 overtime road win over the Los Angeles Rams.
First, Hawes committed a false start on a 1st-and-10 in the second quarter. Next, he was flagged for a third-quarter offensive pass interference penalty on 1st-and-10 from the Rams' 19. He moved early again, picking up a false start on the go-ahead touchdown drive with 2:42 left in regulation.
Against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6, Hawes jumped early for a false start on 2nd-and-goal from the 5, forcing the Bills to settle for a field goal in the opening minutes of the second quarter.
It's time for the "Ivy Leavue meathead" to return to his rookie form.

title: What Assets Do Bills Possess for NFL Trade Deadline Moves?
full_text:
Brandon Beane hasn't been wildly successful at the NFL trade deadline in recent years. His last move was in 2024 when Beane traded for Amari Cooper in an attempt to bolster the receiving corps, but that trade didn't work out the way they hoped.
Cooper had 20 receptions for 297 yards with two touchdowns in eight games and added 41 yards on six catches in the postseason. Perhaps that miss kept Beane from making any moves in 2025, but he should be willing to get back to the table this year to help shore up one of the NFL’s worst pass defenses .
Buffalo enters Week 8 ranked 31st in defensive passing yards and while the addition of Tre’Davious White should help , they need more impact players in the secondary. The question is what assets Beane has at his disposal for the Nov. 10 trade deadline? Let’s dive into that by first seeing what draft capital the Bills have in 2027.
The Bills have a full selection of picks to use at the NFL trade deadline, including a couple of extra picks in the late round from trades they previously made. Here's an updated look at their 2027 draft capital, including a projected compensatory pick, courtesy of Thad Brown .
Round 1: Own pick Round 2: Own pick Round 3: Own pick Round 4: Own pick Round 4 (Projected): Compensatory Pick Round 5: Own pick Round 6: Own pick Round 6: Colts pick (Sedrick Van Pran-Granger trade) Round 7: Raiders pick (2026 draft trade)
Even with the past few drafts being dedicated to defense, the Bills are still struggling on that side of the ball. There might be some hesitation to use a premium pick for a veteran player, but when you take a step back, you can see that doing so isn’t a bad move for the right player.
For example, the Tennessee Titans just received two first-round picks from the Chicago Bears for Jeffery Simmons. That sounds steep but the last two players Buffalo picked in Round 1 are Keon Coleman and Maxwell Hairston. There’s not a soul alive who wouldn’t trade Coleman and Hairston for Simmons, which is why the lack of aggressiveness from top-tier teams can be confusing, to say the least.
As far as players who could be moved, Buffalo is very thin on that front. There was a time when Keon Coleman was considered a trade asset, but he’s been finally coming on strong.
With that being the case, the one name to watch is Joshua Palmer. A free agency addition in 2025, Palmer hasn’t been an ideal fit and had a debut season to forget in Buffalo. He started out the 2026 campaign on a high note, catching touchdowns in Weeks 1 and 2. Since then, however, he’s been quiet and has just four receptions on the season.
Palmer wouldn’t bring back much in a trade, but he could help a receiver-needy team and give the Bills an extra late-round pick.

title: Retired All-Pro Proposes DB Trade Target That Would Be 'Overkill' for Buffalo Bills
full_text:
Buffalo Bills’ general manager and president of football operations Brandon Beane seemed to take the recent bye week quite literally over the past several days.
While players and coaches probably enjoyed some much-needed rest and recovery after a somewhat bumpy 5-1 start in September and October, many fans and outside observers thought Beane and Buffalo’s front office might be busy working the phones in order to facilitate a trade of some sort prior to the start of Week 8 in the National Football League.
The Bills’ offense and quarterback Josh Allen are seemingly doing just fine with first-year head coach Joe Brady still orchestrating the show, but the opposite side of the ball under new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard has been horrendous through six games of the 2026 campaign.
And, with players like Indianapolis Colts’ defensive lineman DeForest Buckner and Pittsburgh Steelers’ cornerback Joey Porter Jr. transactionally shipped elsewhere around the league since the beginning of the month, the idea of Beane sitting on his hands before the NFL’s trade deadline on November 10 seems silly.
If the Bills are ever going to reach the Super Bowl with Allen at the helm, then the former 2024 MVP is going to finally need his defensive counterparts in Buffalo to start pulling their weight, especially when meaningful football is being played by the time December and January roll around on the calendar.
So, with that said, it would be prudent for Beane to admit his roster construction faults from this past offseason and put forth a full-court press on the open market in order to bring in a difference-maker on the opposite side of the ball from Allen.
And, apparently there’s at least one particular player out there who some outside media members believe would be the perfect fit for such a call for help on Buffalo’s defense . . . and it just so happens to be at the same position that coordinator Jim Leonhard used to suit up at during his previous 10-year NFL career.
Los Angeles Chargers’ ninth-year veteran safety Derwin James Jr., who currently has 21 total tackles and one pass breakup in just three games this season after being sidelined with a hamstring injury that he suffered in Week 3 against, ironically, Buffalo.
Given that veteran defensive back C.J. Gardner-Johnson appears to be a giant flop of a free-agent signing so far through six games this fall, which will now include an upcoming one-game suspension for spitting on an opponent against the Las Vegas Raiders, former All-Pro NFL offensive lineman turned media analyst Terron Armstead recently revealed his choice for Buffalo’s next big trade swing in the coming weeks.
“Honestly, I would go defense, for sure. Like, if you can get Derwin James (that would be great). And . . . Derwin, as decorated as he is (and) as many accolades as he’s had, we still have not got a chance to really appreciate him because he plays with the Chargers—and they haven’t had much playoff success—so we haven’t had many national moments to watch Derwin James,” former New Orleans Saints’ and Miami Dolphins’ offensive tackle Terron Armstead recently said Wednesday during an appearance on CBS ’ Just Football .
"It would almost be overkill." @T_Armstead72 proposes a trade for Derwin James that would take Buffalo over the top. #justfootball pic.twitter.com/JwISg969xm
“He has been incredible throughout his entire career. There’s a reason why he’s the highest-paid safety again—for a second time—because (of) what he does and what he brings to a team: pass game, run game, as a blitzer, as a leader, (and) commander of the backend.
“Like, Derwin James (in Buffalo) . . . it would almost be, like, overkill for him going over there (in a trade).”
Although James’ aforementioned elevated salary could complicate matters for Beane and Buffalo’s front office in an attempt to make a move for the former 2018 first-rounder, there’s also another complication possibly on the horizon: his hamstring injury.
Los Angeles Chargers’ head coach Jim Harbaugh revealed on Wednesday that the veteran captain defensive back could possibly land on injured reserve due to a setback he sustained with the soft-tissue ailment.
However, maybe that’s just a ploy?
There’s always gamesmanship going on in the NFL, so it’s possible that Harbaugh tossed that thought out into the open in an attempt to entice any suspecting teams into upping their offer for the star defender.
Could Beane be bluffed into swinging a deal? It’s possible, but not likely. However, the idea is still intriguing, nonetheless.
The previously mentioned Gardner-Johnson has been a disaster in Western New York, and rookie defensive back Jalon Kilgore might not be ready to take on all of the requirements of starting in the NFL at the current moment.
For that reason—and probably many more—making a trade for some sort of running mate for fellow safety Cole Bishop isn’t a bad idea, despite the pass rush productivity up front also suffering as of late .
James Jr. has 705 total tackles, 47 pass deflections, 40 tackles for loss, 36 quarterback hits, 12 interceptions, six forced fumbles, and three fumble recoveries in 101 career starts in the regular season according Pro Football Reference , as well as 34 total tackles, four tackles for loss, and one fumble recovery in five playoff starts, so his résumé clearly speaks for itself.
And, he’s also an incredible leader in the locker room by many accounts . . . which makes the pairing of James in Leonhard’s reeling defense all the more fitting.
For that reason alone, it’s at least a name—or position—for Bills Mafia to keep a close eye on as the trade deadline quickly approaches after Halloween.

title: Todd Wash is Interim DC. Here are 3 Other Options Panthers Should Consider This Offseason
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are making changes after a 3-4 start to the season, firing defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero along with pass game coordinator Jonathon Cooley.
This comes less than 12 hours after Carolina lost its second straight game , showing lapses in defensive coverage and poor playcalling on that side of the ball. This move had to be made; the Panthers' defense has been a complete letdown when it was supposed to be the team's strength.
Even when fully healthy, Carolina was embarrassed against the Chicago Bears in Week 1, and only performed well against Deshaun Watson, and backup QBs Tanner McKee and Cooper Rush.
Now that Evero is gone, Carolina has an interim defensive coordinator. The Panthers hired Todd Wash in 2023 under former head coach Frank Reich. Wash has 20 years of coaching experience in the NFL, and 31 years of coaching experience total.
Before coming to Carolina, Wash spent time with the Detroit Lions and previously had a long stint with the Jacksonville Jaguars before that. He's coached elite players such as Aidan Hutchinson and Calis Campbell.
With a long resume to his name already, Wash will have a shot at earning the official defensive coordinator job. However, if he doesn't, then here are three names to watch in the offseason.
Scott is the defensive backs coach and defensive pass game coordinator for the Seattle Seahawks. Seattle has been one of, if not the best, defenses in the NFL for the last two seasons, and the elite secondary has been a huge piece of that.
Scott joined Seattle in 2022, which was Dave Canales' final season with the franchise before heading to Tampa Bay, so there is some familiarity.
Edwards has experience as a defensive coordinator, having served as the DC for the Minnesota Vikings, Washington Redskins, and Buffalo Bills.
Edwards is in his fourth season with the Buccaneers, currently serving as the pass game coordinator. Like Karl Scott, Edwards spent a single season with Canales. In Canales' lone season with Tampa Bay, Edwards coached the outside linebackers, so he's versatile in where he can coach on defense, and Carolina's pass rush right now looks awful based on Thursday night.
Another pass game coordinator, Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores, would be the dream candidate, but he'll be interviewing for head coaching jobs, not coordinator jobs.
That said, the Vikings' defense is rolling on all cylinders, and Gerald Alexander is a focal point of that staff. Minnesota currently ranks second in the NFL in pass defense, surrendering just 155 yards per game.
Alexander also has a connection to the Panthers, and it's not with Dave Canales. Alexander played for Carolina for less than a full season in 2010. As a player, he had a journeyman career, but as a coach, he's one of the league's more intriguing young options.
Preston is an experienced sports writer focusing on NFL, College Football, NBA, and MMA topics. He is a passionate Charlotte and Oklahoma sports fan and graduated from the University of Science and Arts Oklahoma in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Communications degree with a focus in journalism.

title: 4 Players Who Will Feel the Impact of Ejiro Evero's Absence, Both Good and Bad
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers fired Ejiro Evero from his role as defensive coordinator . Pass game coordinator Jonathan Cooley went with him. The change was a long time coming , and Evero did not do anything to justify more time.
However, whenever someone is fired, there are ramifications, both good and bad. Some players will benefit from a new coordinator. Others will not.
Both Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are excellent cornerbacks, but Horn in particular is elite at press man coverage. He is supremely physical, so not having a coordinator who wants him to play off in a zone is going to be a huge change, and probably a really good one.
Of course, there is the caveat that Horn is on IR right now, but when he comes back, we expect he will do a little better (he was already good) with a different coordinator who might be willing to adjust to the strength of his players more often.
Ejiro Evero's 3-4 scheme was good for Devin Lloyd, who was thriving under the coordinator. The former All-Pro can succeed with anyone, but Evero was able to help bring out the best in Lloyd both in coverage and as a run defender.
We will still see him all over the field, but the importance of inside linebackers will be diluted a bit with a new coordinator. Lloyd and Bobby Okereke might not have as much production, though that doesn't mean they're worse players now.
Whether or not the Panthers will adopt a 4-3 under Todd Wash remains to be seen, but regardless, Derrick Brown is in line to perform better with Wash being elevated and taking over for Ejiro Evero. Wash was the defensive line coach, and last night, the line was actually really good in run defense, and Brown had a breakout game.
Brown has always been good, but he hasn't always thrived in Evero's system. He did make a Pro Bowl under Evero, but he had a few really excellent seasons before Evero arrived in 2023. Look for Brown to return to form soon.
When Jaelan Phillips comes back, he might be in for a very different role. Obviously, he's still going to rush the passer and set the edge, but a 3-4 system like the one Evero used is often much more favorable for edge rushers. They get more creative ways to get into the backfield.
Phillips was playing just fine under Evero, although the bar for him after a $120 million contract is much higher than that. Still, if the system changes at all, we could be looking at an even more frustrating pass rush from Phillips.

title: Panthers Fire Ejiro Evero After Offseason Spending Failed to Build a Top-10 Defense
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have finally moved on from defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero . After three seasons and change, the Panthers are making a change. They allowed 27 points to the Green Bay Packers after allowing 43 on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Sources: Panthers are letting go of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero.
Evero was signed in 2023 and survived the culling of the Frank Reich era, but the results never manifested. Well-regarded, the Panthers continued to try to put good personnel on the field for Evero, but it didn't work out.
After spending a ton on defense in the offseason, the Panthers' defense has been a mess, and Evero's decision-making is right in the middle of that.
The additions of Bobby Okereke, Devin Lloyd, and Jaelan Phillips were supposed to transform this unit into a top-10 group. Phillips has been hurt and the cornerback depth chart is now down to the fifth and sixth players.
Injuries have certainly played a role, but too often, Evero's units were not prepared to play. In Week 1, they were demolished by the Chicago Bears' rushing attack after having all offseason to prepare.
The only good performances this defense has in 2026 are against Cooper Rush, Deshaun Watson, and Tanner McKee. That is not exactly a who's who of quarterbacks.
In Week 7, the Panthers allowed over 250 rushing yards for the second time this season. We suspected that was the final nail in the coffin, but a short week meant they couldn't install a new defensive coordinator until now.
Then, the Panthers had some truly inexplicable mistakes on defense during another loss to the Green Bay Packers. Evero had his fifth and sixth string cornerbacks on the field on third and 13 and dialed up an all-out blitz.
Even if that had worked, it would've led to a field goal, so dropping back into coverage to make the stop would've been safer and smarter. Instead, the Packers scored a touchdown on the play. In an eight-point loss, that kind of swing looms large.
Later, on third-and-two to essentially ice the game, the Packers were likely to pass since Jordan Love was playing so well against practice squad cornerbacks and the run game wasn't working, so Evero left his cornerbacks almost 10 yards off the line in zone coverage, and the Packers converted.
BREAKING: Ejiro Evero has been relieved of his duties as the Panthers defensive coordinator, along with defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley, per the team. DL Coach Todd Wash has been elevated to interim DC, will call plays.
Going with Evero is defensive pass game coordinator Jonathan Cooley. The Panthers are elevating Todd Wash, the defensive line coach, to interim coordinator.
