title: 4 Things the Panthers Have to Fix With Extra Time After Packers Loss
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers could probably use a few days where they don't have to play football.
They just played twice in five days, lost both games and picked up a few more injuries Thursday night against Green Bay. Now they don't play again until Nov. 8 against Denver, and the timing of the break isn't bad for a team that suddenly has a lot to figure out.
Carolina looked like it was starting to put some things together a couple of weeks ago. After what we've watched against Tampa Bay and Green Bay, I'm not so sure anymore. Here are four things I'd spend some time on before the Panthers play again.
I don't know how many more cornerbacks Carolina can lose. Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are already on injured reserve, and the Panthers placed Akayleb Evans on IR before the Green Bay game. Then Will Lee III injured his hamstring Thursday night and had to be carted to the locker room.
That left Chau Smith-Wade, Marco Wilson and Malcolm DeWalt IV as the three healthy corners by the end of the game. DeWalt was making his NFL debut, and Green Bay took advantage of a secondary that was running out of people. Jordan Love threw for 288 yards and three touchdowns, while Christian Watson caught eight passes for 113 yards.
I know Carolina can't just go find another Jaycee Horn sitting at home somewhere, but I'd be surprised if the Panthers don't at least look around over the next week. They need bodies at this point, especially if Lee is going to miss any time.
Carolina isn't in much better shape up front. The Panthers placed Taylor Moton on injured reserve after the Tampa Bay game, Damien Lewis missed Thursday with a knee injury and Corey Bullock left against Green Bay with a quad injury. Jake Curhan ended up at left guard after being elevated from the practice squad.
Bryce Young was sacked six times, and there were a few plays where it felt like Green Bay was on him almost immediately. Young held onto the football too long on some of them, so I'm not putting all six sacks on the offensive line. Still, it's hard to get much going when you're moving guys around up front and your quarterback is getting hit that often.
Getting Lewis back would help. Moton is going to be out for a while, so there's not much Carolina can do about that right now, but I'd like to see the Panthers come out of the extra time with some idea of what they want the offensive line to look like against Denver.
Carolina scored 30 points against Detroit, 34 against Atlanta and then went into Philadelphia and scored 25. It wasn't perfect, but I thought we were starting to see what this offense could look like when Young was playing well and Carolina stayed balanced.
Then the last two games happened. The Panthers scored 13 against Tampa Bay and 19 against Green Bay, and Thursday was especially frustrating because the defense kept giving the offense chances. Green Bay turned the ball over three times, and Carolina got only three points out of those possessions.
Some of it is the offensive line. Some of it is Young, who hasn't played particularly well the last two games. There also haven't been enough plays downfield, and at times it feels like Carolina has to work way too hard just to pick up a first down.
If I'm Dave Canales, I'm going back and looking at what was working against Detroit, Atlanta and Philadelphia and comparing it to what we're seeing now. This offense shouldn't look this different a couple of weeks later.
I liked what Carolina did with Chuba Hubbard on Thursday. Hubbard carried it 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown, but what stood out to me was the seven catches for 38 yards. He finished with 29 touches and 119 yards from scrimmage on a night when Carolina didn't have much else working.
I especially liked seeing him used more in the passing game. Young was getting pressured and there wasn't much happening downfield, so Hubbard gave him somewhere to go with the football instead of waiting for something to open up. Seven catches might be more than he'll normally have, but there's no reason Carolina can't keep using him that way.
Hubbard doesn't need 29 touches every week. The Panthers just need to make sure one of their most dependable offensive players doesn't disappear from the game plan when things aren't going well.
Carolina is 3-4 after losing twice in five days, and the Panthers look a lot different than they did after going into Philadelphia and beating the Eagles . Injuries have certainly played a part in that, and having to turn around and play Green Bay four days after Tampa Bay didn't help.
This time, they have more than four days to figure some of it out.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: 3 Major Takeaways from Panthers' Frustrating Loss to Packers
full_text:
While it wasn't a 30-point blowout, the Carolina Panthers lost in frustrating fashion once again. Thursday Night Football ended with the Green Bay Packers securing a 27-19 victory . The score is a bit deceiving, as the Packers controlled most of the night.
This is Carolina's second straight loss, moving the Panthers to 3-4, and tying them for first place with the Atlanta Falcons. So far, the NFC South is shaping up like many thought it would: a tightly contested division with no team having a winning record.
The game was ugly for Carolina; the offense was ineffective for most of the night after initially taking a 10-6 lead in the first half.
Two weeks can make a world of difference. The Panthers were riding high after winning two in a row against the Lions and Eagles, but now the team has major questions to answer.
Here are three big takeaways from the TNF loss.
Another game, and another injury to the Panthers' secondary. Carolina is literally on their last legs with this room; the injuries have now piled up more than anyone could've imagined. The Panthers' secondary injuries are as follows
Jaycee Horn: IR, torn quad
Akayleb Evans: IR, tricep, knee
Will Lee III: exited game vs. Packers, hamstring
There's still no timetable for Jackson or Horn's return, and Evans got placed on IR this week, so he'll be out for at least four weeks.
Will Lee III has been decent for the Panthers in an elevated role, showing flashes of what he can be long term with great coverage and denial. However, Carolina may not see him on the field soon, as he hurt his hamstring while trying to cover Packers WR Christian Watson.
Carolina needs to make a trade for a veteran corner; it doesn't have to be a star like Sauce Gardner, just someone who can step in and be reliable.
Young finished the night completing 23 of 41 passes for 209 yards, 1 touchdown, and 1 interception. Those aren't good numbers , but anyone who watched the game won't blame Young for struggling.
Against the Packers, Young was sacked 6 times. Furthermore, Young was pressured on 22 dropbacks, which ties his career high. The offensive line is banged up with Taylor Moton and Damien Lewis out, but this is still inexcusable considering how good Young has been when protected.
Rasheed Walker and Monroe Freeling have been major disappointments, especially Walker, who was elite in pass coverage in 2025 and allowed just five sacks.
Obviously, there are injuries. Carolina was without Jaelan Phillips on Thursday night, and has been without Nic Scourton all season.
With the injuries, the pass rush remains awful. The Panthers recorded zero sacks and zero QB hits on Thursday night. No scenario exists where Jordan Love has a clean pocket all game and the Panthers still win; it just can't happen, especially with how banged up the secondary is.
Carolina needs Phillips back sooner rather than later. Creating more pressure will help the defense in some capacity against other great QBs the Panthers will see this season.

title: Carolina Panthers Fans Deserve So Much Better Than This
full_text:
For the first five weeks of the year, the Carolina Panthers looked like they might have finally turned a corner. Historically, things can only go so right for so long before the team inevitably implodes. The best season in franchise history ended with a complete and utter dud in the Super Bowl.
But after five weeks, which came after about six years of struggle with little positivity, things looked like they were turning around. Bryce Young looked like a franchise QB. The braintrust with Brad Idzik was working. There was enough defensive talent to feel good about their chances on a week to week basis.
Fans understandably had some hope. They were 3-2 and at home against a one-win Tampa Bay Buccaneers team. The same old Panthers showed up Sunday and again on Thursday . Those same fans deserve better.
If the Panthers played in virtually any other division in the NFL, being this incompetent would really hurt the Panthers. The fact that they play in the NFC South is the only reason they were relevant last year, and it's the only thing keeping them alive this year.
Everything has gone wrong over the last two weeks, and it's representative of what continues to go wrong for the Panthers. They can never get out of their own way, and a good thing can't stay good for too long.
At virtually every level, the Panthers are failing their fans. The same fans who rocked the Bank after a dreadful loss on the road to the Cleveland Browns. Those fans have been given no reason to continue caring.
On offense, the ridiculously expensive and well-invested offensive line cannot block anyone. Bryce Young doesn't have time to think, and lately, that has been the difference-maker in his performance. He's not doing as well, and it's only partly his fault.
The offensive play-calling has fallen off. Maybe rookie play-caller Brad Idzik was simply off to a hot start as an unknown, but that has come crashing back down to earth and doesn't seem easy to fix.
On defense, injuries have killed the secondary, but Ejiro Evero seems unable to press the right buttons. A bad pass rush with backup cornerbacks is a recipe for disaster, and Evero can't figure it out.
The lack of depth at cornerback and the inability to rush the passer falls on the front office. Dan Morgan has a good reputation, but I'm not sure it's warranted. His 2024 draft is pretty bad, and a lot of investments haven't worked out.
And the fact that he's had weeks to address the cornerback depth and hasn't speaks volumes. The fact that he can't find anyone to rush the passer is troubling, too.
Injuries have certainly played their part, but they've been injured for weeks and haven't done a thing to try and alleviate the rush of players leaving and missing time.
On every level, the Panthers keep doing what they do. They just keep shooting themselves in the foot on an organizational level. And the fans certainly deserve a whole lot better. I just don't know if they're ever going to get it.

title: Bryce Young Report Card: Late Touchdown Saves Him From a Worse Grade
full_text:
I kept waiting for Bryce Young to get going Thursday night, and for most of the game it just didn't happen.
There were a few throws here and there, but the Carolina Panthers couldn't get much going through the air. Young finished 23-of-41 for 207 yards, one touchdown and one interception in the 27-19 loss to Green Bay, and even those numbers probably look a little better than the game actually felt.
At halftime, Young was 10-of-19 for 65 yards with an interception. Carolina had only 80 total yards, and outside of Chuba Hubbard, there wasn't much happening offensively. That was disappointing coming off what happened against Tampa Bay because I expected the offense to look better than this, even on a short week at Green Bay.
Green Bay made things difficult on Young, and the protection didn't always help him. There were several plays where he had somebody around him before he had much of a chance to look downfield, and Carolina ended up leaning on Hubbard underneath. Hubbard caught seven passes for 38 yards, while Tetairoa McMillan led Carolina with six catches for 57 yards.
Jalen Coker had only two catches, but one of them was easily Young's best throw of the night. Facing fourth down with 5:46 left, Young found Coker for a 26-yard touchdown that cut Green Bay's lead to 27-19 and at least gave Carolina a chance to make things interesting late.
The Panthers eventually got the ball back, but there wasn't much time left and the final possession didn't go anywhere. Young took a sack with 22 seconds remaining, and Carolina never got close enough to give itself a real chance at tying the game.
I went back and forth between a C- and a D+, and the touchdown to Coker is probably what kept me at a C-. Young made a good throw when Carolina needed one and was better late, but I'm having a hard time overlooking everything that happened before that.
Green Bay turned the ball over three times, and Carolina scored only 19 points. Young averaged 5.0 yards per attempt and threw another interception after turning the ball over three times against Tampa Bay last week . I'm not putting all of that on him because the protection wasn't great and there weren't a lot of guys running wide open downfield, but Carolina still needed more from its quarterback.
We've already seen Young play much better than this . He threw for 329 yards against Detroit, 287 yards with three touchdowns against Atlanta and 281 yards with two touchdowns against Philadelphia. That's why I'm not giving him too much credit just because things looked a little better late Thursday night.
The touchdown to Coker kept this from being a worse grade, but one good drive wasn't enough to change how I felt about the rest of the night.

title: 4 Winners and 6 Losers From Another Disappointing Panthers' Loss vs. Buccaneers
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers got a couple of early breaks and did very little with them en route to the second straight blowout loss of the season. What a difference a few weeks makes. Once again, we're desperate to move on to the next game, but we have to sit with this one a few extra days this time.
Despite the ugly loss, there were some individual standouts. There were, as evidenced by the on-field product, plenty of standouts for the wrong reasons , too.
Rookie LB Jackson Kuwatch with a forced fumble on the opening kickoff, recovered by OLB Nick Hampton. #Panthers
Linebacker depth (as well as the fact that he was taken as a project in the seventh round) has kept Jackson Kuwatch to a special teams role. But tonight, on a unit that has been much-maligned this year, Kuwatch made a huge play by forcing a fumble on the opening kickoff.
Luke Fortner has to be better than that.
A really bad season continued Thursday night for Luke Fortner. Right after getting possession and getting a first down from that fumble recovery, Fortner got beat badly in pass protection, so Bryce Young had no chance, and the Panthers missed a big chance to score an opening touchdown. It was a microcosm of his season. His run blocking was very solid, but if he can't protect Young, that's not good.
Where has Marco Wilson been all year? Seriously, why have the Panthers been trotting Akayleb Evans out when Wilson was there and Evans is a special teams ace? It makes very little sense, especially with how good Wilson was tonight after being pushed up into the lineup rapidly.
Rasheed Walker is not good. This is not good.
Rasheed Walker's revenge game did not go to plan. He was beat routinely in pass protection again. He is beginning to show why no one really wanted him in free agency, and while he was cheap, he's also been pretty bad. That continued tonight.
How much more can we say about Chuba Hubbard? He has arguably been the most consistent player this year, and he's been one of the best offensive weapons. That didn't stop tonight. The only thing that changed is that his number was called a lot more in the first half, as he's typically been a second-half grind-it-out kind of player this year. He rose to the occasion, though.
Will Lee helped off with a leg injury. Chau Smith-Wade in as the Panthers are down to their 5th and 6th corners.
Will Lee's roller-coaster season continued. He committed two bad defensive pass interference penalties, one of which came while allowing a 53-yard catch. And on that same catch, he got hurt, leaving the paper-thin secondary without its best cornerback. He has to stay healthy, and he has to clean things up. The injury isn't his fault, but the penalties are. And they're frequent.
The Panthers haven't gotten much from Derrick Brown all season, but he finally showed up tonight. He got some pressure on Jordan Love and was a force in the run game, too. It was not enough, but it was good to see Brown put together a good outing.
Third and 13. Another quirky replay angle from prime, but looked like an all up, with at least five on the rush, and the easiest real estate available for an avoidable touchdown. This ends of being like a three on one 🤣 pic.twitter.com/wvR0PGI0oS
Ejiro Evero had the team ready to play better, and they were much more adept at tackling. But his decisions were abysmal. The Panthers couldn't get pressure on the second-worst offensive line, so Evero timed up several useless and ill-fated blitzes, including an incomprehensible one on third-and-13 that led to a touchdown.
Brad Idzik knew the status of the offensive line and the matchup tonight. He scripted a good series and got off to a pretty decent start, but things went completely off the rails after that. He had nothing to scheme up to help his quarterback or the ailing offensive line. It was not a good performance from the rookie play-caller. His calls on what ended up being the final drive of the night were not good.
I feel like I’m rewatching Bryce’s rookie season right now The Panthers O-line has reached an unworkable state
We didn't hear much out of Monroe Freeling tonight because most of the attention was on Rasheed Walker, and for good reason. Freeling wasn't good, either. The Packers abused the left side at will, but the right side of the line was pretty awful, too. So far, the early returns on Freeling are overwhelmingly negative.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: Panthers Have at Least Found an Answer for Josh Jacobs
full_text:
After watching Bucky Irving run all over the Carolina Panthers last week, Josh Jacobs was one of the guys I was worried about coming into Thursday night.
Carolina has done a much better job against him. Jacobs had 10 carries for only 14 yards late in the first half, and while he did score on a 1-yard run, the Panthers haven't allowed him to get much going outside of that.
That's a big change from what we watched against Tampa Bay. Irving ran for 106 yards and two touchdowns on 24 carries, and the Buccaneers finished with 258 rushing yards as a team. Carolina had chances to make tackles and didn't, and by the end of the game Tampa Bay was running the ball pretty much whenever it wanted.
With Jacobs coming up four days later, I thought we might see more of the same.
Green Bay has tried to get Jacobs involved. He had already carried the ball 10 times before halftime, but there just hasn't been much there for him.
His longest run was four yards, and most of his carries have ended with Carolina getting multiple guys around the football. After some of the tackling problems we saw against Tampa Bay, that's probably what I've noticed the most.
Jacobs is going to get his carries, and Green Bay isn't going to completely get away from him with another half still to play. The Panthers are going to have to keep tackling because it won't take much for Jacobs to break one and change his numbers in a hurry.
But this is what I wanted to see after last week. Carolina got embarrassed against the run by Tampa Bay and then had to turn around four days later and face another running back capable of giving them problems.
Through the first half, the Panthers have been much better.

He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Panthers Making One Big Change With Chuba Hubbard Against Packers
full_text:
Chuba Hubbard didn't get many chances to do much last week against Tampa Bay, but that hasn't been the case Thursday night against Green Bay.
The Carolina Panthers have gone to Hubbard quite a bit, both running the football and throwing it to him out of the backfield. He had nine carries for 30 yards and a touchdown midway through the second quarter, along with four catches for 17 yards.
The receiving part is what I've liked seeing. With Bryce Young having trouble getting much going downfield, Carolina has been willing to take the short throw to Hubbard and let him pick up what he can. He's not going to turn every one of those into a big play, but it gives Young somewhere to go with the football instead of holding onto it and waiting for something to open up.
Last week was a weird game because Tampa Bay got ahead early and Carolina had to get away from what it wanted to do offensively. Hubbard finished with only seven carries for 33 yards, although he did catch four passes for 27 yards.
That came after Hubbard ran for 120 yards on 28 carries against Philadelphia . We've already seen this season how much better Carolina can look when it stays with Hubbard instead of getting away from the running game too early.
There was actually some thought coming into Thursday that Carolina could make Hubbard a bigger part of the offense against Green Bay , and that's exactly what we've seen so far.
I also like that Carolina isn't only handing it off and asking Hubbard to run between the tackles. He came into Thursday with 15 catches for 112 yards and two touchdowns, and using him underneath gives Young another option when Green Bay takes away something downfield.
With the way Carolina's offense has looked at times Thursday night, there's no reason to get away from it. Hubbard is getting the ball more, he's giving Young an option out of the backfield and Carolina has already gotten a touchdown out of him.

title: Will Jeffery Simmons Play in Week 8? Ryan Poles Shares Expectation for New Bears DT
full_text:
Jeffery Simmons is officially a Chicago Bear. Now, the question is: will Simmons make his debut in Week 8?
Simmons will have a short amount of time to get acclimated enough to play. After all, he was acquired on Thursday and Chicago will suit up on Monday night in Week 8.
The expectation is that Simmons will play, but that has not been officially confirmed yet. If he does play, Simmons will likely be limited in his first game in Chicago.
That said, any contribution one of the best defensive tackles in the spot can give will be welcomed.
Bears general manager Ryan Poles addressed the media on Friday for the first time since the trade went down and was asked if he believes Simmons will play.
The Bears general manager said he does indeed think Simmons will go, but he did not say that's definitive and will instead leave that decision up to the coaching staff.
"Ryan Poles says he would assume Jeffery Simmons is going to play on Monday but he will leave it up to the coaches," Zack Pearson of Bear Report relayed.
This isn't the first time Poles has spoken on the Simmons trade , as a quote from the Bears GM was included in an article that officially announced the Bears' trade.
"We are fortunate to have the opportunity to add a player, and a human, like Jeffery to our team, and we look forward to Jeffery's leadership and command as we continue to work toward sustained success," Poles said.
Of all the positions on a football field, defensive tackle is one of the easier ones to play at with limited knowledge of a defense.
Adding to the idea that Simmons will play, this is a very important game for the Bears, who will square off against the Seattle Seahawks .
It's important because a matchup against the Super Bowl champs amounts to a measuring stick game for Chicago. If they can beat Seattle, it will go a long way toward showing the Bears are legit contenders in 2026.
Simmons provides a boost both to the Bears' run defense and pass-rush.
Simmons is an elite interior pass-rusher, as evidenced by his four sacks and 24 pressures ranking fifth and third among interior defenders, according to Pro Football Focus .
Simmons ranks 16th among interior defenders in run defense grade, and he has 20 stops, which is tops at the position.
"Jeffery has proven to be one of the most impactful run defenders and disruptive pass-rushers in the NFL, and yet, through his leadership, Jeffery will have the opportunity to create a positive impact across our entire team. We look forward to the work ahead," head coach Ben Johnson said on Thursday night.
The acquisition of Simmons pushes guys like Kentavius Street and Neville Gallimore down the depth chart into backup roles they are better suited for, which improves depth, and he makes the Bears less reliant on disappointing rookie Jordan van den Berg.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: NFL Insider Hints the Bears Aren't Done Navigating Trade Market
full_text:
The Bears pulled off a blockbuster trade on Thursday, landing one of  the league's most dominant players in defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.
They gave up two first-round picks and a fourth-round selection to receive the four-time Pro Bowler (and a fifth-round pick, which matters A LOT), and he should immediately fortify their defense. He's the type of force multiplier that should immediately open up opportunities for the entire defensive line.
Simmons has been double-teamed on 84% of his pass-rushing snaps, and he still leads all DTs in pressures (28). He's a true game-wrecker, and he should allow Austin Booker, Montez Sweat, and Dayo Odeyingbo (on early downs) to eat on the outside.
On paper, he seems like the potential final piece. The final infinity stone that lets Dennis Allen wreck opposing gameplans without sending extra rushers from the secondary. However, NFL insider Ian Rapoport hinted that the Bears might not be done adding to the defensive line ahead of the trade deadline.
Per @RapSheet , the Bears are not done: "Chicago Bears were in on DeForest Buckner... looking at edges, probably still looking at edges." "Ryan Poles has been very, very active." "The Bears were already Super Bowl contenders big time” Khalil Mack?! pic.twitter.com/nkcyygHQOs
While Rapoport specifically mentioned them looking into edge rushers, we just don't see it happening. Not with their current defensive line depth, and the fact they already cut ties with a promising (albeit unproven) player , Jamree Kromah, to get Simmons in the building.
There is one position that makes much more sense if they were to scour the market, though.
The Bears' cornerback room has been their most glaring weakness this season. While his presence should also help the cover men by limiting opposing QBs' time to throw, he won't be running down Christian Watson anytime soon.
They could still add a CB to fortify the secondary, and a few players make sense for Chicago. Riq Woolen is playing out an extremely cheap (at least in terms of base salary, since the Eagles paid him a massive signing bonus) one-year deal, and the Eagles are a sinking ship. He's a great fit for Dennis Allen's man-heavy scheme , and it probably wouldn't cost more than a fifth-round pick to bring him aboard.
Conversely, it would cost next to nothing to trade for Nahshon Wright, who's still waiting to play his first defensive snaps for New York. A late-round pick swap would probably be enough to bring him back into the fold, and it's safe to assume the Bears wouldn't be bidding with any other team for his services.
The Bears opted not to re-sign Wright for a reason, and that reason was presumably on display throughout training camp/practice with the Jets. He's a flawed player in coverage, but his ball-hawking abilities are undeniable .
He led all defenders with eight total takeaways (five interceptions, three fumble recoveries) last season and earned a Pro Bowl nod for his efforts. Even with his coverage warts, it'd be tough to be much worse than Tyrique Stevenson and Jaylon Johnson.
Also, career journeyman Nick McCloud was an injury away from playing significant snaps on the perimeter before getting axed (so they could elevate RB Zavier Scott from the practice squad) earlier this week. The bar is the floor when it comes to the team's secondary depth.

He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Why Super Bowl Ambition, Not Injury Panic, Sparked Pre-Game Trades for Bears and Seahawks
full_text:
The Chicago Bears and Seattle Seahawks sit at the edge of the NFC postseason picture, with the Seahawks on the bubble right now at 4-3. Both teams made major moves ahead of a massive Monday Night Football matchup in Week 8.
Chicago swung for the fences with an unexpected trade for Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. The Bears sent the Titans a 2027 first-round draft pick, 2028 first-round draft pick, and 2027 fourth-round draft pick, receiving a 2028 fifth-round draft pick along with Simmons.
Meanwhile, Seattle acquired guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts. The Seahawks sent the Colts a 2027 third-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round draft pick for the 30-year-old All-Pro guard.
Chicago is thin on the defensive line due to injuries and the like, but there's been recent absences on the edge, not the middle.
Seattle will be missing left tackle Charles Cross due to a high ankle sprain against the Bears, but the Seahawks didn't land Nelson to account for Anthony Bradford's injury woes this season at guard. Nelson is on a different level than anyone on Seattle's interior offensive line. It's clear the Seahawks feel they have a chance to repeat despite some Super Bowl hangover losses to the Washington Commanders and Denver Broncos. There may also now be a fix for one of the league's least effective run games early on.
Many eyes will be on Simmons and Nelson this coming Monday, particularly because it'll be easy to track how each is doing when lined up against each other.
Nelson will get the chance to open up gaps for Emanuel Wilson, who's become Seattle's top running back during an injury-stricken season for the room, as well as the returning Zach Charbonnet. Simmons will get the chance to prevent and plug those gaps in his Chicago debut.
There were already plenty of subplots to be excited about on Monday. The Ryan Poles-John Schneider chess match with their trade deadline splashes taking center stage gives the Manningcast some great X's and O's fodder.
It's either that or the tense Joe Buck-Troy Aikman booth. Unfortunately, America seems to love choosing the dysfunction over the practical, hence reality television still being consumed decades past its expiration date.
Contenders make the right moves during the season, just as much as before it. Both the Seahawks and Bears front offices are letting their fans know that they are taking these next few months seriously.
This is a bellwether game for these two teams. We'll see which franchise better accommodates its midseason splash and moves closer to the top of the NFC.

title: The Winners and Losers from Chicago Bears' Trade for Jeffery Simmons
full_text:
In the long term, the Bears anticipate their trade for Jeffery Simmons means a better pass rush and better run defense this year as they try to win a Super Bowl.
Like with any wins, losses, drafts or signings in the NFL, there are winners and losers with trades.
Here are the winners and losers on this Bears roster following the shocking trade for Simmons. In some cases, both winning and losing comes in varying degrees.
Jeffery Simmons swipes the hands aways & gets the strip sack. Have a pass rush plan! #passrush #titans pic.twitter.com/nsq3um2ZtJ
The Bears defensive coordinator now no longer needs to gamble as much to get a pass rush. Gambling less lets them play more coverage, doesn't put the defense at risk and can help prevent some of the big plays the defense has been allowing. Make no mistake, they are allowing too many big plays. Through Week 7, the Bears are allowing the most yards per play in the NFL despite being ninth in points allowed and eighth in yards allowed. It all says they give up too many big plays by gambling too much with young players in their secondary and by blitzing more often than they'd like. The real cynics could point out how Allen could also be a loser with this move. If they can't begin to stop teams at a better rate and they have talent like Simmons, Sweat and Devin Bush, maybe what they need is another defensive coordinator. But that's a discussion for another offseason.
Dennis Allen might not get much sleep this week as the Bears defense prepares to face the Seahawks. @paytonsun wonders, "How in the heck are they going to stop Jaxon Smith-Njigba?" pic.twitter.com/jflMjtTwHG
Some of his team-high seven missed tackles or his completions allowed when targeted resulted from being out of position while playing too much man-to-man or playing zone with fewer defenders as the Bears blitz. A faster interior pass rush lets DBs be in the position they need to be in order to face the quarterback and knock down or intercept passes.
Jaylon Johnson is completely cooked pic.twitter.com/bLxY5QCkrZ
The defensive linemen protect the linebackers. Edwards has both is health and his production to consider. He's second on the team in missed tackles and with Simmons getting into backfields to break up runs, the role of the linebackers become so much simpler. Also, it becomes more difficult for quarterbacks to play pitch and catch on short drops with receivers under the coverage when they know they could have a good pass rusher at defensive tackle charging at their faces.
With Sweat there is always the concern of double teams. There better be no more talk of this. The double teams probably will come at Simmons now, although that's somewhat difficult to do because Simmons tended to play in numerous positions on the defensive front. In theory, his frees up Sweat to operate one on one or with a back providing assistance. His sack total should increase. Long term, though, it's not accurate to put Sweat on a list of winners. His PED suspension didn't help his cause and made it so his contract guarantees are gone. The Bears can more easily dispose of his contract through trade or by cutting him.
Jeffrey Simmons and Montez Sweat reunited pic.twitter.com/GQ9rIm2TaR
Also, there was that quote by Ben Johnson on Tuesday during his press conference at Halas Hall while talking about the PED suspension and Sweat's production. "I think he's been kind of a steady Eddie guy for us through these first five games with him," Johnson said. They don't pay guys $25 million to be steady Eddie. They pay this much to big-impact players. Now that they'll be on the hook for the remainder of the $105 million, three-year extension the Titans gave to Simmons, look for steady Eddie to be squeezed out of Chicago after this season barring some type of spectacular finish to the year.
No longer does he need to gamble on fourth down all the time because he can rest comfortably knowing they have the ability to stop people on defense. Then again, it might encourage him to gamble all the more. A gambler gambles.
Everyone can stop piling on after he pulled off yet another daring trade no one expected. If if flops, the penalty will be severe, though.  At least he won't have as much work to do starting the next two drafts.  He might even find a way to use Simmons on offense. The Titans did this.
Jeffrey Simmons has offensive touchdowns in 3 of his last 4 seasons. Ben Johnson: pic.twitter.com/wum0Ls3vMg
He was near tears at the press conference in Nashville regarding the departure of Simmons to Chicago, but he needs to look at the bright side. He gets two first-round draft picks the next two years and a fourth next year that he wouldn't have had. It's alot to pay for one player who isn't a quarterback or edge rusher.
Mike Borgonzi said Jeffery Simmons didn't want to leave and was surprised by the trade. pic.twitter.com/dC4b3ZaiUP
They brought in Jarrett with the anticipation he could do what Simmons does. He has been better than last year, but still not a dominant force and his. They can save $13.5 million with only a $4 million cap hit next year by cutting or trading Jarrett. Essentially, Jarrett has been given the remainder of this season to try and win that Super Bowl in Chicago. Otherwise, they'd be paying him $17.5 million next year to be a No. 2 defensive tackle or even No. 3. That's not happening.
His moment in the sun was against the Patriots. They already released him after making the trade in order to make room for Simmons. Expect him to resurface on the practice squad or someone else's roster if they claim him off waivers.
The undrafted rookie from Wake Forest no longer figures to get onto the field at some point this season, unless they have injuries. He's still on the 53-man roster but hasn't been active for a game. The Bears are protecting him from prying hands by keeping him off the practice squad, but they may no longer be able to hold the 53-man roster spot for him.
Jayden Loving collapses the pocket up the middle to pressure Shedeur Sanders and force the bad throw Beanie Bishop is there with the INT and the #Bears are in full control rn pic.twitter.com/OZ3Okzfu9r
Their sixth-round rookie has been on the field 72 plays and has only one tackle. He also has been on for 28 special teams plays. The benefit for having him active and ready is how he can learn from the veterans around him while playing a little. Now his playing time will be cut greatly and who knows if he'll even be on the 53-man roster?
The veteran defensive tackle has been on for only 34% of plays. With another tackle added, those plays need to come at someone's expense. It's easy to wonder if he'll be part of their plans going forward.
Jordan Love gets sacked for the 5th time. What is happening?! pic.twitter.com/HtuAB340NJ
These two pocket passers in the NFC North are going to need to worry about the interior rush from one of the game's best at this. Neither one is particular effective moving outside to throw and when the interior rush is in their face they're going to be more likely to throw it up for grabs.
OMG. This is a terrible trade for the Bears. Why do teams do this? DT is not a premium position even. Plus he's 29 and he's making $100 million guaranteed through 2028. Where is the surplus value here. A+ for the Titans; D-minus for the Bears. https://t.co/zgLuJlc0Jy

title: 3 Nightmarish NFC North Rival Trades the Chicago Bears Would Not Want to See
full_text:
The Chicago Bears made their big move when the front office flipped a 2027 first-round pick, 2028 first-round pick, and a 2027 fourth-round pick to the Tennessee Titans to land defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick on Thursday.
Ryan Poles and Co. might not be done, but the Bears have likely gotten the one big fish they're going to get.
As the NFC North stands, Chicago is competitive. Still, the Bears are a loss against the Seattle Seahawks on Monday Night Football away from last place in the division.
Chicago would be in trouble if these trades took place in the NFC North between now and November 10:
The undefeated Minnesota Vikings landing star running back Jonathan Taylor in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts would be the worst-case scenario for not just the Bears, but the entire NFL.
Minnesota has missed running backs Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones Sr. for much of the year. The Vikings got Mason back this past weekend and could return Jones either this Sunday or the following Monday.
Still, Taylor and Minnesota have been linked. Taylor denied trade rumors to any team , but it ultimately isn't up to him.
If Carlie Irsay-Gordon and Co. pull the trigger on a Taylor deal, and the Vikings are the highest bidder, Minnesota will have its strongest chance in franchise history to win its first Super Bowl.
The Detroit Lions could use a complement for Second-Team All-Pro EDGE Aidan Hutchinson, but GM Brad Holmes isn't going to pay a ransom to land one.
Holmes could opt to give up a day-three draft pick to land former Chicago defensive end Khalil Mack, preventing a reunion in the Windy City.
The Bears could use an edge-rusher, but they cannot afford to give up too much draft capital after the Simmons blockbuster.
Since the Lions haven't been aggressive in the trade market yet, there's more room for a gamble on a 35-year-old rental. It'd be tough to lose out to a division rival for a player who played well during his first stint in Chicago.
The Green Bay Packers, like the Bears, entered trade season with a need in the defensive interior. Green Bay lost Javon Hargrave to a torn Achilles earlier in the season.
Miami Dolphins defensive tackle Zach Sieler has been floated as a potential option for the Packers, just as he was for Chicago.
The Bears made their choice, and it wasn't Sieler. There's the chance for buyer's remorse if Green Bay is able to land Sieler and get as much, or, God forbid, more, than Chicago gets out of Simmons.
If Sieler doesn't work out, he can be cut with no penalty. The Bears will need Simmons to make good on the massive investment it took to land him for years to come.

title: Jeffery Simmons Comes to Bears Only to Face Off with His Old Nemesis
full_text:
For eight seasons guard Quenton Nelson has faced defensive tackle Jeffery Simmon s in the AFC South twice a year depending on their health, and after that amount of time the two must be getting sick of each other.
Two weeks ago they squared off when the Titans beat the Colts and Simmons definitely got the better of it on that day with two sacks, six tackles, six pressures, a forced fumble and fumble recovery. Then Nelson got traded by Indianapolis to the Seahawks early this week.
Finally he is rid of his rival while in the safety of the other conference.
Now Simmons is coming to the Bears by trade, and on Monday night in the first game both will play for their new team they could be renewing their rivalry.
Jeffery Simmons (now a Bear) v Quenton Nelson (now a Seahawk) on the twist not two weeks ago pic.twitter.com/qLqZ8vuMQp
i mean hes a really sharp guy. HEs sbeen working realy hard since he got here getting up to speed.
“I know I need to bring my A-game every time I line up against Quenton,” Simmons told Titans reporters during the offseason. “He plays the game hard. Facing him twice a year for my last seven years, he’s been unbelievable. It’s nothing but respect for Quenton.”
Simmons in the past called it a "heavyweight matchup."
Love the move by the Titans to trade Simmons for two first round picks. Huge haul. Phenomenal player for Bears, who actually have a window to compete for titles.
Nelson apparently has similar feelings about facing Simmons.
"It’s his power and then the way he plays the game," Nelson told The Athletic's Stephen Holder. "He plays hard. He’s got a motor. He’s one of the strongest if not THE strongest D-tackles I’ve gone against.
"And he’s not one dimensional. He can hit you with the pass rush or in the run game. He’s definitely the heart of that defense."
Now he'd be the heart of the Bears defense.
No one is certain yet how much Simmons would be playing because he joins the team at Halas Hall for practice on Friday before a Monday game. In Nelson's case, their plan to use him has already been stated by coach Mike Macdonald.
"He's going to play," Macdonald told Seattle reporters.  The plan is to start Nelson against the Bears.
We'll see if they play but potential for Monday Night Football this week ... Seahawks G Quenton Nelson vs. Bears DT Jeffery Simmons.
Grey Zabel is moving from left guard to right guard to make room for Nelson in this game.
McDonald anticipates a week being enough time for Nelson to pick up a sufficient amount of the blocking scheme to play at left guard.
"I mean, he's a really sharp guy," Macdonald said. "He's sbeen working realy hard since he got here getting up to speed."
After diving into Jeffery Simmons’ film and weighing the cost, here’s my unfiltered take on the Bears trade. THE GOOD: Simmons is an absolute GAME WRECKER. He can line up anywhere along the defensive line, rarely misses time, dominates against the run, and is a legitimate…
It's probably easier for a defensive tackle to play than an offensive lineman on short notice. It wouldn't be easy for either. Khalil Mack joined the Bears in 2018 and in the same week he was playing in the opener extensively at Lambeau Field against Green Bay.
So who has the better of it when Nelson and Simmons faced off in the past?
Without a doubt it was Nelson. Although Simmons had two sacks in the last game, he had the same number for all the games they squared off in from 2019 until this year.

title: Ryan Poles, Ben Johnson Share Thoughts on Bears' Trade for Jeffery Simmons
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have made their blockbuster trade for superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons official.
The team did so with a post on social media and on their official website, and included in the article were comments on the trade from head coach Ben Johnson and general manager Ryan Poles.
The blockbuster trade saw the Bears give up two first-round picks , one in the 2027 and another in 2028, and a 2027 fourth-rounder in exchange for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round selection. Chicago trading multiple first-round picks for a defensive tackle marks the first time that has happened in NFL history .
Poles expressed his excitement for bringing Simmons to the Windy City and talked about what he brings to the team.
"We are excited to welcome Jeffery Simmons and his family to Chicago," Poles said. "We extend our gratitude to the Tennessee Titans and Mike Borgonzi for their partnership and collaboration throughout this process. We are fortunate to have the opportunity to add a player, and a human, like Jeffery to our team, and we look forward to Jeffery's leadership and command as we continue to work toward sustained success."
Johnson lauded Simmons for all of the success he has had during his eight-year NFL career, which includes four Pro Bowls and three All-Pro nods, including one first-team selection in 2025.
"Jeffery is one of the most respected players in the National Football League," Johnson said. "Jeffery has proven to be one of the most impactful run defenders and disruptive pass-rushers in the NFL, and yet, through his leadership, Jeffery will have the opportunity to create a positive impact across our entire team. We look forward to the work ahead."
According to Pro Football Focus , Simmons ranks fifth in pass-rush grade and 16th in run defense grade among interior defenders.
He has also posted 20 stops, four sacks and 24 pressures, ranking first, fifth and third at his position.
The addition of Simmons will bolster a Bears interior pass-rush that has posted just one sack through seven games.
Chicago's run defense needed a boost as well, with Chicago surrendering the 10th-most rushing yards per attempt and sporting the No. 26 run stop win rate, according to ESPN .
Now, it'll be interesting to see if Poles has anything else up his sleeve before the NFL trade deadline falls on Nov. 10.
There has been a lot of smoke about a possible Khalil Mack trade . Pulling the trigger on that deal would only add to the immense amount of excitement surrounding the Bears this season.

title: Bears Release Fan-Favorite Defender After Blockbuster Jeffery Simmons Trade
full_text:
The Chicago Bears shocked the NFL world on Thursday morning by pulling off a blockbuster trade for Jeffery Simmons . They acquired the superstar defensive tackle in a trade with the Tennessee Titans, sending their next two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick in 2027 to Tennessee in exchange for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
This trade represents a seismic shift in the NFC's pecking order, and the Bears suddenly look like the team that's most likely to represent the conference in the Super Bowl. Unfortunately for one player, the Bears needed to release somebody to clear up room on the active roster for Simmons, and that player was fan-favorite defensive end Jamree Kromah. According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , the Bears released Kromah on Thursday afternoon.
I confess to feeling a fair amount of shock by this move. Kromah had himself a fantastic summer with the Bears this year, especially in Chicago's preseason Week 1 win over the Cleveland Browns. In that game, Kromah registered six total tackles, three for a loss, two sacks, two QB hits, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery. He put up another big showing in the Bears' preseason Week 3 win over the Titans .
Though he didn't make the final roster, Kromah did eventually get called up to play in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons and four days later against the New England Patriots. He picked up two tackles in just 27 snaps across those two games and looked every bit like a solid rotational edge rusher. That's a big deal considering how much emphasis general manager Ryan Poles has placed on the importance of having 'waves of pass rushers' to send at quarterbacks.
Of course, Kromah's release may have been inevitable at some point this season, whether the Bears traded for Simmons or not. Ben Johnson's vague injury update on Wednesday not withstanding, the Bears could be getting safety Coby Bryant back by mid-December, at which point they'll have to open up a roster spot. Kromah would likely have been the option to release at that point, but he's already off the roster.
While it's exciting to see the Bears swing for the fences with a blockbuster trade, it's a bittersweet moment to see a hard-working, fan-favorite player get shown the door. Kromah has shown intriguing upside during his limited time on the field, and he may have a long career as a rotational pass rusher ahead of him, whether that's in Chicago or elsewhere.
A former Marine and Purdue Boilermaker, Pete has been covering the Chicago Bears since 2022 as a senior contributor on BearsTalk. He lives with his wife, two kids and loyal dog.

title: Where Jeffery Simmons Trade Ranks Among Biggest Bears Deals Ever
full_text:
Ryan Poles is like most GMs in that he prefers the draft and will occasionally dip into the free agency market.
He's far more reluctant to spend greatly on free agents, but he has been willing to trade and has made two of the biggest deals in team history.
The biggest trade they ever made was by Poles and was in 2023, so Thursday's trade the Bears made for Jeffery Simmons must rank right up there behind it in impact.  No doubt he'll find a way to add back picks with offseason trades but this was earthshattering in scope.
The Bears have had their hits and their misses when it comes to the trade market over the years. The hits seem much bigger but some of the misses were gut wrenching.
20 snaps of Jeffery Simmons dominating in run defense: pic.twitter.com/3ZGiAc7Ycm
Of course, the 2023 trade Poles made is the biggest ever because it meant the Bears could draft Caleb Williams, among others.
Here are the top trades in Chicago Bears history ranked.
Titans got more for Jeffrey Simmons than Browns got for Myles Garrett.
Trading Carolina the first pick in 2023 is easily the biggest deal the Bears ever made and the gift that keeps on giving. Because the Bears acquired the first pick of the 2024 draft to use for  DJ Moore, and picks they used to draft tackle Darnell Wright, cornerback Tyrique Stevenson, punter Tory Taylor, and wide receiver Luther Burden, this one stands supreme for impact. Getting Williams ushered in a new era on offense for the Bears. Wright is their blocking force in the wide zone running game. Burden is their yards-after-catch impact receiver. Taylor looks like one of the league's best punters now. Moore won them a playoff game over the Packers and helped them beat Green Bay to win a division title, then got them a second-round pick when he was traded and they used it for moves made to draft Sam Roush and Malik Muhammad.
The trade itself is not entirely unlike the Khalil Mack trade that Ryan Pace made. Except it's the most anyone ever traded away for a defensive tackle. For Poles, it's a superstar defensive player acquired for a pair of first-round picks and a fourth-rounder.  Gervon Dexter might have been the best Bears defensive tackle drafted since Tommy Harris, and they traded him largely because he didn't fit what they were trying to do in Dennis Allen's scheme to the degree that he would justify paying out a big contract. Now they have their best defensive tackle since the early Lovie Smith coaching era.
Great trade for the Bears, but they could’ve just drafted Carter
Khalil Mack and a conditional fifth-round pick in 2020 came to the Bears and the Raiders in return got first-round picks in 2019 and 2020, a third-round pick in 2020 and a sixth-rounder. The trade triggered a season when the Bears dominated defensively but thanks to Cody Parkey's double doink they still couldn't get past the Eagles in the playoffs and they also still lacked the offensive punch needed to get bigger things done than win a division title. Mack did help them get into the playoffs in 2020 as well, but his first season of 12 1/2 sacks was easily his best and nagging minor injuries held him down thereafter.
This is how Ryan Poles sold it to Ben Johnson. Cole Kmet replacement pic.twitter.com/Av6MhwkM08
Bears founder George Halas needed a quarterback to run his new T-formation. He found exactly the right player using a first-round pick he acquired in a trade with Pittsburgh. He sent offensive and defensive end Edgar "Eggs" Manske to the Steelers for what turned out to be the second pick of the 1939 draft. He drafted Colombia quarterback Sid Luckman and the result was a dynasty. The Bears won four NFL championships between 1940-46 thanks to 1943 MVP Luckman, and their new T-formation. Then they got Manske back and he played a big role in winning the 1940 title.
In 2009, it had become apparent Rex Grossman wasn't the answer. Jerry Angelo traded for Denver quarterback Jay Cutler. While Cutty had some decent years, he was only .500 in terms of wins and losses while playing with a good defense from 2009-12 under Lovie Smith, then played for two more coaches and struggled. The worst part of getting Cutler wasn't just the draft capital surrendered. They gave up first-round picks in 2009 and 2010 and a third-rounder in 2009 for him and a fifth-round pick. But they also had to pay Cutler two big contracts and eventually it kept them adding players they otherwise could have used. Cutler did get them to an NFC championship game and they lost after he was injured in the first half.  The best QBs they could have taken with the first-round picks they dealt was Tim Tebow, so from that end it was fine. But they traded away Kyle Orton to Denver with this deal and they simply could have kept him and used him as starter because his statistics weren't a lot different than Cutler's from that point onward. Cutler had an 85.2 passer rating in Chicago while Orton was 86.3. Orton had a TD percentage of 3.9 and interception percentage of only 2.3. Cutler had a better TD percentage of 4.7 but also a 3.1% interception percentage.
The greatest defensive player in Bears history came to them as a result of a trade. On Dec. 2, 1963, as they were a few weeks away from winning the NFL championship, the Bears traded a 1964 second-round pick and fourth-round pick to Pittsburgh for a 1965 first-round pick. The pick wound up being the third overall pick and the Bears selected Butkus, a force of nature and home-grown talent who scared the NFL into hiding until a knee surgery gone bad ended his career in 1973.
A first, literally: Jeffery Simmons is the first defensive tackle in the common draft era since 1967 to be traded for multiple first-round picks. pic.twitter.com/EOrDCK5MCl
The Bears used one great defensive lineman to acquire another. Veteran Pro Bowl tackle Wally Chambers was traded away after a brief Bears career greatly muted by injury. The Bears sent Chambers and tight end Bob Moore to the Buccaneers for a first-round pick prior to the 1978 draft. The pick was the fourth one of the 1979 draft, and the Bears used it for Hall of Fame defensive tackle/end Dan Hampton. He made two Pro Bowls at defensive end and two at tackle and anchored the 1985 Super Bowl champion defense.
Before everyone says we got fleeced, look at the numbers for draft capital to make this make sense! Y’all forget the math sometimes… Not all first-round picks are created equal. The NFL’s traditional draft-value chart assigns the No. 1 overall pick 3,000 points. The No. 25… pic.twitter.com/vvZSh3ni3y
The Bears, first, lost the coin flip so they could draft Terry Bradshaw in 1970. So they had the second overall pick. With Halas still running the show off the field, they decided it would be better to trade the second overall pick to Green Bay for linebacker Lee Roy Caffey, running back Elijah Pitts and center Bob Hyland. The Packers used the pick for Mike McCoy, who played defensive tackle seven years for them without making a Pro Bowl. But the second pick of the draft netted the Bears virtually nothing. They had 14 starts from Caffey and Hyland and Pitts never even played in a game for them. This was a complete and utter disaster, the worst trade ever made by the Bears and possibly the worst use of the second overall pick in any draft ever. What kept it from being a doomsday move was the team was so bad for about seven years that what did it matter, anyway?

title: Zac Taylor Announces Light Injury Game Status List For Titans Matchup
full_text:
The Bengals are pretty healthy heading into the weekend ahead of their matchup with the Titans. Head Coach Zac Taylor spoke with the media after Friday's practice and confirmed backup safety Kyle Dugger (quad) is going to miss the game and Joe Giles-Harris (calf) is questionable.
Ja'Marr Chase missed one day of practice this week due to rest and a minor ankle injury, but he was a full go in both Thursday and Friday practices.
Meanwhile, the Titans are dealing with a big injury to starting wide receiver Carnell Tate, who missed all of the practices this week with a shoulder injury. He is doubtful along with starting punter Tommy Townsend and running back Tyjae Spears.
No matter who is out there, Cincinnati can't take the Titans lightly even if they are 12.5-point betting favorites and climbing on DraftKings Sportsbook.
The Bengals also do have to overcome the turnover in the backend of the tight end room.
"That'll certainly be a challenge losing a guy like Erick (all), who brought a lot of toughness to what we do, and then losing Tanner (Hudson), who plays a lot of different roles for us; really, he's so versatile, and we feel so good about him in the pass game too," Joe Burrow said this week. "Now those are two huge losses for us that you can't really replace with just two guys."
Cincinnati's elite passer is confident players like Jack Endries can step up in those roles.
"All the things that we talk about in the pass game, Jack seems just to see it and feel it like the quarterback does," Burrow said. "Obviously he's got a ways to go, just being a rookie and seeing all those different looks in a lot of different spots. But we feel good about where he can go, and he also brings some toughness, I think, in the run game as well. I haven't seen too much of it, obviously, because he hasn't been out there really. But I'm excited to see what he can do."
Cincinnati kicks off against Tennessee on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

title: Is There an Opportunity for the Bengals to Pull Off a Massive Blockbuster Trade?
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals' Week 7 win over the Baltimore Ravens was massive. Now, it's time for the team to move on to their Week 8 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.
With the win last Sunday, the Bengals moved to 4-2 on the season, and this week offers them a great chance to stay afloat in the fight for the top spot in the AFC North.
If the Bengals have more goals than just a divisional crown, there could be some moves made by the front office before the trade deadline that will make this team a stronger threat.
A lot of the talk about making a move for a running back has been in the headlines, but what about a trade for a tight end? One name that could possibly be on the block is Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta.
LaPorta has been at odds with the Lions as his recent comments about getting a new contract proved that the tight end is a tad disappointed.
"It’s disappointing that you go out there every week and bear the risk of getting hurt," LaPorta said on Pardon My Take. “I'm going to continue to do my thing and ball out, and in three months, if I don't get to wear the Honolulu blue and play for the Lions anymore, it’s going to be all good. I'll go get paid somewhere else. So whatever.”
That sounds like a player who is ready to move on if his current team doesn't show him the respect he feels he deserves. However, Lions head coach Dan Campbell doesn't seem to think his tight end's comments are anything to worry about.
For the Bengals , tight end is a position that recently took a major hit. With the recent news that Erik All's season has been derailed by a knee injury, the Bengals could use a major talent like LaPorta, but it may be costly.
Spotrac currently has LaPorta's market value at $15 million a season for three years. LaPorta will be 26 by the time the 2027 season begins. To put that in perspective, the Dallas Cowboys signed tight end Jake Ferguson at the same age for a $50 million deal.
Getting LaPorta will come at a heavy price. Not only will the Bengals be expected to give him a new deal, but the team will probably need to trade important draft capital.
LaPorta is sixth in receiving yards for tight ends this season and has three touchdown receptions. He would obviously be a massive upgrade at the position, but would the Bengals be willing to retain him with a new deal?
A trade for LaPorta is unlikely. However, if the Bengals want to go all-in, it couldn't hurt to ask if there is a market for the talented tight end.

title: Bengals Trade Fit for Emerging Linebacker is a No-Brainer Move
full_text:
Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr. have improved this season for the Bengals , but both have still struggled in certain areas, specifically with missed tackles. Together, they've missed 14 tackles in six games, indicating that linebacker remains a weakness on defense, one that could cost them later in the season. One trade candidate could fix that problem, though, as The Athletic has labeled Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley a fit for the Bengals at the trade deadline.
Henley has flashed elite play early in his career. In 2024, he recorded 147 tackles with an 8.7% missed-tackle rate, an interception, and eight passes defended, allowing a 99.1 passer rating. His 2025 season started slow due to severe illness, however, he still recorded 103 tackles with only five misses. He also had two interceptions with five passes defended.
His play in 2026 started inconsistently, but from Week 3 onward, he corrected that and continued to show the traits of an ascending player at 27 years old. He has only missed two tackles all season compared to Knight and Carters 14 combined.
With Henley in the final year of his rookie deal and the Chargers having tremendously underwhelmed this season, now is the perfect time to acquire him at a low cost.
The difficulty of negotiating a contract extension, along with a rebuild set to take place in LA, could reduce the trade compensation to as little as a fifth-round pick. The Bengals could avoid sacrificing even a fifth-rounder in next year's draft by including Shemar Stewart in the deal.
There is also a precedent for what an extension for Henley could look like. If he hits his ceiling, the ideal contract should land somewhere in the range of what Zach Baun and Azeez Al-Shaair commanded at $17-$18 million a year.
Acquiring Henley would give the Bengals, at minimum, a starting-caliber player at the linebacker spot with a high ceiling as a potential rising star.
Should the Bengals look elsewhere for a linebacker instead of Henley, there are still starting-caliber options worth the investment.
Titans linebacker Cody Barton is one example of a trustworthy player at the linebacker spot as he has remained solid at the position in his eight-year career. He has missed no more than seven tackles since 2019 and will turn 30 in November. Barton has solid coverage skills, but his 4.2% career missed-tackle rate shows he can bring down ball carriers.
Another option is Chargers linebacker Troy Dye, who has routinely served as a solid backup with special-teams experience. The team could acquire him to replace veteran Swayze Bozeman, who is currently on Injured Reserve with a fractured forearm. At 30 years old, Dye would likely fill Bozeman's role better than Jack Kiser, whom the team claimed off waivers after Bozeman's injury.
Either Barton or Dye would be cheaper than Henley in a trade and may better align with what the Bengals want to add to their linebacker room.

title: Micah Parsons Picks Bengals to Achieve AFC’s Top Regular-Season Goal
full_text:
Micah Parsons sees the Cincinnati Bengals finishing atop the AFC. The Green Bay Packers star picked Cincinnati on his Bleacher Report show when asked which team would earn the conference's first-round bye.
The Bengals improved to 4-2 with a 35-13 win over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday. Cincinnati erased a 13-0 halftime deficit by scoring 35 unanswered points, giving Parsons plenty to consider when making his prediction.
“I’m gonna say Bengals,” Parsons said in the clip. “I think they’ve been pretty much the most consistent.”
"Ja’Marr’s numbers may not be high. It’s because Tee’s been snapping,” Parsons said.
Higgins offered a strong example in Baltimore, catching six passes for 148 yards and a touchdown. Ja'Marr Chase added five catches for 62 yards and a score, while Joe Burrow finished with 292 passing yards and four passing touchdowns.
Burrow was particularly sharp after halftime, completing 16-of-18 passes for 249 yards. That efficiency helped Cincinnati turn a two-score deficit into a comfortable road win over a division opponent.
“The Bengal defense is playing great,” Parsons said. “It’s not the same Bengals. It’s not the same. I think they low-key win the division.”
The Bengals recorded four sacks against Baltimore and held the Ravens scoreless after halftime.  Cincinnati has 21 sacks through six games, with multiple sacks in each game and at least four in four of those games.
That pass rush gives Cincinnati another way to take control when the offense needs time to find its rhythm. Against Baltimore, the defense kept the deficit manageable until Burrow and his receivers turned the game around.
The uneven start also leaves Cincinnati with something to clean up. Chasing the AFC's top seed will require more complete performances, because even an offense with Burrow, Chase, and Higgins cannot count on five touchdown drives after halftime every week.
Cincinnati returns to Paycor Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 8. A win would put the Bengals at 5-2, giving them a chance to build on their breakthrough in Baltimore and strengthen their standing in the AFC playoff race.

title: Bengals Star React to Titans Jeffery Simmons Trade Before Cincinnati Matchup
full_text:
The Bengals don't have to deal with arguably the best defensive tackle in the NFL this coming weekend, a welcome relief to members of the offense.
Tennessee sent Jeffery Simmons to the Bears today in a blockbuster move ahead of the 2026 Trade Deadline. The 2025 AP First-Team All-Pro is 10th at his position in Pro Football Focus grading this season while leading all interior linemen in ESPN pass-rush win rate and ranking fifth in pressure rate.
Ja'Marr Chase and Ted Karras spoke about the ease of the game plan Thursday, while acknowledging you can't take anyone lightly in the NFL.
"I don't have to block him, but we're definitely glad he made it a little better for us with the game plan," Chase said.
Karras did have to take him on and he is breathing big sigh of relief to not face the eighth-year star.
"Two hours of anxiety last night is gone," Karras joked. "I'm going to take a deeper look and kind of try and predict how they're going to play without them. They got good players. John Franklin-Myers has been playing at the top of his game for a long time. I remember when he was young on the Jets; he's been dangerous forever. So they got a lot of good players over there. So we got to go out and execute and win this ball game, but yeah, I mean, obviously, a dynamic player is on the Bears, so Joe Thuney has to deal with him at practice."
Cincinnati's easy schedule got a tad bit easier with the move, and they cannot afford to lose this game while pursuing the top regular season goal: The AFC's No. 1 seed.
Chase wants to see his team come out much faster than the donut they posted in the first half a few days ago.
"I think we got to look at the bright side of us playing at home," Chase noted. "That's the one thing we got to look at. We're playing at home, so we got to keep the crowd in tight for us. We got to keep the fans ready. And two is just coming out faster than what we did last week. You can't look at this game like they lost Jeffery Simmons and not still be good, you know what I'm saying? Cause they still got good players up front."
The Bengals star also pointed out his ankle is feeling fine after a full day of Thursday practice.
Cincinnati gets a chance to show that hunger at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

title: Bengals Injury Report: Ja'Marr Chase's Status Upgraded on Thursday as Bengals Continue Titans Preparation
full_text:
The Bengals dropped their Thursday injury report ahead of the Titans game, and Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) got upgraded to full status on the report after not practicing due to that small issue and rest in general on Wednesday.
He told the media on Thursday his ankle feels fine.
Kyle Dugger (quad) continues to not practice as he heads toward another missed game this week. Fellow safety Jordan Battle was also limited again with a shoulder injury, but he's been playing through that issue in outings over the last few weeks.
Cincinnati is pretty clean besides those names.
On the Titans' side of things, starting defensive tackle John Franklin-Meyers (groin) upgraded to limited and starting receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice for a second-straight day.
Cincinnati head coach Zac Taylor has had to shuffle around his tight end room due to all of the injuries in recent weeks.
Erick All just went on season-ending injured reserve with a torn ACL, and fellow tight end Tanner Hudson tore a pec this season as well.
"Attention to detail has been really important to him," Taylor said about rookie tight end Jack Endries as he gets primed for more snaps. "Waiting for his moment, you can tell he never knew when his number was going to be called. He's really got to know three different positions and so I've got trust, just watching him operate in practice and in meetings and in training camp, that if needed, he was going to be ready to go, and there was a time where he wasn't needed because we had everybody healthy, and now's that time. So I'm not nervous at all about using him. I think he's earning the opportunity. I'm excited to watch him play."
Taylor also echoed confidence in backup safety PJ Jules, who is filling in for Dugger's reserve role.
"PJ brings a lot of energy. It's really important to him," Taylor noted. "He's done a great job on special teams in his roles. He stepped into safety. So when we need to continue to rely on depth at the safety position, I feel very confident in PJ and Russ (Yeast)."
Cincinnati has a light practice on Friday.

title: 'Guaranteed Super Bowl' - Bengals Pushed to Trade For Star Running Back Amidst Enticing Factors
full_text:
The Bengals need to take advantage of the Colts' fire sale.
Indianapolis is dumping talented players left and right this week following trades to send out stars like guard Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. Jonathan Taylor is in the sights now for many teams, and the Bengals should be one of them.
They already traded away draft capital to completely transform the defense with Dexter Lawrence, and now they could do the same for the offense with Taylor.
Former NFL offensive lineman Breiden Fehoko echoed that sentiment this week. The Bengals need to make another move and go all in on pursuing the AFC's No. 1 seed. It's the easiest path to the Super Bowl, and they have the easiest schedule left in the NFL by a wide margin.
"The Bengals can lock in a guaranteed Super Bowl if they trade for Jonathan Taylor. Teams would choose to either run a light box to defend Ja’Marr (Chase) and Tee (Higgins) or load up to stop JT. YOU CAN'T DO BOTH," Fehoko declared on X .
Our Landon Belote broke down how Taylor is posting solid efficiency running from under center this season, a potential boon to Cincinnati's struggles on that front (a great shotgun runner too), and he's been a consistent force since entering the league in 2020 (one season graded lower than 65.3 overall).
Now, he is going to be very pricey. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Tuesday that the Colts don't want to trade him, and the cost could be a first-round pick. Cincinnati has eight draft picks this coming spring, including an extra projected third-round compensation pick (99th overall).
Also, Taylor starts a new $20-plus million contract extension running next season and in 2028. Alas, that's a problem to deal with in February after making a title run. Worst-case scenario, they can release him for a $10 million cap hit and $11 million in savings during the offseason, but its much more likely they just keep him as the main running back for next season. They only have Tahj Brooks under contract.
They need to try to use that extra pick somehow. They may never get a perfect-schedule storm like this ever again and cannot pass up chances to get better in pursuit of that one seed.
"I think the owner doesn't want to trade. We have two weeks from now until the deadline," Schefter said on The Pat McAfee Show. "I'm sure they don't want to trade Jonathan Taylor. And if I had to guess today, I would say I don't think they will trade Jonathan Taylor.
"But I think there are going to be teams that are interested out there that will try to have conversations, make offers, and if the Colts don't change their stance, they won't trade Jonathan Taylor. But again, I think the owner doesn't want to trade him. For the record, right now. Now, that doesn't mean it won't happen, that may just be their stance to drive up the price."
Cincinnati has to stay aggressive over the next two weeks.
They already have Lawrence as a perfect example of why they should be trading assets for firm talents. Another star add could make them clear AFC favorites.

title: Bengals' Job Sunday Just Got a Lot Easier with Titans Trading Star Defensive Tackle
full_text:
Already favored by 10.5 points Sunday against Tennessee, the Cincinnati Bengals just saw their degree of difficulty plummet further with today’s news of a blockbuster trade sending Titans’ All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears.
A first-round pick in 2019, Simmons has been voted to four Pro Bowls and earned his first first-team All-Pro selection in 2025, when he had a career-high 11 sacks.
Simmons, who also has two second-team All-Pro nods, already has four sacks this season, giving him 46.5 in his career.
Among defensive tackles, Simmons 46.5 sacks rank sixth since 2019 behind Chris Jones (64), DeForest Buckner (54.5), Aaron Donald (51.5), Cameron Heyward (48), Leonard Williams (46.5).
Bengals head coach Zac Taylor talked about facing Simmons during his Wednesday news conference.
“He’s arguably up there with all of the top guys,” he said. “I hate to rank a No. 1. He’s the opponent this week. He’s really good. He gets off the ball. He’s really difficult in one-on-one situations and double-team situations. Really good against the run. Good against the pass.
“If you’re not planning for him, you’ll have some problems.”
Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow was asked about Simmons as well.
“He's really big. He's really strong. He's really fast,” Burrow said. “That's usually a good combination. He's really tough. Seems to love what he does, and you put all those things together, you get Jeff Simmons.”
Simmons sacked Burrow three times in the 2021 Division Round playoff game the Bengals won 19-16.
And Simmons was instrumental in drawing double teams that allowed the Titans to sack Burrow another six times for an NFL-playoff record nine.
In 2022, Simmons punched Bengals center Ted Karras at the end of the game and drew an $11,139 fine from the league,
Today’s move changes the Bengals’ plan, but Tennessee has depth at the position.
Listed behind Simmons on the Titans depth chart is Solomon Thomas, the No. 3 overall pick in 2017. But the 30-year-old Thomas hasn’t had a sack in his last 26 games.
The starter next to Thomas will be John Franklin-Myers, a fourth-round pick in 2018 who also is 30 years old.
Franklin-Myers has 1.5 sacks in four career games against the Bengals while playing for the Jets and Broncos.
