title: Bengals Star Joe Burrow Praises Ja'Marr Chase Speech but Says It's Not for Him
full_text:
The next time the Cincinnati Bengals sleepwalk through a first half and need a wake-up roar in the locker room at halftime, don’t look for quarterback Joe Burrow to be the one bringing the fire the way Ja’Marr Chase did on Sunday in Baltimore.
Also, don’t look for Burrow to give a vanilla answer as to why.
“As a quarterback, at least for me personally, I play worse football when my emotions are at a higher level,” he said. “So I try to be even-keeled through the chaos. I’ve certainly done it before. It’s not what I want to do. I can get my level back down to homeostasis, but I prefer to just keep it there.”
For those of you who arrived here via X, you may be unaware of the concept of “homeostasis.”
Homeostasis (hō-mē-ō-ˈstā-səs): Any self-regulating process by which a biological system maintains a stable internal environment while adjusting to changing external conditions.
While blistering the walls isn’t something Burrow prefers, he welcomed Chase’s outburst following Sunday’s first half that saw the Bengals fail to score on four possessions while gaining just 59 yards.
“I think you know Ja'Marr's captain for a reason. He walks the walk,” Burrow said. “He doesn't talk often, but when he does, obviously guys listen. And I think that was a perfect moment for it. Obviously, when Ja'Marr speaks, it has a lot of impact, and that one certainly did.”
Burrow said Chase didn’t give him a heads up about what he was going to do at halftime.
Chase, who missed Wednesday’s practice with a “Non-Injury Related-Rest/Ankle” designation, is expected to hold his regular weekly news conference later this afternoon, and he could go more into when he decided he needed to say something.
But this is what he said immediately after the game:
“We had 15 plays, maybe two or three possessions, and it didn't go our way at all," Chase said. "We had opportunities to get the ball out of our hands. Joe was putting up with too much pressure, and I came in here screaming, saying somebody got to make a play. Somebody got to make a play, and I told the offense we can't look at our defense the whole time. We got to step this s--t up and make something work.”
What followed was five touchdowns in five series and a 35-0 second-half advantage and 35-13 victory that re-ignited talk and hope about the Bengals being built for a deep playoff run.
Burrow may be the driver for that ride, but he’ll leave the soundtrack to others.

title: Bengals Named Trade Fit for Eagles Veteran Cornerback
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals have a very good roster with a very solid defense, but like every team in the league, there are some holes they could patch up in their effort to win the Super Bowl this season. With the trade deadline quickly approaching this season, the Bengals could be in the market to add another cornerback to their roster.
This isn't a dire need, as their cornerback situation is fine, but that's all that it is. Their cornerback room isn't one of the best in the league, but it does the job. Cincinnati could pursue another cornerback to upgrade the roster if the right one falls into their lap.
Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox recently listed the Bengals as a potential suitor in a trade hypothetical for Philadelphia Eagles starter Riq Woolen.
"According to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , some team executives are already wondering whether the Eagles could make Saquon Barkley and Riq Woolen available," Knox wrote. "Philly might not want to part with Barkley, who should be the centerpiece of the offense once he's healthy. However, Woolen would be a very sensible trade chip.
"The Eagles only signed Woolen to a one-year deal , and cornerbacks are typically in demand. Woolen, who has allowed a career opposing passer rating of just 73.8 , should draw a reasonable return, even for a short-term rental."
Woolen is the perfect short-term rental for the Bengals to look into.
He would help patch up their secondary, which has struggled a little bit at times. Their defense has been much improved this season compared to years past, but the Bengals need to make sure there aren't any glaring holes when the trade deadline passes by.
Woolen is a shutdown option on a short-term contract. This would allow the Bengals to acquire him relatively cheaply, as rentals are far easier to trade for than players on longer-term deals. Woolen would join DJ Turner and Dax Hill as impact players in the cornerback room in Cincinnati.
This group would have the potential to be a top-10 pass defense in the league.

title: Browns Remain Behind in the Trade Market, But Here's How They Can Join The Fun
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers may be out of playoff contention for the 2026 NFL season.
But the Cleveland Browns certainly are.
With the Trade Deadline looming, the Browns will look to bolster the roster on both sides of the ball to maintain a top spot in the AFC North. While both sides of the ball have a few holes to fill, the defensive line has been by far the most banged-up part of the squad.
In order to fortify the group and add to the already talented corps, the Browns should make a move for Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea.
On Thursday, Oct. 29, just two days after the Indianapolis Colts began their fire sale in the trade market, 247Sports' Easton Butler reported that the Buccaneers were fielding calls for Vea. The 6-foot-4, 347-pounder has been dominant for most of his career.
Now, at age 31, Vea is likely looking to be on a contending squad and play meaningful football when the calendar turns over to 2027.
The #Packers and the #Bengals have reportedly called the Buccaneers about DT Vita Vea again, per sources. pic.twitter.com/CJuxzKbSiF
Led by a group sporting second-year standout Mason Graham and exciting edge rusher Jared Verse , the Browns have a young, impressionable line to build around. Adding a player like Vea wouldn't shake up the locker room, but rather give them an experienced star to learn from.
Vea, across the last nine seasons, has dominated the trenches.
With two Pro Bowl selections to show for it, Vea has recorded a whopping 270 combined tackles, 83 quarterback hits, 49 tackles for a loss, 37 sacks and three forced fumbles. His height has also led to him posting 11 pass deflections as well.
Since 2021, Vea has recorded four or more sacks in a season each year , giving him the consistency that Cleveland's line would be looking for.
The biggest appeal of adding Vea would be his ability to improve the Browns' run defense, all while creating more opportunities for the young pass rushers to get into the backfield. Pairing Vea with the likes of Graham and Collins on the inside would give the Browns one of the best defensive fronts in football.
The only concern for adding a player of his status is the contract he is on.
In late August, Vea signed a contract extension with the Buccaneers, adding an extra six million to his $18 million he was already making. That means his contractual value brings him in at nearly $25 million, with another $24 million guaranteed in 2027.
The Browns would have to be willing to take on such a cap hit.
However, as the front office has shown in seasons past, they can finagle the books enough to make the deal work and spread the money out.
The recent trade of defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons to the Chicago Bears provides a useful benchmark for what the Browns should give up to land Vea.
The Bears were able to pull Simmons away from the Titans by sending two first-round picks and a fourth-rounder. That is a pretty big return for the Titans, but Simmons' 11-sack campaign in 2025 put his stock through the roof.
However, the Browns shouldn't be expected to pay that much.
Vea is good; there is no questioning that, but his value comes in at a more reasonable area. The Browns would likely have to give up two third-round picks and a fourth-round pick to pry Vea away. If they were willing to give up a second, due to the Buccaneers' demands, that could get the job done as well.
If Cleveland wants to genuinely compete by the time the regular season comes to a close, the front office should at least explore sacrificing a few draft picks at the trade deadline.
And if Vea ends up on the table, the trigger should be pulled.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: How Jared Verse Stirred the Pot Ahead of Browns-Steelers Rematch
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns take on the Pittsburgh Steelers in a massive Week 8 rivalry matchup, with first place in the AFC North on the line. A war of words has added another layer of intensity ahead of Sunday’s matchup on Nov. 1.
The Cleveland Browns beat the Pittsburgh Steelers at home on Thursday Night Football in Week 4 of the NFL season. In a chippy, back-and-forth game, the Browns defeated the Steelers on a game-winning 56-yard field goal from Andre Szmyt with 10 seconds remaining. Following the game, Browns star edge defender Jared Verse commented on the Steelers' offensive line and their style of play:
#Browns Jared Verse on the chippiness with the Steelers’ offensive line: “I was talking to them crazy. I was telling them, ‘You’re double-teaming, y’all sliding, y’all garbage.’ I don’t have any respect that plays too dirty and does too much extra stuff after the game." pic.twitter.com/9gzUMZEJh7
Verse claimed that the Steelers' offensive line played “dirty,” and while that is up to one’s interpretation, the Steelers’ locker room definitely took notice.
Cam Heyward appeared on The Rich Eisen Show ahead of the Browns-Steelers matchup on Tuesday, Oct. 27. On that episode, Eisen played the clip of Verse’s comments and asked the Steelers defensive tackle to respond:
Heyward defended his teammates and suggested Verse was whining about routine football tactics such as double-teams and chip blocks.  Verse is not a player to back down, and when he spoke to reporters Thursday, Verse had more to say.
Speaking to reporters Thursday, Verse responded directly to Heyward’s criticism. Verse made one thing clear: he is not worried about Heyward or the Steelers' offensive line:
“I’m not worried about Cam, I’m not worried about their OL, I’m not worried about anyone on their team,” - Jared Verse on the Steelers 👀👀👀 pic.twitter.com/KRdQhA2qBf
That confidence faces a significant test on the road. Cleveland has not won a regular-season game in Pittsburgh since 2003, giving Verse an opportunity to help end a lengthy drought while backing up his latest comments. Verse kept his response short and simple as both teams continue to prepare for a pivotal AFC North matchup.
Ultimately, a war of words means little without results on the field. Verse has yet to record a sack through Cleveland’s first seven games of the season, and Heyward plays defense, meaning the two will not line up against each other. Both have bigger priorities Sunday, starting with disrupting the opposing quarterback.
What this back-and-forth does prove is one thing: the Browns and Steelers rivalry is very much back. Trash talk has long been part of this rivalry, but this meeting carries added weight with both teams entering at 5-2 . Both teams are focused on securing first place in the AFC North.
Now it’s time to see which team can back up its words on the field.
Noah Olson is a Northeast Ohio native and lifelong Cleveland sports fan. He graduated from The College of Wooster with a major in Communications and has been sports writing since 2024. As a writer for BIGPLAY On SI, Noah brings a blend of local pride and an insider’s perspective, focusing on thoughtful analysis and storytelling rooted in Cleveland sports culture.

title: Browns vs. Steelers: 5 Key Matchups That Could Decide Cleveland's Week 8 Showdown
full_text:
On the first of October, the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers faced off in the spotlight on Thursday Night Football with first place in the AFC North on the line. Exactly one month later, the two teams will do it all over again in Pittsburgh, with the division lead once again hanging in the balance.
The Steelers have not lost since the Week 4 matchup in Cleveland, and the Browns have only dropped a rain-soaked game in New York. Both teams head into the pivotal game at 5-2, with the Browns owning the tiebreaker for now. The Steelers are rolling, and the Browns will have to succeed in these five key matchups to come out of Pittsburgh with their stamp on first place.
It is cliché to point to stopping the run for a key to any game in the NFL; however, it rings true for Sunday. Jaylen Warren has rushed for over 100 yards three times this season, including 93 yards in his first matchup against the Browns. He is averaging 5.5 yards per carry this season and he can hit for a big play at any moment.
Rico Dowdle missed the first game in Cleveland, but he is back and can provide relief for Warren. The Steelers got away from utilizing Warren against the Browns, and the addition of Dowdle will help them be a more well-rounded offense.
The Browns defense has struggled giving up chunk plays against the run. The more Aaron Rodgers has to throw and take hits, the better the defense can be. The defensive line needs to plug holes and hit Warren before he can get a head of steam going downfield.
The offense finally had a good game running the ball last Sunday. Lanes were open and Judkins showed speed and strength hitting the holes. Dylan Sampson returned and shook off some rust by showing his speed on the outside. KC Concepcion even contributed on creative runs.
The rushing attack needs to be productive to keep Deshaun Watson from obvious passing downs and having the Steelers’ pass rushers feed off the home crowd to create havoc. Hopefully Todd Monken and the offense has unlocked a strategy to upstart the previously stagnant running game.
The first game between these two teams was slow going to start, then Ward picked off Rodgers and the offense came alive. The same was said last week against the Tennessee Titans and the team fed off the defensive leader’s turnover.
The Steelers’ receivers have been great this season, and they have a big-bodied tight end that provides a matchup problem. Rodgers has thrown the ball over 30 times in every game this season. He is not afraid to place the ball anywhere on the field, and the secondary has to communicate and be aware of their assignment to prevent any breakdowns. This game can come down to the turnover battle, and the Browns had two interceptions in the first matchup.
The Steelers pass rush has rattled Cleveland quarterbacks in recent years. The last time Watson played in Pittsburgh he threw a pick six to the defensive end, setting the tone for the game. Spencer Fano will have to continue his great rookie season against TJ Watt and keep Watson upright.
The ball got out of Watson’s hand faster last week in Tennessee and the offense put up 27 points. The defensive line knows that Watson has the propensity to hang onto the ball a little long and they will look to hit him hard. Monken and Watson have to take them out of the game and put the offense in manageable third downs to convert.
The Browns-Steelers rivalry matters. Todd Monken understands that. But when you prepare every week like it’s the biggest game you’ve ever played, your standard doesn’t change. The attention to detail, the focus, the weight room, rehab, practice and film study are already where…
Everyone is well aware that the Browns have not won a regular-season game in Pittsburgh in 23 years. Their roster is filled with rookies and second-year players, and they should not care about the failures that came before them.
“Well, it has nothing to do with our team. I mean, this year, whether it’s where we’re at record-wise, comparing the past or the history against the Steelers, it’s a divisional game," said Monken about playing in Pittsburgh. "It’s bigger because it’s obviously a divisional opponent. The fastest way to get in the playoffs is [to] win your division. ”
The youth on the roster will not have the pressure of winning in the Steel City, allowing them to play fast and free. Monken is rightfully treating this like any other game and is not letting the ghosts of teams’ past haunt the locker room.
The AFC North is up for grabs, and the Browns have the opportunity to be in first place past Week 8 for the first time since 2014. They are 2-2 on the road and 3-0 at home. If the Browns want the division to run through Cleveland, then it starts with them handling the keys to the game in Pittsburgh and changing history.
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: Will Browns Make QB Changes? Monken’s Recent Comments Leave Things Up in the Air
full_text:
Second-year quarterback Dillon Gabriel is officially off the injury report and back in the lineup for the Cleveland Browns.
Gabriel, who the Browns selected in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft, began the year on IR dealing with a back injury.
But how will his return shape up the quarterback room? Even Todd Monken is unsure as the question arose.
Todd Monken on how Dillon Gabriel's activation might change the QB order on Sunday: 'I haven't gotten there yet.'
Despite the young pup being available, it is no question the Browns will stick with Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback.
Watson currently leads the NFL in game-winning drives with five. Currently, he is on track to get himself a brand-new deal to remain the Browns' starter after this season.
However, that is a different story. The main question with Gabriel being back with the team is where he fits.
Without the former Heisman candidate, the Browns had a nicely set depth chart with Watson as the starter, Shedeur Sanders as the backup, and rookie Taylen Green as the third string.
The reason why it worked so well was that Sanders is getting to learn from Watson as the backup, with Green as a possible option to bring in on plays the Browns want to utilize his athleticism.
Now, where does Gabriel fit? Clearly, Monken favors Sanders to be the backup, and with talks of potentially bringing in Green for designed plays, does that mean Gabriel is the fourth string?
While he will most likely slot in above Green, it does bring up another question.
Will the Browns look to deal Gabriel before the NFL trade deadline?
Let's say the Browns want to move on from Gabriel. Where could they send him and what could they get in return?
The best scenario for both parties is a situation where a team just lost their starting quarterback to injury. In that case, Gabriel would get the chance to actually compete for a starting job, and the Browns could get a slightly better package from a QB-needy team.
At the moment, a team that comes to mind would be the Philadelphia Eagles.
A potential package that could benefit the Browns could be sending Gabriel and a pick for tight end Dallas Goedert. This would fill a need of backup tight end for the Brown and Orange, while capitalizing on trading a young player.
As for now, Gabriel remains with the Browns and will find a spot to sit until something changes internally.
Who knows, maybe a team has had their eye on Gabriel since his time at Orgeon and believe in the 25 year old.
Regardless, it's time for the Browns to cut ties with the Hawaii native, who has shown disinterest in playing for the Browns. It truly does not seem like Gabriel is needed or fits on the team any longer.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: This Rookie Breakout Gives the NFL's Most Exciting Team a Major Boost Offensively
full_text:
With the 24th pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, the Cleveland Browns selected wide receiver KC Concepcion.
The former Texas A&M Aggie was a standout in college, recording a whopping 185 receptions, 2,218 receiving yards, 431 rushing yards and 28 total touchdowns across three seasons of ball.
But just a few picks after selecting Concepcion, the Browns decided to add another talented wide receiver to the draft class, selecting Washington Husky Denzel Boston. Boston, unlike Concepcion, was more of a deep threat, providing the Browns with a 6-foot-4, 215-pound frame.
KC Concepcion is currently on pace for 73 catches for 800 yards Denzel Boston is currently on pace for 50 catches and 900 yards Just fantastic production from your two rookie wide receivers #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/FvyDtjQAJh
He was never popping off the stat sheets, but was just a reliable go-to option, especially in the red zone.
To begin their careers in the orange and brown, though, Boston stole the spotlight.
He was just downright dominant in the Browns' first few games of the season, hauling in 16 receptions for 330 yards and three touchdowns over five games . Those numbers were good enough for a whopping 20.6 yards per reception.
Concepcion may have been taken off the board a few picks earlier, but Boston was standing out as the steal of the draft.
However, that was, until Week 7 of the NFL regular season.
Concepcion went off against the Tennessee Titans , slashing through the defense time and time again as he hauled in eight receptions for 129 yards. He averaged 16.1 yards per reception and recorded a long of 32 yards.
Every time it seemed like he would go down, though, he fought for more yards and routinely extended plays.
Highest catch rate vs man coverage among WR this season (min 10 man targets) Garrett Wilson         92.9% KC Concepcion       84.6% Chris Olave               82.4% CeeDee Lamb          75.0% Tee Higgins               72.7% pic.twitter.com/unfryUQ1OI
"I play this game with so much heart, so much effort. I'm finally glad that Browns fans and the Browns community was finally able to see what I can bring to this team," he said after Sunday's game concluded.
His efforts out on the gridiron helped guide the team to a fifth victory of the season, with the Browns now sitting 5-2 overall.
With Boston and Concepcion emerging as threats and complementing each other’s games, the rest of the squad only stands to benefit. More opportunities will come the way of Jerry Jeudy and Harold Fannin Jr. as defenses shift their attention toward the two playmakers, creating a snowball effect.
From there, teams will have to adjust to the passing attack, led by Deshaun Watson, which will in turn open up Cleveland's rushing game.
As Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson return from injury and slowly get back to form, they will have an opportunity to capitalize on those openings and round out the offense nicely.
"It's been a little bit of an up-and-down challenge," head coach Todd Monken said about the Browns' offense. "But that's the NFL, as you try to find your way to be consistent. We're always under construction."
With Concepcion finally finding his form, the Browns have a perfect storm following them as they look to maintain the top spot in the AFC North.
This coming weekend, the Browns will clash with the Pittsburgh Steelers as the two sides face at Acrisure Stadium. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. EST on Sunday, Nov. 1.

title: 3 All-Time Worst Cleveland Browns Moves at the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
When discussing failed trades and the Cleveland Browns, a number of well known names immediately pop up, beginning with the team’s current starting quarterback .
However, when it comes to midseason trades Cleveland’s history is nowhere near as bad, as the team is usually much less active than during the offseason.
With that in mind, here are the Browns’ three worst moves before the NFL trade deadline:
Back in October of 2024, Cooper was the team’s best wideout. He was coming off a personal best 1,250-receiving yard 2023 campaign which led to his fourth Pro Bowl nod, and was the club’s leader six weeks into the season with 24 catches for 250 yards and two scores on 53 targets.
However, Cooper was also on the final year of his deal, and at 30 years old, the Browns were seemingly not interested in extending him beyond that season. Additionally, the team was eager to force more targets towards their shiny new offseason acquisition, wideout Jerry Jeudy, who had cost the team a fifth- and a sixth-rounder in the 2024 Draft. At that point, Jeudy had caught 20 balls for 248 yards and one score off 36 targets.
While Jeudy earned Pro Bowl honors that year in Cleveland thanks to a personal-best 1,229 receiving yards, Cooper struggled with the Bills -- who handed over a 2025 third-rounder and a 2026 seventh-rounder for him and a sixth- -- catching just 20 balls for 297 yards and two scores in eight games for Buffalo.
What wasn’t known at the time was that Jeudy’s production would fall off a cliff in 2025, leading to him becoming an afterthought in the Browns’ current offense, behind rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston.
Yes, Cooper’s compensation was generous given that he failed to leave a mark with the Bills, but there’s no way of knowing if Cooper’s production would have declined so sharply had he not been sent away. And the immediate result was a 2025 offensive unit with the worst wide receiver room in the whole NFL, led by Jeudy and his constant dropped passes, which in turn gave way to the team picking up two wideouts within their first three picks in this year's draft while putting Jeudy squarely in the middle of intense trade speculation in the process .
Meanwhile, Cooper’s compensation would eventually turn into third-round quarterback Dillon Gabriel, currently third on Cleveland’s depth chart after a failed stint as a rookie starter.
During the same 2024 campaign, Cleveland showed the door to another veteran they would end up missing -- enough to try to sign him again this past offseason.
Smith had arrived in Berea via trade in 2023 fresh off a Pro Bowl appearance for the Vikings, his third overall. The cost? Two fifth-rounders for Smith, a sixth- and a seventh-.
He immediately proceeded to start all 16 games that year, posting 5.5 sacks along with 20 quarterback hits and eight tackles for a loss. That led to the Browns signing Smith to an extension before the 2024 season worth $23.5 million over two years, with the team believing they had found the perfect complement for Myles Garrett.
Nonetheless, things started to unravel pretty quickly for the team that year thanks to a 2-7 start and Smith -- who had recorded five sacks up until that point -- was shipped away to Detroit along with a seventh-rounder for a fifth- and a sixth. Smith managed four more sacks for the Lions, finishing his season with nine.
Fast forward to 2026 with the Browns’ inviting Smith to come out of retirement for a tryout after the team dealt Garrett away in the offseason, only for Smith to ironically choose to sign with the Falcons instead , now headed by his former head coach with the Browns, Kevin Stefanski.
Perhaps Cleveland would have just been better off honoring the two-year deal they had with Smith in the first place.
Unlike the previous two instances, Cleveland messed up in this instance by buying, not selling.
At the time, Collins was an up-and-coming young defensive talent on one of the most dominant teams in the league, the Patriots. On the flipside, Cleveland was awful, coming out of a 3-13 campaign that led to the firing of then head coach Mike Pettine and replacing him with Hue Jackson.
The Browns started ‘16 at 0-8 and in shocking fashion went out and acquired Collins -- whom the Patriots did not want to pay top dollar for -- in return for a third-rounder. Cleveland would finish that year at 1-15.
Next, Collins would secure a four-year $50 million deal, only to miss 10 games of the 2017 winless campaign due to a concussion and knee injury.  Collins would start every game in 2018, logging 104 total tackles along with four sacks, but the Browns would end up cutting him during the next offseason after failing to find a willing trade partner for the linebacker.
To this day, it’s still a mystery why an 0-8 team wouldn’t have opted to add draft capital at the deadline instead of spending.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Colts Fire Sale: Where the Cleveland Browns Can Enter the Picture
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are blowing things up.
On Tuesday, Oct. 27, the Colts' front office decided to trade away future Hall of Fame offensive lineman Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and standout defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers.
With both still in the heart of a great career, the Colts moved them to load up on draft capital as they enter a rebuilding period.
Unfortunately for them, but fortunately for other teams across the league, such big swings being made the organization is in fire sale mode. Now, the door is open for teams to start throwing offers in.
The Cleveland Browns, sitting 5-2 on the campaign and in the hunt for a playoff spot here in a few months, should enter the picture and give the Colts a call about two players.
The Browns' defensive line is already good enough as is , with tackles Mason Graham and Maliek Collins leading the way in the sack column to begin the year. The outside, featuring a combination of Jared Verse, Isaiah McGuire, Sam Williams and Derek Barnett, seems to be really solid as well.
However, adding a player like Stewart is something the team should consider.
Coming in at 33 years old, he is approaching the end of his career, but would bring that experience and some more pop to the Browns' line.
Heading into the final year of his contract, the Browns could land him as a playoff piece, giving them the opportunity to remain competitive in a loaded AFC North.
He will provide the team with more depth at a banged-up position, while also helping lead a young room behind closed doors. He would give the team flexibility to shift bodies around if another Graham-type injury occurs.
When the year concludes, the Browns can let him walk to free back up that roughly $14 million in cap space , or sign him to a cheaper deal to retain him moving forward.
With Buckner going relatively cheap, Stewart would likely command a third or fourth round pick, which is something Cleveland's front office should be comfortable giving up if it means they become that much better on the line.
Outside the hashes and down the field, things have been dicey for the Browns this season.
While future Hall of Fame cornerback Denzel Ward has maintained his consistency , the likes of Tyson Campbell, Mekhi Blackmon and Toriano Pride Jr. have had their ups and downs.
To fully round out the unit, the Browns should consider adding in another body to balance out the productivity, especially considering the front office let Martin Emerson Jr. walk this past offseason.
The Colts, being in the spot they are now, could be looking to move Charvarius Ward, who is sitting on a $24 million cap hit for the rest of the season. Being a free agent in 2027, he is likely to walk, as the Colts usher in a new era.
For the Browns, pairing Ward with Ward and Campbell would be a perfect way to round-out the defensive back room.
The Browns have plenty of draft capital available, and if they threw a fourth- and sixth-round pick to Indianapolis, it should get the deal done. Just a few weeks back, the Dallas Cowboys sent a second- and fourth-round pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers for Joey Porter Jr.
Ward hasn't been able to replicate his successes from his days with the 49ers, but still possesses good intangibles.
At 6-foot-1, 196 pounds, he runs a 4.44 forty and owns an 11-foot broad jump.
The Browns may try to run with what they have on the roster right now, but if both Ward and Stewart are on the board still at the trade deadline, they should at least explore what the moves would require giving up.

title: How the Browns Run Game Can Find New Life Following Injury Bug
full_text:
Last Sunday, the Browns won their fifth game of the season over the Titans, something they did not accomplish until Week 18 of last season. Led by Deshaun Watson, who passed for over 300 yards for the first time in his Cleveland career, the Browns offense was firing on all cylinders.
In the pass game, it was rookie KC Concepcion who led the team with 129 receiving yards, Harold Fannin Jr. rumbled his way past 90 yards, and Dylan Sampson contributed nicely also. Those 300+ passing yards should not overshadow the best game that Cleveland has had rushing the ball all season, though.
With Quinshon Judkins and Sampson both back and healthy in the backfield, it completely changes the Cleveland offense.
Sampson missed the past five weeks with a knee injury he suffered in Week 1 vs. Jacksonville, but came back and contributed very nicely in his nine touches. He totaled 77 yards (45 rushing, 32 receiving) and was using his speed to get outside on runs and swing passes to glide upfield. To see Sampson on the field gives defenses a whole other piece of the offense to worry about with the young receivers and bowling ball of a tight end.
Judkins has been nagged with injuries throughout the season but came back healthier than ever on Sunday. He rushed for 96 yards on 17 carries and two touchdowns , but the best indicator he’s healthy was that he hit 21.01 miles per hour on a run, the fastest he's run all season. Those 96 yards were the second-highest mark Judkins has hit in a game in his young Cleveland career, and the retooled offensive line gave him a great chance on each play.
For reference, last season the Browns had the lowest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league at 0.59, as Cleveland backs were getting contacted almost immediately at the line. The team was also among the highest in the league in rushing yards after contact, which gives more credit to Judkins breaking tackles and fighting for extra yards.
In Week 7, though, those numbers were flipped, as Cleveland led the league in rushing yards per play with 6.3 and got 2.43 yards before being contacted by a Tennessee defender, the sixth-highest mark by a team in the week.
Cleveland got some big pops running behind the left side of that line, led by Spencer Fano , Zion Johnson, Elgton Jenkins, and Blake Whiteheart. With that o-line finding its footing and two healthy great options at back, the run game for the Browns could be turning a corner that will provide great balance to this offense.
Hi, I’m Paul, I’m from Northeast Ohio, and a recent graduate of Kent State University. As an Ohio native, I’m a huge fan of the Browns, Guardians, and Cavaliers. Just don’t ask me about my favorite college team, though.

title: Browns DT Room is Set, but the Edges Could Get a Boost With These 3 Trades
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have flipped the script on the season and could be looking to be buyers at the trade deadline to maintain their first-place standing in the AFC North. They could use offensive line help, but players like Quentin Nelson are not typically available at the deadline.
The Browns could use a bolster at defensive end, and there are several options that could be good fits.
The defensive line has been good as a whole, and they are second in the NFL with 20 sacks. However, an improvement at the defensive end position could make them even better. The current starters are Jared Verse and Isaiah McGuire.
Verse came in as a reigning Defensive Rookie of the Year, but he has had zero sacks this season. McGuire got his chance to start after an injury to Alex Wright, and he has performed solidly with three sacks.
The defensive end group is rounded out by Derek Barnett and Sam Williams, both acquired after roster cut downs due to the Wright injury. The Indianapolis Colts shipped off DeForest Buckner for a fourth-round pick, in which the Browns have three in 2027 . These defensive ends can help elevate the Browns’ strength to be even more dominant:
. @JFowlerESPN lists the Browns as a fit to trade for: - EDGE Khalil Mack - EDGE Jermaine Johnson - EDGE YaYa Diaby pic.twitter.com/Eau26cu7Ew
The former All-Pro has three sacks in six games this season . He is 35 years old and is in the last year of his contract. Mack is similar to Buckner, and at most, a fourth-round pick should be sufficient to land him.
The Browns’ defense has a lot of leaders on it, but they are inexperienced. Mack has seen everything an NFL offense can throw at him, and he can share his knowledge with the rest of the unit.
Johnson is on a lowly Titans team that should be selling off parts to get as much as draft capital as possible. He has three sacks and has played in every game this season. He is a free agent after the season and could be a nice depth piece to down the stretch.
He can be had for a late-round pick and maybe even a pick swap in the Browns' favor. He is only 27 years old, and if he puts together a solid last half of the season for the Browns, then they can re-sign him to a longer deal to stabilize the position.
The Buccaneers may be sellers, as their season has not played out the way they had hoped after extending Baker Mayfield. Diaby has three sacks for the Buccaneers this season and is 27 years old. Diaby was a third-round draft pick of the Buccaneers and has 22 career sacks.
Diaby is in the last year of his rookie contract, and like Johnson, if he is productive, then he can be eligible for an extension.
The Browns' defensive line has caused a lot of havoc in the backfield this season, but most of that pressure is coming from the interior. They could use some help on the outside to provide containment when a quarterback tries to escape.
The run defense has struggled this season when Grant Delpit or Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has not played close to the line of scrimmage. An addition of a run-stopping defensive end can free them up to play in coverage.
These players would not take much in return for a trade, and the Browns have plenty of ammunition to obtain their services. The young roster has arrived at least a year early, and they should consider a trade to help win the division this year .

title: Brian Schottenheimer Shares Reason for Excitement About Cowboys' Struggling Defense
full_text:
There really isn't much to be excited about when it comes to the Dallas Cowboys' 2026 defense.
Dallas enters Week 8 ranked dead-last against the run, 24th in points allowed per game and 20th in pass defense.
It's even hard to get excited after the Cowboys put together one of their best defensive performances in Week 7 , when they allowed 21 points to the Philadelphia Eagles, which was the Cowboys' second-fewest points allowed in a game this season.
That's because the Eagles weren't close to full strength . Philly did not have the services of quarterback Jalen Hurts or his top-two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, and Saquon Barkley wasn't healthy and was in and out of the game.
One thing the Cowboys do have going for them is the fact that their defense has gotten healthier in recent weeks, and will continue to do so in the weeks ahead.
And that has head coach Brian Schottenheimer excited for the outlook of his defense.
"You felt (DeMarvion Overshown) coming back, I thought that was great," Schotty said on 105.3 The Fan . "I think getting healthy is a big part of it."
"Overall, I think the health of this defense is what's getting us really excited," he added. "We're getting bodies back and that's huge for us."
Health has no doubt been a factor in the Cowboys' poor showing on defense in 2026, as the unit has been ravaged by injuries at almost every position.
While the edge rushers room has managed to stay healthy, Dallas has been missing players along the defensive line, at linebacker, cornerback and safety.
Jonathan Bullard has missed all but three games , but he was designated to return from injured reserve on Thursday, so he's coming back soon.
At linebacker, Overshown has missed a handful of games and Dee Winters is now hurt and is slated to miss his second game .
At cornerback, Cobie Durant has missed four contests and even new cornerback Joey Porter Jr. has been banged-up. Safety has been hampered by injuries, also, with Malik Hooker, Jalen Thompson and P.J. Locke all missing time.
Hooker has since returned, but Locke and Thompson are both on IR, although Locke is close after he had his 21-day practice window opened up last week.
At this point, the defense getting healthy is one of the last shreds of hope there is for this unit to improve moving forward. The other is a blockbuster trade for a game-changing edge rusher, but we know that's not something Dallas can depend on.
But even if the Cowboys can get back to full strength and acquire the edge rusher they need, there's still a coaching problem with defensive coordinator Christian Parker, and until that improves, Dallas' ceiling will remain low.

title: 7 Cowboys Who Could Be Traded Away if Dallas Becomes Seller at NFL Deadline
full_text:
All of the talk surrounding the Dallas Cowboys has been about the team making a move to add to its roster, and more specifically, to the defense.
It's not hard to see why. Jerry Jones has said time and time again he is open to making at least one more move , and Dallas could certainly use a marquee addition to its putrid defense.
But the Cowboys are also on the brink of Jones having to wonder if it's even worth it to try and save this team with another trade at the expense of shipping off another pick or more.
At 3-4, the Cowboys are very much in the thick of things in the NFC East, but the division also stinks and Dallas isn't anywhere near being able to compete for a Super Bowl, which is the real goal.
If the Cowboys were to lose both of their next two games and fall to 3-6, could they turn around and end up selling at the deadline? Not likely, but we can't rule it out, either.
If that happens, here's seven players who could get moved.
Pickens will be a free agent in 2027 and we remain highly skeptical about the Cowboys' chances of being able to retain him long term. Even Stephen Jones has said that will be difficult to do and, quite frankly, this year has once again taught us that having two great receivers means jack if the defense isn't good.
It also feels like the relationship is starting to deteriorate a bit after head coach Brian Schottenheimer called Pickens out for his poor run-blocking, and there have been effort concerns overall.
This might be the best time to sell Pickens because teams are more desperate at the trade deadline than they are during the offseason, when there are more options.
A team like the Kansas City Chiefs might be willing to pay a hefty price for a wide receiver like Pickens who would instantly be the No. 1 in Andy Reid's offense.
Ferguson has been a total disaster for the Cowboys this season. Not only has he been a terrible blocker, but the veteran tight end has struggled with drops and has even lost a crucial fumble.
He's currently in the midst of his worst season production-wise since his rookie campaign in 2022, and Brevyn Spann-Ford is getting a push as the new TE1 as a result of his struggles.
The Cowboys are surely regretting Ferguson's contract and could look to unload at least a portion of it on a team that needs a boost in the pass-catching department at tight end.
Dallas would get some much-needed future cap relief and a draft pick to replenish their dwindling stable.
Schoonmaker is on his way out of Dallas after this season after he was demoted to TE3 in favor of Brevyn Spann-Ford, who has now seemingly ascended to TE1 with Ferguson's struggles.
Schoonmaker isn't going to garner much, and perhaps as little as a late-round pick swap, but that's better than the nothing Dallas will get when he leaves in free agency in 2027.
We could see Schoonmaker getting traded even if Dallas doesn't wave the white flag on this season. Moving the veteran would also allow Dallas to open up snaps for rookie Michael Trigg.
We had Hooker pegged as a player who could be moved either via cut or trade before the season started after Dallas made several additions to the safeties room this past offseason.
However, Hooker managed to stick and has actually found himself in a key role after P.J. Locke and Jalen Thompson both landed on injured reserve.
We still find it hard to believe that Hooker's relationship with Dallas will extend beyond 2026, so trading him away is a logical move.
Not only is Overshown going to be a free agent in 2027, he is also repped by David Mulugheta and after the Micah Parsons fiasco, we don't need to tell you why that decreases Overshown's chances of re-signing in Dallas.
And, truth be told, the Cowboys shouldn't be interested in bringing him back anyway. Overshown needed to shed the injury-prone label in 2026, but he has already missed a handful of games .
Of all the players who could conceivably be traded away by Dallas at the deadline, Overshown is the one who could net the second-best return after Pickens.
Jones was brought in to compete with Terence Steele at right tackle, but Steele has been good enough to hold on to the job, leaving Jones in a backup role that has allowed him to see the playing field for 21 snaps, with 11 of those coming as an extra blocker.
The trade that saw the Cowboys give up a 2027 third-rounder and a 2027 sixth-round pick in exchange for Jones and a 2027 fourth-rounder is not looking too hot right now, to say the least.
With teams always in the market for more offensive line help, it's possible Dallas could find a suitor for Jones to regain the late-round pick the team gave up as part of the trade.
The overwhelming excite for Miller's homecoming has turned into total disgust after what has been a disastrous tenure over seven games.
Miller has not so much as tallied a single sack and has fallen well short of expectations, even for a 37-year-old edge rusher. If this continues, not only could Miller leave after this season, he may retire.
An over-the-hill edge rusher with zero sacks doesn't exactly sound attractive, but we know Miller plays a premium position, so he may still draw interest. At this point, getting a late Day 3 pick for Miller would amount to a massive win for the Cowboys.

title: 3 Bold Predictions for Cowboys vs Cardinals in Week 8
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys look to do something on Sunday that they haven't done all year and win a second consecutive game. They knocked off the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7 and while the Eagles were banged up, it was a still a confidence-building win for a team that needed something positive to build on.
This weekend, they face a struggling Cardinals team that is 2-1, but has lost five of their past six games. It's a golden opportunity for the Cowboys to get back into the NFC East race , but they have to face their demons to get the win.
Dallas has lost eight of their past nine games against Arizona , including a Monday Night Football showdown last year. Turning their luck around becomes far more likely if these three bold predictions come true.
The Cowboys finally stuck with the run in Week 7 and Javonte Williams rewarded them with 155 yards. This week, look for him to continue to get the ball, especially against the Cardinals who are 23rd in the league against the run .
Williams looked like the player we saw in 2025 and that should continue, especially with offensive coordinator Klayton Adams facing his previous team this week. In this first bold prediction, Williams goes for 125 yards and rushes another touchdown.
DeMarvion Overshown made his much anticipated return to action in Week 7 and he was excellent. He had six tackles, one tackle for loss, batted down one pass, and hauled in an interception. Now that he has a full game under his belt for the first time this season, look for Overshown to continnue to shine. His presence helps as the Cowboys defense puts the pressure on Jacoby Brissett and forces two turnovers, one of which comes courtesy of Overshown.
Dak Prescott went into Week 7 facing a bit of a slump. He had just two touchdowns and four interceptions over the previous two games, both of which were losses for Dallas. He responded well in Week 7, throwing for 212 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions.
There were still some areas to clean up, specifically with his accuracy. Prescott completed just 55.6 percent of his attempts, which is below his season average of 65.2 percent . title: DeMarvion Overshown Believes Dallas Cowboys Poised To Break 30-Year Curse
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys got off to a slow start to the 2026-27 NFL season, but the team now finds itself with an opportunity to string together a winning streak as we enter November.
Dallas is preparing to host the Arizona Cardinals at AT&T Stadium in Week 8, before making a trip to face the struggling Indianapolis Colts in Week 9 . If all goes well for the Cowboys, the team could find itself riding a three-game winning streak entering the NFL trade deadline .
That would position the team to make a move to improve the roster, and potentailly set Dallas up for a postseason run.
With the defense getting healthy in a wide-open NFC East, star linebacker DeMarvion Overshown appears confident that the team will be able to overcome its past demons and end the dreaded 30-year NFC Championship and Super Bowl drought.
Overshown, who made a splash in his return to the field during Monday night's win over the division rival Philadelphia Eagles , recently stopped by The White House podcast to chat it up with Cowboys legend Michael Irvin, where he shared his confidence with "The Playmaker."
DeMarvion Overshown says the Dallas Cowboys will make the NFC Championship 👀 pic.twitter.com/yXWBm9Btj8
"How real is that goal this year of winning a championship? Now, D-Mo, you know, listen, I see your beautiful long hair that you got on your head," Irvin joked while asking about the title aspirations.
"I got my beautiful long hair. I want to keep it. And I need y'all to get to a championship game in order for me to keep it. And should I say goodbye to my locks or can I hold on to them?"
Overshown responded, "Hold on to them, big bro. I'm telling you, I'm telling you right now, like, we got it. We already done laid it out.We done laid out the format. We was like, f*ck, we ain't start off good, but we looking at our division like, sh*t, we got them. We can take this. And it's at the point, man, we going to get in however we get in. Overshown tweaked his hamstring in the season-opening loss to the New York Giants, but made a triumphant return in Week 7. Overshown came through with a team-high six total tackles, two passes defensed, one tackle for a loss, and a crucial interception.

title: Cowboys' CeeDee Lamb Hoping To Break Shocking Cardinals Curse in Week 8
full_text:
Despite how sloppy things have been this season, the Dallas Cowboys still have a solid chance at winning the NFC East and hosting a playoff game.
The team took a positive step in that direction on Monday. After picking up a much-needed win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7, the Cowboys now turn their attention to the Arizona Cardinals.
That sentence alone should make Cowboys fans shiver.
Dallas has lost four straight games to Arizona dating back to 2020, three of which have come at AT&T Stadium.
Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb has been apart of all four matchups. He has yet to beat the Cardinals in his NFL career and knows exactly what's gone wrong for Dallas.
Lamb met with reporters on Thursday and admitted that Arizona has come out with better energy and that the Cowboys have been "very relaxed."
"Yeah, it's just crazy," Lamb said, per the team website. "[We were] being very, very relaxed, and they punched us in the mouth every single time. They've always had more energy. They were more excited, regardless of if it was a 12 o'clock, Sunday night or Monday night.
“I've never beat the Cardinals since I've been in the league, so that's kind of fair to say,” Lamb said. “I wouldn't say heightened focus, but it's definitely another take.”
In the NFL, it's never smart to take any opponent lightly, and Dallas has learned the hard way. Hopefully the Cowboys have learned their lesson, and similar results won't repeat themselves on Sunday.
“They've always had more energy,” Lamb said, per ESPN's Todd Archer. “Just coming out in the game, they're more excited regardless of if it was at 12 o'clock, Sunday night, Monday night. We played them in primetime, they beat us there. So just coming in, treating them as if they are a Super Bowl contending team, which they may be, you know what I'm saying? So hats off to them in their prep and we just got to go match them, if not overpower them.”
Lamb is currently second in the NFL in receiving yards (651) and will look to use hot start to the season as the spark that Dallas needs in order to end its dreadful curse against the Cardinals.

title: Ranking Dallas Cowboys' Biggest NFL Trade Deadline Needs With Under 2 Weeks to Go
full_text:
We are now under two weeks away from the NFL trade deadline and the Dallas Cowboys are widely viewed as a team that could make a move.
That's because owner Jerry Jones has continuously said he is very open to doing more to improve the defense, even if he isn't optimistic he'll actually be able to get something done.
"If we could do it where we sit right now, I would add to it," Jones said on 105.3 The Fan (H/T Tommy Yarrish of DallasCowboys.com ). "But the adding to it is a big statement. It's unlikely we'll get the opportunity from outside coming in. But if it's there, I'll do it."
Another reason is because the Cowboys' defense flat-out stinks and it seems like the only hope to get that unit out of the mud is to inject more talent into it, although we've seen that hasn't worked out thus far after Dallas' offseason overhaul .
But, as we know, that isn't likely to stop Jerry from trying.
With all of that in mind, here's a look at four position groups the Cowboys could look to add to, ranked from least to most dire.
The only concern here is injuries, as the Cowboys have seen two of their offseason acquisitions, P.J. Locke and Jalen Thompson, land on injured reserve over the first half of the season.
If injury issues continue, the Cowboys will need to make a move. If not, a group with Locke, Thompson, Malik Hooker, Caleb Downs, Alijah Clark and Markquese Bell is sufficient.
The Cowboys are probably OK here if everyone stays healthy, but that has proven to be a problem this season because DeMarvion Overshown is injury-prone and has missed five games and Dee Winters is now hurt , also.
Another reason the Cowboys might want to explore adding at the linebacker position is it would help free up Jaishawn Barham for more snaps on the edge, where Dallas desperately needs more production.
There has been a combination of issues at cornerback that should have the Cowboys at least looking at their options on the open market.
While Joey Porter Jr. has been everything the Cowboys could have hoped for, the other boundary spot has been a mess.
Not only has Cobie Durant missed a handful of games due to injury, but DaRon Bland has played like one of the worst at his position in the NFL. Hopefully Durant can step in and shore up Dallas' other boundary spot, but that isn't guaranteed and the Cowboys seem intent on continuing to deploy Bland, likely because of what they're paying him.
If Bland continues to stink and Bland, Shavon Revel and Ameer Speed can't step up, a starting-caliber player will be needed. At the very least, Dallas could use more depth because it is one Porter injury away from disaster.
This is the biggest problem the Cowboys have on defense.
Despite the additions of Rashan Gary, Malachi Lawrence and Von Miller during the offseason, the Cowboys have gotten just 3.5 sacks from the group over seven games.
Miller has zero and Gary and Lawrence have one apiece while Donovan Ezeiruaku leads the group with 1.5.
One of the best ways to cover for the lackluster coverage the Cowboys have seen from is to improve the pass-rush off the edge.
If there's one position Jerry Jones should break the bank for, it's this one.

title: Broncos' Trade Interest in Jonathan Taylor is Real, Insider Claims
full_text:
Despite the return of rookie running back Jonah Coleman, the Denver Broncos are keeping one eye on the NFL trade market 11 days ahead of the deadline.
The Indianapolis Colts' fire sale is on; they've already dealt away All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and Pro Bowl defensive lineman DeForest Buckner. All eyes are now on star running back Jonathan Taylor, including those of the Broncos, according to NFL On Prime insider James Palmer.
"They are one of the teams, I'm told, that is monitoring the Jonathan Taylor situation. It's more than likely he stays there in Indianapolis, but they are keeping an eye there," Palmer said of the Broncos .
This isn't the first we've heard of a Broncos-Taylor connection. Before last week's game against the Arizona Cardinals, Adam Schefter linked the Broncos to Indy's Pro Bowl running back.
Entering Week 8's rematch with the Chiefs, the Broncos' run game ranks 24th in the NFL, averagin 94.9 yards per game. The Broncos believe their rushing struggles are largely attributed to the tough slate of elite defenses they faced through the first six weeks of the season, including top running back J.K. Dobbins.
There could be some truth to that, as the Broncos' ground attack finally showed some signs of life last week against the Arizona Cardinals, whose defense is not ranked high. However, there was a big outlier play in Bo Nix's 62-yard touchdown run.
Corresponding to Denver's improved rushing efficiency last week as the return of Coleman from injured reserve. He led the team in rushing and snaps , averaging 6.0 yards per carry on nine totes. Dobbins took a back seat to the rookie last week, but the veteran assured reporters on Thursday that he's not upset or dissatisfied with his current role, and cares only about winning.
Coleman certainly added a different energy and burst to the Broncos' offense, and it's likely the front office will be watching to see if the rookie and Dobbins can show some more signs of life between now and November 10 before making a decision on potentially pursuing a trade.
Sean Payton has always implemented a running-back-by-committee approach, and even though the Broncos just paid Dobbins, it's still been a rotation. If you trade for Taylor, though, you're wanting to keep him on the field and get your money's worth, but then again, putting him at the top of a committee, with the lion's share of the touches, could help preserve his health and extend his career.
Taylor would be costly, not only to acquire from the Colts, but he just signed a two-year, $44 million extension before the season started. He has a $16.1 million cap number this season. However, his cap numbers climb to $21 million and $22.98 million in 2027 and 2028, respectively.
The Broncos have a couple years left of cost control on Nix, even if they opt to sign him to an extension next offseason when he becomes eligible, so if they team was of a mind to go all-in, it could find room for Taylor. It really would come down to whether the Broncos believed Taylor would be the missing piece to put them over the top.
The three-time Pro Bowler and former NFL rushing champion is a great player, and if there's anything that coud hold back the Broncos from achieving their goals this season, it would be their bottom-10 rushing attack. Taylor would upgrade that immediately, and give Nix a proven foundation to build on.
Taylor and Dobbins are roughly the same age (27). Both will turn 28 in the not too distant future, so the Broncos would have to factor in his age and the high amount of wear-and-tear on Taylor's tires.
As we're seeing around the league, the contenders are swinging for the fences ahead of the deadline. The Chicago Bears gave up multiple first-round picks for Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, while the Seattle Seahawks just landed Nelson, and the San Francisco 49ers acquired Buckner.
The Broncos plan to be contenders now and in the future, but if they really want to capitalize on what remains of Nix's rookie contract, a big move like trading for Taylor would make sense. But it would be contingent on how the next two games unfold for Dobbins and Coleman.
If it's more rushing inconsistencies, it wouldn't shock me to see the Broncos swing for the fences on Taylor. The Broncos have two games between now and the deadline — the Chiefs this week and the Carolina Panthers next — but depending on the market for Taylor, they may not have the luxury of waiting until after Week 9 to make a decision.
That's why the Broncos are, ostensibly, monitoring the Taylor situation. Stay tuned.

title: 3 Keys to a Broncos Revenge Win Over Chiefs in Week 8
full_text:
Denver Broncos fans would like to forget the season opener at Arrowhead Stadium, when the Kansas City Chiefs dominated for almost the entire game. Aside from the Broncos getting an early touchdown, there wasn't much positive about their play.
Since then, the Broncos have gotten better, though they still have areas to clean up, particularly on offense. They may not enter this Week 8 matchup with their starting lineup fully intact, though, with several players limited in practice this week .
However, the Broncos still have a chance to win their rematch with the Chiefs if they can do a better overall job of execution. The Chiefs, to their credit, have played well since Week 1, aside from a bad outing against the Seattle Seahawks last week, but they aren't a juggernaut by any means.
Still, the Broncos have to make sure that things don't go down as they did in Week 1 if they want to win this game. Let's break down three keys to winning the rematch with the Chiefs, all harkening back to Week 1 when these teams first met.
One of the top reasons the Broncos lost the season opener was that the defense had no answer for the Chiefs' most notable free-agent signing of 2026. Walker, coming off a Super Bowl MVP award, immediately made an impact, and it came at the Broncos' expense.
Walker rushed for 173  yards on 23 carries with one rushing touchdown. If you take away his longest run of 60 yards, he still made a clear impact with 113 yards rushing on the other 22 carries. He also had three catches for 18 yards and a touchdown.
While Walker is not the only player the Broncos need to be concerned about, the fact is that the defense's inability to limit him was a big reason for the season-opening loss. When Walker was able to dictate the game, the Broncos' pass rush was effectively neutralized, and it mattered not who was protecting Patrick Mahomes, whose offensive line has dealt with injury issues this season.
Part of the reason Walker dominated was that the Broncos missed too many tackles or took bad angles when defending the run. They have cleaned that up in recent weeks, but they still need to be disciplined and avoid those mistakes if they want to contain him.
If the Broncos can bottle up Walker, the Chiefs will have to pass more often, and that would give the pass rush the chance to do more damage. It won't be an easy task, as Mahomes has taken just seven sacks in seven games, but the opportunities for the Broncos' pass rush will increase if the Chiefs can't get the running game going.
It's worth noting that Travis Kelce had a 59-yard gain on a reception in Week 1, but that again goes back to the lack of discipline by the Broncos' defense. However, Kelce was otherwise quiet. Thus, while Kelce can still do good things, Walker is the player the Broncos need to focus on containing to have a chance against the Chiefs' offense.
The Broncos had two players in Week 1 who didn't get any touches on offense. Both players are coming off good performances against the Arizona Cardinals last week.
The first is Coleman, who got just 6% of the offensive snaps in Week 1 and was otherwise limited to special teams. The coaching staff relied on J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey, with the former held to 36 yards on eight carries and the latter getting just three carries for 18 yards, along with four receptions for 23 yards.
Dobbins hasn't been effective since then, but Harvey has shown he can make an impact. In the meantime, Coleman has proven he should have a bigger role in the offense, particularly after rushing for 54 yards on nine carries against the Cardinals.
The Broncos need to get Coleman more involved in the offense this week. His ankle didn't appear to be bothering him last week, and his presence could do a lot to take some pressure off Bo Nix if he can be the spark in the running game.
Mims was limited in the season opener as he was recovering from a foot injury suffered in the preseason. Now, though, Mims may be poised for an increased role as Jaylen Waddle's Week 8 availability is in question due to a chest injury.
Even if Waddle is cleared to play, his snaps may be limited. That means Mims could be in line for more snaps on offense. The fourth-year receiver has shown he can still contribute on offense, as he had two catches for 53 yards last week, including a 47-yard reception that showed Nix is perfectly capable of attacking downfield.
Coleman and Mims in the mix gives the Broncos more options on offense and that could be an important step to an improved offensive showing — as could the next person we'll mention.
While not everything that happened on offense in the opener was Nix's fault, he didn't look confident. After doing all right on the Broncos' only touchdown drive, he was hesitant to take shots, regardless of the situation, and demonstrated poor pocket presence.
It led to Nix being sacked three times — the most sacks the Chiefs have had in a single game this season. In fact, the Chiefs have seven sacks on the season, so while they can get after the quarterback, they aren't doing so at a high rate.
The Broncos need to give the respect due to Chris Jones, Nick Bolton, and George Karlaftis, but one way to counter what they can do in the pass rush is for Nix to play with more confidence, as he showed against the Cardinals.
The Chiefs have given up an average of 212 yards passing to opposing offenses, so while their pass defense is effective, it's not dominant. They gave up 365 yards passing to Kirk Cousins and 257 yards passing to Sam Darnold, and neither ranks among the top quarterbacks in the NFL.
If Nix plays with confidence, he should do better than the 131 passing yards he had in Week 1, especially at home. It may be asking too much to pass for 350 yards, but if he can get 225 yards or more, that could be enough if the run game comes through and the defense does its job.
All Nix has to do is be willing and ready to take shots downfield when the opportunity is there. The Chiefs' defense does deserve respect, but it's not the dominant unit it looked like in the season opener.
The Chiefs have shown they are a legitimate playoff contender, and one shouldn't read too much into their game last week against the Seahawks. However, one also shouldn't read too much into the Week 1 matchup between the Broncos and Chiefs.
The Broncos have shown they are a better defensive team than they were in Week 1, and they are starting to figure things out on offense. Now it's time for the Broncos to prove that the season opener is long behind them and that they can get it done against a top AFC team and their strongest divisional rival.
Playing at home will help, but so will sharper defensive play, a confident QB under center, and contributions from players who saw little to no action in Week 1. And if the Broncos get the win, they will improve their odds when it comes to the playoffs, the AFC West title, and a high seed.

title: Broncos' Injury Concerns Grow as Two More Key Players Surface
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are gearing up for their Week 8 rematch with the Kansas City Chiefs . If the Broncos are going to avenge their ugly 31-10 loss in the season opener, they’ll need a little luck on the health front.
Three starters were held out of Wednesday’s practice , but things changed on Thursday, with two of those players participating in a limited role. That’s the good news; the bad news is that two new names popped up on the injury report.
Let’s take a look at Thursday’s practice report.
Harvey and Jones popping up on the injury report is concerning, especially after they were unlisted on Wednesday. Both were limited, though, so there’s no reason to fear for their Week 8 availability quite yet.
If Harvey is compromised this week, at least the Broncos have Jonah Coleman back. Coleman can pound the rock and doesn’t have to leave the field on third down because of his receiving and pass-protecting proficiency. Plus, J.K. Dobbins is more than capable of doing it all, too. Let’s hope it doesn’t come to that.
With Hufanga still not participating in practice, it’s not looking great for him this week. Friday will be the ultimate decider, but that’s why the Broncos really need Jones to take it easy on his hamstring. The thought of going against Patrick Mahomes without either of your starting safeties is enough to make any team sweat a bit.
Devon Key is healthy, and Taylor Rapp has done well in playing starter snaps since Hufanga got hurt, but the Broncos would much rather have their starters against Kansas City, or at least one of them. Jones is midway through what has easily been his best as a Bronco since joining the team in 2024.
Meanwhile, it’s great to see Allen and Waddle progress to limited on Thursday after being held out of Wednesday’s session. Both starters went down late in last week’s win over the Arizona Cardinals. Hopefully, there’s enough time for them to heal up in time for this massive Chiefs game.
Surtain remains fully on pace to return to the field this week. And the timing couldn’t be better, given the importance of this game.
If the Broncos beat the Chiefs at Mile High, they’ll take the lead in the AFC West. Dener’s road ahead is significantly easier than Kansas City’s.
The Broncos have a few toughies left on the schedule beyond Week 8, but the Chiefs still have to face the San Francisco 49ers, Los Angeles Rams, Buffalo Bills, and New England Patriots. With a win, the Broncos could have the chance to really pull away in their quest to defend their division crown and repeat as AFC West champions.

title: Courtland Sutton Rejects 'Fluke' Narrative Ahead of Broncos-Chiefs Rematch
full_text:
Few people saw the Denver Broncos' 14-win campaign coming in 2025.
Yeah, the Broncos won 10 games the year prior with a rookie Bo Nix, and made the playoffs as a wildcard team, but they were quickly eliminated from the tournament by the Buffalo Bills in Upstate New York . At that point, though, just making the playoffs was a triumph, after Denver had gone eight straight years without qualifying for the postseason.
The Broncos knew that if they were going to truly become a force to be reckoned with in the conference, they'd have to knock the Kansas City Chiefs off their eight-year perch as AFC West champions. That meant the Broncos had to take care of their own business and when they went head-to-head with the Chiefs, they had to prevail.
And prevail Denver did, sweeping the Chiefs for the first time in more than a decade. Patrick Mahomes suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 15, but Chiefs had already been eliminated from the playoffs. Several weeks before, the Broncos beat a desperate Mahomes-led Chiefs team at Mile High, signaling a changing of the guard.
The Broncos would finish the season 14-3, profitting greatly from an 11-game winning streak. Denver unseated the Chiefs as AFC West champions and earned the No. 1 playoff seed in the AFC, and even exacted some revenge on the Bills in an epic 33-30 overtime win in the divisional round.
We all know how the 2025 season came crashing to a quick and brutal end with Nix's ankle injury. But fast forward to 2026, and the Chiefs are back, sitting at 5-1 going into Week 8.
Meanwhile, the Broncos are 5-2 with the chance to pull away as division leaders if they can vanquish the Chiefs at home on Sunday . Some fans hoped that Kansas City's unraveling last year was a sign that the worm had turned, and that the Andy Reid dynasty was over, but Broncos wide receiver Courtland Sutton knew the Chiefs' identity was still intact.
"Honestly, they're just a really good team, well coached," Sutton said on Wednesday. "They've got a lot of talent over there. The things that they did for such a long time, that identity is still there."
At the same time, the Broncos have forged their own identity. Since Sean Payton arrived as head coach, the tide has turned against the Chiefs.
Payton snapped Kansas City's 16-game winning streak over the Broncos in 2023 with Russell Wilson as his quarterback. In 2024, the Nix-led Broncos split with Kansas City and nearly swept them, were it not for a freak blocked field-goal attempt at the end of regulation at Arrowhead Stadium.
Last year was it's own thing, with the Broncos not only sweeping their long-time division rival, but the Chiefs also missing the playoffs for the first time in the Mahomes era and only the second time since Reid became head coach. Like two ships in the night, as the Chiefs were going one way last year, the Broncos were headed the other direction, and along the way, a winning identity of their own took shape in the Mile High City.
"We know that we have put together a really good team over the past few years, and for us to get to the top of that mountain last year, we understood that we had to knock off who was already up there, and they were the team that were up there," Sutton said.
The Broncos won the AFC West crown in 2025, but according to Sutton, that hasn't changed their mindset as a underdogs. In the Broncos' quest to repeat as division champs, the Pro Bowl receiver doesn't feel like the NFL world is giving them the respect they deserve.
"For us to get that reign last year, I wouldn't say that it's changed our philosophy. I think that we have the right mindset of, 'Hey, yes, we may have won the division last year, but there still doesn't feel as if there's this respect of the Broncos are a really good football team,'" Sutton said. "I think people still think that we rode off a high and there was this fluke of what happened last year."
During the 2026 offseason, the talking points on the Broncos shifted dramatically around the NFL. They were viewed as a bona fide contender, and often ranked as one of the most talented teams in the league.
However, amid Nix's early-season slump and the offense's failure to launch, the NFL world quickly started selling their stock on the Broncos and seemingly writing them off. While it's true that the Broncos have fielded a championship-caliber offense yet, it's important to remember just how tough their initial six-game schedule was, with games against the Chiefs, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Rams, San Francisco 49ers, Los Angeles Chargers, and Seattle Seahawks.
Nix and the offense didn't play consistently well, but Denver kept winning. The Broncos weathered that gauntlet at 4-2 — which was about as well as anyone expected — and after beating the Arizona Cardinals on the road last week, they're now sitting at 5-2 with the chance to get even with the Chiefs and pull ahead in the division.
"So for us, it's, 'Hey, we've got to show up each week and go show everybody and prove to ourselves that we are who we say we are at the end of the day, and that last year wasn't a fluke. It wasn't just a flash in the dark,'" Sutton said.
The Broncos haven't lost to the Chiefs at home since Payton became the head coach. And while people may still be doubting the Broncos, Sutton and company are focused on standing their ground at home, and sending the message that last year's AFC West title wasn't an anomoly.
"It's one of those things that we have to go stand up and stand on ten toes that we are who we say we are, week in and week out," Sutton said. "And this weekend it's against the Chiefs, a divisional game."
For the first time since Nix came to town, the Broncos were blown out by the Chiefs in Week 1. That 31-10 loss stung , not only because it came at the hands of the Chiefs, but also because it was under the bright primetime lights of Monday Night Football .
The Broncos are fully aware of their failure to launch in that game, and it sounds like they're relishing the opportunity to balance the scales in their Week 8 rematch with the Chiefs.
"I know that we have the character and the fight in that locker room to go out there and perform how we want to perform," Sutton said. "We know that we didn't like how we performed last time, but with it being a divisional game, we know that we've got to show up."
Suffice it to say, this iteration of Broncos-Chiefs is going to be a heavyweight bout. The Broncos have a lot to play for, including the division lead, while the Chiefs are coming off their first and only loss of the season.
Mahomes is undefeated against the Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium, and you know he'd love to get back in the win column at Mile High for the first time since 2022, and really signal to Chiefs fans and the NFL that Kansas City is back in the AFC West driver's seat.
Nix is a different quarterback at home. He was out of sorts in that ugly Week 1 loss, but a lot of water has passed under the bridge since then, and his confidence surrounding his ankle recovery is at a season-high after romping for a 62-yard touchdown last week and connecting on several explosive passing plays.
Week 8's action is going to be an epic AFC West throwdown.
