title: Broncos Have 2 Matchup Problems They Must Solve vs. Chiefs
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have a chance to take the top spot in the division if they can beat the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday. The Seattle Seahawks opened the door by beating the Chiefs last week.
The Broncos would also benefit from the schedule, since the Chiefs already had their bye week and still have most of their toughest opponents left on the docket. The Broncos' bye comes in Week 10, so a win on Sunday would put them at 6-2 and the Chiefs at 5-2.
After that Week 1 debacle, the Broncos won't be overlooking the Chiefs, as they may have in the season opener. The Broncos have to focus on winning some key matchups that deal more with their own issues than with what the Chiefs are doing.
With that said, let’s get into the two key matchups of Week 8.
Last week, Nix vs. himself was also a key matchup , but for a different reason. Going into Arizona, it was about him regaining his confidence, which he did with a 62-yard touchdown run, a 52-yard screen-pass touchdown, and several other explosive plays .
This week, it's about finding the consistency and balance Nix hasn’t shown this season.
He still has issues with his ball placement and pocket presence, and they may never fully resolve this season. In fact, it may be part of who Nix is, which isn't exactly the picture of consistency and balance.
That's where Bo's aggressiveness comes into play. He must spread the ball around better than he has, take what the defense gives him, and take calculated risks. This isn’t to say he should go out there and be a gunslinger, but when he sees the opening deep, he should take the shot, like he did last week.
Denver can’t have Nix fall back into the shell he was in for Weeks 4-6, though Week 6 was as much due to the Seahawks' defense as it was his mental state when it came to pushing the ball. The Chiefs rank 21st in explosive pass-play rate allowed and 28th in the last four games, so Nix has no excuse if he crawls back into his shell.
Bo needs to find consistency in being aggressive, both as a runner and as a passer, as well as start carrying one strong game into another, though it could still look very different in the box score. His balance has to come from spreading the ball around more and not favoring one or two receivers, which he did improve on against the Cardinals, while still hunting for explosives without being careless and taking what the defense gives him.
This was an easy one. No player-on-player matchup is more important than the Broncos' collective tackling of Walker.
In Week 1, Denver's missed-tackle rate was 29.8% , up 25% from its historically bad 70-point game against the Miami Dolphins in 2023. Most Broncos fans didn't think defense could ever get worse than that woeful day in Miami.
On top of that, the Broncos allowed 247 yards after missed tackles, with Walker having 108 yards after contact, or 4.7 yards after contact per rush.
If the Broncos want a chance in this one, they can’t let Walker run all over them. That is stating the obvious, but Denver’s defense has done well in shutting down or limiting Patrick Mahomes, especially at Mile High, so allowing Walker to carry the Chiefs would make it much harder to walk out with the win.
Denver’s defense has also allowed a high rate of explosive runs, including over the last four games, which is alarming, since those four games don't count Walker's big Week 1 showing. The Broncos have had serious consistency issues stopping the run, and it stems from more than just bad tackling.
This game is about more than the AFC West standings; Denver's pride is also on the line. It's gut-check time for Vance Joseph's defense.

title: Broncos' First Week 8 Injury Report: Updates on Surtain, Hufanga & Waddle
full_text:
The Denver Broncos released their initial Week 8 injury report ahead of Sunday's pivotal home showdown against the Kansas City Chiefs.
Denver listed wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest), safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), and defensive end Zach Allen (hip) — all starters — as "DNP" (Did Not Practice) following Wednesday's session.
An earlier report indicated that Waddle suffered a re-aggravation of a prior chest issue toward the end of last week's victory over the Arizona Cardinals, and his status for Sunday's game is to be determined.
The injury occurred on a trick play that head coach and offensive playcaller Sean Payton consequently apologized for.
"Why didn't anybody ask me about the dumb reverse call? ... It was awful. I'm sorry," Payton said in his postgame press conference on Sunday. "If you look it up, in 2008, in a similar situation — even a more radical reverse — fumbled, Tampa Bay beat us. I know better. Every once in a while you fall in love with a play."
Hufanga remains on the wrong side of questionable after missing the last two games due to an ankle injury. The former AFC Defensive Player of the Week will need to get in at least limited practices on Thursday and Friday to have a shot at suiting up versus Kansas City.
Allen's apparently hamstring ailment is a new development, though one that, as of this writing, seems unlikely to hold him out of Week 8 action.
Elsewhere on the injury report, left tackle Garett Bolles (hip) and wide receiver Marvin Mims (ankle) were considered limited, while cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle), defensive tackle Malcolm Roach (neck), and inside linebacker Karene Reid (elbow) were full participants.
Surtain appears poised to return from a three-game absence as his ankle presumably is at or near full health.
Of note on the Chiefs' end, cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (personal/knee) did not practice on Wednesday while receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) was limited, and quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee) and tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) were full goes.
In the event that Waddle is inactive on Sunday, the Broncos would be down to Courtland Sutton, Marvin Mims, and Troy Franklin as its primary wideouts, with Pat Bryant (ankle) still on short-term injured reserve.
Although, in this case, some (more) of the receiving work could be spilled onto running back RJ Harvey's plate, the Broncos may take the opportunity to get the ball in the hands of Mims, which Payton has repeatedly insisted remains a priority on his offensive totem pole.
“I think to his credit, whenever we ask something of him—whether it’s intermediate, down the field—he’s been really effective," he said of Mims on Wednesday. "Obviously as a returner, that first return with the ball midfield, those are... I’ve said this before, the receiving now to start the game. [At] minimum there’s a threshold, but to start where we started, those are things that he’s shown us consistently. He continues to have those touches and then where you want to even get him more touches. It’s sometimes a challenge, but certainly he’s deserving.”

title: Broncos' Most Surprising Trade Candidate Is Hiding in Plain Sight
full_text:
J.K. Dobbins doesn't seem happy at the moment.
The Denver Broncos' veteran running back received a season-low 14 snaps in Week 7's 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals. With rookie Jonah Coleman returning from injured reserve, Dobbins took a back seat in the desert, both in snap and touch share.
The Broncos' offense looked different with Coleman on the field , and his versatility as a receiver and as a pass protector gives Sean Payton so much more to work with. When Coleman is on the field, opponents can't be sure whether it's a run or a pass coming, while with Dobbins and RJ Harvey, defenses can play the probabilities more accurately.
In the NFL, it's good not to be predictable. The Broncos have to make the tough decision to continue ceding snaps and touches in Coleman's favor if they have any hope of digging out of being a bottom-10 rushing offense.
Dobbins doesn't appear to be taking this development well, and if he's unable to get his mind right, the Broncos could suddenly become amenable to trading him away . Several teams have serious running back issues right now — including the New York Giants, who've already orchestrated a big trade (quarterback J.J. McCarthy).
The Giants would also make a lot of sense because of head coach John Harbaugh's ties to Dobbins from their time together in Baltimore. Harbaugh drafted Dobbins in the second round back in 2020.
There are other teams in need of some running back help, including the Minnesota Vikings, Green Bay Packers, and maybe even the Carolina Panthers. Dobbins has a long injury history, and while he was dinged up early this season, he's yet to miss a game.
The one fly in the ointment of a potential Dobbins trade is his contract. The Broncos just re-signed him to a two-year, $16 million deal, but only the first year was guaranteed.
That's good and bad. It's good in that a team acquiring him via trade wouldn't necessarily be locked to Dobbins beyond 2026, unless he were to arrive and hit it out of the park.
The bad? A lot of the money gets funneled into Dobbins's 2027 contract. He goes from a $6 million cap number this year to $10 million next year, with a $7 million base salary. That's a solid deal for a mid-level No. 1 running back, but for a second guy in a rotation, it would be a drastic overpay.
Now, it's helpful that nearly half of the 2026 season is over, so the Broncos have already absorbed a good chunk of his contract, and they've already paid out his $4 million signing bonus. That simplifies things somewhat for an interested suitor that's mostly concerned with running back help this season, and less worried about 2027.
With Tyler Badie on injured reserve for three more games, the Broncos would have to really be blown away by an offer to trade Dobbins. They do have Cody Schrader on the practice squad, so if a team made the Broncos an offer they couldn't refuse, there's an immediate running back available to use on game day.
The Broncos love Dobbins. Payton values Dobbins and has given the veteran back a lot of credit for the Broncos' sudden rise in confidence and swagger last year.
Payton's appreciation of Dobbins was reflected last week against the Cardinals. On a drive in which Coleman did the heavy lifting as a runner, moving the chains on two of his three carries, Payton gave the Broncos' only goal-line carry to Dobbins, which he punched in.
However, instead of jumping up and celebrating with his teammates, Dobbins ran straight back to the Broncos' sideline and sat down on the bench. Following the game, he purportedly didn't make himself available to reporters in the locker room, further showing his frustration.
Payton is big on body language. As a leader that guys in that locker room look to, if Dobbins isn't able to get his mind right and frustration continues to show through his body language, the situation could devolve ahead of the November 10 deadline.
But I give Dobbins more credit than that. His disappointment in being rendered second fiddle last week is understandable, but I'd be surprised if we don't see a more chipper energy on Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs. Character has never been a concern with Dobbins.
Iron sharpens iron, after all, so if Dobbins doesn't want to be the No. 2 running back, it's up to him to prove it on the field. And the Broncos will give him that opportunity, provided he gets his vibe back on point.
I doubt the Broncos trade Dobbins. However, he has become as surprise player to watch, given Coleman's rise, Dobbins's antics last week, and the growing need at running back several teams have ahead of the deadline.
Dobbins is an experienced back, and he's healthy. I could see a needy team calling the Broncos, but again, it would take a serious offer to get Payton and company to give up on the veteran back.

title: Broncos' Jaylen Waddle Injury Concerns Grow After Insider Report
full_text:
In a scary moment late in last Sunday's 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals, Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle went down with an injury .
It occurred on a reverse toss to Waddle, which he bobbled and fumbled, but was able to fall on top of the ball and retain possession. Alas, Cardinals linebacker Josh Sweat then fell on top of Waddle, with the ball beneath him.
For a moment, it looked like perhaps Waddle injured his collarbone or shoulder, the way he was holding it, but as he was walked off the field by Broncos trainers, he was moving his left arm around, which was a good sign. He didn't return to the game, but we've been monitoring any updates on his status.
On Wednesday, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Waddle's injury was actually an aggravation of the chest injury he'd been nursing for the previous couple of weeks. The veteran's status for Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs will "be determined at a later time" and based on "how practice goes," per Rapoport.
#Broncos WR Jaylen Waddle, suffered an aggravation of his previous chest injury on the reverse last week and his status for Sunday vs the #Chiefs will be determined at a later time, sources say. Waddle’s availability will be based on how practice goes. pic.twitter.com/OKC4BCVQLA
On one hand, fans should be relieved that Waddle doesn't appear to be headed to injured reserve. On the other, it looks like his Week 8 availability is very much up in the air.
Given the two-score lead the Broncos were protecting late in the fourth quarter, the wideout reverse was a questionable play call by Payton. With how well rookie running back Jonah Coleman was doing on the ground to help close out the game, it made the trickery of the Waddle reverse even more dubious.
Payton beat himself up over the call at the podium following the game.
"It was awful," Payton said on Sunday. "Alright, I'm sorry. And if you look it up, in 2008, in a similar situation, even a more radical reverse, fumbled, Tampa Bay beat us. I know better. And every once in a while, you fall in love with a play."
The Broncos were trying to run the four-minute offense, and salt away the game. On a 1st-&-10 with 4:51 to go, Payton called in the reverse, and the rest is history. Coleman had just busted off a 15-yard run on the previous play and was on a roll, too.
The Broncos acquired Waddle in a blockbuster trade this past offseason, giving up a first- and third-round draft pick to the Miami Dolphins.
Although Waddle's first year with the Broncos hasn't resulted in big-time numbers, he does lead the team in receiving. He's been Bo Nix's most targeted receiver, sitting with 26 receptions on 45 targets for 276 yards and one touchdown.
Waddle has picked up 11 first downs as a receiver and has two carries for 23 yards on the ground. In the Broncos' woefully low-volume passing attack this season, the big numbers haven't been there — with the exception of his 138-yard performance in Week 2 — but Nix dealt with a slump early on in his return from a fractured ankle.
The Broncos faced some tremendous defenses through each of their first six games, which only exacerbated Nix's struggles and limited the receivers. But with the schedule opening up, starting last week in Arizona, the tide could be turning, as Courtland Sutton predicted last week. Nix looked much more like his former self against the Cardinals.
At this stage, the hopes Broncos fans had of Waddle coming to Denver and producing a 1,000-yard season — and maybe even the first Pro Bowl nod of his career — have been dashed. Nix looked improved in Week 7, but unless he suddenly sparks some Star Wars numbers, Waddle will likely finish with a disappointing statistical body of work.
Waddle may not get that elusive Pro Bowl nod or the fourth 1,000-yard campaign of his career, but he's very much on track to feature on a playoff team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. At 5-2, the Broncos are rolling, and they have the chance to take the lead in the AFC West with a win over the Chiefs this week.
Even if Waddle isn't 100%, fans should hope he can make it onto the field this week because he can open up the offense. He and Nix haven't been able to connect on many explosive plays, but opponents still recognize and fear Waddle's speed.
Again, Nix took some big steps in that direction last week in Arizona, finishing with four explosive passing plays, one of which was a 27-yard dime to Waddle down the right seam. It feels like Nix is getting his confidence back , so this is where Waddle's presence could really start paying dividends.
We likely won't know for sure what Waddle's Week 8 outlook is until Friday's final injury report. I wouldn't be shocked if he doesn't participate in Wednesday or Thursday's practice, but if he's at least limited on Friday, it would be a positive omen for his Week 8 availability.
From the sounds of it, though, it's not a serious injury or something fans have to worry about landing Waddle on IR. We'll continue to monitor this storyline closely throughout the week.
Waddle did not participate in Wednesday's practice . He was, indeed, listed with a chest injury.

title: Broncos ILB Alex Singleton Lands Coveted NFL Defensive Award
full_text:
Denver Broncos inside linebacker Alex Singleton was a consistent force in the team's Week 7 win over Arizona — and now he's been recognized for it.
The NFL on Wednesday named Singleton as AFC Defensive Player of the Week, the first such honor of his eight-year career.
Singleton was all over the field amid Denver's 30-16 victory against the Cardinals, recording a whopping 19 tackles (12 solo), one sack, and two quarterback hits. The tackles were the most by any NFL player in a non-overtime game since 2023, per the team.
Amazingly enough, they were also "only" the third-most in any game for Singleton, who notched 21 and 20 tackles apiece in a pair of 2022 contests versus the Chargers and Rams, respectively.
Entering Week 8, the 32-year-old longtime defensive captain leads the league in total tackles (87) by a significant margin; the next closest is 49ers ILB Fred Warner with 71.
Singleton is the second Broncos player to capture AFC Defensive Player of the Week this season. Safety Talanoa Hufanga previously earned the award following his performance in Denver's Week 3 win over the Rams.
Perhaps no Broncos defensive player (with the possible exception of Riley Moss) has been more maligned than Singleton, practically since he initially joined the team — and primarily from within the fan base.
However, even the harshest critic would admit that he's been playing fantastic football of late. The Broncos are doing a good job of hiding his coverage flaws and Singleton himself recovered nicely from his disastrous season-opening, missed-tackle extravaganza against the Chiefs.
Such is why the organization has continually rewarded him with contract extensions, including a two-year, $15 million pact this past March. Such is also why he's maintained his position as ILB1 in the middle of Denver's elite defense, the unheralded engine that makes it go.
"Obviously it’s experience, man. I mean, he can call it for me. He is my eyes and ears on the field," defensive coordinator Vance Joseph said of Singleton in August. "He can make adjustments very quickly with his experience, but he’s a tackling machine.
"He had 170-plus tackles when he was healthy for us for the whole season. So we missed that last year. He’s a hell of a blitzer also. He can cover backs. So obviously having him back this year is going to help our defense go to the next level.”
This is the first Player of the Week honors of Singleton's career. He's the 11th Broncos linebacker to earn the AFC Defensive Player of the Week award. The last linebacker to bring it home was Jonathon Cooper in 2025.
Cody Barton was the last Broncos inside linebacker to win the award (2024). Singleton joins Cooper, Baron, Nik Bonitto, Von Miller, Wesley Woodyard, Al Wilson, D.J. Williams, Glenn Cadrez, John Mobley, and Karl Mecklenburg as the list of Broncos linebackers to earn DPoW accolades.

title: Broncos' Next Four Games Look Different Through Advanced Metrics
full_text:
The Denver Broncos sit at 5-2 after seven weeks and are one game out of first place in the AFC West. It hasn't been pretty, but the Broncos have found ways to win against some quality teams, even with key players out of the lineup.
How good are the Broncos, though? Is this a team that can make a deep playoff run like last season? And how good are Denver's next few opponents?
Let's look at what DVOA, the advanced metric devised by Aaron Schatz, has to say about the Broncos and their next four opponents. Opponent adjustments now account for 70% of a team's DVOA rating.
The Broncos rank 11th in overall DVOA at 12.2%. That would be the mark of a team described as "good but not great," which seems about right for where the Broncos are right now.
On offense, the Broncos rank 16th at -2.6%. "Below average" might be the best term to describe the offense, though the Broncos' offense showed signs of progress against the Arizona Cardinals this past week.
On defense, the Broncos rank fifth at -11.7% (again, DVOA is better for defense when it's negative). That's a sign of a quality defense, though not necessarily an elite defense.
On special teams, the Broncos rank sixth at 3%. On one hand, that's a sign of a solid special teams unit, though not an elite one. On the other hand, it's worth noting that only one team has a special teams DVOA of at least 10%, that being the Minnesota Vikings.
After seven games, the Chiefs sit eighth overall at 15.4%, fourth on offense at 18.7%, 14th on defense at -0.4%, and 29th on special teams at -3.8%.
The Chiefs have a quality offense, but their defense isn't a top unit, though it's solid. Special teams has been an issue, though, namely with kicker Harrison Butker's struggles.
After seven games, the Panthers rank 13th in overall DVOA at 7%, 12th on offense at 5.2%, 15th on defense at 0.3%, and 10th on special teams at 2.1%.
The Panthers are a solid overall team but their defense could be described as below average. While not a team to take lightly, the Panthers aren't as good as the Chiefs.
The Raiders rank 27th in overall DVOA at -17.2%, 18th on offense at -3.8%, 28th on defense at 13.8%, and 15th on special teams at 0.3%.
This team has come back down to earth in recent weeks. While not a team to look past, it's worth noting how bad the Raiders' defense has been, meaning the offense won't have much excuse for not playing well against them.
The Steelers rank ninth in overall defense at 9.2%, 13th on offense at 4.3%, seventh on defense at -11.7%, and 21st on special teams at -0.9%.
The Steelers are going to be a tougher opponent than some might have expected going into the season. It's a road game, the Steelers' defense is among the top units, and their offense has been solid.
While the Broncos won't face as tough of a schedule in the next four games as they did in the first four weeks of the season, they don't necessarily have it easy. The Chiefs and Steelers are both quality teams and the Panthers have shown they can be a good team, too.
If the Broncos can go 3-1 in this stretch of four games, they will be in good shape. It will particularly help if the offense can play better in the next three games, when it will face defenses that don't rank in the top 10.
The good thing to see is that the Broncos' defense is coming around, even with key players out with injuries. The defense has been a big reason the Broncos are 5-2, though the hope is that the unit won't have to do as much of the work in the weeks to come.
We'll talk more about the rematch with the Chiefs later this week, but a win this Sunday at Mile High would do a lot to boost the Broncos' chances of winning the AFC West and making a deep playoff run.

title: Detroit Lions Injury Updates: Pacheco, Branch, Joseph, Harper
full_text:
Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell provided injury updates on several members of the roster, prior to the team practicing on Friday afternoon.
Safety Kerby Joseph has only been limited at practice and has yet to participate in any team periods. He was observed wearing a compression sleeve on his injured left knee on Thursday.
The former NFL tight end indicated players will regularly wear sleeves to reduce swelling, but there was no concerns about his knee at this stage.
Next week, the team will have him participate much more in practice sessions.
Running back Isiah Pacheco has an opportunity to return to action in December. The former Kansas City Chiefs running back suffered a back injury that required surgery and also dealt with a knee injury during training camp.
"He's progressing well. I do think there's a chance we could get him back in late December," said Campbell. "He's put a tremendous amount of work in. He's doing pretty good."
Safety Thomas Harper has been on the injured reserve list after suffering an ankle injury against the Buffalo Bills.
Campbell indicated the talented defender could be close to returning, but has rehabbed well and is progressing enough to be able to return to help the defense at some point in the coming weeks.
Brian Branch, in his initial return to action after suffering an Achilles injury, was on sort of a pitch count in his 2026 season debut. While he played much more in the second-half against the Packers, this week offers Kelvin Sheppard the opportunity to use the former second-round pick however he sees fit.
The sixth-year head man expressed there would not be any limitations on Branch moving forward, as he came out of his first game feeling quite confident.
Sheppard noticed the impact the former Alabama Crimson Tide defender had on his teammates in a Week 7 home victory.
“I think the effect he had on his teammates. One of my favorite things from that game, I don't know if you guys caught this, go back and watch it. It's super cool. On his interception, he's still backpedaling. And right when he opens his hip, the ball's launched. And Chuck Clark, before BB opens his hip, raises his hand," said Sheppard. "And this is what I mean when I say affecting the teammates. He raises his hand. When he sees BB open his hip, he puts both hands in the air. I mean, I've never seen that. I'm like, 'Chuck, you run to the ball.' Nope, the play's over.
"And just what that does for teammates, what that did, the swagger it brings, knowing you have an enforcer who can go cover the number one receiver. BB's a rare player in this league. We're all happy to have him back .”

title: Jared Goff Is Ranked Best NFL Quarterback
full_text:
Jared Goff has been just what the doctor ordered for the Lions so far in 2026.
The veteran signal-caller , and the straw that stirs the drink in Motown, has had a sterling start to the season.
Through six games, the 32-year-old has thrown for 14 touchdowns and 1,788 yards while having yet to toss a single interception. And he's now just one of two quarterbacks in NFL history with that many passing touchdowns without an interception through the first six games of a season. The other QB: Russell Wilson, who accomplished the feat in 2019 with the Seattle Seahawks.
Goff also leads all quarterbacks in the following thus far this season: passer rating (112.5), passing yards/game (298.0) and passing first downs/game (14.67). Plus, he owns the sixth-highest Pro Football Focus overall grade among all qualified passers (82.1).
He's unquestionably been one of the very best signal-callers in the NFL through the season's first seven weeks, and fans and pundits alike have begun to take notice.
Perhaps the most recent example comes from CBS Sports’ Garrett Podell , who ranked Goff as the No. 1 QB in the league entering Week 8.
Additional Lions NFL Insider Analysis: 10 Thoughts Ahead of Week 8 Contest Against Vikings
Goff's continued mistake-free play factored significantly into Podell's decision to move him from No. 3 to No. 1 in his weekly QB rankings.
As he mentioned, “Goff's 223 throws without an interception are the most through the first six games of a season in NFL history.”
That wasn't the only reason why he placed the veteran passer atop his QB rankings, however.
Podell added, “Fresh off winning his duel with Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers at the last second, Goff also ranks second in expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.29), just one one-hundredth behind Josh Allen (0.30). However, Goff has been the much better passer this season, which gets him the nod for the top spot entering Week 8.”
Goff has very well played himself into the MVP conversation in recent weeks, too. And with another strong showing and victory against the Minnesota Vikings Sunday, he might just become one of the league's early MVP frontrunners .
Goff and the Lions are set to battle Kyler Murray and the Vikings Sunday at 1 p.m. (EST) at Ford Field.

title: Spot the Ball: 10 Thoughts Ahead of Lions Matchup Against Vikings
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are coming off a big win over a division rival, and will now be treated to another opportunity to make their claim to being the best in the NFC North.
On Sunday, the Lions will host the 6-0 Minnesota Vikings. Under Kevin O’Connell, the Vikings have started the year unbeaten including a comeback win over the Packers in Week 1.
Now, Detroit will have a chance to deliver their first loss while cutting into their division deficit as they look to make it three NFC North titles in four years. While there’s still plenty of football to be played beyond Week 8, the ramifications of a win or a loss in this game are hard to ignore.
Here are 10 thoughts ahead of the Lions’ Week 8 matchup with the Minnesota Vikings.
Veteran quarterback Jared Goff is off to one of the best starts he’s ever had through six games. He has thrown 14 touchdowns, and has just one turnover which was a fumbled snap in Sunday’s win over the Green Bay Packers.
While the start has been phenomenal, Sunday will be the biggest test he’s faced up to this point of the season. The Vikings come in undefeated, and their defensive coordinator Brian Flores’ blitz-heavy scheme will be an entirely new challenge both for Goff and the offensive line.
Goff is 4-2 against the Vikings with Flores as the coordinator. He has thrown nine touchdowns against four interceptions, with two of those picks coming in the teams’ Christmas Day meeting at Minnesota last year and had five total turnovers in the two meetings. After getting swept by the Vikings last year, Detroit will be looking to get revenge — and Goff staying turnover free against one of the league’s best defenses will be a big key to that effort.
With their win over the Packers, the Lions moved to 4-2 and jumped ahead of Green Bay in the NFC North standings. They currently sit behind the unbeaten, 6-0 Vikings and the 5-2 Chicago Bears heading into Week 8.
Detroit can’t jump into first-place with a win over Minnesota, as they’re currently two games back. However, a win would cut the deficit in half and allow them to hold the tiebreaker prior to their return matchup in Minnesota in December.
On the contrary, a loss would move them to three games behind the Vikings, and a corresponding win by the Packers against Carolina Thursday would push them back into last-place. The Lions have always believed the key to a big playoff run is starting with a home playoff game, which can only be attained by winning the division.
Because of both the current and future implications this game holds, Sunday’s game is a must-win for Detroit to stay in the race for the division title at midseason.
Now in his fourth year as the Vikings’ defensive coordinator, Flores will look to put his stamp on this division rivalry once again at Ford Field. He and former Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson battled for two years, then Flores got the best of John Morton in stifling Detroit’s offense in both games last year.
Now, Lions’ first-year coordinator Drew Petzing will get a chance to out-scheme the veteran defensive play-caller. Flores is widely regarded as one of the best defensive minds in football, and the team’s output through their unbeaten start speaks for itself.
Petzing has the Lions humming through the first six games of the year, though they were held under 30 for the first time all year Sunday against the Packers. Now, he matches wits with one of the game’s top defensive minds with a chance to keep the Lions’ divisional hopes afloat.
The Lions will be facing one of the league’s best defenses on Sunday, and multiple numbers tell the story on just how good the Vikings have been through six games on that side of the ball. They are tied-for-first with Detroit with 21 sacks, and have allowed the NFL’s lowest completion percentage (53.9) and passing yards (1,085) along with the fewest amount of passing touchdowns (three) up to this point in the season.
Young defensive end Dallas Turner has paced the defense with six sacks, while the return of veteran Harrison Smith has fueled the secondary. Cornerback Byron Murphy has three interceptions and will be looking to add to that tally working against Detroit’s plethora of playmakers at receiver.
The Lions tried a new strategy with their secondary against Green Bay in Week 7. Rather than having two cornerbacks play the dominant share of the snaps, they cycled in options in an effort to combat Green Bay’s deep passing game and the natural fatigue that can come with tracking receivers deep down the field on a consistent basis.
Because of this, all eight of Detroit’s active defensive backs in Sunday’s game played at least 14 snaps. D.J. Reed played perhaps his best game of the season, while Khalil Dorsey impressed enough in his 14 snaps to warrant a postgame shoutout from his head coach.
While the Vikings’ style will be different, it’s no secret they have an array of offensive weapons of their own. Justin Jefferson will cause problems, and has a history of playing well against the Lions. However, Detroit’s new strategy is worth exploring for at least another week.
Kyler Murray will get his first opportunity to take on the Lions as a member of the Vikings after signing with them in the offseason. A former No. 1 overall pick of the Arizona Cardinals, Murray spent seven years in Arizona before being released after injuries limited him to five games last year.
It will be a reunion between Murray and his former offensive coordinator, Drew Petzing who now holds the same title with the Lions. In Murray’s career, he is winless against the Lions with an 0-3-1 mark.
In those meetings, Murray has totaled 1,042 yards, six touchdowns and six interceptions. A mobile quarterback who utilizes his legs, he has rushed for 86 yards total in his four meetings with Detroit. Keeping him contained will be a big point of emphasis on Sunday.
After wearing their all-black alternate uniforms last week, the Lions will once again have a different look for Sunday’s game against the Vikings. They will be debuting their “Rivalries” uniforms, which were unveiled in August.
The jerseys are a light silver with black numbers and blue outlines and lettering. Detroit will wear their blue alternate helmets with the uniform to complete the look.
It’s a distinct look inspired by the city’s heritage involving automobiles, and it will be interesting to gauge the fan reaction to seeing them for the first time on the field.
When they were unveiled, the reaction from the fan base was a mixed bag. However, things could change when the Lions are in action. Coincidentally, the Vikings will debut their own new uniforms when they host the Lions in December.
For things to go well for the Lions, it starts and ends with Goff’s performance. In their best-case scenario, Goff tears up the Vikings’ blitz-oriented scheme and has answers for everything pre-snap. Using his array of playmakers, the veteran quarterback distributes the ball evenly, and the Lions strike quickly with explosive plays in the first half.
After halftime with the Vikings forced to adjust, the Lions can churn the clock with their run game. Defensively, Brian Branch shines and they force Murray into multiple turnovers, negating the impact of Justin Jefferson.
Last time the Lions played the Vikings, it was about as disastrous as possible. Goff looked frazzled throughout the game, and the team turned the ball over five times. The worst-case scenario would be more of the same, with Flores out-scheming Petzing and forcing Goff to be under duress throughout the game.
In this scenario, the Lions find some answers after halftime, but the defense is picked apart early by the connection of Murray and Jefferson. Former Lion T.J. Hockenson scores an early touchdown, and the Lions go quietly in a disappointing divisional blowout loss.

title: Could Detroit Lions Make Surprise Trade to Add Depth Behind Jahmyr Gibbs?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have one of the NFL's brightest young stars in running back Jahmyr Gibbs.
Through the first six games of the season, Gibbs has once again proven why he's viewed across the NFL landscape as one of the top talents at the position. His blend of exciting speed and physicality have shown up plenty, and he's been consistent after being essentially handed the reins to the offense when the Lions traded David Montgomery in the offseason.
However, in this six-game stretch to start the season a troubling trend has emerged. Gibbs has been a workhorse in every sense of the word, currently ranking third in rushing attempts (134) and first in total touches (166) to start the year.
With how dynamic and explosive Gibbs is, the prevailing fear is that the team could overuse him which would in turn lead to some of that explosiveness being sapped late in the year. While Gibbs has handled the workload well to this point, and impressed coaches with how effective he has been able to be, one wonders if this is sustainable over the duration of an NFL season plus a potential playoff run.
With an ESPN report earlier in the week stating that the Lions have remained in contact with free agent running back Kareem Hunt after bringing him in for a visit during training camp, it's worth exploring the possibility of the Lions making a deal for running back depth to help offset Gibbs' workload.
Currently, the Lions have utilized Sione Vaki as the second option. Isiah Pacheco, a veteran who came to Detroit on a one-year deal after four seasons in Kansas City, is on injured reserve after having a back procedure and expected to be out until December.
Appearing in all six games, Vaki has totaled 16 carries for 56 yards while also serving as an option in pass-protection on passing downs for the offense.
With the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaching, the Lions have the ability to seek some help from elsewhere to add a veteran option who could give them some production and take a portion of the work off of Gibbs' shoulders.
Some of the top names being floated around at the position can likely be written off as potential Lions targets, with those being Indianapolis' Jonathon Taylor and Philadelphia's Saquon Barkley. However, there are some other intriguing candidates that could fit the Lions' need for depth.
Here are three potential trade targets the Lions could evaluate adding in the event that they want to bolster their depth at running back.
Tampa Bay's Kenny Gainwell and Tennessee's Tony Pollard are two potential trade candidates who currently play for struggling teams. While the Buccaneers appear to have gotten some momentum after a thrashing of Carolina, Gainwell is behind young budding star Bucky Irving and could be an asset they'd be comfortable dealing for a late-round draft pick.
Gainwell has shown some pop throughout his career, which began with four years for the Eagles before spending last season with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Lions fans may remember his performance against the team last year at Ford Field, where he had a 45-yard receiving touchdown just before halftime.
With his ability to contribute both as a between-the-tackles rusher and a receiver, Gainwell has the ability to supplement Gibbs nicely.
Pollard is considered an asset for the rebuilding Titans as he's currently in the final year of his contract. He has built a solid career, as he entered the year with four-straight seasons of over 1,000 rushing yards.
Beginning his career as a backup in Dallas, Pollard quickly asserted himself beginning in the 2022 season when he went over the 1,000-yard plateau for the first time. The following year, he did so again while also notching a career-best 55 receptions.
He signed with the Titans ahead of the 2024 season, and has performed well as their top option despite the team's struggles throughout his tenure. He would be a nice compliment for Gibbs, and give the backfield more of that 1-2 punch it has had in recent years rather than being simply a secondary option.
Another intriguing trade option listed by ESPN on its honorable mentions of trade targets is Kamara. Though not the dynamic two-way threat he was in his earlier seasons, he remains a viable option both as a rusher and receiver who Lions head coach Dan Campbell has experience working with from his days on staff with the Saints.
Through six appearances, Kamara ranks third amongst the Saints' running backs in rushing yards with 125 but has 27 catches for 133 yards and could provide the Lions with a veteran change of pace behind the explosive Gibbs.
The sentimental value of Kamara to the Saints' organization, where he has spent all 10 of his NFL seasons, could theoretically drive up the asking price. However, he's on a one-year deal and if the demand is a reasonable mid-to-late-round pick, he could be well worth the ask to provide the team with some production late in the year.

title: Detroit Lions Week 8 Thursday Injury Report Sees Encouraging Progress
full_text:
The Detroit Lions returned to the practice field on Thursday afternoon, three days ahead of their Week 8 contest against the Minnesota Vikings.
After several starters missed practice on Wednesday, each member of the roster was accounted for on Thursday, including running back Jahmyr Gibbs and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson.
Safety Kerby Joseph and cornerback Ennis Rakestraw were limited at practice. Joseph was seen wearing a compression sleeve on his injured left knee, possibly to assist in limiting any potential swelling.
Prior to practice, defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard praised the efforts of his unit against the Green Bay Packers.
"First and foremost, want to credit the players for the way they went out and performed. High energy, high effort, a lot of details showed up," said Sheppard. "A lot of things we talked about during the week showed up. And also, I don't want to leave out, I'd be remiss to leave out the staff. They're doing a tremendous job right now. I know you guys probably have got this theme of all hands-on deck.
"It's also with the coaching staff right now. So all hands-on deck, trying to just find answers. Just all hands-on deck, whatever it takes mentality," Sheppard added further. "Selfless, sacrificing, those are all words that come to mind when I think of that defensive unit right now. And I just want to credit those guys."
Sheppard believes the efforts of the coaching staff have resonated with the players, resulting in increased trust and understanding of the core defensive principles.
"What we've really done, the things that you're seeing is just a trickle effect of these guys. I told them, I don't think I've ever seen back-to-back games where we went out, we do these keys to victory and they've gone out back-to-back games and I mean hit every single one of them," said Sheppard. "And that's when you know you're trending the right way. That's when you know it's hitting home with the players. But again, we are nothing without them. They are the ones that go out and make it come to life and they're doing that right now."

title: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Minnesota Vikings in Week 8
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will face a second straight NFC North divisional opponent when they take on the Minnesota Vikings Sunday afternoon.
The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), feature both a bottom-10 offense (20.8 points/game) and the league's top defensive unit.
Coordinated by Brian Flores, Minnesota's defense has permitted just 12.3 points a game, and hasn't allowed more than 16 points in a game since Week 2. And most recently, the Vikings surrendered just 10 points in a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7.
Additionally, Minnesota has been extremely stout against the pass thus far this season. In fact, Kevin O'Connell's squad has allowed the second-fewest passing yards (930) and the least amount of touchdowns through the air (three) through the season's first seven weeks.
The Vikings have also already secured seven interceptions, spearheaded by cornerback Byron Murphy's league-high three picks.
So, Lions signal-caller Jared Goff, who has yet to throw an interception in 2026, will face arguably his biggest test of the campaign against Minnesota's stingy pass defense .
Then on the opposite side of the ball, Detroit's secondary will receive one of its toughest assignments of the year, going head-to-head with All-Pro wideout Justin Jefferson. Jefferson, who has surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first six NFL seasons, has accumulated 302 reception yards and three touchdowns in five games this season.
He's unquestionably Vikings passer Kyler Murray's go-to target and one of the very best receivers in the game today.
Subsequently, D.J. Reed, the Lions’ No. 1 cornerback , should get the majority of one-on-one reps with the Pro Bowl pass-catcher.
Additionally, I wouldn't be surprised if Detroit defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard deployed a rotation of corners in the Week 8 tilt. And as a result, I could see the likes of Ennis Rakestraw and Roger McCreary also getting opportunities to defend Jefferson Sunday.
It'll hardly be an easy task for the Lions’ defensive backs group. However, Detroit does have a solid track record against Jefferson, having limited him to under 60 yards the past three meetings between the NFC North rivals . And if the Lions could do it a fourth straight time, it would go a long way toward Dan Campbell's squad notching its fifth victory on the season.
At this present juncture, I'm willing to give Detroit a 61 percent chance to secure the Week 8 victory .

title: Detroit Lions Falling Way Behind Arms Race After Blockbuster Bears Trade
full_text:
The Detroit Lions now have a much more difficult task in order to win the NFC North.
After the Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers made improvements to their roster by making trades, the Chicago Bears are the latest team to pull of a blockbuster trade.
According to multiple reporters, Detroit's NFC North rival has acquired defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and agreed to send the Tennessee Titans first-round picks in both the 2027 and 2028 NFL Drafts. Included in the deal is a 2027 fourth-round pick.
In the last seven years, four teams that have made aggressive trades have went on to win the Super Bowl, including the 2019 Chiefs, 2020 Rams, 2022 Eagles and 2025 Seahawks.
According to Sports Illustrated , "Oddsmakers are loving this deal for the Bears, who entered Week 8 at +1400 to win the Super Bowl at DraftKings Sportsbook . They were the No. 4 team in my most recent NFL Power Rankings after beating New England in Week 7 and moving up in the odds to win the title. Now, DraftKings has the Bears at +1200 to win the Super Bowl this season, which is good for the sixth-best odds in the entire league.
"The move for Simmons should help fix a Chicago defense that is allowing the most yards per play in the NFL this season. While the Bears' advanced metrics are better -- they rank 14th in EPA/Play and seventh in success rate -- this team needs to be better on that side of the ball to compete with the best teams in the NFC."
Granted, many of the bigger deals were executed in the offseason, but teams this season that are favored in the NFC have started to improve their rosters, while Detroit sits patiently, hoping to find the perfect deal.
Detroit has a clear need on defense and were not able to land the prized cornerback that was available in Joey Porter Jr.
The one complaint many supporters have is general manager Brad Holmes is extremely wary of adding external players in trades. The market does tend to be high-priced and would likely cost Detroit draft capital. Holmes has been willing to trade draft capital to target prospects in the draft.
It appears that in order for Detroit to take the next forward from being merely one of the contenders to being realistically in the mix this season is to add to the defense, most notably at the cornerback position.
The Bears lost both games to Detroit last season and are off to a 5-2 start this season.

title: What To Know About Lions Week 8 Official: Will Calls Be Favorable Again?
full_text:
The officiating crew for the Detroit Lions ’ Week 8 divisional showdown with the Minnesota Vikings has been revealed.
On Sunday, Craig Wrolstad’s crew will preside over the battle between the surging Lions and the unbeaten Vikings. Wrolstad has served as a head referee since 2014, and has worked several playoff games in that role including one that is near and dear to the Lions.
Wrolstad was the head referee for the Lions’ first playoff win in 30 years, as they hosted the Los Angeles Rams in primetime for a historic win. The Lions are 5-5 in the 10 games he’s worked as a head referee.
Last season, Wrolstad worked a pair of Lions games . He was the head official for the team’s loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, which featured a controversial call that negated an early Jared Goff touchdown on a trick play as well as a postgame scrum that led to a one-game suspension for Brian Branch. Only four penalties were called in that game, all on the Lions.
Wrolstad also worked the Lions’ overtime win over the New York Giants on Nov. 23. In that game, there were 16 total penalties called with nine on the Lions and seven on the Giants.
Another notable occurrence in Wrolstad’s career came when he was working as a field judge in the Super Bowl between the San Francisco 49ers and Baltimore Ravens when power was lost leading to a lengthy delay.
Through six games, Wrolstad’s crew ranks second in total flags thrown with 108, surpassing Detroit’s officiating crew from last week led by Alex Moore after 20 penalties were called in the matchup between Denver in Arizona. Home teams are 4-2 so far this season with Wrolstad officiating.
The veteran official’s crew has thrown at least 20 total flags in each of the last three games they’ve worked. In addition to Denver and Arizona, he also reffed the Week 6 Sunday Night game between Dallas and Green Bay and a Week 5 game between New England and Las Vegas. Through six games, there has been an even 54 penalties called on both home and away teams.
Wrolstad has thrown 24 flags for offensive holding, which ranks fourth amongst all crews. His second-most common penalty called is defensive pass interference, as he has whistled teams 16 times for that.

title: The Case For And Against Detroit Lions Trading For CB Donte Jackson
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are facing some pressure as an organization to make a move before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
With just under two weeks remaining until teams must make a move or elect to stand pat, the rumor mill is ablaze with potential moves that could boost the Lions. In particular, they're viewed as a team that needs to make a move at the cornerback spot.
Among the potential options is current Los Angeles Chargers veteran Donte Jackson. Now in his ninth NFL season, Jackson is on an expiring deal with the winless Chargers who could be looking to make moves and gain draft capital.
In a recent report from ESPN ranking the top-25 players most likely to be traded, Jackson was named as the 14th best player. The Lions were listed as one of his best fits, along with the Carolina Panthers and Baltimore Ravens.
"Corner is a position of need for several teams, and the Chargers likely could get a draft pick for Jackson," wrote ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. "The 30-year-old has ball production and a reasonable contract -- a $6 million base salary. Plus, he is set to hit free agency in March."
The report from Fowler and Matt Bowen gave Jackson a 25 percent chance of being traded, which is not overwhelmingly high. However, if the Chargers continue to struggle it could increase those odds.
Additionally, the Chargers have two young cornerbacks in Tarheeb Still and Cam Hart that they would benefit from investing in. As a result, Jackson could be expendable .
On one hand, the injury history is a concern for the veteran. He has been sidelined since Oct. 4 with a hamstring injury but was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice. If he's able to return to action this week, it would allow him the opportunity to boost his trade stock with a good performance.
His performance has been up-and-down, as he wouldn't be a dynamite, shutdown option that would drastically change the Lions' fortunes. However, the cost to add him wouldn't be overwhelming as a Day 3 pick would likely suffice, and this is the type of market that the Lions have traditionally made deals in throughout Brad Holmes' tenure as GM.
Detroit displayed a cornerback rotation throughout the win over Green Bay in Week 7 and appears to be confident in what they have. However, bringing in another veteran would be beneficial both for their overall depth as well as elevating the level of competition in the room.
Jackson has proven to be reliable throughout his career, which began in Carolina and included a one-year stint in Pittsburgh before signing with the Chargers before last season. Now, he could have the chance to be a part of a playoff run, and is in a similar position to where Za'Darius Smith was when the Lions traded for him.
Of course, the biggest thing for Detroit in the case of Jackson would be to confirm that he is healthy and would be available for the stretch run. However, if he's clear from a medical perspective, he would provide steady depth at the very least with the chance to be a starter and an impact player opposite of fellow veteran D.J. Reed.

title: Snaps, Studs and Duds: Analysis From Packers’ Win Over Panthers
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers won for the fourth time in five games on Thursday night, beating the Carolina Panthers 27-19.
Green Bay’s defense has held five consecutive opponents to 20 points or less, a first for the team since 2022. With two more takeaways added to the tally, the Packers are up to 15 – one more than last year’s full-season tally.
Here is our weekly analysis of the Packers’ snap counts along with a few studs and duds.
Green Bay played 69 snaps on offense.
Quarterback: For the seventh time in eight games, Jordan Love played every snap. According to Pro Football Focus, he was pressured on 13 of 41 dropbacks. By the official stats, he was neither sacked nor hit.
He was excellent, save for the late interception, which he said would “haunt” him. He finished 30-of-41 passing for 288 yards with three touchdowns.
Running backs: It’s back to old times for Josh Jacobs from a workload perspective. He played 49 snaps, or 71 percent. The other 20 snaps were almost equally divided between MarShawn Lloyd (11) and Pierre Strong (nine). Kaleb Johnson was inactive.
Of the team’s 26 running plays, Jacobs got 21 of them. He averaged just 1.9 yards per carry with a long run of 6. Of his 39 rushing yards, we gave him 37 after contact. Added together, Jacobs got 27 touches for a meager 52 yards, though he did score two touchdowns.
Receivers: Matthew Golden was questionable with a shoulder injury but wound up playing a unit-high 59 snaps. Savion Williams was next with 38. Christian Watson played 34 snaps despite being hospitalized briefly with a broken rib. J. Michael Sturdivant played a season-high 29 snaps, four more than Bo Melton.
Watson caught eight passes for 113 yards. He had 100 yards before the injury and a big third-down conversion late in the game. Golden caught 7-of-13 targets for 79 yards. He had two drops for a league-worst nine; he wasted no time in making amends for the second drop by scoring a 24-yard touchdown on the next play.
Williams was a nonfactor in the passing game, but his 18-yard sprint on an end-around led by Tucker Kraft and Anthony Belton was the team’s only run longer than 6 yards. Sturdivant got one opportunity and made a terrific all-hands over the middle for a gain of 16.
Tight ends: Tucker Kraft played a season-high 61 snaps. That’s a huge workload, even for him, but necessitated by Jonnu Smith being a healthy scratch and Josh Whyle dropping out with a concussion after three snaps. Mark Redman played 27.
Kraft caught six passes for 53 yards and one touchdown; he would have finished with 74 yards if not for an ineligible-man-downfield penalty that wiped out an excellent screen.
Offensive line: The latest rendition of the offensive line consisted of left tackle Jordan Morgan, left guard Aaron Banks, center John Williams, right guard Laken Tomlinson and right tackle Anthony Belton. They played every snap.
Banks was back in the lineup after five games on the sideline due to knee and toe injuries, with Tomlinson moving over to right guard, where he hadn’t played since 2016 and didn’t get a real week of practice to prepare.
PACKERS WIN!! Thank you 2016 Laken 🫡 🙏🏾 #gopackgo #trenchwarfare #TNFonPrime
“Just when you look at it, the way Laken’s been playing, you can’t take him out of the lineup, and I thought Aaron Banks coming back, we went that route,” coach Matt LaFleur explained. “That’s not to take anything away from (Kevin) Zeitler. We feel good about him as well. But we thought that was the move.”
Williams got the nod at center following last week’s injuries to Sean Rhyan and Jacob Monk.
. @Panthers @packers @John_Williams_ first start for John Williams ; pretty good stuff for a 7th rounder out of @GoBearcatsFB #gopackgo #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/jXDj4Ckhou
PFF charged the line with nine pressures – four for Williams, four for Banks and one for Tomlinson, with the tackles pitching shutouts. The run blocking, well, you know how that went.
Green Bay played 73 snaps on defense.
Defensive tackles: It was business as usual with relatively equal playing time. Karl Brooks led the way with 49 snaps. Devonte Wyatt, who had a huge sack on the opening drive to hold the Panthers to a field goal, was next with 40. Rookie Chris McClellan, who had a big fourth-down stop to start the second half, played 27 snaps. Anthony Campbell was next with 25 and Jordon Riley, playing in his second game in less than a week following last year’s torn Achilles, went from 29 to 19.
McClellan was in on six tackles. Everyone else on the unit combined for three (two for Wyatt, one for Campbell). Campbell and Brooks had two pressures apiece.
Edges: It was a typically balanced approach here, too. Lukas Van Ness led the way with 46 snaps. He was followed by Brenton Cox with 38, Barryn Sorrell with 33 and Dani Dennis-Sutton with 32.
All four players had a sack. According to PFF, Cox had a team-high six pressures, followed by Dennis-Sutton with five and Van Ness with four. Next Gen Stats produced similar results, with six for Cox, five for Dennis-Sutton and five for Van Ness.
Arron Mosby played 19 snaps on special teams in what will be his last roster elevation of the season. The next time the Packers want him on the field, it will be as a member of the 53.
Linebackers: With Zaire Franklin inactive for a second consecutive game, Isaiah McDuffie played every snap and Ty’Ron Hopper played 70. They usually are two vital cogs on special teams, so there’s been some adjustment with Hopper playing eight snaps and McDuffie only three.
Hopper was one of the big stars of the show with eight tackles, one sack, two quarterback hits, one interception and three passes defensed. He became the team’s first linebacker since 2000 with one sack, one interception and at least three passes defensed in a game.
Unprompted, coach Matt LaFleur said: “Ty’Ron Hopper, I can’t say enough great things about him, the night he had. What a great performance.”
Nick Niemann, who played one snap on defense, logged a team-high 22 on special teams. Kristian Welch played 19 on special teams.
Cornerbacks: Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse both played 72-of-73 snaps. They did a tremendous job in limiting quarterback Bryce Young and premier receiver Tetairoa McMillan.
According to PFF, Cisse broke up more passes (two) than he allowed completions (one) and Keisean Nixon, who was questionable with a shoulder injury, wasn’t even targeted. Next Gen charged Nixon with two catches for 27 yards and Cisse with one for 11. Whatever, they were excellent.
Carrington Valentine played two snaps and Kamal Hadden played one.
Safeties: Xavier McKinney and Evan Williams played every snap and Javon Bullard was on the field for the 57 snaps of nickel.
Williams had 10 tackles. McKinney had only three, but he had a big third-down breakup that preceded Chris McClellan’s fourth-down stop. Bullard, playing in his 40th game, still doesn’t have an interception but at least he finally has a forced fumble, which came on the lateral play at the end of the game.
Kitan Oladapo played one snap on defense and 18 on special teams.
WR Christian Watson (duh): Watson caught six passes for 100 yards in the first 21 minutes before being hospitalized with a broken rib after a 53-yard catch. Straight out of the WWE, Watson returned from the hospital and finished the game.
“I see Christian running out and he was just resurrected,” Jordan Love said.
He had a big third-down conversion in the final moments.
“Honestly, right when we were finally leaving the hospital,” Watson said of when he knew he could return to the game. “He was like, ‘Everything checked out.’ He asked me, ‘Are you good to still go out there?’ Before I even left, I wanted to go back out there, so I was going to make sure I was going to get back out there if they let me.”
Packers pass blocking: Jordan Love enjoyed his best protection of the season, though it certainly helped that the Panthers were playing without their best pass rusher. From a clean pocket, Love…

title: Packers Report Card: Big Win Over Panthers Comes With Two F’s
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The grades are in, and they are all over the map. The Green Bay Packers looked like they were going to cruise to victory when they took a 27-10 lead in the third quarter against the Carolina Panthers on Thursday night.
As has been the case in Green Bay for most of the season, nothing can be easy. The Packers continue to find ways to make things interesting. A Jordan Love interception gave the Panthers some life. The lack of run game gave the Panthers some hope.
Ultimately, Jonathan Gannon’s crew suffocated the Panthers’ offense in the biggest spots of the game, allowing the Packers to escape Lambeau Field with a 5-3 record.
Jordan Love had one major blemish on the night. His interception early in the fourth quarter took away the chance for the Packers to kick a field goal for what would likely have been an insurmountable 30-13 lead. Had he led Matthew Golden on the play, or seen a wide-open Christian Watson on the other side of the formation, the Packers may have had an even bigger night offensively.
“That’s really the play that is going to haunt me from that game,” Love said. “We had a concept with mirrored goes on the outside. I wanted to take a shot to MG and I saw him go inside on the route and just really a bad decision by me. I left it way inside and the safety was able to come over and make an interception that was really easy.
“In that situation, third down, in field-goal range, I’m really sick about that decision. That’s where I got to be better so we can put a team away and be able to go up multiple scores.”
Before that? He was excellent. He completed 17 of his first 20 passes and all three incompletions could have been called drops.
Watson’s toughness was on full display . He had 100 yards before going to the hospital after suffering a broken rib and coughing up blood, then returned and made a key third-down conversion late in the game.
What a night for Christian Watson. He had 100 yards before he was injured, wound up in the hospital for testing, and then made a key catch late in the game. How did he do it, and why? @JacobWestendorf explains both. ⬇️ https://t.co/aLlVfB2TSX
Love’s 30 completions went to seven different receivers, including a touchdown apiece of Tucker Kraft, Matthew Golden and Josh Jacobs.
Do the Packers need to figure out a way to ask their quarterback to not be superman every night? Yes. Can they rest assured knowing they have a chance in any game they play because of the way Love plays on a weekly basis? Also yes.
The offensive line stinks, though it at least didn’t give up a sack. The receivers lead the league in drops, with two more for Golden giving him a league-worst nine. The run game is nonexistent. None of it matters. Love continues to play high-level football. If they can eliminate some of the mistakes, the offense can reach new heights.
Everything felt like it was in line for a big night for the Packers’ ground game. Or at least something resembling a breakout.
Josh Jacobs was back for his second game and facing the worst rushing defense in football. Instead, the Packers finished with 66 rushing yards and a 2.5-yard average. The only real burst came on a reverse to Savion Williams, which picked up 18 yards. The traditional run game managed 50 yards on 25 carries.
Jacobs wound up with 39 yards on 21 carries. In the first half, he carried 10 times for 14 yards with a long rush of 4. He did create a touchdown essentially on his own when he danced around a would-be tackler at the goal line for a touchdown that gave the Packers a 13-10 lead in the first half.
Jacobs may still be shaking off some rust after missing six weeks of action, but his return has not fixed all that ails them on the ground. The Packers cannot simply rely on their passing game to move the ball as the games get more important.
The Packers became the first team in NFL history to have a winning record through eight games despite having fewer than 500 rushing yards.
“I think that’s an area we’ve got to keep getting better at,” quarterback Jordan Love said. “Keep finding what’s working, but we’ve got to improve because, especially late in the game, you’ve got to be able to lean on that. We did some really good things and I think, obviously, late in the game, it wasn’t good enough. We weren’t able to finish the way we wanted so that’s something we’ve got to improve on, clean up as an offense and be better there.”
If they cannot move the ball on the ground against Dallas or Carolina, the two worst rush defenses in football, it’s fair to ask if they ever will.
The Packers’ pass rush came back to life against Bryce Young and Co. Panthers left tackle Rasheed Walker did not have the revenge game he was hoping for in his return to Lambeau Field as the Packers piled up six sacks from six different players and pressured Young on nearly half of his dropbacks.
Brenton Cox, Dani Dennis-Sutton and Lukas Van Ness combined for 16 pressures. Along with Barryn Sorrell, all four edge players had a sack. Devonte Wyatt had a big one to kill the Panthers’ opening drive, which began at the Packers’ 29 following a fumbled kickoff return.
Young was only able to muster 209 passing yards on 41 pass attempts. That gets knocked down to 176 net passing yards with the sacks.
The Packers’ pass rush has been inconsistent for most of the season, but they have proven themselves to be good at defending opposing passing games.
That’s true despite missing some premier players on the defensive side of the ball. Their fourth preferred linebacker, Ty’Ron Hopper, started in place of Zaire Franklin and had a huge night. He blasted Bryce Young early in the game, chased Young down for a sack, had an impressive pass breakup and was rewarded with an interception after Lukas Van Ness got into his face for pressure.
The only blemish was a 26-yard touchdown to Jalen Coker in which Evan Williams and Keisean Nixon missed tackles on his way to the end zone.
Other than that? It was a big night. Now, Parsons perhaps is set to return to the practice field as the Packers face the biggest test of their schedule starting next week in Foxborough against the New England Patriots.
Chuba Hubbard was the focal point of Carolina’s attack but managed only 81 yards on 22 carries. Green Bay continues to slow down opposing ground games to earn the right to rush the passer.
When they earned the right, they unleashed hell on Bryce Young. The Panthers’ ground game is no slouch, and the Packers were in control most of the night against Hubbard.
Outside of one really bad game against Atlanta’s Bijan Robinson, this group in general has been excellent all season. The Packers have been a mirage before in terms of stopping the run. They’ll be tested in the near future, and as the calendar turns to December with Buffalo and Chicago on their schedule in particular.
If they can continue to slow down opposing ground games when Parsons returns, that will make defense more fun for Jonathan Gannon to call.
It was not exactly a banner night at the office for the Packers’ special teams.
The first quarter alone featured Coleman Owen fumbling on the opening kickoff return, which Carolina recovered and turned into a field goal. Following a touchdown pass from Jordan Love, Trey Smack had a pair of errors, starting with a league-leading eighth missed kick and his third missed extra point of the season.
Smack followed that up with a kick into the end zone for a touchback, gift wrapping the ball to the Panthers at the 35. That drive ended in a touchdown to give the Panthers a 10-6 lead.
Smack received a couple of Bronx cheers from the almost-77,000 fans as he made his other two extra-point attempts in the first half. That’s the situation the Packers’ kicking situation finds itself in at midseason.
If you want any sort of glimpse into how everyone is feeling about the kicking situation in Green Bay, Matt LaFleur told you everything you needed to know.
A long field goal would have given the Packers a 30-19 lead that…

title: After Six-Sack Game, Packers’ Matt LaFleur Has Perfect Six-Letter Word for Jonathan Gannon
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Carolina Panthers entered Thursday night’s game at the Green Bay Packers ranked fifth in total offense and sixth in scoring. Quarterback Bryce Young, running back Chuba Hubbard and receiver Tetairoa McMillan gave them a quality trio of playmakers.
But not against Jonathan Gannon.
The Packers beat the Panthers 27-19 at Lambeau Field. Gannon’s defense was instrumental, highlighted by six sacks coming from six individuals.
“Yeah, that’s great. It was great,” coach Matt LaFleur said. “It was just the relentless pressure. I thought our guys did a great job up front. I think some of the looks that we’re giving them, the opposition, Carolina, are very difficult. We do a lot of different things off of it. So, I think that’s a big-time credit to our defensive staff.”
Then came the money line about Gannon, who he hired in the offseason.
“JG, he likes to use this word a lot. I think he’s a savant. But he does a great job putting those guys in position. But it doesn’t mean anything if they can’t go execute it. So, just the ability for our guys – we’ve got a lot of smart players out there – to go out and be able to do all that, that’s a big-time credit to our players.”
Gannon on a short week put together a game plan that limited the Panthers to two touchdowns, 258 yards, 3.7 yards per play and 5-of-18 on third down.
“I think every time we get to third down, we just trying to get off the field,” Xavier McKinney said. “Even in the huddle, we like, ‘Ay, we need to get off the field right here.’ I thought the play calling was good. Especially on third downs, I thought it was really good. I thought we were pretty much in the right call every time.
“And guys went out there executed. The rush was getting there, so didn’t have a whole bunch of time, so just collectively everybody did what they were supposed to do.”
Young, who the Packers spoke highly of all week, was 23-of-41 passing for 209 yards. McMillan, who ranked in the top 15 in catches and receptions even while playing one fewer game than most receivers, caught only 6-of-11 targets for 58 yards. Young’s 26-yard touchdown pass to Jalen Coker late in the game was the only reception of 20-plus yards allowed.
Young was just 1-of-6 on passes thrown 10-plus yards downfield.
“They executed better,” Young said. “A lot of that stuff was on film, but they do a really good job of disguising. They are a good defense, and we have a lot of respect for them. They were better than us today for sure. They deserved that win. We should have been better. You have to execute better. That’s all it is.”
The mistake-plagued Packers did their best to help keep things interesting. Coleman Owen fumbled the opening kickoff return, handing the Panthers the ball at Green Bay’s 29, but Gannon’s defense held them to only a field goal following Devonte Wyatt’s third-down sack. Early in the second quarter, Christian Watson fumbled, giving the ball to the Panthers at their 37, but they went three-and-out.
That was one of four consecutive series in which they failed to pick up a first down and gained a total of 10 yards.
“I feel like that’s the hallmark of a good defense,” safety Evan Williams said. “You got to be ready at any time. Can’t rely on anybody to help you out. It’s a plus, it’s a cherry on top if the offense is doing their thing and going hard, but our standard is keep them out of field-goal range, keep them out of that half of the field, as a whole. You got to be ready for anything in this league. Anything can happen at any time. I feel like guys responded well.”
Williams and Isaiah McDuffie had 10 tackles apiece and Wyatt, linebacker Ty’Ron Hopper and edge players Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Dani Dennis-Sutton and Brenton Cox all had sacks.
Hopper stole the show. Making his second start for injured team captain Zaire Franklin, Hopper piled up eight tackles, one interception and three passes defensed. He was the first Packers defender since Charles Woodson in 2009 with at least one sack, one interception and three PBUs in a game.
After the Packers took a 13-10 lead in the second quarter, Hopper deflected and intercepted Young to set up a touchdown that extended the lead to 20-10.
“I was just able to get my hands up,” Hopper said. “We knew he was a shorter guy, so they talked about getting your hands up throughout the week. And I was able to do that and get my hands on the ball.”
After the Panthers pulled within 27-19 with 5:37 remaining in the game, Green Bay’s offense had a feeble three-and-out that took barely 1 minute off the clock.
Carolina, which had trailed by 17 points early in the third quarter, suddenly had a shot to at least take the game to overtime. Instead, Gannon’s defense thwarted four consecutive plays, including a six-man pressure on fourth-and-5 that forced Young’s errant pass to McMillan, who was covered by Javon Bullard.
“I think we did our job,” Bullard said. “You know, it ain't always gonna be perfect. We definitely got some things we need to clean up but, at the same time, walked out of here with a ‘W’ against a good team, and that's always our goal at the end of the night. You know, it ain't going to always be pretty, but you get a job done. That's all that matters.”
The Packers produced two takeaways; they’ve had at least two in five consecutive games. Their 15 takeaways through eight games are one more than they had all of last season.
While the defense was making big plays, it wasn’t allowing any. Entering the game, Carolina was seventh with 23 completions of 20-plus yards. The Packers, as noted above, allowed one.
“I just like the aggressive style,” LaFleur said. “They put a lot of pressure on offenses. We knew going into this, I think Carolina led the league in most explosive passes in the league, and they just didn’t allow that to even kind of happen.”
