title: 3 Reasons Why Raiders Need a Win in Week 8
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are in the midst of a four-game losing streak and desperately need a win on Sunday against the New York Jets.
A win would be monumental for the Raiders. Also, it's obvious what a win would do for this team. That said, here are three reasons Las Vegas must beat the Jets on Sunday.
Right now, the Raiders are dangerously close to seeing their season unravel. Another loss, and they would be 3-5 heading into a contest against the San Francisco 49ers. Additionally, the trade deadline is looming .
Las Vegas is already in a mix of teams with at least three losses, shrinking their chances of making the playoffs, which was a realistic aspiration after the first three weeks. A fifth consecutive loss would all but end the team's postseason hopes, given the upcoming stretch of opponents.
This week, head coach Klint Kubiak stated that there's no controversy at quarterback and that Cousins is the starter. However, a fifth straight loss, especially at the hands of the Jets, who just lost to the hapless Dolphins, could change Kubiak's tune.
Cousins has been far from the issue, as the 38-year-old quarterback has accumulated 1,877 yards, 16 touchdowns, and five interceptions while completing 62.6 percent of his passes. However, with a rookie quarterback waiting in the ranks, the longer the Raiders' winless drought continues, the louder the calls for Fernando Mendoza to get an opportunity.
The front office and coaching staff have made it clear that they are being patient with Mendoza. That can only be preached for so long if the team continues to lose games at this rate. If Cousins wants to retain his job, he can't afford to lose on Sunday.
We alluded to this earlier, but the timing of this game is crucial, with the trade deadline on Nov. 10. As we've seen this week, teams are identifying themselves as buyers or sellers . Currently, Las Vegas is in no man’s land, as it's still in playoff contention. At the same time, its playoff aspirations are hanging in the balance.
The Raiders' hands would essentially be forced with another loss, and it would be time to take calls on several players, including Maxx Crosby. If they want to hold out hope and achieve something no one foresaw happening before the season, then winning in Week 8 is a must. This game will provide so much clarity on the direction of this team for the rest of the season.
Logan Lazarczyk is a graduate of the University of Missouri-Kansas City, where he earned a Bachelor of Arts in Communication Studies with an emphasis in Journalism. Logan joined our team with extensive experience, having previously written and worked for media entities such as USA Today and Union Broadcasting.

title: Raiders Week 8 Depth Chart: What Stands Out Most
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' depth chart has few changes on it heading into Week 8. The Raiders largely are what they are. In an effort to change things up amid their losing streak, Raiders offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko noted that Las Vegas switched things up in practice this week.
“We’re always adjusting practice. We don’t ever want to copy and paste practice. So, Klint [Kubiak] will identify things each week that we want to work on, whether it’s something that we want to improve on or something that we want to capitalize on,” Janocko said.
“So, there are different things. Without going into specifics, there’s stuff every week that we are going to do and change. It’s not just the same every week. We’re trying to maximize our style of play and then continuing to improve on places that we feel that maybe we either fell short or that we feel like we can do better on.”
Below is analysis of Las Vegas' most updated depth chart.
Analysis: Cousins is one of the league's best quarterbacks.
As a team, the Raiders have lost four straight games . Las Vegas has scored a total of three points in the past four third quarters combined.
Analysis: The Raiders need more from their overall ground game. Jeanty and Washington have to help themselves out just as much as their teammates need to improve on the offensive line. It may be worth giving Laube more opportunities on offense.
Analysis: Heyward is often in position to make at least one impactful play per game.
Analysis: Forget the stats. Nailor didn't have stats when Las Vegas paid him a pretty penny in the offseason. Also, this offense isn't built to have many receivers with big numbers. The offense is more open with Nailor on the field.
It will be interesting to see how the offense looks with Thornton on the field for the first time this season. It will also be interesting to see how the offense looks with Jack Bech back in the fold.
Analysis: Statistics show that Tucker creates separation more than many receivers around the league.
Analysis: Miller looks to still be working his way back to form after missing nearly all of last season.
Analysis: The Raiders need help at offensive guard.
Analysis: Linerbaum may be overcompensating mentally and/or physically. His contract may also have added some unfair expectations.
Analysis: Las Vegas may have a bigger issue at the right guard position than meets the eye heading into the trade deadline. They certainly will after this season ends, as they must invest heavily in both offensive guard positions.
Analysis: Glaze remains dependable, but still needs improvement. Las Vegas' unwillingness to play Zuhn at guard suggests he is either not comfortable at that position or they are more confident in their starting guards, since both starting tackle positions are solidified.
Analysis: Best tight end group in the league.
Analysis: Las Vegas needs Crosby to turn it up a notch.
Analysis: Expect to see even more rotating between these three moving forward.
Analysis: The departure of Jonah Laulu should wake the interior defensive line up.
Analysis: Las Vegas needs more from Paye. More specifically, they need more from Paye against the run and on an individual level as a pass rusher.
Analysis: Las Vegas must focus on stopping the run to let their linebackers focus on helping slow down the opposing team's passing attack.
Analysis: The Raiders have an undeniable talent in Walker. They must figure out how to maximize his usage without overdoing it. The holes that remain in Las Vegas' defensive backfield and the unit's inability to stop the run leave Walker out to dry the most.
Analysis: Stokes all but eliminates big plays. They need him to eliminate the small ones with more pass breakups, like he did in his first season in Las Vegas.
Analysis: The Raiders need Johnson to be stickier in coverage. However, that is easier to do with a pass rush.
Analysis: Stukes will be tested again this week .
Analysis: Chinn is one of the most dependable players on the defense.
Analysis: One of the league's best.
Analysis: Gay must get back on track.
Analysis: Laube is close to breaking a game-changing play.
Analysis: Just solidifying the punt is a win.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Raiders vs. Jets: 3 Key Matchups To Watch Sunday
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders enter Week 8 with a favorable matchup that could help end their four-game losing skid.
The 2-5 New York Jets have performed better than expected, but are below .500 for a reason and are still a growing team with three first-round picks next spring. This is a great opportunity for head coach Klint Kubiak and the Raiders to get back on track while potentially cooling the push for quarterback Fernando Mendoza into the lineup.
With that in mind, let's look at the key matchups for Sunday's East Coast game, as Raiders fans will get their morning started with a 10 am Pacific kickoff.
Something has to give at some point for the Raiders' run game, which is next to last in yards per game and expected points added (EPA) per rush, according to Next Gen Stats . The blocking in this area has been wildly underwhelming, and it doesn't seem it will get any better, but for the first time in several weeks, Kubiak has a chance to produce on the ground.
The Jets' defense is 24th in rushing yards per game allowed (127.7), 17th in yards before contact per attempt (1.38), and 12th in yards after contact per attempt (2.66). They've tended to give up chunk plays, though, ranking tied for eighth in 10-plus-yard runs allowed per game (22).
This opens the door for the Raiders to get both Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington going on the ground. Hard to hit the gaps when blocks aren't sustained, and Las Vegas has a chance to do this more consistently in Week 8.
There are no easy solutions for the Raiders' pass defense, specifically in coverage. However, one thing I'd like to see more of is zone coverage, specifically Cover 3 and Cover 6 principles that align with those of defensive coordinator Rob Leonard's predecessor in Seattle, Mike Macdonald.
According to Next Gen Stats, the Raiders increased their man coverage rate to 32.1 percent of passing plays over the last four weeks, the seventh-highest, but have allowed a success rate of 54.5 percent, the third-highest. They've also allowed 8.7 yards per play in man (second most), correlating to sending more pressure and blitzes.
Jets quarterback Geno Smith is averaging 9.4 yards per attempt against man, the second-most in the NFL. Having man-beaters such as Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, and Omar Cooper, along with tight end Mason Taylor, has helped in that regard.
Cornerbacks Hezekiah Masses and Darien Porter have looked more comfortable playing zone, as has nickel Taron Johnson. It puts less pressure on Treydan Stukes and Jeremy Chinn at safety. I would love to see the Raiders increase their zone rate against the Jets.
We've got a fun tackle vs. pass rush duo matchup here between the Raiders and Jets. Kolton Miller has had a rough season, as Pro Football Focus has him dinged for the second-most pressures allowed by offensive tackles this season, with 23.
Right tackle DJ Glaze has emerged as a formidable presence in pass protection opposite Miller, allowing a 6.1 percent pressure rate amongst all right tackles with a minimum of 100 snaps, second-lowest in the league.
Second overall draft selection David Bailey has 34 pressures, the fifth-most in the NFL this season. Kingsley Enagbare and Will McDonald IV have combined for 33 pressures this season, the sixth-most. Head coach Aaron Glenn allows his pass rushers to tee off and get after the quarterback, and they are a handful to deal with.
Protecting Kirk Cousins is paramount, and when at his best, Miller could be a stout player at left tackle, given how well Glaze has performed. This is an intriguing matchup in the trenches, one that could have a key impact on Sunday.
Jared Feinberg, a native of western North Carolina, has written about NFL football for nearly a decade. He has contributed to several national outlets and is now part of our On SI team as an NFL team reporter. title: The Case for—and Against—Raiders Trading Maxx Crosby
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders face a few decisions as the trade deadline approaches. In less than two weeks, teams will have to decide whether to make a move or keep their roster as is for the final half of the regular season.
At 3-4, Las Vegas' front office must decide whether the team has realistic playoff hopes this season or if the future is now the focus. The next two games between now and the trade deadline should make the decision easier; even if the Raiders get to 4-4, they have to be honest with themselves.
The Raiders have beaten three of the league's worst teams. Their past four losses made it clear they are closer to the three teams they beat than the four teams they lost to. Still, this season was always meant to be a foundational year for Las Vegas.
Crosby has been the face of the franchise for most of recent history. Trading him now, or even at the deadline, would be a clear signal that the Raiders have fully turned their focus to the future. The haul he would command would likely be worth it, but trading Crosby would leave a void in the locker room.
It would also leave a significant void on the field, as replacing such a loss midseason would be nearly impossible. However, trading him for anything less than two first-round picks, a first-round pick and a player, or another draft pick would be questionable.
The idea of Las Vegas' defense taking the field without Crosby is hard to fathom. Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard recently shared his thoughts on how close Crosby is to making more of an impact on the quarterback moving forward.
“To me, it’s the consistency of disruption. That extra second of getting the quarterback on the ground, the production and the stats, that always comes in time if we just keep getting swings at bat. It’ll happen. You go watch the first two plays of the Rams game. If he doesn’t jump a little bit, you’re talking about a pump fake or not, he’s going to make the play. So, he’s very close,” Leonard said following Thursday’s practice.
The Raiders have far more reasons to trade Crosby than there are reasons not to. As the Raiders continue rebuilding their roster, Crosby will never be a more tradeable asset than he is now. It would be irresponsible for Las Vegas not to at least consider making the trade.
The more games he plays, the more wear and tear his body takes, and the older he gets, the less Las Vegas can trade him for. Given that he should at least reel in one first-round draft pick and likely more, trading him would undoubtedly expedite the rebuild.
The Raiders have fallen behind so often in the past four weeks that it has rendered Crosby and Las Vegas' pass rush useless. However, the Raiders' inability to stop the run has also factored into why they have rarely been in a position to unleash Crosby and his teammates along the defensive line in recent weeks.
"Well, we're not going to run the ball until we stop the run. Until you make the game competitive. You can't be in the fourth quarter chasing points and expect to be a good run team. So, you need attempts, and in order to get those attempts, then we have to stop the run, and we have to keep our opponent out of the end zone," Kubiak said earlier this week.
It will be much easier for Las Vegas' defense to stop the run with Crosby on the roster than without him. However, Las Vegas' front office must do what is best for the franchise's long-term future. On the surface, that would mean trading Crosby to the highest bidder.
Yet doing what is best for the team's long-term future could mean keeping their best player on the roster while he is on a contract that amounts to a team-friendly one. Las Vegas does not have to trade Crosby by any means. Unless they get a deal they cannot refuse, they should refuse to do so.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Two Things Can Be True: Raiders’ Poor Play Didn’t Erase Progress
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (3-4) go to New Jersey this weekend to face the New York Jets (2-5), with the NFL Playoffs, the trade deadline, and a rebuild all on their mind.
One of the many things I like, and would even admit to admiring, about Klint Kubiak, the Raiders' first-year head coach, is that he isn’t afraid of the obvious.
He isn’t out to deceive; in fact, deception is far from his vocabulary, but he also isn’t afraid of his shadow.
Pete Carroll's resume is lengthy and respected. He has earned that. I like Carroll and find him both genuine and warm. But that didn’t change the fact that, in each press conference, you felt like you were being sold a timeshare like the ones you find all over Las Vegas at every kiosk.
That isn’t the case with Kubiak. If he doesn’t want to answer you, he will tell you so, and if he does, he does. He doesn’t hide from the facts. That is a sign of both character and situational awareness.
That brings us to the current state of the Raiders.
They are in the midst of a rebuild we have been talking about since last December. John Spytek has masterfully steered the ship with precision, discipline, and clarity.
They did play terribly on Sunday against the Rams; it was brutal, their worst performance of the season, thus going along with the rebuilding mantra.
But here is where the dichotomy begins to show up: in the midst of that rebuild, they are overachieving and find themselves squarely in the middle of an NFL Playoff push.
I love NFL fans, especially Raider Nation, who see their fandom as a way of life.
But while they get angry at being told the team is squarely in a rebuild and that it's making a playoff push, their frustration is tangible. Justifiably so.
At the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine, GM John Spytek made it clear he builds the roster "the right way," not a quick fix.
I said at the time, and still feel, he dealt Kubiak a solid, but he said it out loud.
Even then, like now, Maxx Crosby was a big topic. Unlike then, Crosby wasn’t asking to leave. However, the quote is still germane to the Raiders right now in October. Spytek stated, "Maxx is an elite player and I've been very upfront from the start when I got here that we're in the business of having really good players on the team and we need a lot more of them. It's hard to build a great team without elite players."
Another thing Spytek said then, that I can report to you, is even more true today than in February: "We're all speaking the same language now. We've got a great process in place. And to me, it's always been about the people that you surround yourself with."
Those words should inspire Raider Nation, but like a late-night infomercial: There’s more!
Back in September, Spytek also said out loud, after the initial roster cuts down to the 53-man roster, something even more telling about the 2026 season: "We made a lot of hard choices, and we've got a long way to go, a lot of work to do with a young roster."
What does that mean in plain-spoken language? The GM made it clear that the organization is taking a methodical approach to player acquisition rather than expecting an immediate turnaround.
Bravo Spytek, and somewhere in the back, Kubiak should have yelled, Amen.
When reminded this week of Spytek’s comments, Kubiak didn’t shrink from them. There is no divide. This leadership team is 100% on the same page. But that doesn’t mean both men can be on the same page and have different roles now.
“I think from our perspective as players and coaches, that’s not something that’s on our mind. What’s on our mind is win the next game, and we’ve played very talented teams and played much more competitive games than that, being the Chiefs and the Bills. Yesterday, when you start the game that slow, you put yourself in position to be behind that much, you don’t give yourself a chance to win.”
The Las Vegas Raiders are a rebuilding franchise, making an NFL Playoff push. Sunday’s loss to the Rams was the worst of the season, and the team and organization are improving. Fernando Mendoza is the future, and Kirk Cousins is the starter, leading the NFL in touchdown passes and third in passing yards.
All of these are true. All of them are in some way contradictory. All of this is complicated and easy.
Welcome to the NFL, where more than one thing can be true.
Hondo S. Carpenter Sr. is an award-winning sports journalist with decades of experience. He serves as the Senior Writer for NFL and College sports, and is the beat writer covering the Las Vegas Raiders. Additionally, he is the editor and publisher for several sites On SI. Carpenter is a member of the Pro Football Writers Association (PFWA), the Football Writers Association of America (FWAA), and the United States Basketball Writers Association (USBWA).

title: Raiders Open Jets Week With Great Injury Report News
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders have lost four straight and are looking for any bit of momentum they can find heading into Week 8. Their matchup against the New York Jets is enough reason to be cautiously optimistic about their chances, but several other factors raise concerns.
Along with playing much earlier than they are used to, the Raiders face multiple foundational issues heading into Sunday. They are not in a position to think Sunday against the Jets will be a cakewalk, regardless of the Jets' record. Geno Smith would love to add to Las Vegas' woes.
Las Vegas appears to be getting healthier after several players participated in Wednesday's practice on a limited basis. That included Brock Bowers, Folorunso Fatukasi, DJ Glaze, Kwity Paye, Ian Thomas, and Quay Walker. Patrick Johnson did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
Tight end Carter Runyon was listed on Las Vegas' Wednesday injury report with a foot injury as he returned to practice from Injured Reserve. He fully participated in Wednesday's and Thursday's practices.
Injuries or not, the Raiders have plenty of issues they need to clean up on offense and defense. Klint Kubiak said the coaches have held the players accountable, and the players have done a solid job of holding each other accountable. The Raiders need more than just accountability, though.
“That’s the NFL. Every week you have to respond, and you’ve got to do it 17 weeks in a row. You can’t sit in those chairs in those team meeting rooms if you’re not an accountable human. If you’re just a talented guy who doesn’t have accountability, you don’t last very long. Those are the guys we’re looking for as we build our program,” Kubiak said earlier this week.
It will be up to Kubiak and his coaching staff to press the right buttons this week to shake things up. Las Vegas has not had the answers in any of the past four weeks. With their roster getting healthier heading into Week 8, the Raiders must take care of business against the Jets.
Thursday's injury report featured many of the same names, with improved statuses. Bowers, Paye, and Walker fully participated in Thursday's practice. Patrick Johnson did not practice again on Thursday. Fatukasi, Glaze, and Thomas again practiced on a limited basis on Thursday.
After not being listed on Wednesday's injury report, offensive lineman Jackson Powers-Johnson was listed on Thursday's injury report after missing practice with a back injury. His status for Sunday's game remains unclear heading into Friday's practice.
Overall, Las Vegas appears to be getting healthier. Time will tell whether that equates to improved performance from the Silver and Black. The past four weeks have shown how low the ceiling can get for this year's Raiders. This Sunday should give them a chance to prove the opposite .
Running back Ashton Jeanty was not listed on the Raiders injury report on Wednesday or Thursday. It is only the third time in eight weeks of regular-season play that Jeanty was not listed on the injury report. Still, his health will remain a significant question until he looks like himself on the field.
Receiver Jack Bech returned to practice this week and is believed to be fairly healthy heading into Sunday. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak recently explained what Bech brings to the Raiders on and off the field. Las Vegas needs all the help it can get at wide receiver, as well as other positions.
“I would start with the energy he brings to our team, his love of the game, his work habits. He just has a whole other aura about him when he’s on the field, and his teammates feel it. Coaches feel it. He’s a really solid run blocker; he’s got strong hands. Really happy to have him back out there,” Kubiak said earlier this week.
Having the likes of Tonka Hemingway and Treydan Stukes fully back, as well as other players such as Jalen Nailor back in the fold, should bode well for a Raiders team that is struggling on both sides of the ball.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Hondo's Raiders Musings: Rebuild, Playoff Push & Trade Deadline
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Raiders (3-4) go to New Jersey this weekend to face the New York Jets (2-5).
But before they make the trip across multiple time zones for a 10 AM PT kickoff, the Silver and Black have a lot of work to do.
Each week, I sit down to write a lengthy article that takes you inside the building and explains what's going on.
It is a unique time of year: in today’s NFL, the first four weeks are more of an extension of training camp because of the Collective Bargaining Agreement and the limitations not only on practice, but on how you can practice.
You then get just a handful of games to assess who you are, and then the NFL trade deadline is at hand.
In the past, the NFL trade deadline came and went with little fanfare, unlike MLB, the NHL, and even the NBA, but those times are changing.
As the Raiders weigh the future under GM John Spytek’s watchful eye and focus on the now with Klint Kubiak leading the way, so much is happening with your beloved Silver and Black, who are in the midst of an epic rebuild and in the playoff hunt.
These are fascinating times to both cover the team and, in your case, be a fan of this storied franchise. There is a lot of talk around the Raiders superstar DE Maxx Crosby and the NFL trade deadline. I will have much more to discuss on this sooner rather than later, but I can tell you this from NFL executives. The Raiders are not shopping him. I can also tell you that, unlike before, he isn't asking to get out.
It is no secret that the Raiders' offensive line has had its share of issues in 2026, but part of the blame for the running game also falls on RB Ashton Jeanty. Klint Kubiak said the running game woes aren’t all on the offensive line.
“It’s a team thing. We can all do things better, running backs, fullbacks, offensive line. It’s a team thing. We’re definitely focusing on different things with each player, but we can all improve.”
On Monday, I asked Kubiak if it was time for rookie OL Trey Zuhn III to get some reps at guard this week, and he answered matter-of-factly, “Yes.”
On Wednesday, the first-year head coach went into more detail about his development.
“I’ve seen a guy who, since the day he got here, has been a Swiss Army knife. He can play so many positions. He’s a very intelligent, hardworking player who’s still ascending and still getting better, and he’ll have his chance.”
WR Jack Bech could be back as early as this week. Whenever Kubiak determines it is time, he talked about what to expect from his sophomore.
“I would start with the energy he brings to our team, his love of the game, his work habits. He just has a whole other aura about him when he’s on the field, and his teammates feel it. Coaches feel it. He’s a really solid run blocker; he’s got strong hands. Really happy to have him back out there.”
Kubiak acknowledged that he felt there was a chance for a Bech return this week when asked if he could be ready for Sunday.
No one is more polarizing on this team than Dont’e Thornton Jr. (DTJ), a terrific young man who has struggled to make an impact. Many, myself included, thought he was headed to season-ending injured reserve (IR) at best, or possibly cut from the roster completely.
Instead, GM John Spytek kept him and elevated him back to the 53-man roster.
Kubiak pulled no punches and served no public relations Kool-Aid when asked what DTJ has to do to play in actual games.
“Well, he’s got to take the spot of another guy, so he’s got to go beat out somebody.”
Aretha Franklin re-released the old song “Respect” in 1967, and it turned into a national craze that still gets crowds dancing when played today.
When Pete Carroll arrived, there was instant respect because of all his championships, and deservedly so. But Kubiak came in and earned respect. Michael Mayer spoke after the loss to the Rams in the locker room, but honestly, it is a theme among all the players.
The locker room loves the tough-love nature of their first-year coach, and he talked about Mayer’s comments and the respect his locker room has for him.
“Well, we’re 3-4, and we’ve got a lot of season to play. It’s nice of Mike [Mayer] to say that, but shoot, we’re right in this thing.”
The Raiders are fortunate to have an elite OL coach in Rick Dennison, and with this being a rebuilding year, Kubiak addressed shaking things up on the OL and giving some guys some fresh, new, and different opportunities.
Has Kubiak settled in on rookie OL Trey Zuhn III at one spot, since he can play all five on the offensive line?
"That’s the thing, he can do a lot. You’ve got to focus in on a few, but he can do it all. He can play tackle, he can play guard, he can play center. He might be able to play quarterback, I don’t know, I haven’t let him try yet.”
Kubiak elaborated on the mental and physical acumen a player needs to move or change positions, as well as what it takes from his staff.
“There are many, especially on the offensive line. Every scheme has its own unique calls and unique techniques. But the great thing is Coach [Rick] Dennison, Coach Mario [Jeberaeel], Pete [Collins] and Ben [Wilkerson] put those guys through all of that in training camp, so there are a lot of reps we’ve banked that we’re now using to our advantage.”
But despite all that, Kubiak made it clear that Zuhn will still practice and potentially play multiple spots. “He has to play multiple positions.”
We live in a complicated world that wants easy answers. The two are diabolically opposed. Football is a complicated game, and while people want quick, easy answers to the Raiders' problems, it isn’t one thing; it rarely is in life or football.
“There’s not one big thing. There are plenty of things we’re working on that we're being intentional about. I wish it was just one thing, but it never is. Whether you’re on a 3-4 team or an undefeated team, you’re always improving your weaknesses, always trying to get players better and get the young players better who are going to play one day. That’s part of the job, preparing for one week and preparing for the future, all in the same day.”
That principle of multiple issues is even clearer when you look at a team struggling to stop the run. Kubiak again took it head-on and made it abundantly clear that it isn’t just one thing.
“It’s tackling, it’s alignment, it’s assignment. It’s just playing a better brand of football and getting back to how we started this season.”
One of the elite things WR Jack Bech does is block, which is a must for a wide receiver in the Kubiak system, and if he can come back this week, Kubiak is excited to have his blocking prowess on the field.
“I think that’s a great point. I think he has a lot of value, but I would also say the receivers who have been blocking before have been doing a really good job. Coach [Zach] Azzanni is as good as it gets with every detail of the game, especially the run game, and his guys are extremely well-prepared.”
Raiders players talked extensively in the locker room this week about accountability and holding each other to a standard. That isn’t something thrown around, and it isn’t something losing teams focus on. Whether intentional or not, it testified to the culture Kubiak is building. He talked about how that talk has translated to the locker room this week.
“That’s the NFL. Every week you have to respond, and you’ve got to do it 17 weeks in a row. You can’t sit in those chairs in those team meeting rooms if you’re not an accountable human. If you’re just a talented guy who doesn’t have accountability, you don’t last very long. Those are the guys we’re looking for as we build our program.”
No veteran leads from the front better than the NFL’s leading TD passer, QB Kirk Cousins. That is why he was at the top of Kubiak’s list to come in here, mentor, and lead while a rookie QB is learning on the bench. Kubiak talked about Cousins' presence and what he brings to the organization.

title: 2 Potential Raiders Trade Candidates Some Might Not Expect
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' 2026 season has been flipped on its head after losing four consecutive games.
After starting the season 3-0 with wins over the Dolphins, Chargers, and Saints, Las Vegas has steadily fallen in the standings with the current losing streak . Over the last several months, the Raiders were viewed as a rebuilding team, but obviously, with the impressive opening three weeks, opinions quickly shifted. Now, the Silver and Black are suddenly staring down the possibility of moving players ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
On Wednesday, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler provided insight into the latest buzz he's hearing around the league about several players being potential trade candidates. Of the 25 players included, Fowler had two Raiders on the list. Here are those players and his latest intel.
Unlike most teams, Las Vegas has a surplus of quarterback options, with Cousins, Fernando Mendoza, and Aidan O'Connell. Obviously, Mendoza hasn't started a single game, but O'Connell has a solid number of starts under his belt with the Raiders.
Earlier this week, head coach Klint Kubiak said that Mendoza will play at some point this season. If Las Vegas continues to lose games, we could see that happen sooner rather than later. Trading Cousins makes sense given O'Connell's experience as a starting and backup quarterback.
Fowler has the Panthers, Giants, and Vikings as potential fits for the 38-year-old quarterback. I don't see Carolina and New York as realistic options. The Panthers seem content with Young. Meanwhile, the Giants recently acquired JJ McCarthy from the aforementioned Vikings, and he is their third different starting quarterback of the season. So, that doesn't make much sense unless the Giants want to add insurance.
The Vikings are in a fascinating situation at 6-0, albeit Kyler Murray has been underwhelming as the starter. If head coach Kevin O'Connell believes that the former No. 1 overall pick is holding the team back, the 15-year veteran could return to Minnesota.
Las Vegas' interior offensive line has been a disaster this season and is the culprit for the team's struggles in the run game. Powers-Johnson was benched in Week 6, and with several teams needing interior offensive linemen, the Oregon product appears to be a prime trade candidate.
We saw Quenton Nelson traded on Tuesday , and while Powers-Johnson is obviously nowhere near the same tier as the former Colts' guard, it shows that other teams around the league are looking for as much offensive line help as possible.

title: How Raiders Can Put Pieces Together, Snap Skid vs. Jets
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders have had an up-and-down season so far. Through the season's first seven games, the Raiders have shown several different versions of themselves. In their three wins, albeit against teams with a combined 3-16 record, Las Vegas played solid football.
In their wins, the Raiders played complementary football, which helped them overcome mistakes. In two of their four losses, Las Vegas didn't show up until the game was legitimately out of reach. In their other two losses, they played well against two of the league's best.
Las Vegas heads into its Week 8 matchup against the New York Jets, aiming to end its losing streak, as a fifth straight loss would be far from ideal. No matter how much spin is put on it, a five-game losing streak would raise many questions about the season's direction.
Even at 3-4 and in the middle of a losing streak, Las Vegas has enough games remaining to turn the season around if they make the right decisions and win the games they can.
Plenty has gone wrong over the past four weeks for Klint Kubiak's Raiders. However, they have also made things tough on themselves, with a long list of mistakes. Few things would have changed Las Vegas' losses against the New England Patriots and Los Angeles Rams.
Those two games got out of hand too fast to believe the Raiders could have won, regardless of what they could have done differently. Las Vegas' losses to the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills made it fair to wonder how good this team could be this season.
Still, four straight losses are four straight losses. Kubiak knows that after the season's first seven games, his team has a lot of things to work on. There is no one thing for Las Vegas to focus on; all options are on the table in terms of its roster and the ways in which it will look to improve.
“There’s not one big thing. There are plenty of things we’re working on that we're being intentional about. I wish it was just one thing, but it never is. Whether you’re on a 3-4 team or an undefeated team," Kubiak said after practice on Wednesday.
"You’re always improving your weaknesses, always trying to get players better and get the young players better who are going to play one day. That’s part of the job: preparing for one week and preparing for the future, all in the same day.”
Las Vegas has handled its four-game losing streak better than it handled its losing streaks each of the past two seasons, but that is no consolation for losing. The Raiders started the season too well to be content with close losses and almost-wins. They have the roster to win games this season.
The Raiders' Week 8 matchup against their former quarterback, Geno Smith, and a Jets team loaded with three first-round draft picks in the 2027 draft is ripe for a Raiders win on Sunday. Yet that is only true if they can fix the issues that have plagued them over the past month.
Many of those issues have started to recur weekly as teams get a clearer idea of what the Raiders do and don't do well. Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins noted several things he feels Las Vegas' offense can improve on heading into their Week 8 road slate.
“We can be better in the red zone. We can be better on third down. When plays are there to be made, you’ve got to make them. It’s a fine line between winning a game and losing a game. It can be one play. It can be one throw. You can say, ‘I’m playing great, having good production, things are going well,’ but if you miss one throw and you lost the game, you missed one throw, and you lost the game, ” Cousins said Wednesday after practice.
"You play with that tension, and you prepare with that tension. I think that's where you say absolutely you can be doing better, because not playing perfect, and the only time you get away with not playing perfect is if you’re winning. Other than that, you either need to be playing perfect or you need to be winning. So, there’s plenty of room for improvement.”
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Tre Tucker's Latest Emergence Has Raiders Excited for Potential
full_text:
Amid a four-game losing streak, a player on the Las Vegas Raiders offense has begun to re-emerge into the spotlight.
Wide receiver Tre Tucker has been one of the most consistent elements of the Raiders roster over the past few seasons, including this year. The former Cincinnati standout is one of the fastest players on the field each Sunday. Las Vegas head coach Klint Kubiak has noticed that as his involvement in the offense has expanded.
After catching five passes for 103 yards and a touchdown, Tucker is seeing his role grow before his very eyes. The chemistry with starting quarterback Kirk Cousins has been a big reason for the sudden jump in production.
It's always important for your No. 1 wide receiver and quarterback to have good chemistry. While there have been bumps along the way, I believe Cousins and Tucker are starting to find the right balance, even if last week's game against the Los Angeles Rams didn't always produce consistent results (five catches on 12 targets).
As mentioned, Tucker's expanded role within Kubiak's explosive passing offense has allowed him and Cousins to build more connections. The veteran quarterback is encouraged by what he's seen.
"Tre’s done a great job. Even more importantly, the chemistry is good," Cousins said. "It’ll keep getting better. But I think just expanding his role and just allowing him to do more and more. As we’ve given him more, he keeps showing that he can do it. I’m encouraged by it and would love to see him keep doing more up ahead."
Tucker has always been known for his speed, and the Raiders are showing he can wear multiple hats on offense, lining up out wide, in the slot, in motion across the formation, orbit motions, and shifts. In the fourth and final season of his rookie contract, Tucker is showing more than usual; you can call it a job interview for the Raiders brass and 31 other NFL teams. Cousins said as much on Wednesday:
"Well, I think we’ve just given him more to do, more routes, more ways to contribute, and I think he’s taken advantage of those opportunities," Cousins said. "I think he traits were always there. Sometimes when you’re really, really fast, it’s tempting to only have him do the fast things and have the slower guys do the slower things."
"There’s nothing wrong with having Tre do those things too and wear different hats. He’s shown he can do a lot. He doesn’t just need to be the fast guy.”
To Cousins' point, Tucker certainly doesn't need to be the fast guy. It's been delightful to see his role expand in the Raiders' offense and the production that comes with it. However, it doesn't take away from the fact that Tucker is still more of a role player and No. 2 wide receiver in most offenses.
To Tucker's credit, he has been great for Las Vegas in recent weeks and past seasons, developing into a dependable pass-catcher. I still believe the Raiders need to add more upper-tier talent at wide receiver, or a high-ceiling pass-catcher with the potential to be one.
They could still pair one with Tucker, assuming he returns next season and beyond. For now, the production continues to prove critics, myself included, wrong while building more chemistry with Cousins.

title: Why the Dolphins Could Be (Very) Quiet at the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
There have been three significant deals around the NFL this week, but that might be just beginning ahead of the trade deadline November 10, and it's pretty obvious that some teams are in selling mode — maybe even firesale mode.
The Miami Dolphins do not appear one of those teams.
The Indianapolis Colts already have unloaded star veterans DeForrest Buckner and Quenton Nelson, while their AFC South counterparts Tennessee Titans just moved star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.
The Los Angeles Chargers have their share of veteran players expected to be traded as well, starting with edge defender Khalil Mack and possibly including star safety Derwin James.
What those teams have in common is they're not going anywhere in 2026 — when it comes to the playoffs, that is — with records of 2-5, 1-6 and 0-6.
The Dolphins are 1-5 and also realistically not going to be factors in the playoff race, and they do have some players who might be of interest to other teams.
That doesn't mean they're in sellling mode and willing to trade any veteran who's not on his first contract and could fetch a decent draft pick in return.
Just Friday morning, for example, SI national writer Albert Breer reported that the Dolphins have taken calls on defensive tackle Zach Sieler and center Aaron Brewer "but quickly rebuffed that."
Yes, they're in rebuilding mode. Yes, they could use all the additional draft capital they can get to beef up their nucleus of young players who hopefully can bring the team back into contention.
But the reality is the Dolphins are going to need good veteran players beyond 2026 and not have a team filled with second-, third- or fourth-year players.
They'll need players like Sieler and Brewer, and linebacker Jordyn Brooks is another who fits into that category.
And, yes, there was a suggestion not too long ago that he could be involved in a trade.
And the same thing we said about Brooks back then applies to Brewer now: Why in the world would the Dolphins trade him now after signing him in the offseason to a contract extension precisely because he represented the kind of player with whom the team wants to fill its roster.
Sieler is a different case because he's over 30 and he's got big cap numbers coming up over the final three years of his contract, but he's also still a very good player (he's the best defensive lineman on the team and there's probably not a close second right now) and he's also a very good leader on a very young team.
Simply put, Sieler is more valuable than whatever the Dolphins realistically could get in a trade, and this won't change unless a team gets desperate for D-tackle help after watching Buckner and Simmons go off the market.
It also shouldn't be dismissed that Sieler has made it very clear — as he keeps getting asked every time he speaks to the media these days — that he wants to stay in Miami, where he's been since the Dolphins claimed him off waivers from the Baltimore Ravens in December 2019.
Edge defender Joshua Uche is another player who has expressed his desire to stay in Miami, citing among other things his respect for first-year head coach Jeff Hafley.
He's another one who was pegged as a trade candidate, in his case because he's a veteran who signed only a one-year deal this offseason and is scheduled to become an unrestricted free agent in March.
But Uche has played more than well enough that the Dolphins should very strongly consider bringing him back at least another season — at the right price, of course.
And, again, it says here he'll be worth more to the Dolphins in 2027 and maybe even 2028 than whatever late-round pick they could get for him.
The one player who always has stood as the most likely to be trade is tackle Austin Jackson, who is the second-longest-tenured player on the team after Sieler.
The 2020 first-round pick is scheduled to become a free agent after the season after accepting a pay cut to return to the Dolphins this year, and his performance in 2026 has been pretty uneven.
Bigger issues are what kind of money Jackson would want in his next contract, whether the Dolphins want to move rookie first-round pick Kadyn Proctor to right tackle, as has been assumed all along, and whether Jackson would want to come back — he hasn't been as adamant as Sieler and Uche about wanting to stay.
The Dolphins probably have an idea by now whether they see Jackson as part of their plan beyond 2026, and if he's not, then it would behoove them to try to get any kind of draft pick for him because they're not likely to be in the free agent compensation game next offseason.
At this time, though, this has the makings of a pretty uneventful trade deadline for the Dolphins even if their record might have suggested otherwise at one point.

title: Thursday Injury Update: Big Names Could Be Missing from Dolphins-Patriots Matchup
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins look like they're going to be without their top rookie draft pick when they try to upset the New England Patriots on Sunday, but they also might not have to face New England's prized offseason acquisition.
Starting with the Dolphins, guard Kadyn Proctor missed a second consecutive practice with a concussion, and it's very difficult to envision him getting clearance to play Sunday.
Based on the NFL's five-step Return to Play protocol, Proctor still has to go through "non-contact training drills" and then "full football activity involving contact."
With the Dolphins down to one practice before a walk-through Saturday, it's again difficult to envision Proctor getting clearance in time and also know that the team is going to err on the side of caution here.
The final injury report will come out Friday and at this time it would be a surprise if Proctor weren't ruled out.
Head coach Jeff Hafley indicated Wednesday that backup Jarrett Kingston would be taking Proctor's reps at left guard during practice. Kingston was the one who replaced Jonah Savaiinaea at right guard after the 2025 second-round pick was injured in the first half of the Week 5 loss at Hard Rock Stadium.
Kingston, who obviously is the No. 3 guard on the roster, was claimed off waivers from the Houston Texans after the cuts to 53.
For those wondering about new guard Christian Haynes, claimed off waivers from the Seattle Seahawks on Wednesday, there's basically zero chance he would start that quickly and he actually probably will be inactive for his first game on the Dolphins roster.
With the Patriots, the big news involved wide receiver A.J. Brown, who the team acquired in a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles in the offseason.
After being limited in practice because of an ankle injury Wednesday, Brown sat out Thursday and now also is dealing with a knee issue.
This sort of downward trend would make it seem unlikely he'll play against the Dolphins on Sunday, though we'll get more info on the final injury report.
This obviously would be an advantageous development for the Dolphins, who had all sorts of problems with Brown when they faced the Eagles in 2023. Brown had 10 catches for 137 yards and a touchdown in Miami's 31-17 loss at Lincoln Financial Field in a Sunday night game that year.
At least the Dolphins got a positive development with cornerback JuJu Brents, who's also dealing with a concussion.
After sitting out practice Wednesday, he was back at practice Thursday, albeit on a limited basis.
This puts him on track to go through a full practice Friday and then get clearance to play against the Patriots.
The rest of the Dolphins injury report Thursday remained the same with the same 13 players on it, highlighted by quarterback Malik Willis.
After earlier this season being listed with a toe issue and then with a thumb injury, this time Willis is dealing with a groin injury, but he was again a full participant in practice Thursday.
Also fully participating for a second consecutive day was edge defender Rob Beal Jr., who has missed the past four games because of a hamstring injury.
The injury report again eight other players listed as limited participants.
On the list was cornerback Reese Taylor, who missed the past three games with a quad injury, and long-snapper Tucker Addington and tight end Will Kacmarek both were on the injury report last week before playing in the 28-25 victory against the New York Jets.
The other five players listed as limited were TE Greg Dulcich (ankle), S Michael Taaffe (neck/foot), S Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder), WR Malik Washington (knee) and WR Jared Wayne (knee).
Besides Brown, the one change on the Patriots injury report involved running back TreVeyon Henderson, who did not practice Thursday because of illness.
Henderson, a second-year second-round pick out of Ohio State, has had a slow start to his 2026 seaosn as the backfield partner to Rhamondre Stevenson, but he did score two touchdowns against Miami in the 2025 season finale.
Starting right tackle Morgan Moses (foot) against was limited, while QB Drake Maye was listed with a right shoulder injury, but he was a full participant.
As expected, DJ Campbell cleared waivers, so the Dolphins now can re-sign him to their practice squad if they choose.
The team's rookie sixth-round pick was waived to make room on the roster when the Dolphins claimed Haynes off waivers, and it's not a reach to predict Campbell will be re-signed and replace converted defensive lineman James Ester on the practice squad.
In former Dolphins news, veteran Charlie Heck has found a team after failling to make the 53-man roster as an unrestricted free agent pick-up. He signed with the Indianapolis Colts.

title: Revisiting the Jaelan Phillips Trade One Year Later and How It's Played Out for the Dolphins
full_text:
As the 2026 NFL trade deadline creeps closer, the Miami Dolphins remain a team to watch because of their status as a rebuilding franchise.
While that rebuilding process got into full swing after the regime change that brought in Jon-Eric Sullivan as general manager and Jeff Hafley as head coach, an argument can be made that it actually began at the trade deadline last year.
The Dolphins made only one deal, but it was one done with an eye toward the future.
And looking back at it almost one year later, it's pretty clear the Dolphins did well when they sent outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips to the Philadelphia Eagles in exchange for a third-round pick.
That pick became the 87th overall in the 2026 draft, and the Dolphins used it on tight end Will Kacmarek from Ohio State as one of their three selections in that round.
The trade of Phillips, done days after Champ Kelly had become interim general manager following the firing of Chris Grier, pretty much was done with the salary cap in mind because Phillips was in the middle of the final year of his contract.
The Dolphins clearly decided they did not want to give Phillips the kind of contract he would be seeking as a free agent, so the idea was to get something for him before he left.
Because the highest compensatory draft pick any team can get for a free agent loss comes at the end of the third round, starting with the 97th overall pick, the Dolphins were able to get something better from the Eagles and they got it a year early.
After Phillips signed a four-year, $120 million deal with the Carolina Panthers in the offseason, it's the Eagles who now will be in line to receive a compensatory pick for losing him, but it will come in the 2027 draft and, again, later than the pick the Dolphins got in the trade.
Phillips' deal with Carolina included $80 million guaranteed, with a cap number that jumps from $10 million this year to over $30 million each of the next three years, according to OverTheCap.com.
The 18th overall selection in the 2021 NFL draft, Phillips has been a solid to good NFL player, but it would be a tough sell for anyone to suggest he's worth the kind of money he got from the Panthers — then again, "the market is the market," right?
For certain, Phillips isn't worth that kind of deal with where the Dolphins are as an organization.
The early returns on Kacmarek suggest he's every bit the blocking stud his scouting report indicated he could be in the NFL, and his role only figures to increase the more experience he gets.
And, yes, the Dolphins absolutely could use Phillips this season to help their struggling pass rush — Chop Robinson's eye-opening metrics notwithstanding — but then again he's once again dealing with injury issues in Carolina.
That unfortunately became part of Phillips' story in Miami and another reason it was impossible to justify giving him a huge contract even though he's still only 27 years old.
When the Panthers face the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on Thursday night, Phillips will be on the inactive list, missing a second consecutive game because of a hamstring injury.
Phillips has 2.5 sacks in five games so far this season — that total, while pretty modest — would lead the Dolphins right now because the team leaders are Zach Sieler and Robinson with two each.
Phillips, of course, missed the second half of the 2023 season and most of the 2024 season because of Achilles and knee injuries, which obviously is just bad luck.
But it doesn't change the fact the Dolphins were right in not wanting to give him that big contract extension and their trade was a very good one at the time that's still very good one year later.

title: What to Know About the Dolphins' New Guard
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins' continuing search for hidden gems landed them a former third-round pick who won a Super Bowl ring last season.
The Dolphins were awarded guard Christian Haynes off waivers from the Seattle Seahawks, making room for him on the 53-man roster by waiving rookie sixth-round pick DJ Campbell.
Haynes appeared in all seven games for Seattle this season and made five starts, but he was waived after the Seahawks acquired eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson this week in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts. He appeared in 24 games as a backup in his first two NFL seasons.
The Baltimore Ravens had announced earlier Wednesday that they picked up Haynes on waivers, but the Dolphins had a higher waiver priority spot because of their worse record — after the third week of the regular season, the overall league standings are used in case more than one team claims a player.
Haynes was a third-round pick out of UConn in the 2024 NFL draft who was the 81st overall selection.
This was his NFL.com draft scouting report in 2024: "Four-year starter and team captain who is sturdy at the point of attack. Haynes plays with football intelligence and sees every snap as a mandate to move opponents and finish blocks. His draft slotting could be affected by a lack of length and being limited to one position, but his determined playing style counters those factors. He’s not overly rangy but wipes out targets on pulling blocks and is capable in space, and in pass protection. The hand usage can get sloppy, allowing opponents to slip away from him, and he has a tendency to do too much grabbing. All things considered, he might outplay his draft slotting and become a solid NFL starter."
Haynes joins a group of Dolphins backup offensive linemen that consists of center Andrew Meyer, guard Jarrett Kingston, guard/tackle Caedan Wallace and tackle Chukwuebuka Godrick.
Where Haynes fit into the 10-man group obviously will come down to what he shows the coaches in practice and how quickly he can learn the offense.
Campbell becomes the second of the Dolphins' 13 draft selections to be cut from the 53-man roster after seventh-round selection Max Llewellyn.
As happened with Llewellyn, it's entirely possible the Dolphins will bring him back to the practice squad if he clears waivers, though now they're OK with taking that chance.
Campbell joined Godrick, claimed off waivers from the Kansas City Chiefs, on the inactive list every game so far this season as the clear ninth and 10th offensive linemen on the roster.

title: Breaking Down a New Willis Issue and the Two Concussions on the Dolphins' Lengthy Injury Report
full_text:
If the Miami Dolphins are going to make it two in a row after getting their first victory of the season, they might have to overcome some injury issues.
Only two players on the active roster missed the first practice ahead of the team's Week 8 game against the New England Patriots, but both rookie guard Kadyn Proctor and cornerback JuJu Brents were out because they're in the concussion protocol.
Because of the fickle nature of concussions, it's impossible to predict whether either or both will be able to play against the Patriots, and Brents was spotted on the outside practice fields at the Baptist Health Training Complex doing conditioning work, which clearly is a good sign.
The first injury report of the week for the Dolphins was a long one with 13 names on it, and a new issue for quarterback Malik Willis.
After earlier this season being listed with a toe issue and then with a thumb injury, this time Willis is dealing with a groin injury, although he was a full participant in practice Wednesday.
Another full participant was edge defender Rob Beal Jr., who has missed the past four games because of a hamstring injury.
The injury report, though, featured eight players listed as limited participants.
On the list was cornerback Reese Taylor, who missed the past three games with a quad injury, and long-snapper Tucker Addington and tight end Will Kacmarek both were on the injury report last week before playing in the 28-25 victory against the New York Jets.
The other five players listed as limited were TE Greg Dulcich (ankle), S Michael Taaffe (neck/foot), S Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder), WR Malik Washington (knee) and WR Jared Wayne (knee). Only Trader had an injury reported in the press box Sunday, so it's possible than any of the other four were injured in practice.
Head coach Jeff Hafley revealed the concussions before practice before taking questions from the assembled media.
Hafley also indicated that backup Jarrett Kingston would be taking Proctor's reps at left guard during practice. Kingston was the one who replaced Jonah Savaiinaea at right guard after the 2025 second-round pick was injured in the first half of the Week 5 loss at Hard Rock Stadium.
Kingston, who obviously is the No. 3 guard on the roster, was claimed off waivers from the Houston Texans after the cuts to 53.
If Brents can't play against New England, then Jason Marshall Jr. would take his place in a normal (four-DB) defensive alignment and Jaylin Simpson likely would be the choice to line up outside with Marshall if/when the Dolphins want to slide rookie Chris Johnson in the slot in the nickel.
New England's injury report wasn't much smaller than that of the Dolphins with 12 names, but the Patriots didn't have anybody miss practice.
The most prominent players among those who were limited were wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) and starting right tackle Morgan Moses (foot).
Quarterback Drake Maye was listed with a right shoulder injury, but he was a full participant.

title: Should the Dolphins Make a Trade Pitch for Former First-Round Pick? And What Should They Offer?
full_text:
We've reached the part of the NFL season when general managers are working the phones, looking to bring a shiny new toy to their city.
In some cases, it's about acquiring the final piece or two to fuel a playoff run. For teams like the Miami Dolphins , it's about gradually building a foundation that could eventually deliver a return on the investment.
The name of the day is Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr., who Sports Illustrated's Conor Orr recently identified as a potential trade target for Miami ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.
With Miami potentially selecting a quarterback early in the 2027 NFL Draft, trading for a young receiver with proven upside could give their next signal-caller a much-needed weapon.
But would Thomas be worth the investment?
After a PFWA All-Rookie campaign when he set Jacksonville franchise rookie records with 87 receptions, 1,282 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns, Thomas' role has gradually diminished to the point where he's now the team's fourth-leading wide receiver in receiving yards.
Thomas has just nine receptions for 105 yards and one touchdown through six games this season, which would rank fifth even in Miami's limited passing offense.
The regression is tangible, perhaps most evident in the fact that Thomas has failed to catch any of the last five passes thrown in his direction.
A look at his film reveals an athletic specimen who still struggles with the intricacies of route running while regularly failing to adjust to passes that require extra body control.
The trajectory that once seemed destined to make him one of the league's premier X receivers has been altered. But it's not like he's had his abilities stolen like Michael Jordan did in Space Jam .
In attempting to develop Thomas into a reliable top receiver, Jacksonville has seemingly moved away from some of the quick-hitting concepts that once allowed him to showcase his natural athleticism.
According to Pro Football Focus charting, Thomas has run just one slant route and no screens this season, limiting opportunities to get the ball into his hands quickly and capitalize on the 4.33-second speed that once had scouts enamored at the NFL combine.
There is still an explosive player somewhere in there. The question is whether Miami would be capable of bringing him back out.
The most recent comparison is Marvin Harrison Jr., who the Houston Texans acquired from the Arizona Cardinals earlier this month.
Houston gave up a 2027 second-round pick and a seventh-round selection in exchange for Harrison and a sixth-rounder, which gives an interesting benchmark for what Jacksonville might seek in return for Thomas.
For Miami, surrendering a pick in the second round should be off the table.
Productive complementary receivers can be found in the second and third rounds with proper scouting, without requiring Miami to gamble on reviving another organization's former first-round pick.
But a fourth- or fifth-round selection?
That's an entirely different conversation.
At that price, Thomas could inject some much-needed speed and life into an offense that has struggled to consistently generate explosive plays through the air.
Tyler M. Carmona is a Miami native whose work has appeared in the Miami Herald and Associated Press. He previously worked as a local television news reporter. He recently graduated from Columbia University’s Graduate School of Journalism and played college football at Savannah State University and the University of St. Francis

title: Dolphins Week 8 Power Rankings Roundup: How Big of a Move Up After First Win?
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins no longer are being viewed as the worst team in the NFL — by anybody.
At least, that's the verdict in our latest weekly survey of NFL power rankings from 10 national outlets — Yahoo Sports, Sports Illustrated, ESPN, The Athletic, NFL.com, USA Today, Pro Football Talk, FOX Sports, The Sporting News, CBS Sports — with the Dolphins posting an average ranking of 29th.
But no one has them 32nd, the worst ranking coming from Conor Orr of Sports Illustrated at 31. The Dolphins were ranked as high as 26th by NFL.com's Nick Shook in the aftermath of their 28-25 victory against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium, a game where the Dolphins never trailed.
This obviously is a move in the right direction after the Dolphins were ranked either 31st or 32nd by all 10 outlets last week.
The Dolphins' next opponents, the New England Patriots, have an average ranking of 10.4, with a high of eighth from USA Today and a low of 11th from six outlets.
At 1-5, the Dolphins now have the third-worst record in the NFL behind the Los Angeles Chargers' 0-6 and the Tennessee Titans' 1-5. The Washington Commanders are the other team with fewer than two victories as they stand at 1-4-1 coming off their bye.
As a reminder, strength of schedule is the tiebreaker for draft position between teams that finish with the same record, with the higher the SOS, the lower the pick. The Dolphins' current combined opponent winning percentage mark of .589 is the highest in the NFL, meaning they would pick lower in any tiebreaker scenario.
That's for down the line, though, because the Dolphins are hoping to win more games after getting on the board against the Jets.
The Sporting News ( Vinnie Iyer)
Analysis: The Dolphins put on their first winning costume of the season with an offense pulling out all kinds of treats with youngster Ollie Gordon II and Caleb Douglas. They were overdue for that much-needed first win under Jeff Hafley. Watch them to play spoiler a few more times vs. better teams.
Analysis: They won! That's a great sign coming out of the bye. They aren't in the cellar of these rankings anymore as the young players continue to improve.
Analysis: “Thinking of me as a little kid in the parking lot as we (came to the Meadowlands), I was one of the those guys flipping off the buses, and now here I am," said New Jersey native and first-year Fins coach Jeff Hafley after his team upset the Jets to finally break into the win column. Way to also flip off all of those observers who thought your team might become the 0-17 bookend to the 17-0 1972 Dolphins, Coach.
FOX Sports (Ralph Vacchiano)
Analysis: Admit it. You knew the Dolphins were going to beat the Jets on Sunday. I mean, if they were going to win one game all season long, that was always going to be it. And of course, it would be at MetLife Stadium. Every Jets fan knew it when they bought their ticket to that game. The Dolphins did it in style, too. Malik Willis threw a 63-yard touchdown pass in the fourth quarter. RB Ollie Gordon ran all over the Jets for 103 yards. And the Miami defense got the big fourth-quarter stop when they needed it. Enjoy it, because things are almost certainly going to get worse — at least until they play the Jets again in Miami on Nov. 29.
Analysis: The Dolphins won a game! Malik Willis posted a passer rating north of 130! Ollie Gordon II ran hard and Caleb Douglas scored two touchdowns! Miami even survived a perfect meltdown scenario and managed to stay intact and ice a victory! Can you tell I’m excited?? Sometimes, it feels good to watch undermanned, rebuilding teams play well enough to emerge victorious. Those types of seasons are already long enough.
The Athletic (Chad Graff and Josh Kendall)
Analysis: Sure, we could focus on the Dolphins’ woeful defensive stats, but let’s focus on their no-doubter of a win. Although the final score made it appear close, they never trailed and were up 21-7 at the half and 28-17 with four minutes left. It was an impressive first victory for coach Jeff Hafley.
Analysis (on the best offseason addition, LB Jacob Rodriguez): The Dolphins were so impressed by their second-round pick this summer that they waived Tyrel Dodson, last season's starter. And the rookie has repaid their faith. Rodriguez set the tone with 14 tackles in Week 1 and eventually set a franchise rookie record with 18 tackles in Week 4. He is second in the NFL in tackles per game (10.2) and 15th in run stop wins (49). General manager Jon-Eric Sullivan said on draft night that Rodriguez would call the Dolphins' defense at some point -- and he was ready to do so in Week 1. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques
Pro Football Talk (Mike Florio)
Analysis: Only five weeks until the next Jets game.
Sports Illustrated (Conor Orr)
Analysis: I think people ripping the Dolphins for celebrating Jeff Hafley’s first win simply don’t get it. The fact that there is this much juice and energy for one of the worst teams in the NFL shows exactly where this team is headed.
Yahoo Sports (Frank Schwab)
Analysis: The Dolphins can relax. There was always the hope that the team with the NFL's thinnest roster could beat the Jets in one of their two meetings, and that happened. Everyone focuses on the winless teams in the NFL but nobody remembers the one-loss teams, so the Dolphins are spared a lot of grief that would have come had their winless season continued through November. They're still probably not the 29th best team in the NFL but they deserved a bump up after outplaying the Jets.

title: What to Know About the Latest Wave of Dolphins Tryout Players
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins' 53-man roster remains a work in progress, as GM Jon-Eric Sullivan has indicated on multiple occasions since the spring, so it was only natural to have more player tryouts Tuesday.
Especially since the team has an opening on the roster.
The Dolphins brought in eight players for tryouts Tuesday, with a heavy emphasis on the tight end position. Four of the players brought played that position, along with two defensive tackles, one quarterback and one defensive end.
As has been the case for most of the tryouts this year for Miami, the list was comprised of young players with little or no NFL game experience.
The list: QB Derek Robertson, Monmouth TE Jaheim Bell, Florida State TE Devin Culp, Washington TE Rivaldo Fairweather, Auburn TE Joshua Simon, South Carolina DE Anthony Goodlow, Oklahoma State DT Cole Brevard, Texas DT Jay Toia, UCLA
Of those eight players, Bell, Culp, Goodlow and Toia are the only ones with NFL game experience, those it ranges from five to 18 games for Culp.
Bell, Culp and Toia entered the NFL as seventh-round draft picks, while the other five were undrafted rookie free agents, including Brevard and Robertson this year. Robertson's only NFL exposure came when he attended the Jacksonville Jaguars rookie minicamp as a tryout player.
This tryout, like all the ones before, shouldn't be viewed as a precursor to a signing, though it has happened this year, most recently with Zane Gonzalez beating out three other kickers to land a spot on the practice squad after the team released incumbent Riley Patterson.
The Dolphins didn't replace Patterson the 53, which is why they have an opening, but Gonzalez can only be elevated for a game two more times before the Dolphins have to put him on the 53-man roster or find another kicker.
The likelihood is this latest tryout was about gathering intel on potential future signings. If we're looking at tight ends, the Dolphins already have three rookies at the position with third-round pick Will Kacmarek, fifth-round pick Seydou Traore and waiver wire pick-up Justin Joly, himself a fifth-round pick of the Denver Broncos.
In a full-circle moment, outside linebacker/edge defender Andre Jones Jr. rejoined the Buffalo Bills practice squad, which is where the Dolphins got him for their 53-man roster before eventually waiving him after three games.
Jones played 45 games on special teams for Miami in those three games.
Elsewhere: -- Former Dolphins punter Matt Haack had a tryout with the Tennessee Titans. -- Tackle Charlie Heck, who failed to make Miami's 53-man roster after signing as an unrestricted free agent in the offseason, had a tryout with the New York Jets. -- Tight end Ben Sims, who was waived/injured after also signing as a UFA in the offseason, had a tryout with the Seattle Seahawks.

title: Examining the Impact of the Nelson Trade on the Dolphins
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is now two weeks away, but there was a significant trade Tuesday.
The immediate impact for the Miami Dolphins of the Indianapolis Colts beginning their expected fire sale by sending perennial Pro Bowl Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks is that their Week 10 game at Lucas Oil Stadium might become a lot more winnable than it once was.
There are potentially other implications beyond that game on November 15, though.
The reported return for Nelson, who will become a free agent after the season and no doubt will get a massive free agent deal, was a third-round pick in the 2027 NFL draft along with a fifth-round selection in 2028.
The trade compensation is important to note as a comparison point for all the teams looking or willing to deal players before the trade deadline November 10.
While they're coming off a victory, the Dolphins remain — or at least should remain — focused on the big picture and treat their personnel with the future in mind, meaning they should listen to offers for any players and maybe seek deals for those they don't see as part of the team beyond this season.
Tackle Austin Jackson has long been assumed on the way out because he's a pretty expensive player in the final year of his contract, he's not having a great year and the Dolphins have their future right tackle on the roster with Kadyn Proctor if they decide to switch him there instead of keeping him at left guard where he's showing great promise as a rookie.
While the Nelson trade compensation doesn't really apply when it comes to Jackson — as it doesn't to a whole lot of offensive linemen around the NFL — maybe it becomes a better barometer for someone like defensive tackle Zach Sieler.
The question, of course, is whether the Dolphins even want to trade Sieler, who's not only a good player in the middle of the defensive line but a leader on a team with an abundance of young players.
While Sieler isn't an All-Pro like Nelson, he is under contract through the next three years after this one, though with no guaranteed salary, giving an acquiring team flexiblity in terms of how to proceed forward with him.
If Nelson fetched a third and a fifth in a trade, what could the Dolphins get for Sieler? The obvious answer is whatever a team — say, the New York Giants — needing help at defensive tackle is willing to give up,
Realistically, it's always felt as though maybe the best the Dolphins could do was get a third-round pick and that likely would entail them giving up a late-round pick in addition to Sieler.
Jackson, because his contract expires, he has a long injury history and has had issues in pass protection, probably wouldn't fetch more than a late-round pick.
That game against the Colts will come five days after the trade deadline, and it's entirely possible that Nelson won't be the only star player gone from Indy by then.
After GM Chris Ballard was fired following the Colts' loss against the Tennessee Titans, it looks like the team is headed for a full rebuild and players like Jonathan Taylor and DeForrest Buckner also could be moved.
One thing for sure, that Colts team isn't going to look the same as the one the Dolphins saw in the 2025 opener when they left Indianapolis with a 33-8 loss.
