title: One Jets DT Has Bulletin Board Material After Ashton Jeanty's Disrespectful Comments
full_text:
As the Jets try to recover from their rock-bottom performance against the previously winless Dolphins last Sunday, all eyes turn to the second of back-to-back home games against the 3-4 Raiders in a Week 8 clash at MetLife Stadium.
While the writing appears to be on the wall for head coach Aaron Glenn after another disappointing loss, there have been just as many concerns on the field as there have been on the sideline. One recurring issue for the Jets has been the poor play from the defensive line, specifically the defensive tackle position.
Veteran DT Harrison Phillips has been a huge disappointment so far, but he should have some extra motivation to step up his game after some recent comments from Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty.
" Yeah, I think we can definitely get the run game going (vs. the Jets)," Jeanty said, per The 33rd Team NFL insider Ari Meirov. "Get back on track. ... A couple guys out there that don't really want to tackle, but I'm not going to say names."
#Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty on facing the #Jets defense this week: "Yeah. I think we can definitely get the run game going. Get back on track. ... A couple guys out there that don't really want to tackle, but I'm not going to say names." 😳 pic.twitter.com/ySSn53MpMC
It is safe to say Jeanty believes he will have no difficulty whatsoever getting the run game going against this Jets defensive front.
On Thursday, Jets defensive coordinator Brian Duker admitted to seeing Jeanty's comments, but reiterated that he has "plenty of confidence" in his unit (h/t SNY Jets ).
Phillips is one of the most respected players on the roster, but the 30-year-old has clearly worn out his welcome in Gotham with just 12 solo tackles against the run and zero sacks through seven weeks. He has been a glaring issue on the interior of the Jets' defensive line, but Jeanty's comments could be exactly what Phillips needs to use as motivation and shut him up to turn his outlook on the Jets around.
Before arriving in Gotham for the 2025 season, Phillips played for the Bills and Vikings across his first seven seasons and recorded a total of eight sacks. During his time with the Jets, Phillips has regressed, with just 0.5 sacks and one forced fumble, both of which came last season.
Pro Football Focus paints an even bigger picture for Phillips through the season's first seven games. He is credited with the 102nd-ranked overall grade (49.2) out of 126 qualified interior defenders, in addition to the 98th-ranked pass-rush grade (56) and the 69th-ranked run-defense grade (52.8). Those grades alone do not tell the entire story, but they point to a player who has been a huge liability on the field this season.
It is not out of the question, though, that he can turn things around in a favorable matchup this week. The Raiders average the second-fewest rush yards per game (74.7 ypg), while Jeanty only has an average of 3.1 yards per carry on 106 touches with one touchdown.
If there were ever an opportunity for the Jets' 24th-ranked rushing defense (127.7 ypg) to capitalize on, this is it.
Phillips has outperformed offseason acquisition T'Vondre Sweat in terms of total tackles (22-17) and one forced fumble, but he has also been outplayed by backup Jowon Briggs, who has 26 total tackles, two sacks, three tackles for loss and a forced fumble. Briggs, however, possesses a worse PFF overall grade (44.4) and run-defense grade (37.4), so the opportunity is certainly in front of Phillips to take advantage.
Even before Jeanty's comments, Phillips was going to have a little more on his plate after Sweat exited the loss to the Dolphins with a knee injury and did not return. He was listed as week-to-week on Wednesday, but the Jets appear to be prepared for Sweat to be out for multiple weeks after signing Amari McNeill to the practice squad on Tuesday.
While the McNeill signing is more for insurance purposes than anything else, Sweat gives the Jets a physical presence up front and is someone who can command double teams with his 6-foot-4, 366-pound frame. His 67.8 run-defense grade from PFF is not where it was last season with the Titans, but it is still the best among the Jets' interior linemen and will be difficult for the team to overcome in his potential absence.
With David Onyemata sidelined on injured reserve after undergoing core-muscle surgery, that has also put even more pressure on rookie Darrell Jackson Jr. , as the depth of the defensive front continues to be tested following Sweat's injury as well. That said, Phillips and Briggs will be relied on to carry the bulk of the load while Onyemata remains out and Sweat deals with his own setback.
Phillips is currently playing in the final season of his two-year deal with the Jets and needs to give the coaching staff some reasons to keep him around beyond this season or even the Nov. 10 trade deadline . His leadership value cannot be understated, but if he can use Jeanty's diss as motivation, he could turn his outlook around on the field and put the slow start to the season behind him.

title: Aaron Glenn's Concerning Comments Could Give Jets Even More Fuel to Fire Him
full_text:
It's important for an NFL head coach to always seem prepared for any situation. The moment a coach is open to the pressures of the job is normally a sign that things may be a bit too much for the leader of the organization.
There are, of course, outliers to that rule. All-time great coaches like Vince Lombardi and Sean McVay have spoken out about the complexities of their job .
"I think what you realize is how hard this league is. How volatile it is. And perspective is everything," McVay said before the season started (h/t Pro Football Talk 's Michael Davis Smith).
The job is hard for any coach to handle, but the great ones are able to do it and guide their teams to wins. The bad ones are unable to do so. For the Jets and head coach Aaron Glenn, it seems they are more on the latter side of that conundrum.
And some of Glenn's Week 8 comments don't necessarily help matters.
Before his second season as head coach began, Glenn had decided to take on more responsibility as a head coach. He also became the team's defensive play-caller in a move he felt would better connect him to the game.
So far, while the Jets' defense has improved, the coaching mismanagement has been an issue no one can ignore. From not taking timeouts in key two-minute situations to challenging low-impact calls on the field, Glenn has struggled with the wide-ranging responsibilities of his job .
Is the coach in over his head? Is there too much on his plate? That's something he answered before practice on Wednesday.
"I wouldn't say that. I could see how you would say that. And it's not easy—I'll be upfront and tell you that—but it's my job to try to make sure these things happen, and I'm going to put the stress on me to be able to do that," Glenn said.
There will be critics who point to this answer as evidence that Glenn may not be the right fit for a head coaching job in the NFL. He may be best suited as a coordinator or top assistant on a staff, much like he was in Detroit.
But his admission is something that also highlights some of the things the Jets failed to notice when they hired him in the first place.
When hiring a head coach, New York has looked for culture setters—people who can command respect from a locker room and get them to play hard. The Jets haven't looked for schematic talents or people who can create a system to get the most out of the talent they have.
In doing so, the "culture-setters" make in-game calls based on feelings instead of sound logic.
It's one of the many reasons Glenn seems so inconsistent at times. Some scenarios he'll be ultra-aggressive, while other times show a passive side.
The numbers are what they are. Glenn is 5-19 as a head coach in the year and a half on the job. He's also failed to win a division game in that stretch. The optics surrounding his answer Wednesday nearly prove the coach is struggling to balance the difficult roles a head coach must deal with.
If Glenn is going to save his job , the Jets coach will need to turn those struggles into success stories... and fast.

title: Jets Have New Trade Market to Explore After Seeing Jeffery Simmons's Price
full_text:
It's another season with the Jets looking like potential sellers ahead of the annual NFL trade deadline . A 2-5 record through seven games has a potential playoff berth looking like the longest of all long shots, meaning that Jets fans should expect general manager Darren Mougey to start selling off plenty of pieces between now and the Nov. 10 deadline.
Trade activity has picked up around the league in recent weeks, especially after the Colts started their fire sale. The Jets could be one of the next teams to enter the trade frenzy, especially after the Titans moved star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears on Thursday, as first reported by ESPN 's Adam Schefter.
Full trade terms, per sources: 🏈Bears receive: Jeffrey Simmons and a 2028 5th-round pick 🏈Titans receive 2027 and 2028 first-round picks, and a 2027 fourth-round pick.
As Schefter's post shows, the Titans got quite the haul back for Simmons , acquiring first-round picks in the next two drafts, as well as a 2027 fourth-rounder. A 2028 fifth-round selection also found its way back to the Bears.
Regardless of the return, it's clear that the defensive tackle market is heating up around the NFL. First it was DeForest Buckner's return to the 49ers, and now the Bears have bolstered their defensive line with a former All-Pro difference-maker.
They might not have a trade chip on Buckner or Simmons's level, but the Jets are rostering one veteran DT who might have some value worth exploring ahead of the deadline.
Several New York veterans are heading towards unrestricted free agency as they play out the final year of their respective contracts, including ninth-year defensive tackle Harrison Phillips. He's been a locker room leader throughout his two seasons in Gotham, but that doesn't mean a potential split shouldn't be on the table.
After all, a change in scenery might benefit Phillips, who hasn't been having the best performance. He's earned a career-worst 49.2 Pro Football Focus grade —102nd among 126 qualified DTs—while his run defense (52.8), pass-rushing (56.0) and tackling (53.9) grades have also noticeably dropped off from last year's numbers (76.4, 56.2 and 61.1, respectively).
The Jets can give Phillips that fresh start by taking advantage of the DT-hungry trade market. He isn't a star needle-mover, but the 30-year-old veteran has 127 games between the NFL regular season and playoffs under his belt, which is the type of experience GMs and coaches love to see in potential rental targets.
Phillips has also slowly shown improvements in recent weeks, adding to why the Jets might want to strike while the iron is hot. The former Stanford Cardinal's production is up over the last four games compared to his first three, and heating up at the right time will certainly give New York the best opportunity to trade him:
Harrison Phillips Weeks 1-3
Harrison Phillips Weeks 4-7
Phillips also carries a cap hit of $7.5 million , according to Spotrac, which is fairly movable, given that it's an expiring contract. His recently improved play makes that cap hit even more worth it, especially if he can keep his foot on the gas pedal.
As for a return, the Jets certainly won't be getting a Simmons-like package back, and that's okay. New York only needed a couple sixth-round picks to acquire him (and get a seventh-rounder back) from Minnesota during the 2025 offseason, making it likely that a similar return is what Gang Green can get back this year. Maybe a sixth-rounder if Phillips has strong performances against the Raiders and Chiefs in the next two weeks.
Teams like the Browns and the Steelers are among potential destinations for a veteran like Phillips, as both AFC North teams are in the playoff mix but also dealing with DT-related injuries. The Vikings and Bills—two of Phillips's former teams—are also among Super Bowl contenders and could explore a reunion if it means putting their respective defenses over the top.
At the end of the day, the clock is ticking for the Jets to make a move. Mougey & Co. need to explore and capitalize on any potential trade interest in Phillips ASAP before other teams put their DTs on the trade block, which would lower his value.
Having proven locker room leaders around is great, but they can't help much if the team is ready to throw in the towel on the season. Phillips helps the Jets more as a trade piece now than he does on the field.
And who knows? Perhaps sending him to a team that can help him finally win a Super Bowl could have him interested in a potential reunion with the Jets once free agency rolls around.

title: Nahshon Wright's Jets Stint Is Officially Beyond Saving as Trade Deadline Looms
full_text:
Repairing and bolstering the secondary was one of Jets general manager Darren Mougey's biggest priorities during the offseason. He used free agency, the 2026 NFL Draft and the trade market to help with that task, which has seemingly paid off through Gang Green's first seven games of the season (even if their record seemingly says otherwise):
Passing yards against per game
Pro Football Focus coverage grade
Even though the secondary is trending in the right direction, some of New York's defensive backs are still leaving plenty to be desired . One of those underperformers happens to be veteran cornerback Nahshon Wright, whom the Jets signed to a one-year contract due to his defensive playmaking. He was coming off a Pro Bowl campaign where he picked off five passes and recovered three fumbles for the Bears, leaving Mougey & Co. optimistic he could do the same in Gotham.
Fast-forward to Week 8, though, and the only thing Wright has intercepted is a harsh dose of reality that his time with the Jets is likely nearing the end.
It's safe to say that Wright isn't a part of the Jets' defensive plans.
The 28-year-old cornerback has played only 22 snaps across three appearances this season, with each opportunity coming on special teams. Even then, his usage in ST coordinator Chris Banjo's unit is regressing, going from 12 snaps in Week 1 and six in Week 2 before he was a scratch for four consecutive games. He returned to action in the Week 7 loss to the Dolphins, playing a season-low four snaps.
On Wednesday, Wright admitted to ESPN 's Rich Cimini that he's "definitely frustrated" and that while he hasn't filed a trade request , he's "expressed" how he's feeling to the Jets.
As frustrated as Wright might be, the reality of the situation is that the Jets have too many bodies on the depth chart ahead of him. Brandon Stephens, despite his struggles, and Azareye'h Thomas will continue to be the starting outside options, while Jarvis Brownlee Jr. and D'Angelo Ponds have the slot covered . There just isn't room for the Hayward, CA native.
Keeping a visibly frustrated player around is never a good idea, especially if the Jets are trying to build positive locker room chemistry. That isn't to say that Wright will become a distraction, especially since he's been nothing short of professional so far, but it's hard to see any real benefit from keeping him around if New York will sit him more often than not.
That's why the Jets should try floating Wright in trade talks ahead of this year's deadline , coming up on Tuesday, Nov. 10. Based on how the season has unfolded, it's hard to imagine Mougey re-signing Wright when he hits unrestricted free agency, which is why it's better to move on from him now to acquire some draft capital (even if it's only a Day 3 pick) rather than continuing to sit him before losing Wright for nothing in March.
As for potential trade destinations, a few teams stand out upon a glance:
Other destinations could emerge between now and Nov. 10, but one thing is clear: the Nahshon Wright experiment has run its course in Gotham, and it's time for the Jets to turn the page—for everyone's sake.

title: Jets' Priority is Clear After Garrett Wilson Addresses Trade Rumors
full_text:
Throughout NFL history, there are many examples of elite wide receivers who were never able to truly compete at the highest level due to their team's inadequacies.
Calvin Johnson and Andre Johnson are just small examples of that reality.
Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson doesn't want to add himself to that list, but the organization is certainly making it hard for him . Since arriving in Gotham in 2022, the Jets have never won more than seven games.
That kind of consistent losing can weigh on a player. At times, it has weighed on Wilson. During the 2025 offseason, there was a belief that the receiver would request a trade if the team brought back Aaron Rodgers. In Sunday's humiliating loss to the Dolphins, video recorded Wilson arguing with Geno Smith and his coaches (h/t Ari Meirov).
Garrett Wilson letting Geno Smith hear it on the sideline. Wilson has 2 catches today with the game in the 4th quarter. pic.twitter.com/BaivlOTxsD
All of this has left Wilson in a difficult situation. Does he want out of New York to get a chance to be a winner? Is his time with the Jets actually coming to an end?
On Wednesday, Wilson answered many of those concerns.
From the moment he stepped on the field as a rookie, Wilson has set out with a clear goal in mind: to turn the Jets into a winner .
So far, thought, that goal has proven elusive. Even in 2026, with the team sitting at 2-5, it seems like the organization just can't put itself in a winning situation. Still, Wilson shut down any talk of considering a change of scenery.
"Yeah, I want to be here, man," Wilson said. "I want to win games, and that's the one thing we've been missing on here. I love it here. Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest, but I'm hopeful."
Wilson's commitment to the Jets is admirable. It actually compares nicely to another former Ohio State Buckeye wide receiver—Terry McLaurin, who went through several quarterbacks and coaching regimes with the Commanders before excelling in 2024.
Unlike McLaurin, though, the Jets have an issue to deal with regarding their top receiver .
They aren't getting him the ball.
In the last two games combined, Wilson has been targeted just nine times for six catches and 70 yards. That's hardly good enough for a top-10 player at his position. While it is true that opposing teams have played New York in a way to take Wilson out of the game, the offensive staff is doing little to scheme their star player open.
Even Smith has admitted to needing to do a better job in feeding Wilson early and often.
Wilson is expecting that his commitment to the Jets will mean the team commits to him. At this point, there's a direct correlation that the receiver is trying to prove.
Every great wide receiver in the NFL wants the football. When they don't get it, they tend to get overly frustrated and demonstrative. In many ways, Wilson's antics are far easier to deal with than some of the other charismatic wideouts around the league.
But his message has remained the same—the Jets haven't won many games, but when they do, Wilson is a big part of it.
"That's my main frustration that may show on the TV or something like that," Wilson said.  But I don't want it to ever be misconstrued. This all comes from a place in my heart of wanting to win. It's frustrating, for sure, because I want to have an impact and I want to help the team. But really, I just want to help the team, man. Sometimes it might come off a certain way when they [show] video, but, man, that's all it's about."
In short, Wilson is asking for the same thing every great receiver asks for: the ball and plenty of targets.
In Wilson's case, the more targets and catches he gets, the better his chances are of being successful. In New York's two wins this season, Wilson has been targeted a combined 18 times. In the three best games for the Jets offense, he's been targeted 31 times.
Get Wilson the ball, and good things happen.
New York agrees with Wilson's premise. That's why the Jets aren't bothered when Wilson may "collaborate" with a coach on the sideline or mumble about targets leaving the field after a loss.
But Gang Green also knows that if things don't turn around soon, eventually there will be a tipping point.
Wilson isn't close to asking for a trade anytime soon. He still wants to help and be a reason why this team turns things around, but his commitment needs to pay off eventually. No one on New York's roster is more deserving of being a winner than he is.
It's time the Jets take that next step for him as well.

title: 5 Jets Who've Clearly Worn Out Their Welcome in New York After 7 Games
full_text:
October isn't over, yet the Jets' season has seemingly slipped away from them . Entering Week 8's clash against the Raiders with a 2-5 record, the playoffs are nothing short of a pipe dream at this point, likely forcing Gang Green to make serious changes—both ahead of the upcoming NFL trade deadline and in the offseason.
Even though 10 games remain, it isn't too early to see that certain Jets shouldn't be part of the organization's long-term plans. Things can change, but for now, these five individuals have worn out their welcome.
Offensive coordinator Frank Reich has been one of the biggest disappointments for the Jets this season. The offensive coordinator has brought the offense back from the depths of last season. However, his situational decision-making has been less than ideal.
The Jets have struggled in the last two minutes of halves and have struggled in the red zone. New York ranks 31st in red zone touchdowns through seven weeks of the season. Reich's play-calling blunders have continued throughout the season, highlighted by the Jets not being able to convert a first-and-goal mere inches from the goal line.
Between the struggles on the field and Garrett Wilson's lack of targets , Reich has been one of the biggest thorns in the Jets' side this season. The offensive coordinator looks out of his depth in today's NFL. Uninspired offensive schemes have given the Jets an offense that can get down the field, but can't finish drives when they need to.
Brandon Stephens has been another issue for the Jets. The sixth-year corner hasn't been terrible, but offenses seem to have figured him out . Stephens has become the defender that opposing offenses target during this Jets' skid.
Stephens has given up 11 catches (68.8% completion rate) for 167 yards and a touchdown over the past four weeks. The Jets have been hurt by his performance, which has played a role in the Jets' 2-5 record.
The former Raven also has yet to record an interception in his two years as a Jet. The corner has also allowed a 100.5 passer rating when targeted this season, according to Pro Football Focus . Stephens' performance this year has been less than ideal, and he may be on his way out of New York sooner than expected.
The Jets signed Tim Patrick on a one-year deal in May. It looks like that one year will be the only one he spends with Gang Green, as Patrick hasn't done much to help the struggling New York team.
The wide receiver has only caught three passes on 59 routes run this season. The biggest contribution that Patrick may have had in a game this year was a (phantom) offensive pass interference that took away an Omar Cooper Jr. touchdown against the Patriots.
Patrick has not lived up to expectations in New York thus far. At best, the former Jaguar has been invisible on the field; at worst, he has been detrimental to the team.
One year may be all that Patrick stays a Jet.
Harrison Phillips has been one of the biggest issues for the Jets' defense this season. PFF has the veteran defensive lineman ranked 102nd at his position this season . Phillips may be crucial to the team's culture, but on the field, he's been a problem.
It seems as if Father Time has caught up to the 30-year-old. Phillips has only recorded 12 solo tackles against the run and has zero sacks on the season through seven weeks. The Jets have had issues with the interior of their defensive line, and Phillips has been a glaring one in 2026.
Josh Myers has had an underwhelming 2026 season. The center is in his second year in New York and has yet to truly perform for the team. Myers has been lackluster this year, ranking 25th out of 35 eligible centers on PFF .
Myers has also been undisciplined this season. The center has had five penalties accepted against him this season, including a costly false start against the Dolphins when New York was attempting to come back.
Myers' arrival shifted Joe Tippmann from the center position, which has also reduced Tippmann's performance. The center signed a two-year extension until 2027. However, if his performance doesn't improve, his time in New York may be shortened.

title: Latest Jets Signing Suggest Bad News for T'Vondre Sweat Injury Concerns
full_text:
Any hope Jets fans had for head coach Aaron Glenn and the team this year hit a low point last Sunday, as Gang Green fell to the winless Dolphins, 28-25, at MetLife Stadium.
The defeat dropped New York to 2-5, and Glenn’s AFC East losing streak continues. With the loss, Glenn became the ninth coach since the 1970 NFL merger to start his career 0-8 against his own division.
Despite the humiliating loss and public outcry from fans over the past few weeks, Glenn is unlikely to be fired mid-season and should have the rest of the year to turn things around. However, he’ll have to do so without defensive tackle T’Vondre Sweat, who went down in the team’s loss to Miami.
The injury occurred in the second quarter when safety Dane Belton attempted to tackle Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis and accidentally hit Sweat’s knee. Although the 25-year-old walked off the field, New York ruled him out for the rest of the game with a knee injury.
Before listing Sweat as week-to-week on Wednesday ( h/t ESPN's Rich Cimini ), New York bolstered the defensive line depth on Tuesday by adding Amari McNeill to the practice squad. The undrafted free agent from Colorado spent the summer with the Kansas City Chiefs before being waived during final cuts.
With David Onyemata still on injured reserve, McNeil’s arrival suggests that the Jets could be without Sweat for multiple weeks.
DT T'Vondre Sweat (knee) and ED Joseph Ossai (ankle) are in the week-to-week category, per Glenn. #Jets
With New York struggling against the run last season, ranking 29th in rushing yards allowed per game (139.5), and transitioning to a new defensive scheme, the team traded edge rusher Jermaine Johnson II to the Titans for Sweat in March.
Since entering the league in 2024, the former Texas Longhorn has quickly emerged as one of the best interior linemen against the run. Sweat has earned a 75 and a 79.2 run-defense grade in his first two seasons, per Pro Football Focus, ranking among the top 10 interior defensive linemen in the category each year.
Sweat hasn’t replicated similar success with the Jets; however, his 67.8 run-defense grade still ranks highest among the team’s interior defensive linemen, per PFF . Although New York’s run defense hasn’t improved with Sweat’s addition, ranking 24th in rushing yards allowed per game (127.7), the unit will suffer in his absence.
With his massive 6-foot-4, 366-pound frame, Sweat commands double teams and clogs the running lanes. Without him, the Jets lack a similar physical presence up front.
Additionally, this isn't the first time Sweat has missed extended time. He missed five games last year with an ankle injury and missed the first three weeks of this year’s training camp with a hamstring injury he suffered in mid-June.
Although we shouldn’t expect Sweat to be sidelined as long as he was last season, the Jets’ decision to bring in McNeill suggests they’re preparing without their starting nose tackle for some time.
McNeill went undrafted after spending five years between Tennessee and Colorado. With the Buffaloes, he earned a rotational role on the defensive line, posting 77 total tackles, seven sacks, 39 pressures, and three forced fumbles in 32 games.
His best season came in 2025, when he recorded 21 total tackles, half a sack, and 11 pressures in nine games, earning an 81.5 overall grade, per PFF . McNeill’s experience and solid production at Colorado earned him an opportunity to prove himself in Kansas City.
Playing 76 defensive snaps across the team’s three preseason games, McNeill recorded one tackle and four pressures. Although he showed some promise, his lack of NFL experience makes it unlikely that we will see McNeill suit up in green and white anytime soon.
New York has relied on a four-man interior rotation, with Sweat sidelined, and will likely split his snaps among Jowon Briggs, Darrell Jackson Jr., Jack Heflin, and Harrison Phillips.
While McNeill gives the Jets additional depth, his signing doesn’t mean we’ll see him on the field. With Heflin’s elevation, New York has other options to help fill the void left by Sweat, including Jackson Jr. and Heflin, who will likely see more snaps in the rotation.
Still, the timing of McNeill’s signing raises concerns about how long the Jets expect to be without Sweat. With New York already struggling to stop the run and Glenn needing wins to save his job , losing one of their key contributors is significant.
In the meantime, Gang Green will need the rest of the unit to pick up the slack and step up quickly before the run defense becomes a bigger problem than it already is.

title: Recently Signed Eagles Will Be Key to Navigating Devastating RB Injury Situation in Week 8
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — This Eagles season can be defined by three words: Next. Man. Up.
In the running back room, those three words can be reduced to two : Apocalypse. Now.
If the situation wasn’t so serious, it would be laughable. Maybe it is, because if you’re not laughing, you might feel like crying. Not that the Eagles are doing either of those things, but when the team has three running backs on injured reserve (Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley, and Damen Pierce), another with a bad back (Saquon Barkley) and one who was waived injured (Carson Steele), well, it’s an apocalypse.
“It’s my first time really experiencing it,” center Drew Kendall said. “But I’m only in my second year.”
You could play in the NFL for a decade and not experience what the Eagles have gone through. They are down their top two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Tay Wicks; offensive linemen have been shuffled in and out to cover for Lane Johnson’s in-season retirement , the trade of Cam Jurgens, and injuries.
But it’s the running back position that’s been ground to a pulp. Their two backs in Sunday night’s visit to the Commanders will be Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue, whom the Eagles already believe in.
“We're constantly coaching every member on the roster,” offensive coordinator Sean Mannion said. “So, when we get Elijah here, and I think it was midway through the offseason program, it's not, 'Hey, we're going to wait and get you up to speed until it's your time to be up on game day.'
“We're constantly priding ourselves on developing every member of our roster. [Running backs/assistant head coach] Jemal [Singleton] does an outstanding job with that room. I know we've had some new faces. Blue, we picked up later on. Elijah, he was here in the offseason, then away, and then back. But it's a credit to all of our position coaches, Jemal specifically with the running backs, that with some roster turnover, with guys needing to step up, they're all mentally capable of stepping in there and executing.”
Mitchell is no stranger to injury. Even as a rookie sixth-round pick of the 49ers in 2021, when he ran for 963 yards and five touchdowns in 11 games, he battled a broken finger, fractured ribs, a concussion, and a knee injury. In the following years, he dealt with MCL, groin, and hamstring strains.
He started training camp with the Eagles but was waived due to injury on Aug. 11. He was brought back to the practice squad on Oct. 20 and is now the likely starter against the Commanders.
Pressed into action last Monday night, when Pierce got hurt in the Eagles' loss to the Cowboys, Mitchell ran for 11 yards and caught three passes for 23 yards on 14 snaps.
Since the Cowboys released Blue this past summer after taking him in the fifth round of the 2025 draft, he's been on and off the Eagles’ practice squad and 53-man roster a couple of times already.
The Eagles hosted him for a top-30 visit when he entered the draft out of the University of Texas. He is expected to have an opportunity to run the ball and maybe return kicks on Sunday night due to the "Apocalypse Now" situation.
“Yeah, man, it’s part of the game—injuries happen,” Blue said. “I’m just trying to do everything I can to pick up the slack and make sure there is no drop-off.”

title: Will The Eagles Develop Buyer's Remorse With Jalen Carter?
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — The common sentiment is that Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter could, and maybe even should, be one of the NFL’s most dominant defensive players. Right now, that remains only a projection more than three years into his career and just months after Carter became the highest-paid defensive tackle in league history.
After Carter was dominated by an admittedly talented Dallas interior offensive line, it’s fair to ask whether Eagles GM Howie Roseman could eventually face buyer’s remorse. Carter failed to record a pressure, much less a sack or tackle for loss, as Cowboys guard Tyler Booker frequently drove him off the line of scrimmage. Dallas finished with 204 rushing yards, including a career-high 155 from Javonte Williams in a 38-21 victory.
"People's standards are bigger than what ours are coming into the season,” Carter said Wednesday. “We all know it's a fresh new season, it's a fresh restart no matter what we did last year, the last 3-4 years don't matter. It's a whole new season, whole new group, new faces, new chemistry in the locker room. It's a restart for us.
“We obviously know we got good players. But we don't go out there saying just because we have good players, we're going to do this on the field. It's not showing right now."
Because of his reputation in Philadelphia, some questioned Carter’s effort, overlooking how quickly the 22-year-old Booker has developed into one of the league’s better guards. Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio dismissed any lack of effort but again pointed to Carter’s week-to-week inconsistency.
“He’s just got to get the mindset to where he’ll be consistent all the time," Fangio said. " ... You just need to have the right mindset.”
Fangio has made similar comments before, but the stakes feel higher after Carter signed his four-year, $152 million extension in July. Through the Eagles’ 2-5 start, Carter has three sacks and three forced fumbles. Those numbers look acceptable for a defensive tackle on the surface, yet two sacks and two forced fumbles came in Philadelphia’s Week 5 loss to the Jaguars—the high point of his season, when he looked like the best player on the field for the first 30 minutes.
Producing at that level only 14.3% of the time underscores that Carter possesses superstar traits but remains far from being a consistent superstar. The Eagles need him to reach that level if they are to maximize their defensive ceiling and justify the organization’s massive investment.
“Not to downgrade Jacksonville or whatever, but the game plan coming throughout the week from the opponents was different. Cowboys played it smarter,” Carter said on Wednesday. “... Whatever you want to call it, and they wanted it more.
Somewhat flippantly, Carter described his performance this season as “trash.” That is not an accurate assessment, but the response reflected a laissez-faire attitude unlikely to play well in Philadelphia.
“Y’all ask me this every year, and I say trash,” Carter said when asked about his performance. “I think you asked for this last year and the year before and I gave you the same answer: Trash. Not to my expectations and I guess not to what the fans want.
“Don’t really matter what they want.”
Lost in that phrasing was Carter’s point that he is trying to meet his own standard, which he views as higher than outside expectations. He declined to speak with reporters after the Cowboys loss, then offered a more defensive explanation Wednesday when pressed on accountability.
“I don’t think I’m a public spokesperson,” Carter said. “I think y’all just want to talk to me because we’re losing.”
Accustomed to winning at Georgia and in his early Eagles career, Carter acknowledged the different atmosphere during a five-game skid, but said the setbacks are not affecting him.
“It was my first time losing,” Carter said when asked whether a 2-5 record has taken a toll on him. “So, obviously, it feels different. It’s a different atmosphere in the locker room after the game and what you guys say online and stuff like that, but it don’t affect me at all.”
For $152 million, maybe it should.

title: 3 Eagles Most Likely to be Traded Out of Philadelphia After Week 8
full_text:
When considering potential trade candidates for the  Eagles ahead of the looming 2026 NFL trade deadline, there are two factors to consider.
Is the player a long-term fit in Philadelphia, and are there teams out there who would be willing to part with assets in order to acquire the player? If the answer to the first question is no and the answer to the second question is yes, then you have a bona fide trade candidate.
With that in mind, here's a look at three Eagles players who are most likely to be traded out of Philadelphia after the team's Week 8 matchup with the Commanders.
When it comes to guys who probably aren't long for Philadelphia but could be of interest to other teams across the league's landscape, cornerback Riq Woolen should be at the top of the list . This isn't necessarily an indictment of Woolen, either. It's more a result of the way the season has gone for the Eagles combined with financial restraints.
The Eagles will likely have to spend a lot of money on extensions for star cornerbacks Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean in the near future, which means they probably won't also be able to lock up Woolen on a competitive deal. If he's likely to walk in free agency anyway, it would make sense for the Eagles to try to recoup some value for him.
If the Eagles were in a position to truly contend this season, they wouldn't look to move on from a starting cornerback who hasn't been bad. But they need to keep an eye on the future at this point, and getting draft capital back for a player who probably won't be on the team next season is a logical move.
For what it's worth, Jeremy Fowler and Matt Bowen of ESPN gave Woolen a 35% chance of being moved before the deadline .
Landon Dickerson is uncertain about his own future in Philadelphia, so we should be uncertain about it as well. When asked about his long-term outlook in Philadelphia earlier this month, Dickerson provided a cryptic response .
The Eagles already traded away one fixture on the offensive line this season in Cam Jurgens; perhaps Dickerson could be next . He's played in just two games so far this season for the Eagles due to injury. If the Birds want to embrace a full rebuild on the offensive line during a down year, they could look to flip the Super Bowl-champion guard for some draft capital and allow the young guys on the line to play for the rest of the season.
Hollywood Brown had his most productive performance of the season in Week 7 against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football. In that game, Brown tallied two receptions for 30 yards. That shows how big of a non-factor he has been for Philadelphia. He was also only on the field in that game because the Eagles were without their top two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks.
It's clear that Brown doesn't have a real role in the Eagles' offense, which makes it extremely unlikely that the team would bring him back in free agency over the offseason. So again, it would be wise to try to recoup some value.
Brown had 587 receiving yards and five TDs with the Chiefs last season, so he still has gas left in the tank. The Eagles haven't utilized him, but other contenders could. Perhaps he could fetch a late-round pick for Philadelphia in a deadline deal.

title: 3 Potential Eagles Trade Targets Despite Nearing Sell-Off Mode
full_text:
The Eagles find themselves in an unfamiliar spot ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10. A disastrous five-game losing streak means Philadelphia general manager Howie Roseman could be in the business of shipping off veteran players , instead of acquiring them for a potential Super Bowl run.
It's never that simple for Roseman, though. He has become a wizard at playing the long game and setting the Eagles up for success in whatever way he can. This year's trade deadline should be no different. Acquiring players hidden on depth charts or seeking a fresh start should be his strategy.
The method of quickly retooling, rather than completely rebuilding , has paid dividends for an Eagles squad that has made the playoffs in eight of the last nine seasons. Being smart in the margins makes a massive impact. With that being said, here's a look at three potential trade targets for Philadelphia.
It's no secret that the Eagles' backfield has been decimated by injuries in 2026. Tank Bigsby (core), Will Shipley (foot), and Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) have all landed on the injured reserve. Starter Saquon Barkley has dealt with a stinger, a hamstring injury, and a back injury during a chaotic campaign .
Bigsby and Pierce are free agents at the end of the season, leaving the Eagles without a bruising back to pair with Barkley in 2027. Shipley excels more in the open field and as a pass-catcher. Seattle's Emanuel Wilson sticks out as a trade target, given his willingness to run over defenders with authority.
That was niiiiice 😮‍💨 TOUCHDOWN EMANUEL WILSON. 📺: @SNFonNBC pic.twitter.com/YfJgdXKJ4Y
Wilson has racked up 403 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 111 carries. The 27-year-old has been the Seahawks' lead back at times, but remains behind Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price in the pecking order when everyone is healthy. In his career, Wilson has averaged 4.2 yards per carry.
Wilson is playing on a one-year contract, which could be considered a drawback. However, it means the price to acquire him will not be sky-high. Roseman could throw a late-round pick Seattle's way and re-sign Wilson in the offseason if he proves he can pound the rock when Barkley needs a rest.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Matt Bowen linked Cincinnati defensive end Shemar Stewart to the Eagles when they outlined their top 25 NFL trade candidates . They cited the fact that he has fallen out of the Bengals' defensive line rotation, even being a healthy scratch against the \\ Ravens in Week 7.
I agree that Philly is a logical landing spot for Stewart. Injuries come into play here again . Defensive ends Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) and Nolan Smith Jr. (concussion) are banged up. Offseason acquisition Jonathan Greenard has yet to look 100% healthy in his reps since returning from an ankle injury.
Stewart was praised coming out of college for his ability to collapse the pocket with power before he became a 2025 first-round pick. His 6'5", 265-lb frame makes him an imposing figure to offensive linemen. Stewart has posted 14 tackles, two sacks, and one pass breakup across 11 NFL games.
Not only would Stewart provide immediate depth, but he would provide upside beyond 2026. Stewart will remain on his rookie contract for 2027 & 2028. That gives Philly defensive line coach Clint Hurtt time to fine-tune Stewart's pass-rush package. He could be a steal at the predicted price of a Day 3 pick.
Philadelphia cornerback Riq Woolen has become a popular trade target for contenders in search of help in the secondary. While it makes sense to ship off his expiring contract, it would leave the Eagles shallow at the position. Jonathan Jones, Kenny Moore II, or Kelee Ringo would see increased snaps.
One avenue Philly could pursue is acquiring a cheap veteran corner to play out the rest of 2026. If it goes poorly, Roseman can let the player leave in free agency. If it goes well, Roseman could re-sign him as Quinyon Mitchell's new partner on the outside. Nahshon Wright of the Jets fits that mold.
It was only a year ago that Wright earned a Pro Bowl nod and led the NFL with eight takeaways in Chicago. He logged 80 tackles and 11 pass breakups over 17 games in 2025. The 28-year-old has struggled to carve out a role in New York after signing a one-year deal, playing only on special teams. On Wednesday, Wright admitted his frustration to ESPN 's Rich Cimini.
Also: CB Nahshon Wright tells ESPN that he's "definitely frustrated" by having no role on defense. Asked if he has requested a trade, he said, "Not formally...(But) I've expressed my feelings (to the team)." https://t.co/wTfBKk1Bn6
A late-round pick swap may be all it takes to pry Wright off the Jets roster. That's a small price to pay for someone who has shown he can use his wingspan and ball-hawking instincts to turn a game on its head. Roseman's known for under-the-radar moves, and Wright should be the next beneficiary.

title: Riq Woolen's Eagles Future Remains Up in the Air as Trade Rumors Swirl in Week 8
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. – Riq Woolen won a Super Bowl ring with the Seahawks last year. He thought that when he signed with the Eagles a few weeks later, he might be able to go back-to-back, the way LeGarrette Blount and Chris Long did in 2016 and 2017, when those two won it all with the Patriots, came to the Eagles, and won it all again.
It looks like it isn’t going to happen that way for the cornerback. He may not even finish the season with the team he signed a one-year contract to represent, because his name is near the top of a list of tradeable players as the season slips away.
“You hear (the trade rumors), but nobody knows the truth,” Woolen said. “You guys on social media and whatever news outlet, y'all can say a million things, but y'all really wouldn't know until you get a talk with the GM and you get a talk with your coach.
“So, other than that, I mean, you can see me going to any team, or you can hear anything about me going to team, but to me, that doesn't matter, just because I'm here every day working with these guys.”
Woolen had one of his worst games as an Eagle in Monday night’s loss to the Cowboys . He declined to answer questions in the locker room afterward but was available on Wednesday as the Eagles prepare to visit the  Commanders on Sunday Night Football.
“I gotta be where I'm at, and to get where I wanna go, I have to go through the things, and that's me being with my team, me being a great player, me getting better every game, and being someone they can rely on while I'm here,” Woolen added.
Woolen’s had at least one interception in each of his first four years in the league, including a Seahawks franchise record of six as a rookie. Yet, in 99% of the defensive snaps so far, Woolen doesn’t have a single INT this year.
There are still 10 games to play, but again; will he play all of those in Philly?
“I was in Seattle last year, and my name came up in trade reports,” Woolen said. “I still had to come here and work every day because my brothers need me. They don't need my mind to be anywhere else. So that's my job here. Me being in Philly, I worked my butt off with these guys all off season, and so I'm gonna ride with these guys throughout the season, no matter if we're undefeated or we don't win a game.
“I've worked my butt off with them. They worked hard as hell too … I'm right here in Philly, and it's a place I wanna be.”

title: One Eagle Is an Even Bigger Trade Candidate After Bears Acquire Jeffery Simmons
full_text:
As the action heats up before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline , a lot of eyes are on Eagles general manager Howie Roseman. After years of being perennial Super Bowl contenders, the Eagles enter Week 8 with a pitiful 2-5 record. Although it isn't impossible to squeak into the playoffs to make another title run, there's also a decent chance that Roseman & Co. decide to sell off some pieces in favor of future draft capital—opportunities to retool don't happen all the time, after all.
If Roseman is on the fence about selling certain players, he might want to make a decision now that the action is reaching a fever pitch. The Titans joined their AFC South rival Colts as sellers this fall, sending star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears on Thursday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
Full trade terms, per sources: 🏈Bears receive: Jeffrey Simmons and a 2028 5th-round pick 🏈Titans receive 2027 and 2028 first-round picks, and a 2027 fourth-round pick.
The Bears also receive a 2028 fifth-round pick in the deal, while the Titans get first-rounders in the next two drafts , as well as a 2027 fourth-round selection.
Watching all that draft capital enter Tennessee's pocket should have Philadelphia's interest. Along with the 49ers acquiring DeForest Buckner from the Colts, it's clear that the trade market for defensive tackles is heating up and might only get hotter over the next few weeks.
Fortunately, the Eagles have someone who can help them capitalize on the action.
Moro Ojomo certainly doesn't have Simmons's accolades, stats or experience, but that doesn't mean that the Eagles shouldn't see what they can get in a trade for the former 2023 seventh-rounder.
After all, Ojomo is facing uncertainty as he plays out the final year of his rookie contract. Sure, the Eagles could offer him a short 'prove-it' deal to extend the experiment, but everything that's happened so far this season indicates that the former Texas Longhorn could benefit from a fresh start.
Ojomo only has six tackles through seven games, missing 21.7% of his attempts en route to a career-worst 27.9 tackling grade on Pro Football Focus . His pressures per game have dropped to 2.3 from 3.2 last year, and that's without mentioning that he still doesn't have a sack.
For comparison, Ojomo recorded his fourth sack in Week 8 against the Giants last season.
But even though the current campaign hasn't unfolded as planned, exploring a potential trade is still worth the Eagles' attention.
Names like Simmons and Buckner coming off the board mean DT-hungry teams will have no choice but to consider a rental like Ojomo if they want to fix their D-line's interior. Perhaps a change of scenery can help him get back to the player who broke out in 2025 to the tune of 17 solo tackles, six sacks, 54 pressures and a broken-up pass in 17 games (nine starts). He also recorded two solo tackles in one playoff game, possessing the January experience NFL head coaches love to see, especially at only 25 years old.
It's not unrealistic to think that the Eagles could acquire a Day 3 pick based on Ojomo's resume and what a potential turnaround could look like. Something like a 2027 sixth-rounder makes sense, potentially including a condition that improves it to a fourth- or fifth-round selection depending on Ojomo's production and playing time.
The Eagles will face the Commanders and Giants before the trade deadline, giving Ojomo multiple chances to shape his future. Strong performances will only increase his trade value , and if the Eagles have no plans to bring him back in the winter, it's better to rip the bandage off and start fresh now.

title: Makai Lemon Complicates Front Office Criticism in Eagles' Disappointing Season
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA—The locker room was mostly empty as Eagles rookie receiver Makai Lemon put the finishing touches on the outfit he’d wear into the unseasonably mild South Philly night in Tuesday morning's wee hours. Lemon had just had a career night, but it came in a loss to the rival Dallas Cowboys, 38-21.
His performance shouldn’t get overlooked. Nor should the fact that the first-round pick has progressed each week and is proving why general manager Howie Roseman may have gotten this pick correct.
“I feel like that’s the way anything goes,” said Lemon. “The more you do something, the more you're gonna get comfortable at it. That's where I'm at.”
Added quarterback Tanner McKee, who threw him his first career TD: "He's a tough player. He can make people miss with the ball in his hands. He can run people over, and he has great hands. That touchdown pass that he caught was a little bit behind him. They had a whole player that was coming across the middle, so I wanted to throw it to his body. It was a little more outside his frame than I wanted it, and he made a great grab. I just think he's a really good player.”
Roseman has been under the fans’ microscope for the past two drafts. Not good enough is what many in the fan base have been saying.
When you look closer, you see that the GM may have found the future at center in 2025’s fifth-round pick Drew Kendall. That year also produced Jihaad Campbell with the next-to-last pick in the first round, and he has work to do to improve, but he was one of the last players to leave the locker room after losing to the Cowboys, while others on the defensive side vanished into the night, declining to say anything about their poor play.
Maybe safety Drew Mukuba figures it out, too, after arriving in the second round of ’25, but it doesn’t help the final four players taken that year, among the 10 picks Roseman made, are already off the team.
Then there’s the 2026 class, with Lemon as the headliner, but others are already making their mark, including third-round offensive tackle Markel Bell and seventh-round outside linebacker Keyshawn James-Newby, who has been elevated from the practice squad over the past two weeks.
In this season that appears to be going nowhere, it could be evaluation time for several players taken in the draft in the past two years. Bell has already shown the potential to be the starting right tackle for a decade.
“Every time he goes out there and practices and plays, I think he gets better,” said head coach Nick Sirianni. “He's obviously very talented. I'm excited that we have him here on our football team. He deeply cares. He's tough. He loves football, and I think that can go a long way.”
Sirianni called Monday night’s game the best Bell has played this season, and it was just his third start.
Monday night was Lemon’s best game. He finished with seven catches for 67 yards, including a tough 4-yard touchdown on third-and-goal. He helped keep the drive alive with a 15-yard catch on fourth-and-one.
“I think we've all seen the growth of Makai Lemon, who I think is really going to be a good football player and already is,” said Sirianni. “We know he's talented, but he has everything. He's got all the right stuff in my opinion. He's tough. He works his butt off. He loves this game. He cares deeply and excited about that.”

title: Nick Sirianni Downplays One Big Eagles Concern After Monday Night Loss
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni pushed back Wednesday against suggestions that a lack of effort contributed to his team’s fifth straight setback, a 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys on “Monday Night Football.”
“I did not see an effort issue on Monday night,” Sirianni explained. “Obviously, it was other things, which I’m sure you guys will ask me about. There were other things. But effort in no way, shape or form was an issue there.”
The comments came as the Eagles sit at 2-5, and in the midst of enduring their longest skid in the Sirianni era as well as the franchise’s first five-game losing streak since 2016.
The Cowboys controlled the line of scrimmage, rushing for 204 yards paced by Javonte Williams’ career-high 155 on the ground, while Dak Prescott threw three touchdown passes.  Dallas' interior offensive line, particular guards Tyler Booker and Tyler Smith dominated against high-priced Eagles' defensive tackles Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis.
The Eagles’ defense as a while under coordinator Vic Fangio, finished without a sack, quarterback hit, or tackle for loss and allowed 416 total yards.
Sirianni explained that the staff grades every play for assignment, alignment, and effort . He acknowledged that no team bats 1.000 on effort, and that coaches highlight both positive standouts and negative ones for the team. But after reviewing the film, he said nothing stood out as an effort-driven breakdown explaining the result.
“I didn’t look at the tape and say, ‘Hey, this was an effort issue and this is why this play happened or that play happened,’” the coach said.
The questions over effort reflect a broader search for answers in Philadelphia.
The offense, missing starting quarterback Jalen Hurts, turned to Tanner McKee, who completed 23 of 35 passes for 211 yards, one touchdown, and one interception.
Saquon Barkley returned on a pitch count and scored early but was limited by his hamstring, as well as a back issue. Bright spots included rookie receiver Makai Lemon’s first career touchdown catch, but the added offense could not match Dallas after the Eagles briefly led 21-20 in the third quarter.
Sirianni did say he understands why outsiders focus on effort amid a losing streak.
“I get it. I would understand, everyone is looking for answers,” he said. He added that he keeps evaluations “tight to the vest” and grades film objectively based on process rather than solely on the outcome, stressing the importance of preparation from Monday through Saturday.
The remarks also land against recent comments from former Eagles quarterback Nick Foles, who said on his podcast that “culture” is an issue in Philadelphia, pointing to changes including the departure of longtime offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland.
Sirianni noted that Foles is not inside the building and that the organization must ignore outside noise, focusing instead on internal relationships and players who “deeply care.”
With two games left before the Eagles' bye week and the trade deadline approaching on Nov. 10, Sirianni and his team face mounting pressure.
Sirianni has framed the stretch – with games Sunday at Washington and Nov. 8 against the New York Giants - as an opportunity to control what they can control, improve daily, and stay locked in, leaning on past midseason turnarounds in 2021 and 2024.
Whether the film shows effort was not the problem—or whether execution, scheme, injuries, and other factors continue to overshadow it—will be tested further in the coming weeks.

title: 3 Eagles Who Should Be Untouchable Ahead of the Trade Deadline
full_text:
With how the 2026 NFL season has gone, the Philadelphia Eagles are expected to be "mild" sellers leading into next month's trade deadline, which makes sense. There's no reason why the Eagles shouldn't try to recoup some value for guys they don't view as long-term pieces .
But there are some players that the Eagles should absolutely hang onto, regardless of how poorly the season has gone.
It's worth noting that the players included below have all been mentioned, to some degree, in trade talks in recent weeks. There are a couple of other players who are obviously untouchable; the Eagles wouldn't even think about moving on from them, including cornerback Quinyon Mitchell and wide receiver DeVonta Smith.
Here are four Eagles who should be untouchable ahead of the trade deadline.
Cooper DeJean has struggled this season , especially compared to the All-Pro standard he set for himself in his first two seasons in the league. He's already allowed more receiving TDs this season than in his first two seasons combined.
According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Cooper DeJean has allowed 4 Rec TD on 40 targets this season after allowing 1 Rec TD on 125 targets in the 2024 and 2025 seasons combined. 😬 https://t.co/fSFHq8RS59
That's certainly not ideal. However, it's not a reason to bail on a 23-year-old defender who was seemingly on an elite trajectory and an integral part of a defense that won the Super Bowl two seasons ago, especially when the entire defense has struggled.
DeJean has played more safety this season compared to previous seasons due to a lack of depth at the position, and he has struggled with the transition at times , by his own admission. Moving forward, it might be in the Eagles' best interest to allow DeJean to focus on the slot corner role, where he has excelled, as opposed to bouncing him back and forth.
If they continue, DeJean's struggles could become a factor when it's time for him to ink an extension with the Eagles in the offseason. But trading a proven young player because of one stretch of relatively poor performances would be a mistake.
It's been a tough season for Saquon Barkley, as the star back has been heavily hampered by injury issues. He missed several weeks due to a hamstring injury. Barkley was limited in his return against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 due to a back issue. Plus, he's been running behind a makeshift offensive line all season when he has been on the field, so his output has been extremely limited.
But Barkley has still shown flashes of the explosive back who led the league in rushing just two years ago and totaled 3,145 rushing yards over his first two seasons in Philly.
Saquon on the move 💨 DALvsPHI on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0s6Ju1e0r8
The conditions have been far from ideal this season, but I believe Barkley can still be an elite back in the NFL. Plus, it's not like the Eagles have a star back in waiting. If they moved on from Barkley, they would have to address the position through the draft and free agency, and they already have plenty of areas like that. Factor in the dead cap hit the Eagles would take on by trading Barkley, and a potential move becomes even less attractive or likely.
B aun is another veteran who seems like a potential trade candidate heading into the deadline, but the Eagles shouldn't consider parting with the two-time Pro Bowler.
The veteran linebacker has been the heart of Philadelphia's defense since he signed with the Eagles before the 2024 season, and that remains the case. He's leading the team in tackles and tackles for a loss this season.
Baun's play hasn't declined, and at 29 years old, he should still have productive play ahead of him. The Eagles need linebackers, and getting rid of the best one they have wouldn't be wise.

title: 3 Potential Moro Ojomo Trade Destinations That Make Most Sense for Eagles
full_text:
A five-game losing streak and a laundry list of injuries put the Eagles in line to be sellers at the upcoming NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10. It's not a familiar spot for general manager Howie Roseman to be in, but one he can use to put Philadelphia in position to compete for a Super Bowl in 2027 and beyond.
Trading away veteran players on expiring contracts is the easiest way to increase Philly's draft capital. That includes pros like cornerback Tariq Woolen and wide receiver Hollywood Brown . What's more intriguing is trading away a high-upside player on an expiring deal like defensive tackle Moro Ojomo.
Ojomo has risen from a seventh-round draft selection in 2023 to an impactful pass-rusher on a defensive line rotation that hoisted the Lombardi Trophy. He is entering his prime at 25 years old. The Nigerian native has logged 79 tackles, eight tackles for loss and six sacks through 49 career games.
Here are three trade destinations for Ojomo that make the most sense from the Eagles' perspective.
It would be logical to send Ojomo out of the NFC in hopes that he doesn't sign a long-term deal with a direct competitor of the Eagles. Jacksonville is no stranger to trades with Philly. Roseman acquired running back Tank Bigsby and offensive lineman Fred Johnson from the Jaguars just last year.
Jacksonville currently sits atop the AFC South with a 4-2 record. A menacing run defense has been the backbone of their success, giving up a league-leading 72.2 rushing yards per game. The same defensive line has struggled to frustrate quarterbacks, though, ranking 22nd in sacks per game (1.8).
Ojomo has posted a 17% pass-rush win rate , according to ESPN analytics. That has him ranked 17th among defensive tackles. It's only a matter of time before those strong reps turn into game-changing sacks. Pairing Ojomo with Arik Armstead would give the Jaguars a dangerous duo in the trenches.
The Browns were not expected to be buyers at the deadline entering the season; however, they boast a 5-2 record, with four of their next six games coming against teams with a losing record. There's a path to a playoff spot and opportunities to improve via trades. The Eagles should take advantage.
Cleveland's defensive line depth took a hit when Mason Graham suffered a left MCL sprain and an ankle sprain on Oct. 1. He returned to the field in Week 7, playing limited snaps and even limping off at one point. Head coach Todd Monken said it will be a while before Graham is 100% healthy (h/t Daryl Ruiter).
Acquiring Ojomo would be a way for Cleveland to give Graham and other defensive tackles crucial rest. Ojomo's quick first step and violent hands would fit in well on a disruptive defense. The Browns own a combined 18 picks in the 2027 and 2028 NFL Drafts. They can create quite an enticing offer.
There's an avenue Roseman can take other than simply selling Ojomo for draft capital. Acquiring a young player capable of helping the Eagles for years to come would be ideal. It would just take some finessing, like packaging Ojomo with an early or mid-round pick to a team in complete win-now mode.
The Lions' Super Bowl window is open with quarterback Jared Goff and running back Jahmyr Gibbs playing at an elite level. There have been reported contract disputes between Detroit and tight end Sam LaPorta. The Iowa product is in the final year of his rookie contract and is seeking a long-term deal.
LaPorta is exactly the kind of player Roseman should target and satisfy with a new deal. The 25-year-old has averaged 50.8 receiving yards and scored 23 touchdowns in 48 career games. LaPorta could form a compelling one-two punch with Eli Stowers, assuming the Eagles move on from Dallas Goedert.
As for Detroit, Ojomo would solidify a defensive line that already has Aidan Hutchinson tormenting opposing quarterbacks. The Lions could sign Ojomo to a multi-year deal if things work out, or earn a compensatory pick by letting him leave in free agency. It's a home run swing Howie should take.

title: Steelers Get Positive Updates on Roman Wilson, Derrick Harmon
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are missing a few of their players, but there is more clarity on two of them for the future.
Ray Fittipaldo of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette gave updates on both Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson (finger) and defensive tackle Derrick Harmon (foot) and where they stand in their respective recovery processes while remaining on the reserve/injured list.
In his weekly Steelers chat on October 29, Fittipaldo noted that Harmon has not yet been included with the rest of the rehab group with the team's other injured players.
"He has not been in the rehab group with other injured players," Fittipaldo wrote.
As for Wilson, however, Fittipaldo noted that Wilson just began working with that rehab group earlier this week ahead of Pittsburgh's Week 8 game against the Cleveland Browns.
"He was in the rehab group at practice for the first time yesterday, so he's starting the process," Fittipaldo wrote.
Harmon suffered his foot injury in Week 4 against the Browns and was placed on IR after the contest.
Pittsburgh's rematch with Cleveland this week marks the fourth game Harmon will be out for, meaning that he is eligible to be activated in Week 10 following the team's Week 9 bye.
Whether or not Harmon is back that early remains to be seen, however.
As for Wilson, he sustained his finger injury at the end of the first half in Week 5 vs. the Indianapolis Colts and was then placed on IR before the Steelers' Week 6 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
As a result, this week's bout with the Browns is the third contest Wilson will be sidelined for. He's required to remain on IR for Pittsburgh's Week 10 game against the Cincinnati Bengals, and then will be eligible to return in Week 11 vs. the Philadelphia Eagles.
The likely next step for both Harmon and Wilson as they look to work their way back for Pittsburgh is to have their 21-day practice windows opened while remaining on IR.
That won't happen next week since the Steelers will be on bye, though it could be a possibility in the lead-up to their Week 10 bout with Cincinnati.
Head coach Mike McCarthy delivered some good news on the long-term prognosis of Pittsburgh's group of players currently on IR, stating that he thinks, "all of those guys have a chance" to come back for the team this season.
Beyond Wilson and Harmon, that unit includes Michael Pittman Jr. (foot), Sebastian Joseph-Day (triceps), Gennings Dunker (knee) and Jack Driscoll (ankle).
Logan Lee is also on IR , though that occurred during training camp, and he does not have a return designation, meaning he is out for the season.
The Steelers just got back a key defensive piece from IR in DeShon Elliott last week for their Week 7 game vs. the New Orleans Saints, and they also emerged from that contest without any notable injuries as well.
It remains to be seen when exactly each player on IR will return to practice and be slated to play again, but the fact that they all seem likely to suit up in 2026 according to McCarthy is fantastic news for a Pittsburgh team that's 5-2 and looking to make some noise in the AFC.
