title: How Steelers Can Beat Browns' Denzel Ward
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers are preparing for their most important game of the regular season so far, as they meet the Cleveland Browns in a critical Week 8 matchup. Both teams enter with a 5-2 record and a chance to show that they are legitimate contenders for the division title and in the conference.
The Steelers enter with a wave of momentum and confidence. They've won three consecutive contests, and despite some blemishes and imperfections, this team is right in the thick of things. To win this contest, however, the Steelers have to solve the Browns’ biggest strength on defense. Cornerback Denzel Ward is playing like the best CB in the NFL, and he’s going to give the Steelers’ offense fits in this Week 8 showdown.
For the Steelers, it's a challenge that a championship-caliber team can and must overcome. Thankfully for head coach Mike McCarthy and his offense, their previous matchup, plus another loss in the Browns' schedule, can give them the keys to taking down Ward and the Cleveland defense in Week 8.
There genuinely might not be a better cornerback in the NFL right now than Denzel Ward. Through seven games, he has two interceptions and six passes defended. But the most impressive thing about the five-time Pro Bowler's start is how dominant he is when targeted.
Quarterbacks have a better chance of just throwing the ball away, rather than going after Ward with a passing attempt. According to data from Pro-Football-Reference , Ward has been thrown at 39 times but has allowed just 16 completions. That's a 41% completion rate and an average of 9.6 yards per reception.
The key for the Steelers is to get wide receiver DK Metcalf going early. In their earlier meeting, the Steelers were able to produce some numbers with Metcalf, and their method for doing so was getting him the ball quickly in space via screens. On the first offensive series of that Week 4 game, the Steelers tried to send Metcalf deep on a go-ball, but it was incomplete because of Ward's coverage on the sidelines.
Next, they sent two quick screens to him later in the drive, and that's when the yards started to pick up, with 22 yards after his first two receptions. Things went quiet for Metcalf until the fourth quarter, when he and Rodgers connected for a 43-yard bomb early in the fouth quarter. That play was successful due to the bunch formation on one side, which got Metcalf away from Ward and Tyson Campbell. This way, they were able to create a one-on-one matchup in the slot between Metcalf and the Browns' nickel corner, which was an easy one for DK to win.
That's going to be a huge part of this game for the Steelers . The battle of wits between McCarthy and the Browns' defense. Getting Metcalf away from Ward is going to be crucial as they try to keep the passing game on an upward trajectory.
A team that produced impressive passing results against Ward and the Browns was, surprisingly, the New York Jets. Geno Smith and Garrett Wilson combined for 104 yards in their Week 5 contest, and they accomplished it through surprisingly simple, yet effective methods. In the likely event that the Steelers cannot avoid the matchup of Metcalf and Ward, they have to utilize plays and concepts that can create opportunity for their top receiver.
The Browns play a lot of man-to-man coverage. According to data from Sharp Football Analysis, the Browns far and away employ the most man coverage plays in the NFL, deploying it 42.4% of the time so far this season. When you have a player of Ward's caliber, it's easy to rely on that, since a majority of the time he single-handedly eliminates receivers from the board.
But the Jets countered the Browns' defensive scheme with a ton of mesh concepts. This is a fairly common play type in today's NFL, consisting of two crossing routes over the middle of the field, and the Jets had the perfect wide receiver in Garrett Wilson to take advantage. His speed across the middle, plus some strategic pick plays and rub routes, gave Wilson just enough space to get open.
Heading into Week 8, the Steelers should take a bit from the Jets' playbook. With Metcalf's speed, they have to find a way to create separation for him, something this offense continues to struggle with. These mesh concepts can, hopefully, give Metcalf some breathing room when he goes up against Ward.
It's going to be an absolute war between the Steelers and Browns in Week 8. To get past their rival and take the top spot in the AFC North, they have to win the passing battle . If they follow this guide, they will likely get the result they are looking for.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: 5 Potential Options for Steelers CB Trades
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- One of the most pressing needs for the Pittsburgh Steelers is at cornerback. The trading of Joey Porter Jr. may have been justified, at least if you ask the organization, but it also left a glaring hole in the defense.
Without him, the Steelers lack a number one cornerback. Furthermore, their inability to play man-to-man coverage is beginning to be taken advantage of. The team's reliance on soft zone coverage is no longer effective, and their lack of foot speed continues to show up on film.
That's why the Steelers need to land a starting cornerback before the NFL Trade Deadline. These five defensive backs could all fill the void in Pittsburgh as they look to upgrade the secondary.
The Steelers need someone who is long and quick. They might not be able to land a player who can be a long-term option, like the top two players on this list, but they could land a seamless fit like Miami Dolphins defensive back JuJu Brents.
Brents is by no means a star on defense, but he's been quietly steady in Miami this season. At 6'3" and over 200 pounds, he's a big and physical player who can line up on the outside and make life difficult for a number two receiver.
Experienced and versatile, Charvarius Ward is an option the Steelers could bring in with little fanfare, but high expectations. Simply put, Ward has been a rock-solid cornerback his entire NFL career.
The difficult thing with Ward is that he's under contract through the 2027 season and his cap hit for next season is just under $25 million. For a starting cornerback, that's fine, but the 31-year-old is not the player the Steelers want to tie that much money to beyond 2026. If the Colts eat some of that money, there is certainly a deal to be worked out, and the Steelers could use his presence on the outside for the rest of this campaign.
42 cornerbacks recorded at least 10 pass breakups in 2025, according to SumerSports , and one name that doesn't get talked about enough is Rasul Douglas. Last year, he was one of the few bright spots on a miserable Miami Dolphins defense. He finished the 2025 campaign with 13 passes defended and two interceptions over 813 snaps.
The 32-year-old veteran is now with the Washington Commanders, and he continues to stand out. He's on a cheap, one-year contract, but plays like a starter still. He's recorded five pass breakups and an interception to begin the 2026 campaign, and he brings an edge that would fit right in with the Steelers' defense.
A Super Bowl winner with the Seattle Seahawks last season, Riq Woolen is on a one-year contract and in a losing situation with the Philadelphia Eagles. He's a monster on the outside. He's physical and specializes in one-on-one situations. Sure, he's susceptible to penalty calls, but that's nothing the Steelers haven't seen before.
For a day three pick, which the Eagles will ask for, the Steelers could land a temporary solution with championship experience.
Times are tough for the Los Angeles Chargers. They are closer to the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft than a postseason berth, and it's nearing time they reach their own fire sale.
The Steelers could swoop in and land a starting corner on the outside for the rest of this year and next season in Cam Hart, a former fifth-round pick of the Chargers. The 25-year-old would give the Pittsburgh defense precisely what they lost with the JPJ trade. Hart is 6'2" and has a long wingspan, which are tailored perfectly to being a playmaker on the outside.
And making plays is exactly what he's doing in Los Angeles, despite the team's continued struggles. Hart has posted two interceptions and six pass breakups in six games, and quarterbacks are completing 61.9% of their pass attempts when targeting him in coverage.
Most importantly, he can play man coverage with success. Playing on his rookie deal, the Steelers would be walking into another contract negotiation in the offseason, but it won't be as dramatic as the last one with a starting cornerback in Pittsburgh.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers’ Troy Fautanu Responds to Jared Verse Smack Talk
full_text:
Pittsburgh Steelers left tackle Troy Fautanu addressed Cleveland Browns EDGE rusher Jared Verse's comments ahead of a crucial Week 8 matchup between the two teams.
While speaking with reporters on October 29, Fautanu offered not to directly respond to Verse's claim from directly after Cleveland's 27-24 victory in Week 4 over Pittsburgh that the Steelers were "dirty".
"I don't know what he's talking about honestly," Fautanu said. "I got no comment, I'm just excited to play this game. We're gonna go out there and continue to play our game."
Fautanu also noted that Verse's comments have not fired him up personally and that he's approaching this week's bout with the Browns as "just another game".
"Personally not really," Fautanu said. "It's just another game, I'm gonna approach it as such, and it's a big game because it's the next game."
Fautanu's move from right tackle to left tackle this season has come with its ups and downs thus far.
The 2024 first-round pick has allowed 20 total pressures and four sacks over seven games this year as compared to 31 pressures and three sacks across 17 contests in 2025 (per Pro Football Focus ), meaning he's regressed a decent amount from a statistical perspective in pass protection.
In what was arguably Fautanu's best performance of the campaign vs. Cleveland in Week 4, though, he allowed just a single pressure and no sacks over 46 reps as a pass blocker (per SumerSports ). That included 16 snaps in which he took on Verse, and Fautanu shut him out over that span.
With both the Browns and Steelers sitting atop the AFC North at 5-2, even if the former currently holds the tiebreaker due to a 2-0 record within the division while the latter is 1-1, this week's game is among the most consequential regular season matchups between the two sides in quite a long time.
The exchange of words has only added to the rivalry and excitement for the contest too, with Cameron Heyward stating on "The Rich Eisen Show" on October 27 that Verse's comments "will be addressed," while the latter added on October 29 that Cleveland is "about to make Pittsburgh ours."
Verse has been quiet this season (zero sacks, 12 pressures per PFF ) after arriving in the trade that sent Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in June, but the Browns' defense as a whole is tied for the third-best pressure rate in the NFL at 42.7 percent (per SumerSports ) and has recorded the sixth-most sacks of any team with 20.
Cleveland sacked Aaron Rodgers five times in its victory over Pittsburgh earlier this season, and though the Steelers' offensive line has certainly improved as the year has gone along, the unit has still given up 22 sacks (tied for second-most in NFL, per SumerSports).
Limiting the Browns' pass rushers will be paramount to coming away with a victory, and Fautanu's matchup with Verse in particular is one that Pittsburgh has to gain the upper-hand in.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Get High Asking Price for Colts WR Josh Downs
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers are in the market for wide receiver help as the trade deadline nears. With multiple players dealing with injuries, the team's offense could use a rejuvenating boost over the coming weeks.
One of the Steelers' top targets is Indianapolis Colts pass catcher Josh Downs. The 25-year-old is one of the most attractive names available, and the Steelers have been linked to his services.
But according to insider Adam Schefter, the Steelers will have to pay a premium to bring in the talented playmaker. Speaking on his podcast, he shared that the Colts are seeking a third-round pick in any trade talks to deal for Downs.
“The Colts have told teams they’re looking for third-round value,” he said on The Adam Schefter Podcast. “Nobody’s willing to do that right now.”
It seems like the Steelers might be caught in a game of chicken with the Colts and the rest of the NFL. It’s clear that this team needs help on offense, and it’s a poorly kept secret that they are willing to make a deal.
But at that price, the Steeler s must stand firm. The Colts are in the midst of a complete teardown. They have sent out two of their best players on either side of the ball, with multiple more top veterans expected to go before the deadline as well.
Which is why the Steelers, and the rest of the league, are trying not to budge. If they wait out the Colts, a more acceptable trade return could bring Downs to Pittsburgh. A fourth-round draft pick, for example, is a deal the Steelers may be eager to make, but giving up a third is too rich for general manager Omar Khan.
If the Colts hold firm on wanting a third-round pick for Downs, the Steelers will have to look elsewhere for reinforcements. But that’s not the worst thing, as that third-round pick could net them a better player.
The player that many have clamored for is Jacksonville Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. A former 1,000-yard receiver who is under 25 years old, he would likely command that day two draft pick in return.
But if the Steelers view him as a major upgrade on offense, that third-round pick doesn’t feel so expensive anymore.
Some other names that have popped up as the NFL Trade Deadline nears are Los Angeles Chargers pass-catchers Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, as well as Philadelphia Eagles players like DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks.
Even with the news on Downs , the Steelers are still in the mix. Just like they are with nearly every available wide receiver ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Jared Verse Fires Back at Steelers: ‘About to Make Pittsburgh Ours'
full_text:
The war of words between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns has continued ahead of their Week 8 matchup at Acrisure Stadium.
While speaking with reporters on October 29, Browns EDGE rusher Jared Verse took another shot at the Steelers and said that he's "not worried" about anyone on the team and that Cleveland is going to "make Pittsburgh ours" this weekend.
“I’m the same as I’ve always been. I’m just going in ready to dominate,” Verse said on Thursday, per Ashley Bastock of Cleveland.com. “Obviously I’ve been waiting for this one for a good little bit. The whole bulletin board material and things like that. I’m just ready to put (my) hands on them. I’m just gonna keep it simple like that.
“I’m not worried about Cam. I’m not worried about their O-line. I’m not worried about nobody on their team. We’re out there to dominate. We’re about to make Pittsburgh ours on Sunday.”
#Browns Jared Verse on the Steelers and Cam Heyward’s comments this week: pic.twitter.com/c3n2nqNmJz
Following the Browns' 27-24 victory over the Steelers on Thursday Night Football in Week 4, Verse called Pittsburgh "dirty" and stated that he was looking forward to another matchup between the AFC North rivals.
"They were talking crazy. I was telling them, ‘Y'all double-teaming and sliding and you're garbage.’ I don't have respect for anybody that plays too dirty and does too much extra s*** after the game," Verse said . "I can't wait to see them again. It's going to be a great time when I see them again."
Cam Heyward responded to those comments during an appearance on "The Rich Eisen Show" this week, and said that Verse's remarks "will be addressed".
“Double teaming, sliding, chipping, are those not allowed in our game?” Heyward said . “Yeah, I got the bruises to prove it. But we don’t whine about it, baby. It’s part of the game. And so, I’m looking forward to this game. It’s gonna be a fun game. Both teams are in position to do a lot of work in this division, as they say.
“The AFC North is on fire and I’m glad I’m in the kitchen because I like it that way. But those are words that were said and they will be addressed.”
While Pittsburgh and Cleveland are tied atop the AFC North at 5-2, the Browns hold the tiebreaker due to their 2-0 record in the division while the Steelers are 1-1.
With the Baltimore Ravens sitting at 4-3 and the Cincinnati Bengals at 4-2, the divisional race seems likely to be heated down the stretch of the regular season.
As such, the Steelers must take advantage of the remaining opportunities in front of them, especially against the first-place Browns this week.
Given Verse's comments and the already heated nature of the rivalry between Pittsburgh and Cleveland, the stakes of their upcoming matchup couldn't feel higher.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Mike McCarthy Drops Injury News That Gives Steelers Even More Hope
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have had some of the worst injury luck in the NFL this season, but there's optimism within the fan base.
The team has lost multiple starters already, with seven players currently on the Injured Reserve, plus another on the Practice Squad Injured Reserve.
As the team tries to win its sixth game of the season and take hold of the AFC North divisional lead , the Steelers remain hopeful that they will get a few of their key players back.
And head coach Mike McCarthy's latest update only adds more hope for the Steelers. Speaking to the media before the team's practice, he was asked about the status of the organization's injured players.
His response was an extremely encouraging one, as he shared that each player on the IR has a chance to return this season.
"I think all of those guys have a chance," he said. "I think they'll all have a chance to come back."
The update from McCarthy is huge, but it doesn't provide a ton of clarity. The team has multiple wide receivers out currently, including two of the top three players on the depth chart.
Both Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson have missed time, but with McCarthy's latest comments, there is suddenly a renewed belief that the receiving group could return to full health for the stretch run.
The player most likely to return first is Roman Wilson. After he dislocated his finger several weeks ago, it was unclear whether he would be good to go again in 2026.
He remains out until after their Week 10 contest, but he will likely be back on the field quickly once his practice window is reopened.
Meanwhile, Pittman Jr. deals with a foot injury that has kept him out of action for four of the Steelers' seven games so far.
The severity of his injury remains a mystery, but if it were season-ending, McCarthy surely would have clarified when he was recently asked.
He is eligible to have his practice window opened beginning in Week 9, but the team has not indicated that they plan to do so.
On the defensive side of the ball, the team is waiting for two key contributors to return.
Defensive linemen Derrick Harmon and Sebastian Joseph-Day were both forced out of action, robbing the Steelers of valuable depth up front.
Thankfully, the defense has persevered without two of their top players, but it's not preferable that they manage much longer.
Harmon is slated to be back first. The second-year defensive tackle has one more game that he must be on the IR for, meaning he could rejoin the team next week.
Like Pittman Jr., the team has not indicated whether or not they will open his window when their Week 9 preparations begin.
It wasn't anything official, but McCarthy certainly inspired hope with his latest comments.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Former Player Says Joey Porter Jr. Didn't Hurt Steelers
full_text:
A former Pittsburgh Steelers offensive linemen does't think the team has been as negatively impacted by the loss of Joey Porter Jr. as anticipated.
On the latest episode of his "Snap Count" podcast, Trai Essex laid out the reasons why he believes the Steelers have held up just fine without Porter Jr. as their No. 1 cornerback this season.
"I think they did not fumble the bag the way that these boys are playing right now," Essex said . "Initially, yes, do everything you can to bring [Porter Jr.} back. He is family, he is legacy, he has done everything that you want as a Steeler up until that point.
"From a talent standpoint and a depth standpoint, yes, I absolutely thought we needed him and I thought we fumbled it when we traded him away. But the way they've been playing since then, we have the 11th-ranked pass defense in the NFL. They've been doing what they're supposed to be doing."
Would Pittsburgh's defense be better off with Porter Jr. as opposed to without it? The answer to that question is undoubtedly yes.
Porter Jr. has played at a star level in his three games for the Dallas Cowboys since the Steelers dealt him for a 2028 second-round pick and conditional 2027 sixth-rounder on September 30.
Back to Essex's point, however, Pittsburgh has not taken as devastating a hit as expected without Porter Jr. on the field this season, and one of the main reasons for that is Jamel Dean.
When Dean signed a three-year, $36.75 million deal with Pittsburgh in free agency this past offseason, he was set to serve as the team's No. 2 corner opposite Porter Jr.
Because Porter Jr. did not play at all for the Steelers leading up to his trade as a result of his contract dispute, Dean was thrust into that top role at the position.
The 30-year-old has been fantastic while handling those duties too, and there was no bigger example than when he helped lead Pittsburgh to a Week 6 comeback victory over his former team, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, with six passes defended and an interception late in the fourth quarter that helped send the game into overtime.
It's no surprise that Dean has played so well, as he was a staple of Tampa Bay's defense for seven seasons and won Super Bowl LV with the team in 2020, but it just goes to show that the Steelers already had a contingency plan of sorts in place if the Porter Jr. situation went haywire, even if that wasn't the intent when the former was initially brought in.
Dean does come with some durability concerns, and he did miss Pittsburgh's Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with an ankle injury.
When he's out on the field, though, he's been a truly indispensable part of a Steelers defense that's proven to be a top-10 unit in the league overall.
Regardless of Dean's performance so far this season, however, Pittsburgh would benefit from adding a cornerback ahead of the November 10 trade deadline.
Asante Samuel Jr.'s had his moments, though he's been inconsistent while primarily serving as the team's No. 2 corner.
Third-round rookie Daylen Everette has shown some flashes too, but he has logged just 14 defensive snaps over the past two weeks and is still pretty raw.
The Steelers don't really need help in the slot with Jalen Ramsey as the starter and Brandin Echols as his backup there, so really their need comes on the boundary.
With Sean Murphy-Bunting and Terell Smith not seeing the field at all on defense in their three games on the 53-man roster while the same can be said as a whole for Doneiko Slaughter, Pittsburgh doesn't have a littany of options on the outside.
The defense is in good shape overall, though it's easy to see a world in which the group's lack of a bona fide corner next to Dean on the boundary could come back to haunt them down the stretch of the regular season and into the playoffs if they get there.
For that reason, cornerback is right up there with wide receiver in terms of the Steelers' biggest needs before the trade deadline.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Should Call Chargers About Up-And-Coming CB
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers should take advantage of teams tossing in the towel near the trade deadline. Organizations that are ready to set sail toward the 2027 offseason and are doing so by selling to other teams that remain in the playoff hunt.
No team is closer to their season being over than the Los Angeles Chargers, and luckily enough for the Steelers, LA might have the best option for Pittsburgh in terms of a cornerback trade.
The Steelers are reportedly interested in making a move at cornerback before the trade deadline. That should come as no surprise as the team has struggled to stay consistent in the secondary all season, and their solution to the problem was shipped to Dallas for a 2028 second-round pick earlier in the year.
So, how do they fix it? Well, the first call they may want to make it the 0-6 Chargers.
Who would they asking about? Cam Hart.
Hart is just 25 years old, turning 26 this season and has 36 games with 16 starts of experience in the NFL. He's recorded three interceptions, including two through six games this season. In 2026, he's also added six pass deflections to his resume and is holding opposing quarterbacks to a 61.9 completion percentage, without giving up a touchdown.
The Steelers moved on from Joey Porter Jr. because of his contract situation, but their need for a young cornerback didn't leave with him. Hart has two years left on his rookie deal, which gives Pittsburgh the rest of this season to decide if they're going to sign him in the spring.
If not, they move on to the final year of his rookie deal. From there, it's about deciding whether or not they see him as the future.
Trading for Hart is probably more expensive than a lot of names floating around out there, but not by much. The Steelers aren't going to get away with a Day Three draft pick, but could easily land him for a Day Two pick.
Maybe they toss a fourth-round pick the Chargers' way and it gets done. Maybe they need a third-rounder. But without a full year of starting experience, you'd have to imagine that you're trading for upside and not production.
That works in Pittsburgh's favor.
There doesn't need to be much hesitation from the Steelers if a fourth-round pick does get the job done. If Hart is available and the Steelers want a cornerback, it just makes too much sense.
This team is a contender and they need to make contender-level moves at the trade deadline. Cornerback and wide receiver top their list . And no name is bigger than the one in Los Angeles.

title: Ranking Steelers WR Trade Options
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have a very important decision to make ahead of the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline. At 5-2, the team is in position to buy and add more pieces for a playoff push. At the same time, the Steelers know what awaits them in 2027. A new quarterback and multiple roster changes will happen, and the Steelers will need the 2027 NFL Draft to replenish talent on both sides of the ball.
That leaves general manager Omar Khan in a bind. Does he prioritize this year's team and their Super Bowl ambitions or the future of the organization?
To give this year's team a chance, they have to add another playmaking wide receiver.
One of the more disappointing options that could be acquired is former Los Angeles Chargers first-round pick, Quentin Johnston. He has size at 6'3" and possesses straight-line speed. That much the Steelers could benefit from.
But Johnston comes with huge red flags, the most notable is his inconsistent hands. In five games this season, he already has three drops. Add in his injury history, and Johnston poses a real boom-or-bust potential. If it worked, the Steelers would look like they hit the lottery. That's a big if, however, and if the gamble doesn't pay off, the team would be in a Mike Williams-esque situation once again.
It's a complexity to many as to why the Brian Thomas Jr. experiment is failing, but that's the reality for the Jacksonville Jaguars. Where folks are split is whether or not a change of scenery will bring back the BTJ he was as a rookie in 2024.
Maybe playing with Aaron Rodgers unlocks that player, but it's no guarantee.
What Thomas Jr. brings, without question, is size and strength, plus the ability to explode downfield. That's what made him so good, once upon a time, and that's what the Steelers could benefit from the rest of the way.
A quick, explosive receiver who can separate from defensive backs, 25-year-old Josh Downs is one of the top fits for the Steelers. In a very tough situation currently with the Indianapolis Colts selling off pieces for pennies on the dollar, Downs is likely the next to go during their liquidation sale.
For the Steelers, they could take advantage and get a player with both a 700- and 800-yard season for a day two or day three draft pick. That's a steal, and while he's not a superstar, Downs solves a ton of issues for this offense. He's also the most realistic trade target out there.
A name that recently popped up as a trade candidate and the better option from the Chargers is former second-round pick Ladd McConkey. After a 1,100-yard season as a rookie, he regressed statistically in 2025 with just 789 receiving yards.
But what remains is an extremely intelligent route-runner and a player who can make those difficult catches. That sounds exactly like the type of receiver Aaron Rodgers wants to throw to.
Acquiring McConkey will be difficult, admittedly. The Chargers are bad, really bad, but are they ready to give up on a productive and still-developing 24-year-old receiver while they still have a franchise quarterback? It would take me a lot of convincing to give him up, but maybe the Steelers can make the right trade proposal that brings McConkey to Pittsburgh.
This one isn't so much about trade rumors swirling, it's more about how perfect this addition would be for the Steelers. The 27-year-old DeVonta Smith has been a productive and playmaking receiver since he entered the league. The Eagles are in a difficult spot, and they've already moved on from a few key pieces.
What makes Smith so enticing is twofold. The first is how he would complement Rodgers and open up the passing game. His speed, his ability to create separation and his extensive route tree would be a gift to Rodgers and the offense. Secondly, Smith is one of the most affordable receivers compared to how excellent he is. His salary cap hit for both 2027 and 2028 is less than $21 million, making it a bargain compared to the 1,000-yard production he annually produces.
Smith also will cost the Steelers the most, but he's easily worth it as long as the cost doesn't involve a first-round draft pick. He'd be an absolutely perfect fit in this offense and give the Steelers a legitimate, Super Bowl-quality offense.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: What Should the Seahawks Do With Anthony Bradford?
full_text:
The making of an omelet requires the breaking of a few eggs. And in the case of the Seattle Seahawks trading for Quenton Nelson , those eggs have come in the form of a third round pick, a fifth round pick, and ten million dollars in 2026 cap commitments. There’s a fourth egg as well that is less obvious, but worth considering, in the form of Anthony Bradford.
Mike Macdonald laid it out during yesterday’s press conference. Quenton Nelson will take up the left guard position, and Grey Zabel is going to right guard. This means Anthony Bradford is hitting the bench. It’s probably the best decision the team could make right now, although I have serious concerns about it, but it leaves Bradford in an unfortunate spot .
Bradford is a little more than four months away from hitting the open market as a free agent. The next ten games plus postseason was going to go a long way in determining his value on his next contract. For him to get benched at this juncture is tragic for him, after the work he did helping this team win a super bowl last season. I can’t help but feel for him.
Because of this, I wonder if the Seahawks might turn around and flip Anthony Bradford between now and the trade deadline. Such a move could recoup the fifth rounder the team gave up in the Nelson trade, leaving just the third, which likely gets recouped as well if Nelson walks in free agency in March. There’s nearly two weeks to find a suitor for him.
It’s also a chance to do right by Anthony, who deserves a chance to start right now, and is good enough to do so despite his shortcomings. Also keep in mind the nature of the upcoming 2027 draft class, which looks excellent so far, so giving up some depth for another shot at that class is a reasonable risk. If Beau Stephens is ready to be a backup, then it makes sense.
I’m concerned about the Grey Zabel element of this switch-up . I’m old enough to prefer my right guards to be road graders who can overwhelm with strength, and I don’t see Zabel as being that. Combine that finesse skillset with his lack of experience on the right side, and I could see this being a bumpy transition. Maybe bumpy enough to get Bradford back onto the field.
So maybe you hold onto him just because of that. Even if that doesn’t happen, an injury is always in play, and holding onto Bradford bails you out if either guard goes down. We got a decent look at Stephens over the last month, and he doesn’t look ready to fill in. Ultimately, this team is trying to win it all this season, and that’s worth a lot more than a day three pick.

title: The Biggest Position of Need for Seahawks in 2027 NFL Draft
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are trading away draft picks to acquire Indianapolis Colts offensive lineman Quenton Nelson , but the team is still holding on to its first-round pick.
The Seahawks have a boatload of picks to work with in next year's draft , where they will be looking to add some youth to their pass rush unit.
"Dante Fowler Jr. hasn't appropriately replaced Boye Mafe for the Seattle Seahawks. Uchenna Nwosu is also on an expiring contract. Expect GM John Schneider to invest heavily at pass rusher again this coming offseason," NFL Draft On SI contributor Justin Melo wrote.
The Seahawks have a lot of experience at the pass-rushing positions, but free agency is going to come sooner rather than later for several of them. Uchenna Nwosu is not under contract for the 2027 season, and neither is DeMarcus Lawrence, who announced his retirement at the end of the season, meaning he won't be back next year either.
Dante Fowler Jr., the No. 3 overall pick in the 2015 NFL Draft, has stepped in to replace Boye Mafe, who left in free agency for the Cincinnati Bengals, but he is not off to a great start in his Seahawks career. Fowler has managed to record just one tackle in seven games so far for the Seahawks.
Players like Boubacar Traore from Notre Dame and Yhonzae Pierre from Alabama could make sense for the Seahawks, depending on where they end up in the first round and where these prospects line up on the big board at the end of April.
Needless to say, the Seahawks should be looking at pass rushers on each day of the draft, as bringing in talent across the board should help them, not just on defense but on special teams as well.
Injecting some youth into the unit could backfire if the Seahawks find the wrong people, but Seattle has always built through the draft. That is how they are going to continue to evolve as they seek another Super Bowl title.
In the meantime, the Seahawks are back in action on Monday Night Football against the Chicago Bears . Kickoff is scheduled for 5:15 pm PT at Lumen Field. Fans can watch the game on ESPN or stream it on the ESPN app.

title: Seahawks Have 'Best Defense in Football' Entering Matchup vs. Bears
full_text:
Similar to the Legion of Boom in the 2010s, the current Seattle Seahawks' "Dark Side" defense is only growing in infamy around the NFL as they continue to strike fear in opposing offenses.
There was no better example of that than in Week 7, when the Seahawks handed the Patrick Mahomes-led Chiefs offense their worst-ever performance in primetime. Kansas City didn't have a single snap in the red zone, totaled just 213 yards and picked up 11 first downs. Running back Kenneth Walker III, who entered the game averaging 133 rushing yards per game, finished with 14 carries for 36 yards.
After losing three of its previous four games, Seattle's defense is riding high into a Monday night game against the Chicago Bears in Week 8. The Bears are well aware of the caliber of defense they're facing.
Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was asked on Wednesday about his thoughts on facing the Seahawks after how they shut down the Chiefs. Williams gave Seattle's defensive unit a lot of credit, but also welcomed the challenge.
“Obviously, that’s the best defense in football right now, for stats-wise and players and scheme,” Williams said. “So, it’s going to be fun for us; it’s going to be a challenge for us, and we accept that challenge. We gotta go out there, we gotta execute, we gotta do our part.
“They do a good job with punching the ball out, interceptions — I think they’re second in the league or something like that with the amount of turnovers that they’ve had … They’re fully equipped over there to do whatever they need as a defense and as a team, and so like I said, it’s going to be a fun challenge for us.”
Seattle's defense is allowing the fewest total yards per game (233.9), the fewest passing yards (144.4) and the sixth-fewest rushing yards (89.4) through seven games. They rank fourth in points allowed per game (17.9) and are tied for the second-most takeaways (12).
The Seahawks are essentially dominating in every area, and Bears head coach Ben Johnson is well aware of how difficult it will be for his offense to move the ball.
“I think they do a great job affecting the quarterback, number one. Up front, they’ve got good rushers, and they’re able to get [to] and affect the quarterback without having to pressure a whole lot in passing downs,” Johnson said. “So, when you’re able to do that with just four rushers, I think it’s really hard to get guys open with a lot of space. They’re doing a phenomenal job taking away explosive plays in the passing game, and it’s hard to stay on schedule consistently and march it down the field and score in the red zone on these guys, and that’s what they try to make you do.”
The potential All-Pro defensive line duo of Leonard Williams and Byron Murphy II are two of the main culprits in what Johnson is describing, and it's further amplified by the edge rushers. Linebacker and defensive back Nick Emmanwori is emerging as one of the most unique players in the league, and he's adding a whole new dimension to the Seahawks' pass rush.
“You combine that with the fact that it’s hard for a lot of offenses to even get started — the number of three-and-outs on tape is pretty astonishing as well,” Johnson added. “It’s hard to run the ball; hard to throw the ball, and it’s going to take a team effort here to win this one this week.”
The Seahawks (4-3) and Bears (5-2) kick off at 5:15 p.m. on Sunday, Nov. 2, at Lumen Field. Both teams made blockbuster trades this week, with Seattle adding All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and the Bears picking up All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , adding further intrigue to the matchup.

title: Seahawks' Quenton Nelson Discusses 'Bittersweet' Trade From Colts
full_text:
Former Indianapolis Colts guard and future Hall of Famer Quenton Nelson is on his second day with the Seattle Seahawks since being the primary piece in a blockbuster trade on Tuesday.
Nelson, a three-time All-Pro and eight-time Pro Bowler, spent the entirety of his NFL career with the Colts prior to the trade. Now in his ninth season, Nelson bolsters an already-competent Seahawks offensive line that could now move to being one of the best in the league.
In his first media appearance since the trade , Nelson told reporters that he has mixed feelings. While he's excited to be with the Seahawks, he will cherish his time in Indianapolis.
“The reaction, I’ve got to admit, was a little bittersweet,” Nelson said. “I formed a lot of great relationships in Indy; great community there. But definitely excited for this next chapter being here in Seattle. I mean, just driving in and the other couple of times I’ve played here, it’s a beautiful state, a really cool city. All the nature here is sick. And then getting to meet some of the guys, everyone’s been super welcoming already, and the coaches as well … It’s a family here: the equipment [staff], the trainers, it’s been a great day and a half so far.”
Rumors were already swirling days before the trade, but Nelson said he tried not to let it affect him. The veteran guard is a free agent after this season, and the Colts weren't going to give him a viable contract extension.
Nelson said he was "controlling what I can control" and "being my best every day" as a potential trade loomed. He did have discussions with interim general manager Ed Dodds in the days leading up to the deal, Nelson added.
“I met with Ed [Dodds] the day before the trade, and he told me that they were fielding calls and there were a few teams interested, one of them being Seattle,” Nelson said. “He [asked] how do I feel about it, and I was like, ‘If that’s what you guys got to do, then great,’ and I was happy when he called me in the next day and told me it’s Seattle.”
Nelson spent his first day at the Seahawks' facility meeting with offensive line coaches John Benton and Quinshon Odom, trying to learn as much of the scheme as possible. Head coach Mike Macdonald expects Nelson to start at left guard on Monday night against the Chicago Bears.
“It’s a lot of the same stuff, just different terminology,” Nelson said. “Yeah, a lot of different terminology. So, just trying to learn that. Coach [Odom] and [Benton], we met a lot all throughout the day yesterday, and they’re just pouring everything into me, so I really appreciate them. Also, [center Jalen] Sundell stayed around, which was nice. He was there with me all night last night, answering any questions I got. The guys here have been great so far.”
As a veteran who has excelled in his career, Nelson has a better shot than most to quickly learn and adjust to a new system in just a few days. That doesn't make it easy, however, and Monday will be his first major test in a Seahawks uniform.

title: Seahawks Injury Report With Updates on Jadarian Price, Charles Cross, More
full_text:
The first practice report of the week typically sells the potential worst-case scenario, as players get listed for any minor issue and get held off the field for rest as much as anything else. So don’t let what you’re about to see alarm you too much. But we can also get an idea of where things might go, so let’s have a look to see who is dealing with what right now.
At first, this report is daunting, so let’s take it piece-by-piece. Zach Charbonnet (knee) , Quenton Nelson (knee), and Brady Russell (wrist) were full participants, so nothing to concern yourself with there, and Charbonnet is expected to play this week. Jaxon Smith-Njigba and DeMarcus Lawrence didn’t practice, but they’re just rest days, so that’s fine too.
Limited participants today included just-benched Anthony Bradford (knee) , Tyrice Knight (hip), Drew Lock (right elbow), Patrick O’Connell (toe), Connor O’Toole (hamstring), Chazz Surratt (calf), Drake Thomas (ankle), and Leonard Williams (achilles). The concern in this group to me is Williams, as this is a new injury to my knowledge and achilles wounds can linger.
Charles Cross (ankle) was out , as expected. Velus Jones Jr (hamstring) missed as well, although he’s probably days away from getting waived with the return of Price and Charbonnet. Rashid Shaheed (knee) was out, although the word on him remains positive. The worry would be Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) being a DNP, since I believe the ankle issue is new.
The Bears, in terms of week-to-week injury issues, are holding up very well for the moment. They only had five players listed, and of those five, only one of them, Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), was out. Not to downplay Monangai’s importance to the Bears, of course, but he’s missed the last three games already, so they’re familiar with his absence.
D’Marco Jackson (ankle) and Malik Muhammad (toe) were limited, and should be fine for gameday. Both players are important parts of Chicago’s defense, playing over half the snaps for that unit this season. Worth keeping an eye on, obviously, but hard for me to believe they miss a game right after getting the mini-bye week from the Thursday game.
T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Jack Sanborn (concussion), two linebackers, were full participants, so not much to say there. For the most part, the injury issues the Bears have are more long-term, with players like Coby Bryant, Cole Kmet, Braxton Jones, and Dayo Odeyingbo on injured reserve. Eyes are on Monangai as we go through the week.

title: Why Seahawks' Quenton Nelson Could Have a Rough First Game
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks (4-3) shocked the NFL with the trade for eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts. This is a defining move that should easily help the offense be more efficient and dangerous. Nelson is one of the league's top interior offensive linemen and has a chance to help the struggling running game.
​Nelson will likely make his Seahawks debut in the Week 8 home game on Monday Night Football versus the Chicago Bears (5-2). The Bears have been good, but not great on the defensive side of the ball this season. With Seattle and Chicago making moves to improve their roster , Nelson might not have a dominant performance that the 12 are expecting on Monday.
​Nelson might be one of the most efficient guards in the league, but any player is going to experience some culture shock after being traded to a new team. He has been with the Colts for the first eight and a half seasons. During that time, the Colts have gone from a playoff contender to a team tanking. Nelson joins a Seahawks team that has a completely different culture and fit, and different teammates and play style.
​He goes from creating running lanes for an elite running back like Jonathan Taylor to now blocking for a Seahawks offense that might know who their starting running back will be on Monday. The Seahawks will either have Zach Charbonnet fully back from his ACL injury, rookie Jadarian Price back from his chest injury, or Emaunuel WIlson starting his fifth consecutive game .
​He will also have to pass-protect for quarterback Sam Darnold, who has been more of a longer-yardage passing quarterback than the Colts’ Daniel Jones. The Seahawks are averaging 6.6 net yards per pass attempt while the Colts are only averaging 4.9 yards, which is ranked second to last in the league.
​The Seahawks are facing a Bears team that traded for four-time Pro-Bowl defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans. Nelson and Simmons have faced each other often as divisional rivals, but now they face each other with teams that are legitimate Super Bowl contenders.
According to Brian Nemhauser , Nelson and Simmons faced each other in 19 one-on-one matchups in four games where they were both healthy. Simmons won four of those reps, including two key pressures. Nelson won four reps, but two of those reps were with help from other offensive linemen.
​The Seahawks’ offense will face a Bears defense that has 613 rushing yards through seven games, which is the eighth-fewest in the league. This was before Chicago traded for one of the league’s best interior defensive linemen. He could have an easier time adjusting to a new defense than Nelson, who is learning a new offensive scheme. Nelson will likely want revenge against Simmons for his previous Titans team defeating the Colts.

title: Seahawks Make Big Lineup Change for Bears Game
full_text:
After the Seattle Seahawks made a blockbuster trade for future Hall of Fame guard Quenton Nelson on Tuesday, the main question that arose was where he would play along the team's offensive line.
Nelson has played his entire eight-year NFL career as the Indianapolis Colts' left guard, but the Seahawks have the 2025 No. 18 overall pick, Grey Zabel, in that spot already. Zabel was an immediate boost for Seattle's offense at that position during their Super Bowl-winning season.
During his press conference on Thursday , Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed that Nelson will play left guard and Zabel will slide to right guard. Macdonald also said they expect Nelson to play on Monday night against the Chicago Bears.
“Yeah, [Nelson is] going to play left guard, and Grey’s going to slide to the right,” Macdonald said.
Zabel has experience at right guard from college, where he played multiple positions during a five-year career at North Dakota State. Macdonald and the Seahawks' staff expect that to ease his transition to the right side of the line.
“That’s the thought, is that he’s had a lot of experience playing on the right side, so that will help with the learning curve,” Macdonald added. “But, these things, there’s a process that has to be had, and we’ve got the right guys for the job, but we understand it’s a process as well and we’ve got to attack the heck out of it.”
Zabel, instead of working next to left tackle Charles Cross, will now have Abe Lucas to his right and Jalen Sundell to his left for the first time in his NFL career. Cross may also miss the game against the Bears, as he injured his ankle in the Seahawks' Sunday night win over the Kansas City Chiefs.
“It’s going to be a process,” Macdonald said. “Again, we’ve put a lot of time and effort into the chemistry of our offensive line, and we’ve got a couple of things shaken up right now. But the guys will do a great job of meshing and getting on the same page, and I think we’ll be better for it.”
Macdonald also discussed what he liked about the acquisition of Nelson, describing him as "decisive, shocking and relentless" in his style of play, and that's a big reason why they couldn't pass on adding him to the offensive front.
However, even amid the excitement, Macdonald acknowledged how it impacts the other players already on the team. Especially since Anthony Bradford, who has made 40 starts for the Seahawks over the last four seasons, now heads to the bench.
“Also, I just felt like it’s necessary saying, I think our offensive line probably played its best game of the season this past Sunday night, and I just want to be clear this isn’t a commentary on any of our personnel or anything like that,” Macdonald said. “We love our guys; it’s a situation where you understand how it affects the guys that have been here and are working really hard and have earned a great role on our team.
“But also, two things can be true at the same time: It’s an opportunity to bring along an all-time, probably a sure-fire Hall of Fame guard with a great track record. And from our understanding about the type of person he is, to join our locker room, it was just an opportunity that is going to make the Seahawks better.”

title: The Best, Worst and Likeliest Scenarios for Bears vs. Seahawks
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are taking on the Chicago Bears in Week 8's edition of Monday Night Football at Lumen Field.
The Seahawks and Bears are both in the NFC playoff picture as they try to jostle for positioning among the wild cards. That makes this week's contest super important, and the Seahawks hope the best-case scenario comes out on top. Here's a look at three possible outcomes for the Seahawks and Bears this week.
The Seahawks showed how dominant their defense can be after holding Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs to a single field goal in their matchup last week. The defense will be able to help them win games, and if they can do that against the number one offense in the league, they could probably do that against anybody.
It won't be easy against the Bears, who boast the third-best offense in the league, but the Seahawks will have the home crowd with them on primetime, and that should be a factor.
Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has looked strong throughout the season, but he has also struggled at points during the year, most notably in Week 2 against the Minnesota Vikings, when the offense scored just 3 points and he threw for 138 yards. He suffered an injury in that game and was out for a couple of weeks, but he has returned and thrown for over 300 yards in his past two games. If the Seahawks can catch him on an off day, they should have a chance to stay in the win column.
The defense will keep the Seahawks in games, but the offense has to do its part as well. Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has struggled with turnovers at points during the year, and it has led to some stalling within the offense.
Running the football helped against the Chiefs, and that should be the team strategy against the Bears as well. Getting Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back to the field will be a big help, but there could be some rust that needs to be shed. This might be the game they end up doing that.
A lot can go wrong for the Seahawks' offense, and if the defense gives up 14 to 17 points, it may not be enough for Seattle to win.
I'm anticipating a low-scoring game on both sides, mainly because the Seahawks' defense is allowing just 17.9 points per game, which ranks fourth in the NFL.
The Seahawks will be able to control the tempo as they usually do at Lumen Field, and that should create a very low-scoring affair. It won't be an easy game for the Seahawks to win, but if they can take the momentum they built after beating the Chiefs, they should be able to have the confidence to beat any team in their path, including the Bears. The Bears are one of the better teams the Seahawks will face on the schedule between now and the end of the season.

title: Seahawks Game Plan vs. Bears Changes After Jeffery Simmons Trade
full_text:
Another layer of preparation has been added for the Seattle Seahawks as they take on the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football in Week 8.
The Bears have made a big splash, acquiring All-Pro defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons in a trade with the Tennessee Titans . The Bears sent a pair of first-rounders and a fourth-round pick for Simmons, who is one of the best defensive linemen in the league. That should certainly boost their defense as they face the Seahawks, who have been inconsistent with the run throughout the season.
This matchup should be intriguing to watch during the game as the Seahawks could see the return of rookie running back Jadarian Price and veteran Zach Charbonnet, who was activated to the 53-man roster ahead of last week's game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
The Bears saw the Seahawks trade for Quenton Nelson earlier in the week from the Indianapolis Colts and felt they needed to make a trade themselves. Whether the reasoning behind the Simmons trade and the timing of it were a direct reaction to the Nelson deal remains to be seen. Still, it's hard to believe that the trade Seattle made earlier in the week didn't contribute to this.
By making a big trade for a high-level player, it sets the tone around the league that others need to improve the roster if they can, which is what Chicago ended up doing. They paid a much steeper price for Simmons than the Seahawks did for Nelson, but the idea was there.
The Week 8 contest also marks Nelson's potential debut with the team. Nelson is very familiar with Simmons from their duels in the AFC South twice a year ever since the latter joined the league in 2019.
Throughout Simmons' career against the Colts, he is 7-6 in 13 games. During those contests, he has recorded 51 tackles and seven for loss, with five sacks. When the Titans faced the Colts in Week 6, Simmons had six tackles, including two sacks and a fumble recovery as Tennessee beat Indianapolis 26-20 in their lone win this season.
Now, Nelson has a chance to get revenge on Simmons with their new teams in a game with much higher stakes.

title: The 49ers Should Trade a First-Round Pick for a Proven Difference-Maker
full_text:
The 49ers traded a fourth-round pick for DeForest Buckner this week. That was a good first move.
It should not be the only major move the 49ers make before the trade deadline, as Matt Maiocco thinks it will be. Because it wasn't really a major move. It was a shrewd, cost-effective move for a player who's past his prime. Plus, he might not be on the team next season. He will be a free agent.
And the other contenders aren't done making big-time trades. The Bears just sent two first-round picks to the Titans for Jeffery Simmons, who might be the best defensive tackle in the NFL right now.
In addition, they've been linked to Chargers edge rusher Khalil Mack, who probably will get dealt before the deadline. The Bears are all-in for 2026. They're mortgaging their future to win this season, something the 49ers haven't done yet. They're keeping their options open.
Meanwhile, the Seahawks and Vikings seem to be making trade offers for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, who singlehandedly could tip the balance of power in the NFC if he lands on one of those teams.
And then there's Maxx Crosby, who probably will get traded to a contender if the Raiders lose their next two games, which seems likely. Their opponents will be the Jets and the 49ers.
The 49ers can't just sit back and watch other teams trade for all the best players on the market. They have to be aggressive, too. Because this season is their best opportunity to win a Super Bowl with their current corps of players that happens to be the oldest corps among the legit contenders.
Sure, the 49ers were the best team in the NFL in September and October, but other teams are improving, and they're extremely banged up. Mike Evans has Achilles tendinitis. And if he tears that Achilles, the 49ers, as currently constructed, would be cooked.
Fortunately for the 49ers, they have their first-round picks for 2027 and 2028, and should be eager to trade them for the right player. Because the future doesn't matter. Those picks are expendable. The only thing that matters is winning the Super Bowl this season and not wasting another golden opportunity with an elite roster.
The 49ers aren't good at drafting in the first round anyway. In 10 years, the only first-round picks who have gotten second contracts from the 49ers are Nick Bosa and Brandon Aiyuk. The 49ers would have been better off had they traded all their first-round picks from the past decade for proven veterans.
But the 49ers haven't traded a first-round pick for a veteran since Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch joined the organization in 2017. That's the biggest difference between them and the Rams, who have a Super Bowl ring largely because they trade their first-round picks almost every year. They traded two first-round picks for Jalen Ramsey and won the Super Bowl shortly after.
Lynch should be on the phone right now with the Jets, offering two firsts and a fourth for wide receiver Garrett Wilson. Whatever it takes. Get it done.
And if the Jets simply refuse to trade him, the 49ers should call up the Raiders and trade two firsts for Maxx Crosby. He's not a wide receiver, but he still would fill a need and would be better than any pass rusher the 49ers would draft with one of those late first-round picks.
Get serious, 49ers. If you do nothing else and you don't win the Super Bowl, someone should get fired.

title: The Case for and Against the 49ers Going All-In on a Big Trade
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers made a big splash for DeForest Buckner , but they still have two weeks to go until the trade deadline. They also did not spend much in terms of draft capital on the trade, and while they took a chunk of salary, they are not tied to him beyond this year. So, they could still make another big move in the coming weeks.
Reports are that while the team is going to explore more moves, they might be similar to Keion White last year, and not quite like Christian McCaffrey. There is an argument to be made for both sides.
The 49ers' biggest need was defensive tackle. They were not getting Alfred Collins back this year, so they needed defensive tackle more than other positions. While they are injured at other spots, they are expected to get most of their players back.
Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel are expected to be back by the bye week, and De’Zhaun Stribling will be back this season. Trading for a wide receiver would force one of them out of the picture or force the team to cut someone like Jordan Watkins.
That would be to add a receiver like Brian Thomas Jr . or Jerry Jeudy, who are both having bad seasons. A trade for Garrett Wilson would likely cost something similar to Jeffery Simmons, which seems like a lot.
At edge rusher, Nick Bosa is expected to be back soon, and Mykel Williams is a former top-15 pick. If they added a big-name edge rusher, the development of rookie Romello Height would be stalled.
The same would be said at left guard or cornerback. If Connor Colby struggles or Nate Hobbs fails to replace Jack Jones, the team would turn to Carver Willis and Ephesians Prysock. They would delay their progress with any big additions.
Adding depth gives them a chance to protect themselves if they come along slowly while also giving their youth chances to take steps.
Obviously, an all-in move that pushes these two to the sides has its benefits as well. Playoff experience is underrated, and adding a veteran who is either hungry for a ring or knows how to win one could be what the team needs.
Will they go over the top, will they make a small move, or will they stand pat?

title: The 49ers Might Not Make Another Big Move Before the Trade Deadline
full_text:
After a 6-1 start, the San Francisco 49ers enter their Week 8 bye looking to bolster their roster for a playoff run with Super Bowl 61 aspirations.
The 49ers went all in, trading a 2027 fourth-round pick to the Indianapolis Colts for two-time All-Pro defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.
Fans and media have speculated that the 49ers will continue this aggressiveness and attempt to trade for New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson or Los Angeles Chargers pass rusher Khalil Mack; yes, these players are game changers, but the 49ers can find answers within.
The 49ers' biggest concern is at wide receiver after a fast offensive start to the season stalled in the last couple of weeks due to injuries at the position.
Last week against the Atlanta Falcons, the wide receiver struggles boiled over, and a 49ers wide receiver didn’t have a single catch until the second half. The Niners were without Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson.
On Tuesday, head coach Kyle Shanahan said the three wide receivers will have a chance to return after the bye week, making it unnecessary to trade for Wilson , especially with recent developments from receiver Jordan Watkins. The 49ers will also get back first-round pick De’Zhaun Stribling, who will return at the end of the season.
Wilson’s four-year, $130 million contract kicks in next season, affecting the 49ers' future salary cap. This move would be the opposite of the 49ers' move to get Buckner on a one-year rental; it would be a long-term investment.
The 49ers have also been in trade speculation around Mack. This move would improve the defensive front but would also stunt the development of an already crowded unit.
The 49ers' current edge rushers are Keion White, Mykel Williams, Romello Height, and Nick Bosa, who has dealt with an injury this season, but Shanahan said Tuesday he has a chance to be back after the bye week.
The only justifiable reason the 49ers should trade for Mack or any other edge rusher is if there is still concern about Bosa’s injuries.
Another position that hasn’t been mentioned in trade speculation but should be reviewed in the bye week is cornerback. In the last two games without Upton Stout, the 49ers allowed 257 passing yards, up from their season average of 224.
Stout is expected to be back after the bye week, but his absence revealed a glaring hole at cornerback.
Ashtyn Davis and Jack Jones, whom the 49ers released to make roster space for Buckner, replaced Stout, and both struggled.
If another 49ers starting cornerback gets injured again, they will be in a similar spot as the last couple of weeks. Right now, the backups are rookie Ephesians Prysock, Davis and Nate Hobbs, who is currently on injured reserve with no designation.

title: Cheap Alternatives to 49ers' Splashy Trade Targets
full_text:
While the San Francisco 49ers made a big swing for DeForest Buckner, it did not cost much draft capital. There are a few other big names that fans want the team to add over time before the trade deadline. However, there could also be some strong alternatives that could be had for a cost lower than Buckner. Who are the day-three trade values?
Dickerson is a three-time Pro Bowler; he is signed beyond this year, and he is still 28 years old. The Philadelphia Eagles traded Cam Jurgens for a second-round pick, and they probably view Dickerson in higher regard. The 49ers can give a massive pick for a player with injury concerns, or they can send a day-three pick or a pick swap for Bredeson.
Bredeson is also 28; he has 60 career starts, and he is also signed through 2027. This is a strong alternative.
Thomas has a 1,282-yard season under his belt, and he is still 24 years old. Still, he is averaging less than a yard per route this year and is going to cost a second-round pick .
Johnston does not have the same ceiling, but he has back-to-back 700-yard seasons. He is averaging 1.07 yards per route run, so a slight step above Thomas this year. The Chargers are 0-6, and Johnston is set to hit free agency this year. A former first-round pick could cost a sixth-round pick for the 49ers. The 49ers can see how good of a fit he is and either let him walk or look to extend him. At the trade cost, it is worth exploring.
Mack is the name that 49ers fans want the most. Still, a lot of teams want Mack, and the bidding war for an aging rental might get out of hand. Armstrong is also in the last year of his deal on a 1-4-1 Commanders team.
He is six years younger than Mack and had 5.5 sacks last year, the same number as Mack. Armstrong has 34 sacks in his nine-year NFL career and is a good run defender. The 49ers need depth behind Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams. The addition of Armstrong fills the role at a better draft cost.

title: One Player Greatly Benefits From 49ers Releasing Jack Jones
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have released cornerback Jack Jones on Wednesday to make room for DeForest Buckner on the 53-man roster.
Cutting Jones was an easy decision for the 49ers. He played terribly in the Week 7 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. It's been a theme for him all season, except Week 1.
His performance against Atlanta was the last straw. His presence will not be missed. Now that he's gone, there's one 49ers player who will greatly benefit from his release.
It's rookie Ephesians Prysock. He played a role in the 49ers releasing Jones, out of everyone else they could've chosen from.
He got in a couple of snaps against the Falcons. It was the start of the 49ers turning the page from Jones to Prysock.
This is 100% the right move for them. Jones was a walking penalty. He provided nothing but negative plays every single time he was on the field.
At least with Prysock, the 49ers will build up a player who gives long-term benefits. Jones doesn't, which isn't anything surprising.
Jones has never been a good player. At his best, he's a hit-or-miss player. But this season, he's been mostly a miss. The only time he was solid was in Week 1.
Since then, he's been a negative factor. Now, Prysock might be a liability as well, but he can learn from those mistakes.
The 49ers drafted him for a reason. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris had to have advocated for him or been interested to some degree.
He saw something in Prysock. He probably would've been in a better position on the team had he not gotten hurt before the season. In his limited showing, Prysock was pretty solid in the preseason.
There's a lot to like about him, especially his physical traits. He gives the 49ers a tall and lengthy option at cornerback, which they don't have with Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green.
The 49ers will bring Prysock into their dime package the same way they did with Jones. But now they can play with the matchups if they want him on a bigger receiver.
I don't think the moment will be too big for him either. The most important thing is that the 49ers get him developed. They couldn't do that with Jones on the roster.

title: How the 49ers Plan to Replace Jack Jones After Releasing Him
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers released cornerback Jack Jones as the corresponding move for the acquisition of DeForest Buckner. The move is a bit surprising considering Jones has played 93 snaps this season and played 22 snaps as recently as Week 7.
The team elected to keep depth instead of a player who was seeing the field, so one of the depth pieces is likely to step up. Who is going to get a chance now that Jones is gone?
The 49ers signed Hobbs after an injury-filled year with the Green Bay Packers ended with him getting released. The injuries have followed Hobbs to San Francisco, as he spent the first seven weeks on the IR. That team has not confirmed his status yet, but they have noted that he is close to returning. Before getting hurt last year, Hobbs was viewed as a potential starter.
So, the team can play him in dime situations to push Deommodore Lenoir into the slot.
The 49ers' fourth-round rookie has been eased into getting a chance. He was inactive to start his career, but has been getting looks on special teams since Week 5. After two weeks of special teams work, the 49ers got him on the field for the first time in Week 7.
Prysock only played two snaps. However, his progression in practice has led to more work. It appears as though the team is ready to give him a chance in NFL action now. Prysock had seven weeks to learn; now he gets the bye week to reset and get ready for a limited role. He would be a great option to replace Jones on the outside. Playing him in minimal dime scenarios is also a great way to dip his feet into the mix.
The 49ers mostly need a player for dime snaps, but if Upton Stout remains injured, the team will need a slot as well. Lenoir can move into the slot if they are high on Hobbs and Prysock. However, the backup in the slot has been Davis so far this year. The issue is that the 49ers have been electing to play Jones over Davis.
Hobbs has gotten healthy, and Prysock is a progressing rookie. Those two would have to be unready for Davis to have a big role out of the bye.

title: 49ers Trade for DeForest Buckner Looks Even Better After Jeffery Simmons Trade
full_text:
The 49ers just might know what they're doing when it comes to trades.
They got DeForest Buckner for a fourth-round pick. Meanwhile, the Chicago Bears just traded two first-round picks and a fourth-rounder to the Tennessee Titans for Jeffery Simmons and a fifth-round pick, according to reports.
Good gracious, that's a ton of draft capital to give up. To be fair, the Bears are going all-in, which is to be commended. And Simmons absolutely is a great player. He's a three-time All-Pro. But he's 29. His best days are not necessarily ahead of him. And he misses games every season.
There's a reason the Bears were interested in trading for Buckner before the 49ers got him -- he's cheaper than Simmons, and he's really good, too. Not as good as Simmons, and three years older than him, but still dominant. Still able to win one-on-one matchups. Still drawing double teams at a high rate.
The 49ers were able to land Buckner because they drafted him and presumably would be more open to extending his contract than the Bears would be. In Chicago, he'd be a one-year rental. Now, he might be able to finish his career where it started.
And the 49ers still can make another move, one as big as the Simmons trade if they want to, because they still have their first-round picks in 2027 and 2028. The Bears are out of picks, which means they're out of big moves. This is their team, for better or worse. And it certainly looks imposing on paper.
But the 49ers aren't done. They have roughly two weeks to pull off a blockbuster move of their own.
As of now, the Jets seem like an intriguing trade partner. They're not going to the playoffs this year and could be interested in selling certain players to load up on picks for 2027.
If wide receiver Garrett Wilson becomes available, which is no certainty, the 49ers just might trade their first-rounders in 2027 and 2028 for him. He's that good.
If the Jets want to hold onto their young franchise wide receiver, they could trade the 49ers Will McDonald IV instead. McDonald is a 27-year-old edge rusher who's signed through 2027. He would be an upgrade over Romello Height and Mykel Williams when it comes to rushing the quarterback, and he would give the 49ers insurance in case Nick Bosa doesn't make a full recover this season.
Stay tuned. The Bears might be done making big moves, but the 49ers probably aren't.

title: 3 Reasons the 49ers' Bye Week Comes at a Perfect Time
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers will not play a game this week, as they're on their Bye. It's a bummer for fans since they won't see their favorite team play.
But the Bye Week comes at a perfect time for the 49ers. In fact, there are three reasons to support that. Let's dive into what those reasons are.
The 49ers have no interest in moving on from Eddy Pineiro despite his struggles. Pineiro has the yips. It's undeniable at this point. Usually, it's a mental hurdle.
There was no way he was going to get over it by continuing to play games. Otherwise, he would've overcome it by now. With the Bye Week here, Pineiro can disconnect from football.
This is a perfect mental reset for him. He can erase all of his struggles he's had on the field and flip to a brand-new page starting in Week 9.
If he starts making his kicks, the Bye Week will be what helped him. It's the only fix for the yips. If not, he'll never break through. For now, the 49ers will hope it helps him get back to the player he was last year.
With no game to be played this week, the 49ers can turn all of their attention to the trade market. They've already taken advantage of it by acquiring DeForest Buckner from the Indianapolis Colts.
I think it's safe to say they will make another trade. The 49ers only gave up a 2027 fourth-round pick, so they have more than enough draft capital to reel in another premier player.
It probably won't occur this week, but thanks to the Bye, the 49ers can pay close attention to the games being played. They can make note of any displeased players in hopeless situations.
Buckner was one player. Can they find another? The Bye Week grants them the time, and especially the focus, to do it.
If the 49ers had their Bye in Week 5, it would've been brutal. That's the worst time to ever have it because teams are still relatively fresh and, in theory, shouldn't be heavily injured.
Even a Bye Week late in the season would be better. Thankfully, the 49ers got the hookup from the NFL schedule makers, as their Bye falls perfectly in the middle of the season.
They have a ton of players who are injured or playing through pain. This week off comes at a perfect time for them to focus on resting and recovering, especially for their wide receivers.
It's also a big benefit that it splits their season into two halves. That way, once they emerge from their Bye Week, they'll be in much better shape for the playoff push.

title: What It Would Cost the 49ers to Trade for Brian Thomas Jr. and is He Worth it?
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have been connected to Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. often in the past couple of weeks. After they were tied to DeForest Buckner in the media, the move was made, so anything is possible, and the rumors could have more legs than expected.
The big question is going to come down to cost. San Francisco added Buckner, who is productive, for a cost that was not significant. Most thoughts right now are that the Jaguars' asking price will be a bit more than that.
The biggest issue for the 49ers' chances of getting a bargain deal done is the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade. The Houston Texans traded a second-round pick for Harrison, and they also sent a sixth-round pick to get a seventh-round pick back.
Harrison still has a strong perception around him as a number four overall pick. However, Thomas was taken 23rd overall. The difference that will make Thomas more valuable on the trade market is that Thomas has flashed more production in the NFL.
Thomas has 146 catches for 2,115 yards. He averages 1.87 yards per route run in his NFL career. Harrison has 112 receptions for 1,618 yards. He averages 1.49 yards per route run. It is hard to find any stats that show Harrison as a more productive receiver.
However, almost all of that is due to his rookie season. Thomas had 1,282 yards as a rookie and has struggled since then. Still, while he averaged 1.45 yards per route run in year two and is currently at 0.95 yards per route run this year, Harrison is still not proving much more.
He averaged 1.58 yards per route run in his second season, but right now he is at 0.79. As a cautionary tale for 49ers fans, Harrison has four catches for 40 yards in his two games with the Texans since being traded.
The Jaguars do not have much of a need for Thomas, and the 49ers' lack of depth and talent at receiver makes them a strong trade fit. However, if Jacksonville compares Thomas to Harrison and will likely want a second-round pick back in return
If that is the case, the 49ers have to start thinking about alternatives. A second-round pick for a struggling wideout is risky.
