title: 3 Dream Trade Targets That Would Transform the 49ers
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have made it clear that they're all-in on their Super Bowl run this season. That's why they traded for DeForest Buckner.
Don't expect them to stop there either. Another trade is certainly on the table , but some of them are dreams that most likely won't turn into reality. Let's dive into the three dream trades that could transform the 49ers.
With Nick Bosa struggling to stay healthy this season, the 49ers need to strongly look at edge rushers on the trade market. Maxx Crosby should be one of those targets.
He's been a name that has been linked to the 49ers dating back to February, when Crosby initially wanted out of the Las Vegas Raiders.
Crosby wound up with the Baltimore Ravens for a day before the Ravens backed out of the deal. That lowered Crosby's value after they failed his physical.
If the 49ers want Crosby, a first-round pick should get the job done. It would be well worth it, too. They need a premier edge rusher to wake up their pass rush.
Crosby has only registered two sacks, but he's the only real threat on the Raiders' defensive front. He's still managed to tally 31 pressures, which would lead the 49ers.
Unfortunately, I doubt the 49ers can bring Crosby in. The Raiders are unlikely to be sellers, despite it making sense, especially since trading Crosby already failed once before.
Another dream trade that would be tough for the 49ers to pull off is for Khalil Mack. I know that's shocking to say, considering the Los Angeles Chargers are the last winless team.
If any team should be sellers, it's them. Mack is their greatest trade piece as well. The 49ers could easily send them a second-round pick for Mack.
He's tallied three sacks and 18 pressures. He has decent numbers despite the Chargers trailing most of the game, so the pass-rushing opportunities aren't plentiful.
The reason I don't see the Chargers trading Mack is that they haven't fired offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. If they haven't made that move, then it must mean they want to hold off.
Either they're going to sink with the ship, or they're not ready to make any moves yet. I'm not sure the 49ers can wait that long. There have been no reports of their interest in trading anyone, either. It's rough.
You cannot log in to social media without seeing Garrett Wilson being pushed onto the 49ers. Whether it's fans or pundits, Wilson to the 49ers is being widely discussed, and understandably so.
Their wide receiver depth is in a state of emergency with all of the injuries.  But the biggest concern is Mike Evans. Will he make it late in the season with Achilles tendinitis?
It's a tough spot to be in. Evans is crucial to the 49ers' success. He's been the MVP of the team. Acquiring Wilson would help quell that concern.
Unfortunately, Wilson has no chance of being traded to the 49ers. There hasn't been a single notion that the Jets are considering it.
Any idea that he is headed to San Francisco is just conjecture. A pipe dream. The 49ers would ascend dramatically with him, but it'll never happen.

title: Buccaneers Reveal Good News and Bad News Before Falcons Game
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are set to play a crucial game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday.
With a Carolina Panthers loss on Thursday night against the Green Bay Packers, the Bucs remain just 1.5 games out of the division lead. If Tampa Bay wins on Sunday against the Falcons, they'll be within half a game of the NFC South crown.
The Bucs lost their game at home to the Falcons last year during the infamous "3rd & 28" scenario, but they beat the Falcons on the road to begin that season. They had a lot of help from their rookie wide receiver that year, but one year later, that wideout won't be available for Tampa Bay during this matchup.
Todd Bowles confirmed that wide receiver Emeka Egbuka will be out for Sunday.
Egbuka was a big contributor in Tampa Bay's win against the Falcons last year, but he won't be playing in this game. Egbuka suffered a concussion against the Pittsburgh Steelers and appeared to clear protocol on Thursday, shedding a black non-contact jersey for his regular one, but he wasn't participating at all on Friday.
Egbuka has also been dealing with a foot injury on top of his concussion. Bowles said Friday that Egbuka cleared concussion protocol, but that his foot is still injured.
Tackle Luke Goedeke, meanwhile, was out last week against the Carolina Panthers with a calf injury and he did not participate in the first two days of practice. He did participate in this last day of practice this week, and Bowles said that he has a chance to play on Sunday, which is very encouraging for the Bucs — Goedeke has been an excellent right tackle this season.
If Goedeke can't go, though, Ben Chukwuma will fill in for him instead. Chukwuma filled in for Goedeke against the Panthers last week, and he played well — Bowles praised his effort the following Monday. He'd be up again to replace Goedeke, and if Goedeke cannot go, the team would certainly feel good about his abilities heading into Sunday.
The Bucs play the Falcons at 1 p.m. in Raymond James Stadium Nov. 1. They won't have their star wideout, but they could have one of their best offensive linemen.

title: Bucs Finally Have a Huge Advantage Against Falcons Nobody is Talking About
full_text:
Tampa Bay has always been a hot spot for transplants from up north. With that, those people have brought their fandom for other teams to the community that boasts three professional sports teams of their own.
That has been obvious for years whenever you tune into Tampa Bay Buccaneers home games.
While plenty of Bucs fans make up the crowd, over the years, there has consistently been a large contingent of opposing fans in the stands.
It's becoming an issue that has brought frustration amongst Tampa Bay fans, and that couldn't have been clearer than when the Pittsburgh Steelers fans practically took over Raymond James Stadium.
However, in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons, the Bucs will likely have an advantage in the stands.
Despite Atlanta being relatively close to Tampa compared to numerous other organizations, their fanbase is not known to travel well, and those Atlanta natives don't make up a large portion of those who have moved to the area or visit during the cooler months of the year.
It should align with the Bucs having their most fans in the stadium this season. That is big for a team that can live and die by momentum.
Fans and crowd noise can carry a team to victory, and the Buccaneers will be hopeful that their fans bring it on Sunday as they search to start 2-0 in the division and continue their midseason turnaround.
It's the most important game up to this point in the season. With the Panthers losing to the Packers on Thursday night, the Bucs could find themselves right at the top of the division if they beat the Falcons on Sunday.
With a win, the Bucs, Falcons, and Panthers would all have three wins on the season, but the Bucs would be 2-0 in the division. There is nothing quite like the NFC South.
There is a ton on the line this week, so the fans must bring the atmosphere to help the players on the field continue their recent surge of great play at every level.

title: Buccaneers Have a Major Problem Nobody Expected This Season
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers' passing offense is averaging 150.4 yards per game. That is the worst in the entire NFL and is certainly not what fans and the organization had in mind this season when thinking about the offense.
There are a lot of factors as to why this aspect of the game has been so disappointing. Baker Mayfield missed three games due to a dislocated thumb, you had undrafted free agent rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels filling in and the offensive line has struggled to keep either quarterback upright to make plays.
However, there are too many good players in this offense for the passing attack to be this poor. Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin Jr., Ted Hurst III, Tez Johnson and Cade Otton have simply not been getting the football enough, and that is both on the quarterbacks and offensive coordinator Zach Robinson.
One thing the Bucs have been doing well under Zac Robinson is running the football. The team is coming off one of the best team rushing performances in franchise history, and head coach Todd Bowles even went so far as to say the run game is their calling card.
"I mean, I think that's our calling card. We play a lot better when we run the ball very successfully, whether we're home or on the road," Bowles said. "We haven't had much success at home, running the football or winning at home, but we've got to turn that around and win a home game."
Robinson has also said that this offense needs to be established through the run game.
"Yeah, if we can do that every week, that would be outstanding," Robinson said. "You always want to be able to establish a run and be able to have things that play off of the run game. Then, there [are] going to be weeks where, shoot, you might not have as many run opportunities and you're going to get back on track. That's the nature of the NFL — everything is week to week. If we can play like that, it'll definitely help us out in the long run."
Time will tell if we do see legitimate improvement in the passing game going forward. But it seems like right now the team is content to be a run-first offense and take shots in the passing attack when they can.

title: Buccaneers Players We Could See Moved Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
Many people assumed that if the Tampa Bay Buccaneers lost to the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, it would all but seal their fate — not just as a team destined to miss out on the postseason, but as one that would become open for business ahead of the trade deadline in order to get a head start on retooling the roster ahead of next season.
The Bucs did win that game, though. They beat the top team in the NFC South 43-13 in their first divisional matchup of the season, and they did so in convincing fashion. As a result, many believe that the Buccaneers will put any plans for a potential fire sale on hold — at least for now.
That being said, there are plenty of experts who still believe it's a matter of when, not if, the Buccaneers will commit to trading  in order to acquire some extra draft capital
On Wednesday, ESPN released a list of the top 25 trade candidates in the NFL, and a three different Buccaneers were listed.
The first Buccaneers trade candidate named in the article was the Buccaneers' talented fourth-year edge rusher, Yaya Diaby. Diaby is coming off his best game of the season on Sunday where he put up an impressive stat line that included three sacks, three tackles and three QB hits.
Diaby is in a unique situation. Not only is he an impending free agent, but the player behind him on the depth chart, David Walker, has been incredibly productive in the limited opportunities he's received so far this year, leading the entire league with a pass-rush win rate of 24.6%.
Highest pass rush win rate this season among edge David Walker                    24.6% Aidan Hutchinson          24.2% Nik Bonitto                        20.2% Chase Young                    20.0% Princely Umanmielen   20.0% pic.twitter.com/pxwe1QFpX8
ESPN predicts that Diaby has a 35% chance of being traded, and sees the best team fits being the Browns, Seahawks and Cowboys.
After several injury-riddled seasons, Chris Godwin finally came into 2026 at full health. Unfortunately, with Mike Evans no longer beside him, Godwin has struggled to establish himself as the consistent weapon he once was for the Buccaneers' offense. That being said, poor quarterback play and questionable offensive schematics could be more to blame than Godwin himself.
Either way, ESPN still sees Godwin as one of the top 25 trade candidates in the NFL right now, and they believe he could be appealing in the right situation. The Chiefs and Commanders were both identified as possible trade partners for the Bucs as it relates to Godwin.
Here's what NFL expert and analyst Matt Bowan had to say about Godwin's appeal on the trade market:
"Godwin has yet to top 50 receiving yards in a game this season, and his play speed is declining," he wrote. "However, he still has value as a slot target with outside flex. He can use his coverage awareness to find open grass. And Godwin is willing to work the heavy traffic areas of the field on middle-of-the-field concepts."
ESPN believes that Chris Godwin has a 15% chance of being traded this season.
Robinson has been the Buccaneers' best free-agent acquisition by a mile, as the veteran DT has been a major factor against the run while also leading the team with two interceptions. Not only that, but Robinson has been a strong, vocal leader in the locker room and someone who leads by example on the field with a relentless and aggressive style of play.
For teams that aren't looking to break the bank by trading for a top tier DT like the 49ers and Bears have already done, Robinson could be the perfect fit for a team that is looking to reinforce the trenches on the defensive side of the ball.
ESPN gave Robinson a 30% chance of being traded and listed the Rams, Ravens and Giants as potential suitors.
Whether the Buccaneers do indeed become sellers ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline will likely depend on how they perform this week in another divisional game vs. the Atlanta Falcons. If the Buccaneers pull off another victory, it would not be surprising to see the Bucs stand pat and try to make a push up the standings. If they lose? The chances of the players listed above suiting up for another team this season will surely increase even more.

title: Why Buccaneers Must Follow Titans With Jeffrey Simmons Trade
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is quiet some years and loud in others, and this year seems to be a big year for the league when it comes to trades.
One of the biggest trades in recent memory took place on Thursday. The Chicago Bears traded for Tennessee Titans star defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons, giving up two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick to acquire his services. It's a big splash for the Bears, and it also means the Tampa Bay Buccaneers will face him in two weeks, in Week 9.
The Bucs, meanwhile, are struggling to start the season. As the trade deadline looms, should they be shopping their own elite DT, Vita Vea, after the Simmons trade?
Yes, they absolutely should. There's no better time to make it happen and get some capital back.
Let's make one thing clear — the Buccaneers will not get two firsts for Vita Vea. They won't even get one.
Vea is 31 years old. He's also a nose tackle, whereas Simmons is more of a three-tech defensive tackle, and Simmons plays a more valuable position. Finally, Simmons was already extended by the Titans prior to this season, so he was more desirable as a trade target because the Bears will not have to extend him — Vea got a one-year extension this offseason, but any team that would acquire him would still have to pay him sooner rather than later.
Vea will not command that capital. The Bucs would probably be fortunate to get a third-round pick for Vea, but that doesn't mean the Bucs shouldn't do it.
The Bucs are currently 2-5. Unbelievably, they still have a shot at the division, as they're just 1.5 games out, but they're likely to, at best, finish with a similar record to what they did last year. At worst, it'll be much worse, and Tampa Bay will bring in a new head coach and potentially new front office members.
Either scenario means that the Bucs should be sellers , not buyers. Vea is a prime candidate to sell, and his value could be at its highest it has been as an arms race is beginning to take off in the NFL before the trade deadline. It's not just Vea — the Bucs should be listening in on offers for everyone.
For now, though, Vea remains a Buccaneer, and if the Bucs can string together a few wins against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 and the Chicago Bears in Week 9, he likely will for the rest of the year. If they lose those two games, though? Keep an eye on the Bucs in the trade market.

title: Rob Gronkowski Believes Buccaneers Were His Ultimate Career Choice
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' 2020 Super Bowl run feels both like yesterday and also forever ago.
Besides a few leftover players from that Super Bowl run, much of the team looks completely different.
That Super Bowl-winning team was stacked with talent and production, and the Bucs are still working on figuring out how to build a roster that could resemble it.
One of the key players from that team was tight end Rob Gronkowski, and he spoke with the Today Show during an episode of "Glass Half Full" about the one career move that was the best thing to happen to him.
"Best thing that ever happened to me in my career was going to Tampa Bay," Gronkowski said. "The Bucs, I mean, it was a team that never rivaled against the Patriots. I didn't want to go to Miami or the Jets or something. That would be weird.
"I have too much love for New England, you know? And in that sense. I never believed Tom [Brady] was going to leave New England, by the way. I was like, 'yeah, right'... I was like, 'You do what you do in free agency. If it lines up and you actually do it, I'll look into the situation.'"
"Things I feel like are going to come my way for a lifetime now since I went to Tampa and won another Super Bowl."
Gronkowski came out of retirement in 2020 once Brady made his decision to join the Bucs in free agency, and eventually made his way to Tampa Bay after the team struck a deal with the New England Patriots.
Gronkowski was instrumental in the team's Super Bowl run and finished his two-year stint with the Bucs with 100 receptions for 1,425 yards and 13 touchdowns.
Gronkowski had most of his success with the Patriots, but once he laid some roots in Tampa Bay, his popularity across the league soared, bringing him multiple different business and personal opportunities along the way.
Gronk still has a strong relationship with the organization and Tampa community, so it's clear that it was a great career move for him — not only to win another Lombardi Trophy, but also to further his connections and build lasting relationships in a city that has plenty to offer.

title: Baker Mayfield Addresses Awkward Kevin Stefanski Reunion Ahead of Bucs-Falcons
full_text:
Baker Mayfield left the Cleveland Browns in 2021 under some dubious circumstances.
After getting drafted by Cleveland with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft, Mayfield would be the franchise guy until the team traded for former Houston Texans superstar Deshaun Watson and traded Mayfield away to the Carolina Panthers.
This would be the start of an odyssey that would see Mayfield go through many struggles before finding his place once more as the franchise quarterback of the Buccaneers. The head coach who started this whole journey was none other than the current Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski.
Stefanski was the head coach of the Browns at the time of Mayfield's departure and was one of the head decision-makers to send Mayfield packing.
When asked about facing his former coach and current Falcons Head Coach Kevin Stefanski and if their familiarity with each other will have any impact on this week's game, Mayfield kept it curt.
"No, I haven't spoken to him since 2021," Mayfield told the media.
When asked on whether the way things ended between him and Stefanski in Cleveland still 'eats at him, Mayfield didn't seem bothered.
"No, I'm doing alright," He said.
Now this is true that Mayfield is doing better than "alright" — he's the franchise quarterback of a new team and is making the most money ever in his career. However, Mayfield is also a man who has been known not to forget, so he could have a bigger chip on his shoulder than normal going into this upcoming game.
The team is also eager to get their first home win of the season after starting out 0-4.
"Very eager. We talked about that this morning. We haven't won a home game yet. It's not just about that — obviously, this division game is extremely important, but [we] definitely need to get our mojo back at home."
It would be a very poetic situation if Mayfield were to exact a small amount of revenge on the coach who cast him aside in Cleveland and prove him even slightly wrong that he bet on the wrong player.
The only other time Mayfield has played against a Stefanski team was when he was with the Carolina Panthers and Stefanski was still with the Browns. Mayfield came up short in that matchup, but this is a chance at redemption.

title: The Biggest Swing the Buccaneers Can Take at the Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are right back in the thick of things in the NFC South as we approach the midway point of the 2026 season.
They won their first division contest against the Carolina Panthers to bring their record to 2-5, with hope still attached to being able to turn it around.
One aspect the Bucs have yet to figure out this season has been the passing game. No matter who has been behind center, neither Baker Mayfield nor Jalon Daniels has been able to get things going, specifically, when it comes to pushing the ball downfield.
While some of the struggles can be attributed to the play calling by Zac Robinson, we believe Tampa Bay could make a big splash before the trade deadline to help things in the aforementioned area of the offense.
The passing game has obviously struggled this season — ranking dead last in the league — and could use a high-pedigree, explosive threat who can stretch the field.
His combination of size, speed and talent is something that allows him to beat corners in almost every facet. With most of the Bucs' wideouts struggling and rookie Ted Hurst still trying to earn Mayfield's trust, BTJ would come in as a young, proven player that Mayfield would likely feel more comfortable with.
The skill set is obvious, but it would also be a steal for the Bucs considering his recent decline in production since Liam Coen took over, along with the fact that he is still on his rookie contract.
Instead of spending on an expensive vet, it would be a gamble on a young, gifted player who could be looking for a new home so he can shine the brightest.
The Jaguars and Buccaneers have rarely done business with one another over the years, with the most recent trade coming via the NFL Draft in 2022, which was just pick swaps.
However, the two franchises are more familiar with each other than ever given Liam Coen's ties to Tampa.
Would Jags' general manager James Gladstone be more willing to pick up the phone for Licht and company if they are interested in Thomas Jr.?
If they are, would Licht be willing to part with high draft capital even though he's struggling a bit in his third season? The easy answer would be yes.
BTJ is a former first-round pick and exploded in his rookie season for over 1,200 yards and ten touchdowns, good enough to earn him Pro Bowl honors. And despite his struggles, he could find the Bucs' offense more simplified and better suited to his game.
With promise still clearly there with Thomas Jr., it would be a no-brainer to offer an early 3rd-round pick for his services. The high upside is there, but it remains to be seen if Licht has what it takes to make such a drastic move.

title: Buccaneers Could Be Getting Crucial Defensive Player Back
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got their first big win they needed last Sunday when they defeated the Carolina Panthers 43-13. That win put them 1.5 games back from the NFC South lead, and now, they have another key matchup that could put them closer to the lead.
The Bucs face off against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday in Raymond James Stadium in another big divisional matchup. If the Bucs win this game and the Panthers drop their Thursday Night Football matchup to the Green Bay Packers, the Bucs will be just 0.5 games out of the NFC South lead.
They'll need every ounce of firepower they can muster to make that happen. And they could be getting a big player back on the defense when they do go to play the Falcons.
Buccaneers defensive back Antoine Winfield Jr. suffered a rib fracture against the Green Bay Packers in Week 4. He's since missed three games, and if he were to miss this upcoming one, it would be his fourth game out of the lineup.
That doesn't look like it's going to happen, though. Winfield Jr. participated in practice on Wednesday — he participated last week in a black non-contact jersey, but this week, he's in his regular uniform and looks to be ready to take some hits.
Good news and bad news from Day 1 of practice in Week 8 — Antoine Winfield Jr is in a regular contact jersey and could be ramping up to go, but Emeka Egbuka is in a non-contact jersey and we didn’t see Luke Goedeke out here at all pic.twitter.com/lsS2nqV1ma
Winfield is one of the highest-paid defenders in football, playing on a four-year, $84.1 million deal he signed after an All-Pro season in 2023. Winfield has 15 solo tackles and one forced fumble in the four games he has played in Tampa Bay so far.
Safety Ifeatu Melifonwu has been playing in Winfield's stead. Melifonwu has put up six solo tackles in three games.
The Bucs are still dealing with some injuries, however. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka is still in concussion protocol and is playing with a black non-contact jersey. Offensive tackle Luke Goedeke, who did not play last Sunday against the Panthers, was also not practicing, and linebacker Josiah Trotter did not appear during the practice window on Wednesday.
The Bucs will face off against the Falcons at 1 p.m. on November 1. It will be Michael Penix's first game starting at quarterback in Raymond James Stadium, and Winfield could be a key piece in containing him on Sunday.

title: Should the Bucs Become Sellers at the Trade Deadline Like the Colts?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are in a weird spot right now.
No, the season has not gone the way they have wanted it to. The Bucs are just 2-5, they have one of the worst passing games in football and they have some aging players who haven't produced like expected.
Yes, they are still in the thick of the NFC South fight — they're just 1.5 games back from first place and could get half a game back should the Panthers lose on Thursday and the Bucs beat the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday.
Another team with the same record, the Indianapolis Colts, have decided to become major sellers at the trade deadline. They dealt star guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks for a third-round pick and a fifth-round pick, and they traded defensive tackle DeForest Buckner back to the San Francisco 49ers for a fourth-round pick.
The Colts have the same record as the Bucs, but they are in far from the same divisional situation. So should Tampa Bay act like them and become sellers at the trade deadline?
There are arguments for and against. But we think they should be.
Yes, it's a tricky scenario. The Bucs could play catch-up in the division if they get hot, and a string of wins would put them right back in the picture despite the fact that Tampa Bay started its season 0-4.
But for the future? The Bucs are not going to win the Super Bowl. Their future with head coach Todd Bowles is likely limited as well, and so far, they've had just one year with a double-digit win total since 2022. They have aging players on the roster, and now is the time to maximize that value and really get something from those players.
Players like Vita Vea, Antoine Winfield Jr. and Chris Godwin could net some return. Yaya Diaby had a strong game against the Carolina Panthers, but he hasn't looked elite otherwise and is on a contract year — that could save the Bucs some money next year and net some picks.
The Bucs may want to hold on to these players. They're franchise players general manager Jason Licht drafted, and as it stands, the Bucs still have a shot at winning the NFC South — based on how every other team in the division has looked, it might even be a good one.
But what then? Do the Bucs limp into the playoffs, maybe with a losing record? Do they once again get bounced in the first round? Do they even make it at all with such a poor start? Far more things are likely to go wrong than right for this team, and this iteration of Tampa Bay will not be around for much longer.
If that's the case, the Bucs should make like the Colts. They should be taking calls on anyone, and the more draft picks they can get for the future, the better. Plenty of players on Tampa Bay's roster still have value while not producing much this season, and those players are the ones that Tampa Bay should be open for business on.
The Bucs will likely take this game by game. The next one is against the Falcons at 1 p.m., and if they lose that game, they might shift into selling mode before the trade deadline. If they win, they'll likely run the roster they have — even if that would be a mistake.

River Wells is a sports journalist from St. Petersburg, Florida, who has covered the Tampa Bay Buccaneers since 2023. He graduated with a journalism degree from the University of Florida in 2021. You can follow him on Twitter @riverhwells.

title: Titans Players Shocked by Simmons Trade — Why Their Week 8 Response Could Define 2026 Season
full_text:
Titans fans were properly heartbroken when longtime favorite Jeffery Simmons was traded to the Chicago Bears yesterday. The argument for the franchise is clear: Two first-round picks would be hard to turn down for just about anybody. This rebuild finally has some real steam.
Yet, there's an emotion to this move that can't be so quickly dismissed. According to Albert Breer, Simmons himself even shared in that emotion. In a behind-the-scenes look at how it all went down, Breer reported that Simmons was "a bit heartbroken and didn’t want to leave."
Saleh told the rest of the team minutes after the news was broken to Simmons; one prominent player even asked "Why did we do this?" Yet, Saleh took the meeting to set the stage for a potential turnaround moving forward.
Week 8 is going to be a turning point for the Titans either way. How the team responds to the Simmons move agains the Cincinnati Bengals could very well define their season.
Breer wrote that Saleh conceded to his team that the normal reaction from any player in this circumstance would be something along the lines of: "What the ----," to which Breer added, "and think the organization was mailing it in and no longer care about the 2026 team."
"The abnormal thing would be to acknowledge it was the business, and use the opportunity’s result to compete and improve," Breer continued.
That will be the difference for Tennessee in just two days. On the road against a 4-2 team that boasts one of the best offenses in the league, a 1-6 Titans squad will have the opportunity to do the seemingly impossible and upset the Bengals freshly absent their best player.
To mirror Saleh's own sentiment, a normal response from a roster that suddenly lost their rock mid-week would be to phone it in and mourn his absence with a lifeless loss. However, the abnormal response would be for the defense to tick up without him, and at the very least, swing hard in defeat.
The Titans' response in Week 8 sets the stage for the rest of this year. Even if more guys get moved, it'd likely be more predictable names that haven't defined this franchise like Simmons did. Trades are part of the business, but losing someone like Simmons is different.
With a relatively new general manager and a new head coach leading the way, how will this mixed-and-matched Tennessee squad answer? Saleh himself acknowledged yesterday that his job is dependant on wins and losses. We've seen rebuilds stretch out over multiple decision-makers before.
In fact, the Titans' ongoing rebuild is the perfect example. No matter what the outlook for this franchise is going forward, it's on him to find a way to win right now. It's on him to get his guys to buy in, even after the team's beating heart was traded away.
"Hours later, the team had a spirited practice, one of its best of the season," said Breer, noting what came right after the Titans' team meeting. That's a good sign, and fans shouldn't yet be discouraged until we see what this team looks like without Simmons for the first time since 2019.
All the same, punches can't be pulled after Week 8. If this group doesn't have the pieces to take Saleh - Mike Borgonzi, the franchise, the fans - where they need to go, we'll know definitively in two days.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Predicting a Second Titans Trade Following Jeffery Simmons Deal: Another Defender is Sent Packing
full_text:
Franchise cornerstone Jeffery Simmons is officially a Titan no more. Tennessee sent the captain DT packing today in exchange for two first-round picks from the Chicago Bears. It's a pain to lose Simmons, and fans should absolutely mourn that loss... but what a haul for Tennessee.
Those draft picks will be crucial for the Titans over the next two offseasons and, handled correctly, could make the difference in Tennessee finally climbing out of their eternal rebuild. Check out our new first-round mock draft following the Simmons trade today.
But trading away a piece like Simmons, when he wasn't even deemed the most likely candidate, suggests a fire sale. It suggests the Titans aren't done. That's why I'm predicting that Tennessee makes another trade, and it may come even sooner than we thought.
I believe the next Titan to go will be CB Alontae Taylor. The buzz surrounding a potential Taylor trade has risen since his benching in Week 6, and NFL Insider Ari Meirov just gave us another reason to anticipate the move.
Meirov reported today that Taylor is a player that "Tennessee would be willing to trade," although the stipulation is that there would need to be a market for Taylor. Given his rough start to the season, that could be a hangup.
All the same, Taylor was signed to a $58 million deal in the first place because of his success as a nickel corner with the New Orleans Saints. After failing to move Taylor to the outside, Tennessee is between a rock and a hard place with their recent CB acquisition.
Not only does Saleh tend to utilize CBs almost like linebackers in his unique defensive system - which, as Meirov noted, doesn't suit Taylor's skillset - but the team also has a solid nickel already, in Marcus Harris. Even given his expensive signing, it makes complete sense for the Titans to move on from Taylor.
Ultimately, I think they will. Tennessee is bound to lose money on Taylor's deal, but if we're stacking up on draft stock, the move looks worthwhile.
With teams like the Pittsburgh Steelers, Buffalo Bills, and Detroit Lions all in the rumored market for a CB, the closer we get to the deadline, the more likely those franchises may be to make a risky deal like this one. Anything Tennessee got out of Taylor at this point would look like a win due to his struggles.
Eat some of the money? Sure. Get a, say, fifth-round pick? Even better. At this point, it's about loading up on young talent and getting out of deals that could limit this team's full rebuild going forward. Taylor may only be seven games into his Tennessee tenure, but he may be the top candidate to go.

title: How Jeffery Simmons Trade Begs a Brutal Question About Cam Ward's Future With Titans
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans sent shockwaves throughout the entire league when they decided to trade the face of their franchise, star DT Jeffery Simmons , to the Chicago Bears for a massive draft haul that included two first round picks.
While this trade undoubtedly gives the team the ammo it needs to start turning things around eventually, it also raises one interesting question: what does this mean for QB Cam Ward?
You could argue that they’re just acquiring as much draft capital as possible knowing this team obviously still needs a lot of work.
However, you could also argue that they don’t make this move if they genuinely believed Ward was close in his development to getting this team back to being competitive.
One moment that stood out during today’s press conference occurred when Titans general manager Mike Borgonzi was asked to name the current face of this franchise now that Simmons is gone, and he failed to specifically name any player... including his first-pick QB.
Easton Freeze of AtoZ Sports directly asked Borgonzi whether or not this move sends an underlying message about how they feel about Ward going forward:
“No, I think the message is we know we have to get better as a team. And [with] 53 guys on the roster, we know that we have to be better this year, next year, the year after. And this draft capital will give us the opportunity to [be better]. We have a lot of work to do, and we have to make the right decisions.”
HC Robert Saleh shared the same tone when asked a similar question: “This has nothing to do with Cam and everything to do with trying to continue to build a roster that’s competitive with the NFL greats… This has nothing to do with Cam.”
Only time will tell how this franchise truly feels about the young quarterback they’ve already invested so much in. But one thing is for certain, this front office now has the ammo to move up and down the board come draft weekend.
They also have the ammo to pull off a blockbuster trade of their own should a fellow struggling team like the Chargers make QB Justin Herbert available this offseason. Obviously, that’s something that sounds crazy right now, but having this type of ammo at their disposal gives this front office the flexibility to attack any possible scenario that intrigues them.
At minimum, the Titans are now set to enter the offseason with four first-round picks over the next two drafts to play with. How they use these picks is anybody’s guess. But for their sake and their fans' sake, whatever they decide to do, let’s just hope they finally get it right.
Shaun is a longtime Titans fan who has years of experience in the field. He missed being on the team beat, and is here to change that. He also writes scripts for EA Sports' Madden games, where fans may have heard his work.

title: Titans Mock Draft: Outlining an Ideal 2027 First Round After Jeffery Simmons Trade, Including a QB
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans trading Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears essentially set the next phase of their rebuild into motion. General manager Mike Borgonzi took the sort of massive swing that this franchise needed to rearrange the pieces once more.
Although now, with two first-round picks in next year's draft, the stakes are higher than ever for Borgonzi and the Titans' brass to get those selections right. In the spirit of early mocks for a 1-6 team, I'm taking a swing at those two picks.
These positions are based on NFL.com's 2027 draft order entering Week 8, which is about the best you can ask for an entire half-season away from finished results. Let's get to mocking.
I've already circled a handful of defensive prospects that the Titans could take to try and fill the hole Simmons leaves on defense. While not a DT, there are few better defensive prospects on paper than South Carolina EDGE Dylan Stewart.
Stewart, a big-body, 6'5" 250 lbs EDGE, has two sacks and three forced fumbles for the Gamecocks this season. The pass rusher is a premier defender in the SEC, and in his third year, has hit a peak that has him well beyond elite conversations.
He'd be a good pick anywhere for the Titans, even if they somehow managed to sneak into the top spot. Stewart's ability to shrink the pocket and slip around linemen for fast TFLs is unlike any other prospect in the 2027 class.
In Saleh's defense, the 21-year old would be a plug-n-play spark for a group that just lost their best player. Stewart is a no-brainer in the early first round, and I don't believe anybody would be upset with that investment.
This next one, however, I'm prepared to take a little heat for.
I get it, Cam Ward is only in his second season. But the QB's regression should alarm fans beyond the point of "he'll get there." More here on Ward's struggles and Tennessee's immediate options.
But what about the future? If the Simmons trade makes anything clear, it's that the Titans don't believe they can compete right now. This team is racing toward another full reset, and that wouldn't be the case if it was only a matter of time until Ward finally gets right.
Not only is drafting a QB an option next year, but it's almost likely at this point. After using their more valuable first on a long-term defensive asset, I have the Titans taking a late-first risk on Notre Dame's signal caller, CJ Carr.
All the times we say “Ugly release”, “Bad footwork”, “Poor vision-one read”, “No pocket presence/escapability” … Yeah we don’t have to say that for Notre Dame QB CJ Carr at 21 years old pic.twitter.com/DAYhE6LER9
Jordan Reid slated Carr as the fourth QB in his draft rankings from earlier this month. Reid reported that AFC area scout said the following of Carr: "I think he's the most NFL-ready from an awareness and processing standpoint."
Sure, Carr may not be as explosive as guys like Drew Mestemaker and Trinidad Chambliss, but he's arguably the safest bet of the bunch. Through seven games in his junior campaign with the Fighting Irish, Carr has thrown 16 touchdowns to just one interception. Notre Dame is 6-1.
He boasts an 84.8 QBR and 1,639 yards on the year. At the end of the day, the tape doesn't lie. Carr is an extremely good decision-maker with natural arm talent and visibly high football IQ. He's the opposite of Ward as a prospect in many ways, and that's just what Tennessee needs.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: 3 Titans Most Likely to Be Traded Next After Dealing Jeffery Simmons: Tony Pollard Tops the List
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans have officially waved the white flag for the 2026 NFL season, as the franchise traded its best player, All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, to the Chicago Bears in a midseason blockbuster.
Chicago is sending two first-round picks, one in 2027 and the other in 2028, and a 2027 fourth-round pick to Tennessee for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick. The Titans received a haul for the four-time Pro Bowler, but will now kick-start yet another rebuild.
With Tennessee dealing Simmons less than two weeks before the November 10 trade deadline, there's a solid chance general manager Mike Borgonzi seeks offers for other veterans on the roster. Let's take a look at three Titans players who could be packing their bags and heading elsewhere after the Simmons' trade.
Pollard feels like the most obvious choice to go next. The 29-year-old running back is having another productive season so far with 478 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 4.3 yards per carry, and he turned in his best game of the season against the Cleveland Browns in Week 7 with 129 yards and three scores.
ESPN's Dan Graziano believes Pollard is more likely to be moved at the deadline than other running backs potentially on the market, such as Jonathan Taylor of the Indianapolis Colts and Saquon Barkley of the Philadelphia Eagles. A running back-needy team, like the Seattle Seahawks or Denver Broncos, could offer Tennessee an early Day 3 pick for Pollard, which would be a nice return for a running back nearing 30 in the final year of his deal.
Hooker, who came from the same draft class as Simmons in 2019, is under contract through 2028. However, if the Titans are committed to another rebuild, moving on from Hooker would be a logical move.
The 28-year-old is a viable starting safety with playoff experience, which should make him attractive to contenders on the trade market. Hooker has tallied 46 tackles and two interceptions in six starts this season.
If the Titans decide to trade Hooker, long snapper Morgan Cox would be the lone remaining player from the 2021 team that was the No. 1 seed in the AFC. Life moves fast in the NFL.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler said earlier this week that team around the league believe Johnson could be available for the right price . The former New York Jet was one of the Titans' prized offseason additions, but is set to hit free agency in the spring and may not be a long-term piece on the defense.
Johnson has posted three sacks and 21 quarterback pressures this year, and could provide value to a contender as an explosive complementary pass rusher. Tennessee could land an early Day 3 pick for Johnson's services and continue stockpiling picks in 2027 and 2028.
With Simmons gone, no veteran player on the Titans is necessarily safe. Things are about to get very interesting in Nashville ahead of the November 10 deadline.
Dharya Sharma is a sportswriter from Nebraska who has been covering the Tennessee Titans through his website, SharmSports, since 2023. He is also an NFL and NBA writer for The Sporting News and had a previous stop with Sportsnaut. Follow him on X @SharmSports

title: Who the Titans Must Target in 2027 NFL Draft After Trading Away Jeffery Simmons
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans traded Jeffery Simmons today. Perhaps the greatest Titan to ever do it on defense, if not in general, Simmons has been the anchor of many good and bad Tennessee teams. Moving him has been a possibility in recent seasons, but it never seemed like it could happen.
Well, it did happen, and Tennessee got two first-round picks (and a fourth-rounder) in return. We can cry and wear out #98 jersey to bed later, but right now, it's all about the future as a result of this historic trade haul.
Here are three players the Titans have to target with the 2027 first-round selection they just received from the Chicago Bears. We're fully focused on the defensive side of the ball with this one.
Xavier Gilliam is at the top of this list, and not just because he's already sharing a state with the Titans. The DT, in his first year with the Volunteers after two seasons with Penn State, has absolutely broken out for the orange and white.
Through eight games for Tennessee, Gilliam has a whopping six sacks, as well as two forced fumbles and 25 total tackles. Just about every other time this guy makes contact, it's either behind the line or the ball is coming loose.
One of the biggest risers this year has been Tennessee DT Xavier Gilliam and he should be in the DT1 convo Will Echoles is safer but Gilliam has the twitchy athletic traits you can't teach Burst, lateral agility, violence, flexibility, balance were all on display vs Arkansas pic.twitter.com/El7E9Jl30F
Gilliam's past with the Nittany Lions is less than alluring, but what he's accomplished with the Volunteers suggests a more permanent leap than something temporary. His burst and ability to work off linemen makes him an impossible prospect to ignore.
Echoles is the more popular pick at DT, evidenced by his top-10 spot in Jordan Reid's draft ranking, and is the other DT that Saleh and Tennessee should have circled to succeed Simmons next year.
What Echoles lacks in explosiveness he makes up for in diehard consistency. The Rebels' DT has 21 total tackles and 1.5 sacks in his first year as a starter, finding ways to disrupt opposing offenses with a great footwork and ability to get pressure fast.
Last month in a win over the LSU Tigers, Echoles posted an absurd seven pressures, three TFLs, and one sack. He's got the tools to develop into a star at the next level, and at just 20 years old, all it would take is the right system to get him there.
You can say a lot about Robert Saleh, but the one thing that can't be knocked is his system. The Titans' defense poses a promising laboratory for a player like Echoles to grow within.
While it may be natural for the Titans to draft a DT to patch up Simmons' absence, stretching out to the edge for arguably the best defensive talent in the draft would be nothing to wave a hand at.
A South Carolina Gamecock in his third year, Dylan Stewart has shot up draft boards with two sacks and three forced fumbles this year. His movement as an EDGE and burst are simply unmatched in this draft class.
Stewart's ability to find holes in opposing offense lines - and then beat everyone to those holes - suggests the sort of invaluable high IQ that elevates a playmaker's floor. He's likely going to be a top five pick (if not higher) regardless of the team or fit.
If Tennessee ends up with a high selection as expected, it may be a matter of going talent-first and taking Stewart. He's the sort of player you're thankful to grab at any spot; the details can be worked out later.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Winners and Losers: Titans Trade Star DT Jeffery Simmons to Bears in Blockbuster Deal
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans have done the unthinkable... or have they? After years of trade rumors floating around star DT Jeffery Simmons, the Titans have finally taken the biggest swing possible in their rebuild and made the trade.
Simmons is being dealt to the Chicago Bears, per Tom Pelissero, in return for two first-round picks and a fourth-round selection in Nashville. The Titans send a 2028 fifth-rounder in return. This is Tennessee committing to a complete overhaul under Robert Saleh, and it makes sense on paper.
However, it's impossible not to be shocked by this news. Simmons is the definition of a franchise cornerstone, and just yesterday, he addressed a potential trade with little fanfare. In the aftermath of the move, here are the immediate winners and losers from the Titans-Bears agreement.
The Bears are sending two first-round picks and a fourth-rounder to the Titans for Jeff Simmons. A monster deal. https://t.co/yue0reyeOF
This is as simple as it gets. General manager Mike Borgonzi will have two first-round picks to work with - one in each of the next two years. The impact of losing Simmons will be felt immediately (we'll touch on that), but the value here is truly unheard of.
On top of the two first-round selections, the Titans will get a complimentary 2027 fourth-rounder to boot. At 29 years old, to pretend that Simmons doesn't have any gas left in the tank is silly. He's got four sacks this season already.
All the same, eight seasons deep into his career as a Titan, that can only last for so long. The Bears are giving up assets in an effort to contend right now, and Tennessee is doing the opposite in the hopes to contend later in Robert Saleh's new regime.
These picks will be pivotal, but to have them in the first place is massive for a team stuck in the mud.
Naturally, it must be pointed out that Saleh's d-line is about to get a whole lot worse. The unit has already struggled to produce on a consistent basis in spite of Simmons - Tennessee sacked Deshuan Watson just once in their loss last Sunday.
With Simmons out of the picture (who has accounted for nearly half of the team's 11 sacks up to now), pieces like John Franklin-Myers and Jermaine Johnson II will have to pick up the slack in disrupting opposing offenses.
Still, what Simmons leaves behind simply can't be made up this season. Perhaps recently-claimed DT Jonah Laulu will help blunt this blow, but the Titans just lost one of the best players this franchise has ever seen.
You can argue that it's good for the team and accept that it will greatly lessen their defensive impact in the meantime.
Finally, we come to an underrated loser in this whole ordeal. The Jacksonville Jaguars, who currently have a hold on the AFC South division and are in the market for a DT, will have to pay a whole lot more for one now.
Not only would it have been improbable for the Jaguars to pry the best DT on the market away from an in-divison rival, but now that Simmons has gone for a truly outrageous price, you can expect remaining options to be limited to a premium.
Compare the trend to OL Tyler LInderbaum signing a deal north of $80 million with the Las Vegas Raiders in the offseason. Prices are about to skyrocket, and the Titans are to blame in this instance.
Tennessee loads up on stock for the future and manages to make life harder on the Jaguars in the meantime. That's a win for the Titans, but for a Jacksonville defense that already lost DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers, this is a stinging defeat.
Circling back to the aforemention Franklin-Myers, the 30-year old DL steps in as the sort of resident veteran remaining on this defense with Simmons gone. The Titans will be asking more of Myers now than ever.
But that's a win for the former Denver Bronco. Myers has 1.5 sacks up to now, and PFF has him graded at 31st among 126 qualified DLs in the NFL. That's the upper echelon, making him perhaps the only "elite" defender left on the line.
Myers has yet to rise to the heights of his 7.5-sack campaign last season, but perhaps an uptick in responsibility in Saleh's defense will do just that. Not only did Tennessee lose a great defender, but they lost a literal captain of this team.
He may be a relative newcomer that was signed earlier this year, but Myers is about the only d-lineman left that balances efficient play with years of experience in the league. Myers is a natural successor, and winner, in this defense.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: New Titans DT Jonah Laulu: More Potential Than You Might Think
full_text:
No, the Tennessee Titans didn't claim DT Jonah Laulu yesterday as a way to brace fans for a Jeffery Simmons trade... at least, I can't imagine that being the case. This is simply a player swap on the waiver wire (where Tennessee dropped DT Timmy Horne) in an effort to improve.
After a knockout performance in Week 6, leveling six sacks, Robert Saleh's defensive line slowed way down in the following game vs. the Cleveland Browns. The unit struggled to pressure Deshaun Watson on a consistent basis, logging just one sack by the end of the contest.
That result left fans feeling like the week prior was more a fluke than anything else. I wouldn't go that far - the d-line certainly has the pieces to succeed - but it's probably fair to say at this point that they aren't quite there yet. You could say the same for most every unit on this Titans team.
However, a little change can go a long way, and the pickup of Laulu may be more promising than looks. Where Horne had zero career sacks through three seasons, Laulu has 5.5, including a half-sack this year. There's smoke to this fire.
Four of Laulu's total sacks came in a breakout 2025 campaign. The former Oklahoma Sooner played in all 17 games for the Las Vegas Raiders, netting 51 total tackles and five passes defended to go with his sacks.
In the Titans' loss to the Raiders last season, Laulu was directly responsible for a Cam Ward interception due to hitting him on the throw. Laulu also sacked Ward with a nice spin on the inside shoulder to get free. At 26 years old, Laulu may be older than your average three-year veteran, but he still has ample time to grow in the right system.
Take Tennessee DE Jacob Martin for example, who is 30 this season and has 3.5 sacks. Martin has been a pivotal playmaker off the edge, and at this rate, could break his career-high total of 5.5 sacks from last season. It's about circumstance.
Laulu, in spite of all the Titans' woes, is stepping into a beneficial circumstance for any defender in that he's playing under Saleh. He may have slipped up in the Raiders' new regime, but the DT's 2025 stat sheet points to a player with more under the hood than a half-sack.
If I had to bet on any coach popping that hood, it's Saleh. Laulu isn't guaranteed to get an extended shot in Nashville, but if he does, the third-year DT has the tools to make a splash.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Weighing Bold Changes to Fix Titans' Offense: Mitch Trubisky Question Gets Real, Brian Daboll Must Adjust
full_text:
In February, the Tennessee Titans announced the hiring of former AP NFL Coach of the Year recipient Brian Daboll as offensive coordinator as a member of Robert Saleh's all-new coaching staff.
Daboll told the media he decided to come to the Titans over other offers due to his relationship with Saleh from their time as head coaches in New York and to work with QB Cam Ward. 10 months later, the Daboll-Ward pairing has culminated in the second-to-last scoring offense in the NFL as the Titans sit at a disastrous 1-6 record.
Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns at home has soured any remaining chance at a playoff chase for Tennessee.
Throughout the season Tennessee's offense has struggled to move the ball, ranking dead last in yards per game. Tennessee also has the lowest average time of possession, which is three minutes less than the 31st-ranked Los Angeles Chargers, who are still winless. These bottom-dwelling stats are even more embarrassing when considering how aggressive the Titans were in free agency.
The Titans spent more than any other team in the NFL in the most recent free agency period. Tennessee signed 28 contracts for more than $330 million .
The biggest signing of the offseason went to WR Wan'Dale Robinson. Robinson received a four-year deal worth up to $70 million after he broke out with the Giants in 2025 with a 1,000-yard receiving season. Daboll coached Robinson in New York for more than three seasons.
While there's no denying Robinson is a talented wideout, he only has 29 receptions and his 205 receiving yards rank 85th in the NFL.
The next highest offensive deal went to TE Daniel Bellinger, a three-year deal worth up to $24 million. Bellinger played for Daboll alongside Robinson in New York. In all seven games played this season Bellinger has been nearly non-existent in the passing game, only recording six receptions for 34 yards and zero touchdowns.
The Titans have been terrible on the offensive side of the ball this year; you just can't mince words regarding their current state. Something has to change.
One of the biggest head-scratchers from Titans' season has been Daboll's refusal to shake up personnel. The best example of Daboll's stubbornness has been with the running backs. His all-in approach with RB Tony Pollard has been questionable.
Pollard has consumed 112 of 161 total carries from Tennessee running backs this season. Rookie RB Nick Singleton has only seen offensive snaps in three games this season despite being completely healthy.
Backup RB Tyjae Spears was a scratch against the Browns amidst a knee injury and sharp decerease in snaps. Two weeks ago against Houston, Spears led the Titans in receptions with nine catches on nine targets for 28 yards.
In Week 4, Daboll called for a handoff to Pollard at the goal line four times in a row against the Ravens, which resulted in a 14-point swing after Pollard got stuffed on each attempt. Similar struggles unfolded against Cleveland, where the Titans were unable to score on the goal line, which resulted in a turnover on downs and a major momentum swing.
Tennessee has been one of the worst scoring offenses in the red zone this season, to boot. That brings us to the QB problem.
Ward is playing like someone who should be benched. Daboll hasn't developed Ward (he's seemingly done the opposite up to now) despite an improved offensive line and additional weapons with Robinson and fourth overall pick WR Carnell Tate surrounding the QB.
In Ward's first seven career starts last season, he threw for 1,356 yards and four touchdowns to five interceptions with a 70.9 passer rating. The Titans had a 1-6 record in that stretch. With Daboll this season, Ward has thrown for 1,179 yards and four touchdowns to five interceptions with a 73.8 passer rating. Like last season, Tennessee is 1-6 by Week 7 with Ward under center.
Ward has only been sacked 11 times this season compared to 30 times by Week 7 in 2025.
According to PFF , Ward ranks in the bottom 10 of qualified passers in touchdowns, throws beyond 20 yards, and has an average depth of target. These stats are especially concerning with teams like the Falcons, Ravens, Buccaneers, Eagles, Bears, Vikings, Commanders and Giants starting two or more different passers this season due to injuries.
After losing to Cleveland on Sunday, Ward has a 4-20 overall record as a starter. Even if the move isn't permanent, the second-year QB and Tennessee both may benefit from sitting him right now.
Believe it or not, backup QB Mitchell Trubisky was the Titans' third-most expensive signing of the offseason ($10.5 million over two years), and has also played under Daboll. Trubisky and Daboll shared one season together in Buffalo, where he saw limited clock as the backup to future league MVP QB Josh Allen.
Daboll had served as the offensive coordinator for the Bills for three seasons prior to his hiring by the New York Giants for head coach in 2022. Nonetheless, Daboll and Mitchell have familiarity. Mitchell is a 10-year veteran with a 31-26 record as a starting quarterback .
The former second overall pick in the 2017 NFL Draft last started in the NFL for the Pittsburgh Steelers in 2023. While Trubisky isn't a solution to all the Titans' offensive problems, his experience shouldn't be undermined.
Over the past two seasons with the Bills, Trubisky has thrown for 492 yards and six touchdowns to zero interceptions across 13 appearances. Having Ward sit behind a seasoned veteran like Trubisky could offer a new perspective for a day-one starting quarterback.
I'll say it if nobody else will: The Titans should turn signal calling duties to Trubisky and offer their fans something different. That may have been an overreaction a few short weeks ago, but at 1-6, what does Daboll have left to lose on that side of the ball?
Isaiah is an award-winning journalist and photojournalist. title: Smoke Rising Around Titans Trading Tony Pollard: Where the RB Could Go, and What Tennessee Could Get
full_text:
Today, ESPN's Dan Graziano reported that Tony Pollard is "more likely" to be moved before the trade deadline than backs like Jonathan Taylor and Saquon Barkley. Coming off his best game of the season, the Titans' veteran RB could strike the perfect balance on the market.
If the Colts don't move off their aforementioned superstar back, in Taylor, Pollard presents as a promising "fallback plan," as Jeremy Fowler put it in his own report. Pollard ran for three touchdowns and 129 yards in Tennessee's loss to the Cleveland Browns last Sunday.
With the trade deadline approaching in November 10, every week from here on out will matter for Pollard's market, and he could be moved at any time. Even if the Titans may have to wait for someone like Taylor to fall in one place or another, the smoke is rapidly rising around a Pollard trade.
I'm here to take a look at potential landing spots for Pollard, as well as what the Titans could realistically get for the back if he were to be traded.
The Seattle Seahawks have long been circled as a destination for Pollard. With Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price both dealing with injuries, backup back Emanuel Wilson has been Seattle's go-to guy in the backfield. However, Wilson is averaging just 3.6 yards per carry right now.
Charbonnet will be the guy when he returns, but the volatile state of the Seahawks' backfield could still open the door for Pollard to get safe, complimentary touches. The Denver Broncos are 24th in the NFL in rushing yards per game according to TeamRankings (94.9) and have been widely pinned as a landing spot for Taylor.
Again, any team in the market for Taylor could realistically settle for Pollard in the case that Indy looks elsewhere. One of the worst offenses in the league, in Denver, could swing on someone like Pollard to bring a sturdy veteran presence to a run-by-committee backfield.
That brings us to the Minnesota Vikings, another one of the least effective offenses in the league. Brian Flores' defense has covered up a scoring unit with little to no reliability. With Aaron Jones Sr. fading out of consistency at 32 years old, and longtime Vikings backup Jordan Mason just now returning from a Week 1 injury, Pollard makes sense here, too.
Pollard could click in as a slightly younger, more effective option than Jones, spell Mason in his return, and help guide rookie back Demond Claiborne just as he has Tyjae Spears and Nick Singleton in Tennessee.
As a footnote of sorts, the New York Giants were also mentioned by Jordan Schultz as a team looking for an RB. The market is there for Pollard, but what exactly would it look like for Tennessee?
The Titans aren't securing a first-day pick for Pollard or anything like that. However, with the back in the final year of his contract and Tennessee still enduring a rebuild, any sort of draft capital would be a win at this point.
A fourth-rounder feels like best-case scenario, but depending on the buyer, the Titans could potentially make that happen. Prior to this season, the Pittsburgh Steelers dealt 2025 third-round RB Kaleb Johnson to the Green Bay Packers for a 2028 sixth-round pick.
Pollard is six years older than Johnson, but to a team in need of an immediate contributor that's trying to contend, Pollard may be worth that price or better. We're talking proven contributor vs. pure potential. Anything less than a sixth almost doesn't seem worth it for Tennessee at this point.
Then again, if Pollard is headed out this offseason either way, what do you have to lose? Pollard's field could swing a few rounds in either direction, but if there are multiple buyers interested, Tennessee should be able to squeeze out a decent day-three selection.
We'll keep you posted as news continues to build regarding the Titans and Pollard. Fans should keep a thumb on the pulse of this one ahead of Tennessee's matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Jayden Daniels Looking to Snap Dubious Streak Dating Back to Last October — Commanders Daily
full_text:
The Washington Commanders are trying to dig out of an early-season hole. Their star quarterback is also trying to break free from a streak nobody ever wants to be a part of, as he hasn't won a game as a starter since October 5, 2025 , against the Chargers, which will be 392 days on Sunday. In that amount of time, Washington is 0-7-1 in his starts, including four injury-interrupted appearances. The team has also had two offensive coordinators during that timeline, with Kliff Kingsbury leaving this past offseason and David Blough being promoted.
Seattle was already up 31-7 at halftime last season, well before Daniels injured his elbow in the fourth quarter. The four starts he finished ended in losses by one, two, and six points, along with the tie against the Giants. Against New York, Daniels ran for 103 yards and two touchdowns, helping Washington build a 14-point fourth-quarter lead. The defense couldn't hold it, and the offense stalled late . Washington still had a chance to win, but Daniels and Quinn both took responsibility for the clock-management failure that kept the Commanders from attempting a potential winning field goal.
Jayden Daniels threw three touchdowns but also an interception. He accepted responsibility for the late botched exchange that gave Chicago its winning possession.
At Dallas: October 19, 2025
Dallas led 27–15 at halftime. Daniels left with a hamstring injury in the third quarter; Marcus Mariota later threw a pick-six.
Washington trailed 31–7 at halftime, well before Daniels’ fourth-quarter elbow injury.
At Minnesota: December 7, 2025
Daniels completed 9 of 20 passes for 78 yards and an interception before another elbow injury ended his appearance.
At Philadelphia: September 13, 2026
Early offensive struggles preceded two Daniels touchdown passes. The late two-point attempt was stopped.
At Dallas: September 20, 2026
Daniels dislocated his elbow before halftime. Mariota played the second half.
Washington surrendered a 14-point fourth-quarter lead, then failed to attempt a potential winning kick before time expired.
At San Francisco: October 19, 2026
Washington gained 90 first-half yards. Daniels finished with 300 passing yards and two touchdowns, but the comeback ended with a sack.
Blough gave an assessment of Daniels on Thursday : "I think his superpower is how he protects the football. And you never want to take that away from him. And at the same time, you go back and look at every snap and see where we can improve. So whether it's changing how we're reading a concept or seeing something that might show up on tape, we try to evaluate everything as we go back and look at the, I guess, three and a half games he's gotten," Blough said. "So we're happy with where he's at. There's always room to improve. So, you know, looking forward to continue that process." The offense has a specific place to start coming out of the bye. “And then the biggest hangup for us as a unit so far has been third and fourth down. So we've got to be able to, you know, when everybody knows we're going to throw it, we've got to be able to hit our landmarks, protect, throw, catch, coach, play better, you know, coach and execute better at that point,” Blough said. Washington gets its first chance to show what's changed against Philadelphia on Sunday night. A win would move the Commanders to 2-4-1 and give them their first division victory of the season.

title: Commanders Rookie Power Rankings: Sonny Styles' No. 1 Spot Faces a Real Challenge
full_text:
It's been two weeks since we last visited the Washington Commanders Rookie Power Rankings , but Washington has only played one game since then. The 23–17 loss to San Francisco gave us another look at the rookies before the bye, and while some have strengthened their cases, others haven't done much to help theirs. That said, here is where the class stands after six games.
There's not much reason to move Sonny Styles from the top spot, even if his PFF grades have slipped a bit since our last rankings. Styles followed his 13-tackle performance against the Giants with another 13 against San Francisco, adding a pass defensed while playing 53 of Washington's 62 defensive snaps. Through six games, he leads the team with 46 tackles, along with a sack, an interception, a forced fumble, and four passes defensed in 361 defensive snaps. The grades tell us there's still work to do. Styles has dropped from a 71.6 overall PFF grade to 68.9, putting him 24th among 74 qualifying linebackers. His coverage grade has fallen from 75.1 to 72.7, while his 58.0 run-defense grade and eight missed tackles remain areas that need improvement. Still, we're talking about a rookie who has started all six games, handled the green dot when needed, and is already leading Washington in tackles. That's enough to keep him at No. 1.
Sonny Styles was all over the field last night, posting 13 total tackles, 4 stop tackles, and 1 PBU pic.twitter.com/KOjcUWiDnQ
Antonio Williams made a pretty good case for moving back into the top spot against San Francisco, catching three passes for 50 yards, his most since the season opener. What makes those catches more interesting is when they happened. Williams ran 35 routes but wasn't targeted until the fourth quarter, when all four of his targets came on third down. His three receptions accounted for all three of Washington's successful third-down conversions. Through six games, Williams has 18 catches for 205 yards and a touchdown, with PFF giving him a 74.0 overall grade, 23rd among 76 qualifying receivers. He's also yet to be charged with a drop. The bigger news is what comes next. With Terry McLaurin out for the season, Dan Quinn has already said Williams should see more targets . He played 45 of 67 offensive snaps against San Francisco (67%), so the opportunities have been there in terms of playing time. Now we'll see if Washington actually gets him the ball more often.
More workload expected for Antonio Williams with Terry McLaurin out for the rest of the season. Today OC David Blough talked about how you can see Williams’ process refining, you can’t deny that the ball finds him & they’re really happy with where he’s at. pic.twitter.com/aNysJm5Bdp
Drew Stevens continues to give Washington reasons to feel better about its kicking situation. He made his only field-goal attempt against San Francisco, a 51-yarder, bringing his streak to seven straight makes and his season total to 10-of-12 (83.3%). He's also now made three field goals from at least 50 yards, setting a Washington rookie season record , while his 57-yarder against Seattle remains the longest by a rookie in franchise history. The extra points still need attention, with Stevens sitting at 10-of-13 (76.9%), although two of those failures came under unusual circumstances. His 57.3 PFF field-goal grade ranks 29th among 32 qualifying kickers, but seven straight makes and two franchise rookie records after six games are nothing to dismiss.
There isn't much new to report on Matt Gulbin, who hasn't played an offensive snap since starting at right guard against Indianapolis. He finished that game with 64 snaps and remains at 72 for the season, earning a 63.2 overall PFF grade with a 62.7 in pass blocking and 60.9 in run blocking. He's allowed two pressures, including a sack and a quarterback hit, without committing a penalty. With Sam Cosmi back at right guard and Lucas Patrick starting at center , Gulbin hasn't been needed again. His starting experience in London is enough to keep him fourth for now.
Joshua Josephs' playing time had been gradually increasing before the San Francisco game, but that trend went in the wrong direction. After playing 20 defensive snaps against the Giants, he dropped to 13 against the 49ers, bringing his season total to 86. PFF now has Josephs at 44.6 overall, down from 49.0 in our last edition, with a 53.9 pass-rush grade and just one pressure on 34 pass-rush snaps. His 64.4 run-defense grade is considerably better, but the pass-rush production that made him stand out during the preseason still hasn't arrived. With Kaliakmanis moving back toward third-string duties, Josephs' regular playing time is enough to move him up one spot.
We haven't seen Athan Kaliakmanis since his debut against Indianapolis, when he completed 15-of-33 passes for 186 yards, a touchdown, and an interception after Marcus Mariota injured his knee. He was back on the sidelines against San Francisco, with Jayden Daniels playing all 67 offensive snaps. Mariota has since returned to practice , so Kaliakmanis could move further away from another opportunity. For now, his 54 snaps in London remain the only regular-season work we have to judge him on.
Tanoa Togiai remains on Washington's active roster, but we're still waiting to see him take his first regular-season offensive snap. He was inactive again against San Francisco, leaving his biggest accomplishment so far unchanged: making the 53-man roster as an undrafted rookie. There's nothing new to judge him on until he gets onto the field.
With the Eagles coming to Washington on Sunday, the rookies will have another opportunity to show where they stand. As the season moves forward, playing time and production will continue to determine who moves up, who falls, and who stays where they are. title: Commanders’ Depth Faces Three Games in 12 Days With Their Season on the Line
full_text:
On Sunday night (November 1), the Washington Commanders host the Philadelphia Eagles; they’ll be playing for the first time in 13 days after a tale of two halves against the 49ers on MNF. The following week, Washington will host the Rams on Sunday, November 8, before they travel to play the Giants on Thursday Night Football on November 12. For those doing the math, that's three games in 12 days, with the New York game coming on the short week. After the events of the last few weeks, it's understandable to question some things with the staff, but Commanders head coach Dan Quinn acknowledged the task ahead: "We certainly know what's ahead over the next, you know, three games, and all of them in the conference and two of them are in the division. So, um, our focus right now is just on Philadelphia now," Quinn said.
That starts with the defensive line. Daron Payne played 53 of Washington’s 62 defensive snaps against San Francisco, while Shy Tuttle played 28 and Tim Settle played 25. Javon Kinlaw added 27, and if he can’t go against Philadelphia, somebody has to take on that work. Quinn and Daronte Jones need a rotation that gives Payne dependable relief, especially with a short week waiting at the end of this stretch. Washington needs to know what it can get from the rest of that group. With Jer'Zhan Newton's 21-day window open , he'll be an option again once he's activated. Newton and Charles Omenihu were limited in Wednesday's practice, while Javon Kinlaw remained sidelined with his knee . Newton and Omenihu could give the defensive front a boost, especially Omenihu, who can play inside and on the edge. One name to watch for usage moving forward is Trey Amos. Against the Niners, Washington played Amik Robertson 62 snaps, while Amos and Rasul Douglas both had 36. It'll be interesting to see whether that number jumps or drops, with Douglas playing fairly well lately. With Terry McLaurin out for the season , a lingering question of who gets his targets now remains unanswered. According to Quinn's comments on Monday: "Antonio [Williams] is one that you'd see getting more targets to go." That's probably true, but with Stefon Diggs and Treylon Burks in the mix, and Van Jefferson just signed to the active roster, the receiving room still looks pretty crowded.
DL ramming into a tackling dummy as ADL coach Darryl Tapp SCREAMS in their ear. Johnny Newton is the second player pic.twitter.com/eF0yk4hjGq
I’d get the rotation going early against Philadelphia. If Newton is activated, give him a defined role up front, and keep Douglas involved as Amos works back in. On offense, I’d give Williams planned opportunities from the opening drive and use this week to get the other receivers comfortable with their assignments. Quinn has options. He and his staff have had the bye to settle those roles and get the groups working together, and at 1-4-1, Washington has little room for another loss Sunday.
